summary: Study B: checklist vs generic review on 22 held-out flawed/clean analysis packages, 3 replicates, blinded grading with adjudication and code verification

review.summary: The headline conclusion, that neither readout transfers from K562 to RPE1 and that the RPE1 label is to blame, comes from a bug in the scoring metric. circ_corr (the Jammalamadaka coefficient) centres the predicted and the true angles separately, each on its own mean direction. RPE1 phases are spread almost evenly around the circle (resultant length R = 0.043), so the label's mean direction (11.8 deg) carries no real information. The transferred predictions have a mean direction of about 227 deg. The coefficient then comes out close to cos(difference of the two means) = -0.82, which matches the reported -0.814. The per-cell agreement is actually good. Median angular errors are 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against about 90 deg for shuffled predictions. 81% of RPE1 cells are predicted within 45 deg. The mean signed error is 3.8 deg. Valid circular agreement measures are clearly positive for both readouts: correlation with a shared centre, mean cos(error), and Fisher-Lee correlation. The validity gate and the verdict depend only on the sign of this broken metric. The log even says 'worse than chance (90deg)' while printing errors of 24 and 16 deg. So the SUMMARY claims of no valid transfer, an invalid RPE1 label, retention of about -0.9, and nothing learned about generalisation cannot stand. On the same data, expression transfers better than the model activations. Smaller problems: the expression baseline contains the marker genes that define the label (partly circular); K562 and RPE1 are normalised differently; the two datasets' labels are built from different marker sets (87 vs 93 genes); and the CV labels are computed with all K562 cells, including the held-out folds (mild leakage).

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 39-43 (circ_corr) and 67, 74 (its use for within/transfer)
findings.description: The Jammalamadaka circular correlation centres each variable on its own sample mean direction. That is not valid when the phases are spread almost evenly around the circle, as cell-cycle phase is. The RPE1 label's mean direction is close to arbitrary. The frozen predictions have a different mean direction, so the sine terms come out anti-correlated even though per-cell predictions match the label closely. The reported transfer scores of -0.814 (model) and -0.796 (expression) are an artefact of this, not evidence of failure.
findings.evidence: I reproduced the run exactly (model JS = -0.8142, median error = 23.95 deg). RPE1 true phase: mean direction 11.8 deg, R = 0.043 (almost uniform). Model predictions on RPE1: mean direction 226.7 deg, R = 0.34. cos(difference of means) = -0.82, close to the reported -0.814. Per-cell agreement: mean signed error 3.8 deg (R of errors 0.79); 81% of cells within 45 deg; median error 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against a shuffled-prediction null of about 90-93 deg (1st percentile 90-92 deg). JS computed with a shared centre (the true mean) gives model 0.848 and expression 0.899. Mean cos(error) is 0.79 and 0.88. Fisher-Lee rho_T on a 1,500-cell subsample is 0.55 and 0.73. Dropping the RPE1 cells with label >270 deg flips the model JS to +0.52 while the median error stays at 28 deg. Within K562 the two mean directions are almost the same (29.5 vs 28.5 deg), which is why the within scores are positive.
findings.recommended_action: Replace circ_corr with a measure that holds up when the data are spread evenly around the circle. Options: mean cos(predicted - true), Fisher-Lee rho_T, or JS centred on a shared reference. Report median/mean angular error against a permutation null. Rerun and report within, transfer and retention on the corrected measure.

findings.description: The pass/fail gate needs transfer > 0 AND median error < 90 deg. Both readouts easily meet the error condition and fail only on the sign of the broken circ_corr. The verdict text and log message ('both below chance', 'both worse than chance (90deg)', 'The target's phase label is not cell cycle') contradict the numbers printed in the same line.
findings.evidence: Log: 'model -0.814 (24deg), expression -0.796 (16deg) -- both worse than chance (90deg)'. Errors of 24 and 16 deg are far below (better than) the 90 deg chance level. The JSON records model_valid=false and expression_valid=false only because the transfer value is negative.
findings.recommended_action: Fix the metric (F1) and recompute the gate. Base validity on a permutation test of angular error or a proper circular association, and correct the verdict and log wording. With the corrected metric both readouts pass.

findings.description: The headline result is wrong: the table, 'Both fail on RPE1, and in the same way', 'Neither passes the validity rule', 'No valid transfer'. Both readouts recover RPE1 phase well with no refitting. The retention values (-0.91, -0.87) are ratios built on the artefactual metric and mean nothing.
findings.evidence: See F1. Corrected retention is about 0.95 (model) and 0.98 (expression) with shared-centre JS, or about 0.69 and 0.87 with Fisher-Lee (within 0.79 and 0.84). Median error rises from 12.6 to 24.0 deg for the model and from 10.8 to 16.0 deg for expression, against a chance level of 90 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite the Result table and bullets with the corrected metric. State that both readouts transfer well above chance.

findings.description: The claim that the RPE1 marker-PCA label is invalid ('RPE1 is not a valid target for this variable') has no support. The frozen K562 readouts reproduce the RPE1 label cell by cell, and the summary's own orientation checks (S peak at 45 deg, G2/M 97-109 deg later in both datasets) show the label is consistent. The recommendation to drop RPE1 and choose another target follows from the metric bug, not from the data.
findings.evidence: 81% of RPE1 cells are predicted within 45 deg of their RPE1 label. The mean signed error is 3.8 deg. Both orientation diagnostics in the log are consistent (K562 G2/M at 153.8 deg, RPE1 at 142.1 deg). The only real difference is that the predicted phases are less evenly spread on RPE1 (R = 0.34; too many cells in the 180-270 deg bins). That is a calibration shift, not an invalid label.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the 'label is the problem' interpretation and the 'pick a different target' recommendation. If useful, describe the phase-dependent calibration shift of the transferred predictions.

findings.description: The summary says the run 'says nothing about generalisation' and declares no comparison. Once the metric is fixed, the run does give a comparison: expression transfers better than the C2S layer-21 activations. The model loses more accuracy on transfer and has lower agreement on RPE1.
findings.evidence: Transfer median error: model 24.0 deg vs expression 16.0 deg (within: 12.6 vs 10.8). Fisher-Lee on RPE1: 0.55 vs 0.73. Mean cos(error): 0.79 vs 0.88. Shared-centre JS: 0.848 vs 0.899.
findings.recommended_action: Report the comparison with uncertainty (bootstrap over cells) and caveats (F6, unequal inputs). Do not claim the run is uninformative.

findings.description: The expression readout's features include the 87 marker genes whose PCA defines the phase label. The expression 'point of reference' is therefore partly a reconstruction of the label rather than an independent baseline, which inflates its within and transfer scores compared with the model.
findings.evidence: Ridge on the 87 marker genes alone: within JS 0.978 (4.2 deg median error), transfer median error 13.1 deg. Ridge on shared genes without the markers: within 0.876 (14.2 deg), transfer median error 18.2 deg. The reported version with all genes: within 0.919 (10.8 deg), transfer 16.0 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Exclude the label-defining marker genes from the expression baseline, or report results both with and without them. Also consider how many marker genes appear in the model's top-512 cell sentences.

findings.description: The two h5ad files are not in 'the same format' as the README says. RPE1 X is log1p of counts normalised to 10,000 on its own panel. K562 X was evidently normalised on a larger gene set before subsetting. The frozen K562 StandardScaler/ridge is then applied to RPE1 data on a different scale, which mixes normalisation differences into the expression transfer.
findings.evidence: expm1(X) row sums: K562 min 7,447, median 9,137, max 9,573; RPE1 exactly 10,000 for every cell. Mean log-expression per entry: K562 0.466 vs RPE1 0.394.
findings.recommended_action: Renormalise both datasets the same way on the shared gene panel before the expression readout, and correct the README.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py line 59 (marker intersection per dataset); README.md line 36
findings.description: The ground-truth phase is built from different marker sets in the two datasets: 87 genes in K562 and 93 in RPE1. Source and target labels are therefore not defined identically, and the README mentions only the RPE1 coverage. The gene lists also hold 42 S and 52 G2/M genes, not the full Tirosh/Scanpy 43/54.
findings.evidence: Missing in K562: WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8, UBE2C, GAS2L3. Missing in RPE1: E2F8 only. Log: 'SOURCE ... (87 cc genes) | TARGET ... (93 cc genes)'.
findings.recommended_action: Build both labels from the marker genes shared by both datasets (87), or show that the result does not change; document the coverage for both datasets.

findings.description: The K562 phase labels used for 5-fold CV come from a PCA and orientation fitted on all 3,000 K562 cells, held-out folds included. This is mild transductive leakage into the 'within' score, which is also the denominator of retention.
findings.evidence: phase_angle_oriented(src) is called once on the full source before the KFold loop. The SVD, the standardisation and the top-200 S/G2M peak orientation all use every cell.
findings.recommended_action: Note this as a limitation, or fit the label PCA/orientation inside each training fold and project the test cells.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's documented error is that the Jammalamadaka circ_corr centres each variable on its own circular mean. On RPE1 the true phase is near-uniform (R = 0.043) and the predictions are concentrated (mean about 227/235 deg), so the score comes out negative (-0.814 / -0.796) even though transfer works. F1 meets both parts of the detection rule. (a) It says the negative transfer scores are an artefact of the statistic, not failed transfer. (b) It gives the mechanism and computed alternatives. I re-ran these inline and the numbers match. Own-mean centring, RPE1 true mean 11.8 deg with R 0.043, prediction mean 226.7 deg with R 0.341. Shared-centre JS is 0.848 / 0.899, which is the key's exact correct value. Mean cos(error), equal to R_diff, is 0.79 / 0.88. Median error is 24 / 16 deg against about 90 deg chance. F2 detects it through the gate: both readouts fail only on the sign of the broken circ_corr, while their errors are far below the 90 deg chance level. F3 applies the same point to the headline table and retention, citing F1's mechanism and corrected values. F4 applies it to the 'RPE1 label is invalid' conclusion and shows per-cell agreement (81% of cells within 45 deg, mean signed error 3.8 deg).

findings.reason: This is exactly the key's error: circ_corr centres each variable on its own mean, which breaks with a near-uniform truth and concentrated predictions. All the evidence numbers I checked match an inline re-run and the key. Model cc -0.8142, true mean 11.8 deg with R 0.043, prediction mean 226.7 deg with R 0.341. Shared-centre JS 0.848 / 0.899, mean cos(error) 0.79 / 0.88, 81.5% of cells within 45 deg, mean signed error 3.8 deg. Dropping cells with label >270 deg gives cc +0.52.

The key names the gate at line 131 as part of the error. The finding correctly says both readouts fail only because the artefactual circ_corr is negative. Their median errors (24 / 16 deg) are far below the 90 deg chance level, so the log text 'both worse than chance' contradicts its own numbers.

This is the wrong_result from the key ('no valid transfer', negative retention). The finding blames the metric (citing F1) and gives corrected positive values. Its shared-centre retention of about 0.95 / 0.98 is consistent with the key's corrected retention of 0.89 / 0.96, which the key computes with R_diff.

The key lists 'the RPE1 marker-PCA angle does not measure cell cycle, so RPE1 is not a valid target' as part of the wrong result. The finding correctly says this follows from the metric bug, and backs it with per-cell agreement and the consistent orientation diagnostics (G2/M at 153.8 deg in K562 and 142.1 deg in RPE1, S at 45 deg in both).

The numbers are correct: expression beats the model on transfer by median error, mean cos(error) and shared-centre JS. But the key says the two readouts get different inputs and the summary deliberately declines to rank them as a stated caveat. Pushing for a model-vs-expression ranking is therefore not a load-bearing problem. It is partly a downstream consequence of the documented error.

It is true that the label-defining marker genes are among the expression features. The key calls this a design property of a marker-defined label, shared by both versions of the analysis, and lists treating it as the load-bearing error as a possible false alarm. The finding does not claim it explains the sign of any score, so it counts as a minor, non-load-bearing caveat.

Confirmed. expm1(X) row sums are 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 (min / median / max) in K562 versus exactly 10,000 in RPE1, and mean log-expression is 0.466 vs 0.394. The two datasets were therefore normalised on different gene bases, and the README's 'same format' glosses over this. It is a genuine but small confound for the frozen expression transfer. That transfer still works well (16 deg median error), so it does not change any headline claim.

Confirmed. 87 vs 93 markers, missing in K562: WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8, UBE2C, GAS2L3; missing in RPE1: E2F8. The lists hold 42 S and 52 G2/M genes. The key states these counts as known facts, and orientation is consistent across datasets. This is a documentation point with no material effect.

It is true that the unsupervised label PCA and orientation are fitted on all K562 cells before cross-validation. But this is the standard way to define a ground-truth label, not leakage of readout parameters. The scaler and ridge are fit inside each fold, and the key says the within scores are valid (they agree with R_diff to 0.011). At most a trivial limitation.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets both parts of the detection rule. (a) It says the transfer scores of -0.814 and -0.796 are an artefact of circ_corr and not evidence that transfer failed. (b) It gives the mechanism: each variable is centred on its own mean, the true RPE1 phase is near-uniform (R=0.043, mean 11.8 deg) and the predictions are concentrated (R=0.34, mean 226.7 deg). It also gives the contradiction with median errors of 24/16 deg against a chance level near 90 deg, and computed alternatives that show strong positive transfer. Those alternatives are circ_corr with a shared centre (0.848/0.899) and mean cos(error) (0.79/0.88), which matches the key's R_diff of 0.789/0.878. I reproduced all of these numbers inline. F2 detects the error at the gate: both readouts fail only on the sign of the broken statistic while their median errors are far below chance, and they pass once the metric is fixed. F3 states the headline and retention are artefacts of the metric and gives corrected values. F4 states the 'RPE1 label is invalid' conclusion comes from the metric bug, citing per-cell agreement.

findings.reason: This is the key's error, with the right location (lines 39-43, 67, 74) and the right mechanism (each variable centred on its own mean; truth near-uniform, predictions concentrated). I reproduced the numbers inline: true R 0.043, mean 11.8 deg; model prediction R 0.341, mean 226.7 deg; shared-centre circ_corr 0.848/0.899; mean cos(error) 0.788/0.878; mean signed error 3.8 deg; 81.5% of cells within 45 deg; dropping labels above 270 deg gives +0.524. It also correctly notes the within scores are valid because the two means coincide.

The key names the gate at line 131 as part of the error. Its failure rests only on the sign of circ_corr, and the log message 'both worse than chance (90deg)' contradicts the 24/16 deg errors printed on the same line. The finding concludes that both readouts pass under a corrected metric, which matches the key's correct_result.

This targets the key's wrong_result in SUMMARY.md: the table, 'both fail', 'no valid transfer', and retention of -0.91/-0.87. Its corrected retention from shared-centre circ_corr (0.848/0.897 = 0.95, 0.899/0.919 = 0.98) is arithmetically right and close to the key's 0.89/0.96 from R_diff.

The key's wrong_result explicitly includes the summary's conclusion that the RPE1 marker-PCA label is not cell cycle and that RPE1 is not a valid target. The finding correctly traces this to the metric bug and cites per-cell agreement and consistent orientation (G2/M peaks at 153.8 and 142.1 deg). Both points agree with the key's known true facts.

The numbers are right: I reproduced transfer median error 24.0 vs 16.0 deg and shared-centre circ_corr 0.848 vs 0.899. Interpretation 3 is partly a downstream consequence of the bad metric. However, the summary declines to rank model against expression mainly because the two readouts get different inputs, which the key accepts as a stated caveat. Arguing that a comparison should be reported is secondary and does not overturn a headline claim.

The facts are true and I reproduced them: 87 markers among the shared genes; markers alone give within 0.978 (4.2 deg) and transfer 13.1 deg; without markers, within 0.876 (14.2 deg) and transfer 18.2 deg. But the key treats marker overlap as a design property of a marker-defined label, shared by both versions of the analysis. It does not explain the sign of any score, and the summary does not compare the readouts head-to-head, so it is not a load-bearing problem.

Confirmed inline. expm1(X) row sums are 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 (min/median/max) for K562 and exactly 10,000 for RPE1, and mean log-expression is 0.466 vs 0.394. So the README's 'same format' is inaccurate, and the two datasets' expression inputs are normalised differently before the frozen K562 scaler is applied. This is a real but small preprocessing inconsistency (expression transfer still works, at 16 deg). It is distinct from the key's false alarm about the source-fit scaler.

Confirmed: the lists hold 42 S and 52 G2/M genes; K562 is missing WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8, UBE2C and GAS2L3, and RPE1 is missing only E2F8. The key lists the 87/93 coverage as a known fact. The difference in label construction is real but trivial, and orientation is consistent across datasets.

It is true that the unsupervised label PCA and orientation use all K562 cells before CV. But the scaler and ridge are fit inside each fold (the key flags 'within-source CV leaks' as a false alarm), the label is an unsupervised definition of ground truth, and the key notes the within scores agree with R_diff. At most a negligible limitation.

review.summary:
I reproduced the run exactly: within 0.897/0.919 and transfer -0.814/-0.796 match outputs/transfer_rpe1.json and the log. The headline conclusion does not hold. The readouts did not fail to transfer, and the RPE1 label is not invalid. The negative "transfer" scores are an artifact of the Jammalamadaka circular correlation in circ_corr. It centres each variable on its own sample circular mean, and here both phase distributions are close to uniform or bimodal (resultant length 0.04 for the RPE1 truth). The predicted mean (227 deg model, 235 deg expression) and the true mean (12 deg) therefore end up about 215 deg apart, which flips the sign. Every other measure says the frozen readouts transfer well:
- Median error is 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against a permutation null of about 95 deg.
- 81% of RPE1 cells are predicted within 45 deg.
- The cos and sin correlations are +0.85 and +0.86.
- The Fisher-Lee circular correlation is +0.56 (model) and +0.74 (expression).
- The same coefficient with any common centre is +0.62 to +0.90.
- A readout built only on the 87 marker genes that define the label (within 0.978, 4 deg) still scores -0.82 with a 13 deg median error.

The RPE1 phase label behaves just like K562's: S-score and G2M-score profiles across phase bins are nearly identical. So the validity gate, the "below chance / label is not cell cycle" verdict, the retention values and SUMMARY interpretations 1-3 all rest on a broken metric. With sound metrics, the run does show transfer, and the model loses more accuracy than expression does. Checks that held up: data alignment (row_cell_ids is the identity), the gene counts, 93 of 94 markers present in RPE1, and the orientation/no-mirror check. The K562 vs RPE1 normalisation difference has no effect on the results.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 39-43 (circ_corr), used at lines 67 and 74; SUMMARY.md lines 11-12, 19-20
findings.description: The transfer score uses the Jammalamadaka circular correlation, which centres each angle on its own sample circular mean. Both the true and the predicted phase distributions are close to uniform or bimodal (G2/M and G1 modes), so those means are poorly defined and can lie far apart. Here they sit about 215 deg apart, which flips the coefficient's sign even though the predictions agree closely with the truth. The reported transfer correlations of -0.814 and -0.796 therefore do not measure how well the readouts transfer, and the headline 'Both fail on RPE1' is wrong.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced: transfer JS -0.814 (model) and -0.796 (expression). Resultant length of the true RPE1 phase is 0.043 (circular mean 11.8 deg). The predicted means are 226.7 deg (model) and 235.2 deg (expression).

Other measures on the same predictions:
- Median error 24.0 and 16.0 deg, against a permutation null of 95.2 and 94.5 deg.
- 81.5% of cells within 45 deg (model).
- corr(cos pred, cos true) = 0.845; corr(sin, sin) = 0.860.
- Fisher-Lee rho_T = +0.564 (model) and +0.741 (expression).
- Resultant length of the difference (pred - true) = 0.789 and 0.878, with mean offset 3.8 deg.
- The same JS formula with a common centre gives +0.62 to +0.90 for every centre from 0 to 315 deg (+0.85 when centred on the true mean).
- An expression readout built only on the 87 label-defining marker genes (within JS 0.978, 4 deg) still gets transfer JS -0.817 with a 13 deg median error.
- Bootstrap 95% interval of the code's JS for the model transfer: -0.90 to -0.51.
findings.recommended_action: Replace circ_corr with a measure that does not depend on each sample's own mean. Options are Fisher-Lee rho_T, the mean resultant length of (pred - true), or circular-circular correlation with a common reference. Report these alongside the median and mean angular error and a permutation null, then rerun and rewrite the Result table and bullets.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 129-138 (validity gate and verdict); outputs/transfer_rpe1.json 'verdict'; outputs/run_log.txt; SUMMARY.md lines 21-22, 29-30
findings.description: The validity gate requires transfer > 0, so it fails both readouts purely because of the sign artifact in F1, even though both pass the median-error condition by a wide margin. Whenever the gate fails, the verdict and log message print a fixed text saying both readouts are 'below chance' / 'worse than chance (90deg)' and that the target label 'is invalid' / 'not cell cycle'. These statements contradict the numbers printed in the same line and are never tested anywhere. The SUMMARY repeats them ('Neither passes the validity rule', 'No valid transfer').
findings.evidence:
The log reads: model -0.814 (24deg), expression -0.796 (16deg) -- both worse than chance (90deg). The target's phase label is not cell cycle.

But 24 and 16 deg are far below the 90 deg chance threshold the code itself uses (CHANCE_ERR_DEG = 90; the permutation null is about 95 deg). model_valid and expression_valid are False only because of the first condition, r['transfer'] > 0.
findings.recommended_action: Base the gate on a sound association measure (see F1) and on the median error compared with a permutation null. Generate the verdict text from whichever condition actually failed, and drop the fixed claim about label validity. Rerun, then update the JSON, the log and the SUMMARY.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 31-34 (Interpretation 2) and lines 49-50 (Next); code/transfer_test.py lines 135-138
findings.description: The summary claims the RPE1 marker-PCA angle does not measure cell-cycle position and that RPE1 is not a valid target. No analysis supports this, and the data contradict it. The RPE1 label has the same relationship to the S and G2M module scores as the K562 label. The K562-fit readouts recover it with 16-24 deg median error. The recommended next step, abandoning RPE1, follows from this false conclusion.
findings.evidence:
Mean S-score / G2M-score by 30 deg bin of the oriented phase.

K562:
- 0 deg: +0.23 / -0.18
- 30 deg: +0.27 / -0.07
- 120 deg: +0.00 / +0.36
- 150 deg: -0.11 / +0.40
- 270 deg: -0.26 / -0.32

RPE1:
- 0 deg: +0.21 / -0.21
- 30 deg: +0.26 / -0.07
- 120 deg: +0.02 / +0.50
- 150 deg: -0.07 / +0.38
- 270 deg: -0.23 / -0.40

The two profiles are nearly identical. The PC1-PC2 variance ratio is 0.31 for K562 and 0.35 for RPE1. A markers-only readout transfers with a 13 deg median error.
findings.recommended_action: Withdraw Interpretation 2 and the 'pick a different target' recommendation. If the label needs validating, report direct checks such as the S/G2M score profiles across phase in both datasets.

findings.description: Retention is computed as transfer / within on the flawed coefficient, which gives meaningless negative values (-0.91 and -0.87). Robust metrics give retention well above zero, and different for the two readouts.
findings.evidence: With Fisher-Lee rho_T: model 0.564 / 0.774 = 0.73; expression 0.741 / 0.829 = 0.89. With the resultant length of (pred - true): model 0.789 / 0.886 = 0.89; expression 0.878 / 0.913 = 0.96. Median error goes from 12.6 to 24.0 deg (model) and from 10.8 to 16.0 deg (expression).
findings.recommended_action: Recompute retention from a sound metric (F1), or report error-based degradation instead. Rewrite the table and the retention statements.

findings.description: The summary says the two readouts 'fail by almost the same amount' and that the run 'says nothing about generalisation' (model vs expression). Once the metric artifact is removed, both readouts transfer, and the model loses clearly more accuracy than expression. That is a substantive result, subject to the input-mismatch caveat the summary already gives, which the summary currently suppresses.
findings.evidence: Model: Fisher-Lee 0.77 -> 0.56; median error 12.6 -> 24.0 deg (almost doubled). Expression: Fisher-Lee 0.83 -> 0.74; median error 10.8 -> 16.0 deg. The JS 'transfer' values look similar (-0.81 vs -0.80) only because both are dominated by the same mean-centering artifact.
findings.recommended_action: After fixing the metric, report the model-vs-expression transfer comparison with uncertainty (for example a bootstrap over cells) and the appropriate caveats, rather than stating that no conclusion is possible.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 111-121 (expression readout features); README.md 'Readouts'; SUMMARY.md lines 43-45
findings.description: The expression reference readout includes the 87 marker genes from which the phase label is computed by PCA. This makes the 'point of reference' partly tautological, since a linear readout can largely reconstruct the label from its own inputs. Its within score is inflated by this, so it is not a clean reference for the model. The summary's Limits section does not mention this.
findings.evidence: Using the code's own fit_apply: markers-only (87 genes) gives within 0.978 with a 4.2 deg median error. Excluding the markers (6,457 genes) gives within 0.876 with 14.2 deg, compared with 0.919 and 10.8 deg using all 6,544 genes.
findings.recommended_action: Report an expression baseline that excludes the label-defining marker genes, or at least disclose the overlap and its effect, when using expression as the reference for the model readout.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets both parts of the detection rule. It says the negative transfer scores (-0.814 / -0.796) do not show failed transfer, because the Jammalamadaka circ_corr centres each angle on its own circular mean. It explains the mechanism: the true RPE1 phase is near-uniform (R = 0.043, mean 11.8 deg) and the predicted means sit near 227 / 235 deg, about 215 deg away, so sin() flips. It also backs this with three independent lines of evidence: (1) the small median errors (24 / 16 deg against a permutation null of about 95 deg); (2) R_diff of 0.789 / 0.878; (3) a common-centre circ_corr of +0.85, or +0.62 to +0.90 across all tested centres. I reproduced all of these exactly. F2 also detects the error. It says the transfer > 0 gate fails both readouts purely because of the sign artifact, while both readouts pass the median-error condition by a wide margin (24 and 16 deg vs the code's own 90 deg threshold). It also shows that the fixed verdict text 'worse than chance / label not cell cycle' contradicts the printed numbers.

review.summary: The headline conclusion is wrong. The summary says neither readout transfers from K562 to RPE1 and that the RPE1 phase label is invalid. Both claims rest on the Jammalamadaka circular-correlation formula in transfer_test.py, which gives an unreliable result here. That formula subtracts each variable's own circular mean. The RPE1 phase label is almost uniform around the circle (mean resultant length R = 0.043), so its mean direction is effectively noise. The frozen predictions centre about 145-155 deg away from the label's mean (model 226.7 deg, expression 235.2 deg, label 11.8 deg), and that offset flips the sign of the coefficient. By every robust measure the transfer works well. Median angular error is 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against 93 deg for shuffled labels. Mean cos(pred - true) is 0.79 and 0.88. The same coefficient computed around a common centre is +0.85 for the model, and the uniform-marginal corrected coefficient is +0.43 and +0.52. The validity gate then fails both readouts only because it requires a positive coefficient. The script's message says both are "worse than chance (90deg)" while printing errors of 24 and 16 deg, and the verdict string blames the target label by hard-coded text, with no test behind it. The SUMMARY repeats all of this: negative scores and retentions, "no valid transfer", "the label is the problem", "says nothing about generalisation", and the advice to drop RPE1. Its own evidence argues the other way: the phase orientation matches across datasets and the errors are small. Once scored correctly, expression keeps more of its accuracy than the model (median error 11 to 16 deg versus 13 to 24 deg; ratio of mean cosine of the error, transfer over within: 0.96 versus 0.89). Minor issues: the expression baseline includes the marker genes that define the label, and the two datasets were library-size normalised differently.

findings.evidence:

- Median error: 24.0 deg (model) and 16.0 deg (expression). A permutation null gives 95.2 +/- 1.6 deg and 93.9 +/- 1.9 deg (minimum 91.5 and 88.3).

A bootstrap of the circular correlation gives a 95% CI of [-0.90, -0.48], very wide next to the median-error CI of [23.2, 24.7] deg, which shows the statistic is unstable. On synthetic uniform phases with 20 deg noise and matching means, the same function returns +0.94. The summary's own table shows transfer errors of 24 and 16 deg, close to the within-K562 errors of 13 and 11 deg.

findings.description: P1: neither within nor transfer circular correlation is anchored to a chance distribution. The only chance reference is an analytic constant of 90 deg for median error, and the gate does not even rely on it in effect. No permutation null was computed for any score. A one-line permutation null would have shown that -0.81 is far from the null mean but in the wrong direction, while the median error is far below chance. That contradiction was never examined.
findings.evidence: Permutation null with 200 shuffles of the RPE1 label: circular correlation 0.001 +/- 0.018; median error 95.2 +/- 1.6 deg (model) and 93.9 +/- 1.9 deg (expression). The summary reports every score without a null mean, SD or percentile.
findings.recommended_action: Report every within and transfer score as observed vs permutation null (mean +/- SD, p95), using the corrected metric. If the score and the error disagree in sign relative to chance, treat that as a pipeline error.

findings.description: P6: the headline is a null finding ('no valid transfer'), but the metric and gate were never run on a case where transfer is known to succeed. One example is a K562 split-half 'transfer' in which the phase label is recomputed independently on the held-out half. Another is a target label equal to the true phase plus noise but with a different circular mean. Either would have exposed the artifact in F1. The within-K562 CV is not a valid positive control, because the predictions and the label share the same circular mean there (29.5 vs 28.5 deg).
findings.evidence: Within-K562: label mean 28.5 deg, prediction mean 29.5 deg, and the coefficient is positive. RPE1: label mean 11.8 deg, prediction mean 226.7 deg, and the coefficient is negative while the error is small. No synthetic or split-half control appears in the code or outputs.
findings.recommended_action: Add a positive control. Recompute the phase label independently on half of K562 or on a planted synthetic phase, apply the frozen readout, and confirm that the metric and gate report a pass. Do this before interpreting any failure.

findings.description: 'The S peak sits at 45 deg in both' is offered as evidence that the phase conventions agree, but it holds by construction: the rotation step forces the S peak to 45 deg in each dataset. Only the S-to-G2/M separation and the flip decision carry information. The G2/M peaks differ by 11.7 deg (153.8 vs 142.1), a residual convention mismatch that adds to the transfer error. Saying a mirrored axis is 'ruled out' is correct, but the evidence given for it is weak.
findings.evidence: cc_phase.py line 96: rot = deg2rad(s_at_deg) - mu_s, so s_peak_deg is always 45.0. run_log.txt lines 2-3 show G2/M peaks at 153.8 and 142.1 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Drop the S-peak equality as evidence. Report the G2/M-peak offset between datasets and its likely effect on transfer error, or align conventions on several markers.

findings.description: P2/P5 circularity: the phase label is atan2 of the first two PCs of the 87 standardised marker genes. All 87 are inside the 6,544-gene feature set of the 'expression' readout, which is presented as the point of reference. That readout therefore partly rebuilds the label definition, not an independent simple baseline. In addition, the label PCA and orientation are computed on all K562 cells, including the CV test folds, so the within-CV labels are built transductively.
findings.evidence: An expression readout on the 87 marker genes alone gives within 0.978 (4.2 deg) and transfer error 13.1 deg. With the marker genes removed: within 0.876 (14.2 deg), transfer error 18.2 deg, mean cos 0.84. The transfer still holds without the markers, but the within baseline is inflated by the label construction.
findings.recommended_action: Report the expression baseline with the label-defining marker genes excluded, as well as with them. Note that the model's cell sentences also contain these genes. If the label is meant to be held out, compute the label PCA within CV folds.

findings.description: P8: headline numbers are given to three decimals with no CI or bootstrap. Ridge alpha (1000), the layer (21), the CV seed and the orientation parameter (top = 200) are fixed at single values with no sweep, and alpha was not tuned on the source.
findings.evidence: Alpha sweep, model transfer median error: 32.6, 29.0, 24.0 and 21.4 deg at alpha = 10, 100, 1e3 and 1e4. Bootstrap of the transfer circular correlation: [-0.90, -0.48]. No uncertainty is reported anywhere in the outputs.
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap the corrected metrics (1,000 resamples) and report 95% CIs. Tune alpha within source CV, and report a sweep over at least three settings plus several seeds and layers.

findings.description: P7/P4: conclusions about target validity and generalisation rest on one source-target pair (n = 1 cell line each), one layer and one seed. The 3,000 cells per line are the CV unit, while the claim is about cell lines. RPE1 barcodes carry gem-group suffixes (e.g. -34, -42), but the K562 index has no barcodes, so batch or lane structure cannot be checked or grouped.
findings.evidence: Only one target (RPE1) and one source (K562) are analysed. KFold(5, shuffle=True) is run over cells. K562 obs index values look like '113', '231'; RPE1 index values look like 'AAACCCAAGCGGACAT-34'.
findings.recommended_action: State the inference unit (one cell-line pair). Add at least one more target or source (e.g. HepG2 or Jurkat from the same screen series) and several seeds and layers before making general claims. Group CV by gem group where possible.

findings.description: P10: there is no environment file or pinned package versions, and the activation-extraction code is not included. The manifest records only 'prompt': true, not the prompt text. The data provenance is undocumented: which Replogle release, how the 3,000 control cells were sampled, and how expression was normalised. The activations cannot be regenerated or checked.
findings.evidence: README lists 'numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and anndata' with no versions. The manifest has no prompt string, tokenizer or model revision. There is no extraction script in code/.
findings.recommended_action: Add requirements with pinned versions, the extraction script, the exact prompt and model revision, and a data-provenance note covering source files, sampling seed and normalisation.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 fully meets the key's detection rule. Part (a): it says the negative transfer scores (-0.814 / -0.796) and retention values are artifacts of circ_corr and that the 'both fail' claim cannot stand. Part (b) is supported in all three accepted ways. The mechanism: each angle is centred on its own circular mean, the RPE1 label has R = 0.043 and mean 11.8 deg, predictions have R = 0.341 and mean 226.7 deg, and the 215-deg gap flips the sign of the sin product. The contradiction: median errors are 24 / 16 deg against a permutation null near 95 deg. Computed alternatives: mean cos(error) 0.788 / 0.878 (the key's R_diff 0.789 / 0.878) and Fisher-Lee +0.55 / +0.73. F2 also qualifies. It ties the failed gate and the hard-coded 'label is not cell cycle' verdict to the sign artifact from F1, and it points out that the 'worse than chance (90deg)' text contradicts the 24 / 16 deg errors. I re-ran the pipeline inline: transfer cc -0.8142, median error 23.95 deg, prediction R 0.341 and mean 226.7 deg, label R 0.043 and mean 11.8 deg, mean cos 0.788, permutation-null error about 94.7 deg. These match both the review and the key.

findings.reason: This is exactly the key's error: circ_corr centres each variable on its own mean, the true phase is near-uniform and the predictions are concentrated, so the score comes out wrong-signed. I reproduced it inline: cc -0.814, median error 23.95 deg, label R 0.043 at 11.8 deg, prediction R 0.341 at 226.7 deg, mean cos 0.788, 81.5% of cells within 45 deg, bias 3.8 deg. Its corrected conclusion, that both readouts transfer, matches the key's correct_result.

This covers the downstream part of the documented error: the gate fails only because of the artifactual sign, and the verdict and summary wrongly conclude 'no valid transfer' and that the RPE1 label is not cell cycle. The key's known facts confirm the RPE1 label is a valid cell-cycle phase. I checked the phase-bin marker profiles: G2/M peaks in the 135-180 bin in both lines, and S is high in 0-90 deg in both. One small slip: in K562 the S maximum is in the 45-90 bin (0.25), not 0-45 (0.24), but this does not change the conclusion. It is also true that the verdict string is hard-coded and the '(90deg)' chance text contradicts the printed errors.

It is true that no measured null was computed and that the 90-deg floor is assumed. The key mentions this as context for the error, but its detection rule says that pointing out a missing floor is not enough on its own. My permutation check matches the review: cc null about 0.00 +/- 0.019 and error null about 94.7 +/- 1.6 deg. This is a genuine methodological gap, but the finding does not on its own claim the headline is wrong.

There is indeed no positive-control path. Its claim that within-K562 CV is not a valid control for this artifact is correct: I measured a within prediction mean of 29.5 deg against a label mean of 28.5 deg, and the key notes that the ridge intercept pins the predicted mean. This is a genuine process weakness, but it is not itself the headline error.

It is correct that the S peak at 45 deg holds by construction (rot = s_at_deg - mu_s), and the G2/M peaks are 153.8 vs 142.1 deg. The finding agrees that the orientation conclusion is right, so it is not the orientation false alarm. Its suggestion that the G2/M offset adds to transfer error is slightly overstated, because the best rotation is only about -4 / -2 deg. This is a trivial point about the quality of the evidence.

The facts are true: all 87 K562 markers are in the 6,544 shared genes, and the label PCA uses all cells. The key, however, lists the marker overlap as a shared design property and not an error. The finding correctly rates it minor, and its own numbers show transfer still works without the markers.

It is true that there are no CIs and alpha, layer and seed are fixed. My bootstrap gives a cc CI of about [-0.90, -0.50], close to the review's figure. The key lists missing CIs and the fixed alpha and layer as non-load-bearing design choices, and the finding treats them that way.

The single cell-line pair is true, and the index formats are as stated: K562 '113', RPE1 'AAACCCAAGCGGACAT-34'. The summary already states the same-lab limit. This is a generality caveat and is not load-bearing.

It is true that versions are not pinned, the extraction script is missing, and the manifest records only 'prompt': true. This is a reproducibility and documentation issue that does not affect the result.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets every part of the key's detection rule. (a) It says the negative transfer scores (-0.814 and -0.796) and the retention values are artifacts of circ_corr, and that both frozen readouts actually recover RPE1 phase. (b) It gives the mechanism: each angle is centred on its own circular mean, the RPE1 label is near-uniform (R = 0.043, mean 11.8 deg), the predictions are concentrated (R = 0.341, mean 226.7 deg), and the roughly 215 deg gap between the means flips the sign of sin(). It also shows the contradiction with the median errors (24 and 16 deg against a permutation null near 95 deg) and gives computed alternatives that show strong positive transfer (mean cos 0.788 and 0.878, Fisher-Lee +0.55 and +0.73). I re-ran the pipeline and reproduced R = 0.043, prediction mean 226.7 deg with R = 0.341, mean cos 0.788, 81.5% of cells within 45 deg, and a null median error of about 95 deg. F2 also detects the error at its downstream location. It names the gate at line 131 and the hard-coded verdict, says the gate fails only because of F1's artifactual sign, and notes that the 'worse than chance (90deg)' text contradicts the 24 and 16 deg errors. It also shows directly that the RPE1 label is a valid cell-cycle coordinate. I verified its phase-bin S and G2/M profiles exactly.

findings.reason: This is exactly the key's error: the circ_corr own-mean centring flips the sign with a near-uniform truth and concentrated predictions. Its numbers match the key's known true facts, and I reproduced them (R 0.043 / 0.341, means 11.8 / 226.7 deg, mean cos 0.788, median error 24 deg vs null of about 95 deg). Its conclusion, that the transfer works and the 'both fail' claim cannot stand, matches the key's correct result.

This finding covers the gate (line 131), the verdict string and SUMMARY Interpretation 1-2, which the key's error location names as the consequence of the bad statistic. It says the gate fails only because of the artifactual sign. The 'both worse than chance (90deg)' log text is indeed false next to errors of 24 and 16 deg, and the verdict text is hard-coded. I reproduced its direct check of the RPE1 label: S is highest at 0-45 deg, G2/M peaks in the 135-180 deg bin, and the profiles match K562's. This agrees with the key's fact that the RPE1 label is a valid cell-cycle phase.

It is true that no measured or permutation chance floor exists and that 90 deg is an assumed constant; I reproduced a permutation null median error of about 95.0 +/- 1.6 deg. The key mentions the assumed floor as context, but says that noting a missing floor is not enough to detect the error. Here it is a supporting methodological gap that F1 and F2 already cover, not an independent headline error.

The reason given, that the within-K562 CV cannot expose the artifact because the label and prediction means coincide, is correct: I measured 28.5 vs 29.5 deg, which matches the key's note that the ridge intercept pins the predicted mean. The gap is real and would have caught the error, but it is a methodology recommendation, not the cause of the wrong result.

It is correct that the S peak sits at 45 deg by construction (rot = s_at_deg - mu_s), so equal S peaks are weak evidence. The finding agrees that a mirrored axis is ruled out, so it is not the orientation false alarm. Its suggestion that the 11.7 deg G2/M offset adds to the transfer error is small at most: the key says the best rigid rotation is only -3.8 / -2.5 deg. This is a trivial presentation point.

The overlap between the marker genes and the readout features, and the transductive label PCA, are design properties that the key lists as a known fact and as a possible false alarm when treated as load-bearing. The finding itself rates this minor and says transfer still holds without the markers, so it is true but not consequential.

It is true that there are no CIs and that alpha, layer and seed are fixed. The key lists missing CIs, a single seed and the alpha/layer choices as possible false alarms if treated as load-bearing, because the effects are far from the floors. The finding rates them minor, so this is a valid but trivial point.

It is true that only one source-target pair is analysed, and the barcode observations are correct. However, the summary already says the run says nothing about generalisation and states the same-lab limit. This is a generic scope caveat.
It is correct that there are no pinned versions or extraction script and that the manifest records only 'prompt': true. This reproducibility and provenance point does not affect any result.

review.summary:
The headline conclusion, that neither readout transfers from K562 to RPE1 because the RPE1 phase label is invalid, does not hold. I reran the pipeline inline and got the logged numbers exactly. The negative "transfer" scores (-0.814 for the model, -0.796 for expression) are an artefact of the Jammalamadaka circular correlation (circ_corr). That statistic centres each variable on its own circular mean. Here the label is almost uniform around the circle (resultant length 0.043), while the predictions are biased and pile up about 215 deg away from the label mean, so the sign flips. By every agreement measure, both readouts actually transfer well:
- Median angular error is 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against a permutation null of about 94-95 deg.
- Mean cos(error) is 0.79 and 0.88.
- The Fisher-Lee circular correlation is +0.56 and +0.74.
- 81% of RPE1 cells are predicted within 45 deg.
Running the same model readout the other way (RPE1 to K562) gives +0.87 with a 25 deg error. A synthetic check (uniform label, accurate but biased predictions) gives circ_corr -0.73 at a 16.7 deg error. Both show the sign carries no meaning here.

The validity rule then rejects both readouts on that artefactual sign alone. The script's verdict text is hard-coded and says "both worse than chance (90deg)" right next to errors of 24 and 16 deg. It also asserts, without any test, that the target label is "not cell cycle". In fact the RPE1 label is at least as coherent as K562's: the top-200 S-score cells concentrate at R=0.945 (K562 0.935), and the G2/M score correlates with the angle at r=0.93 (K562 0.88).

Once the metric is fixed, the run does say something about generalisation. Expression transfers better than the model: its median error is about 8 deg lower (cell-level bootstrap 95% CI 7.0-8.7). This holds for ridge alpha from 10 to 10,000, and still holds when the 87 marker genes are removed from the expression features (18 deg). The summary does not report this negative result for the model.

Smaller problems:
- The expression baseline is circular: the phase label is computed from marker genes that are also expression features.
- Retention is defined as a ratio of correlations, which means nothing here.
- There are no confidence intervals, no permutation null and no sensitivity sweep.
- Only one cell-line pair, one layer and one seed were tested.
- Provenance and environment details are thin.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1, null model: present and unaddressed.
- P2, trivial baseline: a baseline is present, but it is circular and its result is not reported.
- P3, endpoint–object mismatch: present (the metric does not measure agreement; the label is built from the features).
- P4, unit of inference: present and unaddressed (minor).
- P5, selection / double-dipping: present (the label is derived from the features).
- P6, positive control: absent for the claimed null; a simple one would have exposed the problem.
- P7, single condition: present.
- P8, stability: present and unaddressed.
- P9, language overreach: present (a negative result is attributed to an invalid label without testing it).
- P10, reproducibility: partly addressed; the code runs and reproduces exactly, but provenance and versions are missing.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py:39-43 and :74 (circ_corr used as the transfer score); SUMMARY.md:9-12 (table) and :19-20
findings.description: The headline transfer scores of -0.814 (model) and -0.796 (expression) come from the circular correlation statistic, not from failed transfer. The Jammalamadaka coefficient centres each angle on its own circular mean. The RPE1 label is almost uniform around the circle (resultant length 0.043, so its mean direction is close to noise). The frozen predictions are biased and concentrated (resultant length 0.34 for the model, 0.22 for expression), with their mean about 215-223 deg away from the label mean. Centring the two variables on means that differ by about 180 deg flips the sign of the coefficient even when predictions match the labels cell by cell. So the sign of 'transfer' says nothing about whether transfer worked.
findings.evidence: Inline rerun reproduces the JSON exactly. Model transfer: circ_corr -0.814, yet median error 24.0 deg, mean cos(error) 0.788, 81.5% of cells within 45 deg, Fisher-Lee circular correlation +0.56. Expression transfer: circ_corr -0.796, median error 16.0 deg, mean cos(error) 0.878, Fisher-Lee +0.74. Permutation null for median error is 94.8 / 94.0 deg (5th percentile about 91-92), so the observed errors are far better than chance. Running the model readout the other way (RPE1 to K562) gives circ_corr +0.870 at a similar 25.1 deg error. Synthetic check: uniform label, accurate predictions with a constant bias toward 220 deg, gives circ_corr -0.726 at a median error of 16.7 deg. The sign is negative at every ridge alpha tested (10 to 10,000), while the errors stay at 15-33 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Score angular prediction with an agreement measure rather than an association measure. Options: mean cos(predicted - true), median or mean absolute angular error, or Fisher-Lee correlation, each with a permutation null. Then re-derive the within, transfer and retention numbers and rewrite the Result table and bullets. Done this way, both readouts transfer well.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py:129-138 (validity gate and verdict); outputs/run_log.txt:10; outputs/transfer_rpe1.json ('verdict'); SUMMARY.md:21-22
findings.description: The pass/fail rule requires transfer > 0 AND median error < 90 deg. Both readouts pass the error criterion by a wide margin (24 and 16 deg) and are rejected only by the artefactual negative sign from F1. When nothing passes, the script writes a fixed explanation: 'both below chance; target label is invalid for this variable' and 'both worse than chance (90deg). The target's phase label is not cell cycle.' It prints this right next to errors of 24 and 16 deg, which are far better than chance. The verdict is a hard-coded conclusion, not the outcome of any test of the label.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt line 10 says 'model -0.814 (24deg), expression -0.796 (16deg) -- both worse than chance (90deg)'. 24 and 16 are both below 90, and lower error is better. Lines 134-138 emit the 'target label is invalid' text whenever the list of passing readouts is empty, whatever the cause.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the sign criterion with a test of the agreement metric against a permutation null. Remove the hard-coded diagnosis from the verdict string. If label validity matters, test it directly (see F3). Rerun, then update the JSON, the log and the summary.

findings.description: The interpretation that 'the RPE1 phase label is the problem' and 'RPE1 is not a valid target for this variable' is inferred by elimination from the shared negative scores. It was never tested, and the data contradict it. The RPE1 marker-PCA angle tracks cell-cycle markers at least as well as the K562 angle does. The 'Next' step (choose a different target dataset) follows from this false premise.
findings.evidence: Measured on the oriented labels. Top-200 S-score cells concentrate at resultant length 0.945 in RPE1 vs 0.935 in K562. Top-200 G2/M cells: 0.990 vs 0.989. corr(S score, cos(theta - 45 deg)) is 0.863 vs 0.859. corr(G2/M score, cos(theta - G2/M peak)) is 0.93 vs 0.88. PC1-2 variance ratio is 0.35 vs 0.31. Readouts fit on K562 predict the RPE1 label with 16-24 deg median error, which could not happen if the label were not cell cycle.
findings.recommended_action: Withdraw Interpretation items 1-2 and the 'Next' recommendation. State that both readouts transfer from K562 to RPE1, and report the corrected agreement metrics with nulls and CIs.

findings.description: The summary says the run 'says nothing about generalisation' and that the model is not compared with expression. Once the metric is fixed, the run gives a clear and stable comparison: the expression readout transfers better than the model's layer-21 readout. This is a negative result for the model that the write-up does not report (checklist P2/P9, 'own the negatives'). The summary's caveat that the two readouts get different inputs still applies, but the size and stability of the gap should be stated.
findings.evidence: Transfer median error is 24.0 deg (model) vs 16.0 deg (expression); mean cos is 0.788 vs 0.878. Cell-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples) of the median-error difference (model minus expression): 7.9 deg, 95% CI 7.0-8.7. The mean-cos difference is -0.090 (CI -0.101 to -0.079). The gap holds at alpha 10, 100, 1,000 and 10,000 (model 21-33 deg, expression 15-18 deg). It also holds when all 87 marker genes are removed from the expression features (18.2 deg at alpha 1,000).
findings.recommended_action: Report the corrected model-vs-expression transfer comparison with CIs, together with the input-mismatch caveat. Say plainly that layer-21 activations do not transfer phase information better than expression.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py:54-69 (label built from marker expression); code/transfer_test.py:111-121 (expression features include the same markers); README.md:15-16, 24-28
findings.description: The expression readout is meant as the 'point of reference', but it is circular. The phase label is atan2(PC2, PC1) of standardised expression for 87 (K562) or 93 (RPE1) marker genes, and all 87 K562 markers are among the 6,544 expression features. So the expression readout is partly recomputing the label from its own inputs, which inflates its within and transfer scores relative to the model. In addition, the label PCA and orientation are fit on all K562 cells, including the CV test folds, which is transductive. The labels are also defined differently in each dataset (different marker counts, separate PCA loadings, S-to-G2/M separation 109 vs 97 deg), so transfer error mixes readout error with label-definition mismatch.
findings.evidence: 87 of the shared genes are S/G2M markers. With them removed, expression transfer error rises from 16.0 to 18.2 deg (alpha 1,000) and mean cos falls from 0.878 to 0.838. The run log shows 87 vs 93 cc genes and S-to-G2/M separations of 108.8 vs 97.1 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Use an expression baseline that excludes the label-defining markers, or define the label on held-out genes. Fit the label PCA inside each CV fold. Report how much of the transfer error is due to label-definition mismatch, for example by projecting RPE1 onto the K562 marker loadings.

findings.description: Retention is defined as the ratio of two correlation coefficients (transfer / within). Here it inherits the arbitrary sign from F1, giving -0.91 and -0.87. It does not express how much accuracy is kept.
findings.evidence: The same model readout gets retention -0.91 for K562 to RPE1 and +0.94 for RPE1 to K562, although the transfer errors are nearly the same (24 vs 25 deg).
findings.recommended_action: Define retention on an agreement metric anchored to chance, for example (chance error - transfer error) / (chance error - within error) using the permutation-null error, or a ratio of mean-cos values.

findings.description: No numbers are anchored to a computed null, and none come with uncertainty or a sensitivity range (checklist P1/P8). The chance value is a fixed 90 deg rather than a permutation null; the actual null median error is about 94-95 deg because the predictions are not uniform. No permutation null was computed for circ_corr; its SD of about 0.018 would have shown that -0.81 is a strong systematic association, not a chance-level failure. There are no bootstrap CIs, ridge alpha is fixed at 1,000, the CV seed is fixed, and only layer 21 is tested. No positive control for the metric was run (P6); the synthetic check in F1 would have exposed the artefact.
findings.evidence: Permutation nulls (200 shuffles each): circ_corr SD 0.017-0.018, median-error null mean 89.8-94.8 deg. The outputs contain no CIs or sweeps. The alpha sweep moves model transfer error from 21 to 33 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Add permutation nulls (mean ± SD, 95th percentile) for each metric, bootstrap CIs, and at least a 3-point alpha sweep and multiple seeds. Include a positive control for the scoring function (synthetic accurate-but-biased predictions, and the reverse transfer direction).

findings.description: All conclusions rest on a single source-target pair (one K562 and one RPE1 control population from the same screen series), one model layer and one seed (checklist P7/P4). The 3,000 cells per line are the only unit of resampling, and there is one biological sample per cell line, so cell-level statistics overstate how far the result generalises. This applies equally to the corrected conclusion (transfer works, and expression beats the model).
findings.evidence: There is one activation file per dataset (layer 21 only), and the manifests list layers [21]. Neither h5ad has obs metadata (no batch or GEM-group column), so no grouped analysis is possible.
findings.recommended_action: Frame the claims as specific to this one pair. Add at least one held-out target (another dataset or batch) and further layers or seeds before making general statements about the model's cell-cycle representation.

findings.description: Provenance and reproducibility are thin (checklist P10). The h5ad files have empty obs, so nothing in the data confirms that the cells are non-targeting controls or come from the same lab and platform; K562 obs names are bare integers. The code for activation extraction and data subsetting is not included, and package versions are not pinned. The analysis code itself is deterministic and reproduces the outputs exactly.
findings.evidence: src.obs and tgt.obs have no columns. K562 obs_names look like '113', '231'. RPE1 obs_names are barcodes with suffixes such as '-34'. The README lists dependencies without versions. Environment used for the check: numpy 1.26.4, scikit-learn 1.8.0, anndata 0.12.10, scipy 1.17.1.
findings.recommended_action: Add obs metadata (perturbation label, GEM group or batch, source file), the extraction and subsetting scripts, and pinned package versions.

F2 also qualifies. It says the gate (transfer > 0) rejects both readouts only because of this artefactual sign, and it backs that with the 24 / 16 deg errors being well below 90 deg, so the verdict is invalid.

findings.reason: This is the key's error, stated correctly. circ_corr centres each variable on its own mean; the RPE1 label is near-uniform and the predictions are concentrated, so the sign flips. The negative scores therefore do not show failed transfer. review.summary: The headline result ("both readouts fail on RPE1 with circular correlation about -0.8, no valid transfer, the RPE1 phase label is invalid") does not hold. It comes from the metric, not from the data. circ_corr in transfer_test.py is the Jammalamadaka coefficient, and it centres each variable on its own circular mean. Both phase distributions are close to uniform on the circle (resultant length 0.08 for K562, 0.04 for RPE1), so the mean of the true labels is essentially undefined. The frozen-readout predictions are more concentrated: their circular mean is 227 deg (model) and 235 deg (expression), while the RPE1 truth mean is 12 deg. That opposite placement of the two means flips the sign of the statistic. Per cell, the transfer is good. Median angular errors are 24 deg (model) and 16 deg (expression), against 90 deg for random guessing and 68 deg for the best constant guess. 81% / 91% of cells fall within 45 deg of the truth. The mean offset is 3.8 / 2.5 deg. The per-component Pearson r of cos and sin is 0.85-0.91. Recomputing the Jammalamadaka coefficient with one shared reference direction gives +0.85 / +0.90; the Fisher-Lee coefficient gives +0.56 / +0.74. Median errors stay at 12-36 deg in every 60-deg phase bin. So both readouts transfer, and the expression readout transfers better than the model readout. The validity gate, the hard-coded verdict string, the negative "retention" values and all three interpretation points in SUMMARY.md are therefore wrong. Blaming the RPE1 label is also contradicted by the run's own orientation check. Other problems found: the chance anchor and null are weak, there is mild label circularity (the expression features include the 87 marker genes that define the label), the "S peak at 45 deg in both" evidence is true by construction, there are no confidence intervals and only one seed, and reproducibility scaffolding is thin. Checklist verdicts: P1 present and unaddressed. P2 clean (an expression baseline exists). P3/P5 present (marker circularity), minor. P4 mostly clean: cells within one line; there is no batch metadata, so it cannot be checked. P6 present and unaddressed: no positive control for the metric before accepting a null. P7 partly acknowledged: one source/target pair, one layer, one model. P8 present: no CIs or seeds; an alpha sweep I ran shows the median errors are stable. P9 present: the hard-coded "label is not cell cycle" wording and the summary's interpretation go beyond the evidence. P10 present: no pinned versions, no extraction code, model revision not pinned.

findings.location: code/transfer_test.py lines 39-43 (circ_corr), used at lines 67 and 74; results in outputs/transfer_rpe1.json and the SUMMARY.md results table
findings.description: The transfer score uses the Jammalamadaka-SenGupta circular correlation, with each variable centred on its own circular mean. For near-uniform phase distributions (a full cell cycle) that mean direction is undefined. The sign of the coefficient then depends on where the two marginal means happen to sit, not on per-cell agreement. The reported transfer scores of -0.814 and -0.796, and the retention values of -0.91 and -0.87, are artefacts of this. The readouts actually transfer well.
findings.evidence: I re-ran it inline. On RPE1 the true phase has resultant length 0.043, with circular mean 11.8 deg. The frozen model predictions have resultant length 0.34 and mean 226.7 deg; the expression predictions have 0.22 and 235.2 deg. Per-cell agreement is high: median error 24.0 / 16.0 deg (permutation null 94.7 +/- 1.7 deg; best constant predictor 68 deg). 81.5% / 90.7% of cells are within 45 deg, and the mean offset of pred - true is 3.8 / 2.5 deg (resultant 0.79 / 0.88). Pearson r of cos and sin is 0.85/0.86 (model) and 0.91/0.91 (expression). Jammalamadaka with a common reference direction gives +0.85 (model) and +0.90 (expression); Fisher-Lee (no mean) gives +0.56 / +0.74. Median error is 12-36 deg in every 60-deg phase bin. Within K562 the score is positive only because the two means happen to line up (pred 29.5 deg vs truth 28.5 deg). Bootstrapping keeps the artefact stable (CI -0.90 to -0.51), so a confidence interval would not have exposed it.
findings.recommended_action: Replace circ_corr with a statistic that does not depend on the marginal mean directions: Fisher-Lee, the mean resultant of (pred - true), or the median/mean angular error compared against a permutation null. Re-run, and rewrite the results table and retention. With the corrected metric, both readouts transfer (model about 24 deg and expression about 16 deg median error, against 13 and 11 deg within K562), and expression transfers better than the model.
