The README's '105 single perturbations' describes the subset correctly and does not claim all 105 are used (66 enter the kept pairs), so that 'discrepancy' is weak. These are generality and reproducibility caveats, not errors.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key (B3100, status 'clean') has no documented error, so error_detected is null. No finding claims the ceiling halves are non-independent. F1 says outright that the ceiling uses independent halves, and F8 raises only the minor aggregation point the key lists as valid. So none of the findings falls into the key's false-alarm trap. I re-ran the main reviewer checks with the package's Python. Feature/target coupling: sum-only 0.422 with shared noise vs 0.225 with independent halves. Additive null: sum-only 0.178, saturation+gene 0.261. Jackknife SE: 0.087 vs naive 0.036. Per-pair slopes: SD 0.23, replicate r 0.91. Ceiling: 0.710 vs 0.752, 3 negative split-half r, 22 pairs above their own per-pair ceiling. A control-half split removes the per-gene offset gain completely: it is +0.03 with a shared control and -0.002 to -0.007 with an independent control half.

findings.reason: This is the feature-target noise coupling the key lists as a valid other_real_issue (key check: 0.425 vs 0.227). I reproduced it: shared-noise target gives sum 0.422 / saturation 0.434 / +gene 0.450; independent target gives 0.225 / 0.222 / 0.232. Additive-null simulation: sum-only 0.178, saturation+gene 0.261 (reviewer: 0.180 / 0.257). 22 of 115 pairs exceed their own per-pair ceiling. The finding does not claim the ceiling halves are dependent; it says the inflated numerator makes the share-of-ceiling comparison misleading. That is a consequence of the coupling, not the ceiling false alarm. It undermines the headline 0.370/0.406 and 49-54%.

Claims 2-3 ('mostly shrinkage', 'most of the interaction is not pair-specific') are overclaims by the analysis's own numbers. (0.406/0.752)^2 = 0.29, and pooled 0.211/0.566 = 37%; both are under half of the reliable variance. I confirmed the per-pair heterogeneity with fully independent replicates: per-pair shrinkage slope mean -0.11, SD 0.23, 5th-95th percentile -0.47 to 0.31, 30% positive, replicate correlation 0.91. Per-pair sum-only correlations range from -0.51 to 0.95 (10th percentile -0.15). None of this is in the key, and none of it contradicts the key's known true facts.

The ceiling/floor (saturation) mechanism in the title and claim 2 is asserted but never tested. With independent noise, the saturation features add nothing over sum-only (0.222 vs 0.225). Shrinkage is no weaker for genes where the singles push in opposite directions: independent-half slope -0.195 for opposite-sign vs -0.173 for same-sign; in the top 10% of |s|, -0.196 vs -0.189. Saturation predicts the reverse. My exact values differ from the reviewer's because of the seed, but the direction is the same. The issue is not in the key.

The arithmetic is correct: corr/ceiling is a correlation ratio, and the share of reliable variance explained is (0.406/0.752)^2 = 0.29. Calling 46% the 'unexplained reliable signal' is therefore a misstatement; it is about 71%. The issue is not in the key. It changes the size of claim 4 but not its direction: headroom remains, and is actually larger.

The key lists 'per-gene offset leaks test information' as a false alarm, on the grounds that the offset uses only training-pair I. F5 makes a different claim: every pair's I shares the same control-mean error, so the training-pair mean carries that shared noise into the test predictions. The data confirm this. Splitting the controls (training I and features built with control half 1, test I with half 2) drops the per-gene gain from +0.028 to +0.032 down to -0.002 to -0.007. Under the additive-null simulation the gain is +0.083, larger than the observed +0.029. So the reported per-gene gain, and part of the best model's 0.406 / 54%, is a noise artifact. The GroupKFold-by-single recommendation is only a stricter variant, but the core claim holds.

This matches the key's valid other_real_issue: the bootstrap over pairs ignores that pairs share singles. I confirmed it: 66 distinct singles across 115 pairs (PTPN12 in 12, KLF1 in 11), naive SE 0.036 vs delete-one-single jackknife SE 0.087. There is no paired test of the model differences. The key calls this issue minor. It widens the intervals but does not by itself overturn the headline result.

The additive model's n = 0 and corr = 0 are by design (key known true fact and listed false alarm). F7 accepts that the correlation is undefined and only objects to presenting it as 'exactly 0'. It is also trivially true that sum-only's per-pair correlation is ±corr(dA+dB, I). These are presentation points, not errors.

This matches the key's minor other_real_issue exactly. I confirmed it: mean of per-pair ceilings 0.710 vs 0.752, and 3 pairs with negative split-half r. The share moves only from about 54% to 57%. The single-split remark is minor too: the key reports the ceiling is stable across seeds (0.740-0.752).

Generality, the missing subset-building script, unpinned versions and no sweeps are reproducibility and scope remarks. The README's '105 singles' is accurate for the subset (the log shows 105). It is not an inconsistency with the 66 singles used in the kept pairs. Overall true but trivial.

review.summary: I re-ran the scoring inline and it reproduces outputs/ exactly: 6 of 21 concepts pass, mean best F1 is 0.360 and 19 of 21 concepts have a margin of at least 0.1. The headline still cannot stand. code/score_concepts.py:140 picks each concept's "best feature" as the one with the highest split-B F1 out of 5,035 scored features. That means the held-out split is used to choose the feature, and the reported F1 is the best of thousands of test-set scores. Only the threshold is tuned on split A, so the SUMMARY's statement that the reported F1 is held out is false. When the feature and threshold are both chosen on split A and scored once on split B, only SIGNAL (0.833) and DISULFID (0.721) pass. The features chosen on A for REPEAT, COILED and DNA_BIND score F1 0.003, 0.002 and 0.000 on B, and the one for ZN_FING scores 0.245. The CSV's own f1_a column already shows that the "passing" REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING features are weak on split A (0.05 to 0.29). The comparison with a random predictor is not a useful test. Its baseline F1 is about 0.001 to 0.03, so the margin is almost equal to F1, and the negative control VARIANT clears it (+0.354). A null that keeps which proteins carry each label gives REPEAT and VARIANT the same best F1 as reported. VARIANT is mostly two whole-protein spans. The other passing concepts rest on only 3 to 29 proteins per split, so their F1 values are very uncertain and the set of passing concepts changes with the split seed. The interpretation goes beyond the evidence: the "monosemantic" and "bonded cysteines" wording, the claim that F1 is a lower bound, and the six features named as candidates for causal tests.

findings.location: code/score_concepts.py:140 (best = np.nanargmax(s['f1'][:, ci]), where s['f1'] is split-B F1); README.md:64; SUMMARY.md:8-10, 13-23
findings.description: Each concept's best feature is the one with the highest split-B F1 out of 5,035 features. Only the threshold is tuned on split A. The held-out split is therefore used to choose the feature, and each reported F1 is the best of 5,035 test-set scores, which biases it upward. SUMMARY says the reported F1 comes from proteins that were not used to tune it. That is false, and the 6/21 headline depends on this selection.
findings.evidence: In the CSV, the passing features score far lower on split A at their own threshold (f1_a) than on split B: REPEAT 0.046 vs 0.626, COILED 0.290 vs 0.519, DNA_BIND 0.146 vs 0.517, ZN_FING 0.114 vs 0.501. I re-ran score_all and chose each concept's feature by split-A F1 instead, then scored it on split B. The split-A choices were REPEAT feature 919 (B F1 0.003), COILED 1401 (0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.000) and ZN_FING 1593 (0.245). Only SIGNAL (2936, 0.833) and DISULFID (1925, 0.721) pass, so 2 of 21 rather than 6 of 21. For 9 other seeds (0-8) plus the swapped A/B direction, choosing on A passes 2 to 5 concepts. Only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass every time.
findings.recommended_action: Choose the feature and the threshold on split A only, for example with nested cross-validation inside A. Then score that one feature once on split B. Better still, cross-fit over both directions and several protein splits and report the spread. Rewrite the headline table and the text accordingly.

findings.description: The 'margin over random' compares the best of 5,035 features, chosen on the test split, with the expected F1 of one random predictor. For rare concepts that baseline is about 0.001 to 0.03, so the margin is essentially F1 itself. It does not correct for choosing among many features, and it ignores the fact that labels cluster within a few proteins. The claims '19 of 21 concepts at least 0.1 above random' and 'mean margin +0.342' therefore say nothing about specificity.
findings.evidence: random_f1 in the CSV is at most 0.031 for every concept except DOMAIN (0.21) and REGION (0.06). The negative control VARIANT has margin +0.354 and MUTAGEN +0.306, and both count toward the '19 of 21'. As a check I ran a null that circularly shifts the labels within each protein. This keeps which proteins carry the labels but puts them at the wrong residues. Rerunning the pipeline on it (4 replicates) gave these best split-B F1 values: REPEAT 0.58 to 0.64 (reported 0.626), COILED 0.37 to 0.48 (0.519), VARIANT 0.34 to 0.36 (0.358), MUTAGEN 0.31 to 0.34 (0.310), HELIX 0.225 to 0.23 (0.229). For SIGNAL (0.15 to 0.23 vs 0.833) and DISULFID (0.11 to 0.14 vs 0.721) the null is far lower.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the analytic baseline with a permutation or shift null that repeats the full feature-selection step. Report a per-concept p-value or FDR and gate on it. Leave the negative control and other non-residue keys out of the aggregate statistics.

findings.description: The negative-control result is misreported, and the control itself is degenerate. VARIANT misses the gate only because its F1 is below 0.5. It clears the margin test, and it scores above 14 of the 21 concepts (all but SIGNAL, DISULFID, REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND, ZN_FING and TRANSMEM). With a different seed it passes the whole gate. Its labels are mostly two long spans that cover nearly all of two proteins. The control therefore measures whether a feature recognises those proteins, not whether features detect residue-level properties they should not.
findings.evidence: From the CSV, VARIANT has F1 0.3585 and margin 0.3545, so it is inside the '19 of 21'. Running the script's own procedure with seed=2, VARIANT passes the gate (pass list: DISULFID, PROPEP, REPEAT, SIGNAL, VARIANT). VARIANT's best split-A feature (5079) reaches F1 0.656 on A. 949 of the 986 VARIANT positives come from two single runs: CWC27_HUMAN positions 6-471 (length 472) and SMAD6_HUMAN positions 13-495 (length 496). 98% of the split-B positives are in SMAD6. All 145 true positives of feature 3889 are in that one protein.
findings.recommended_action: State plainly that the negative control clears the margin test and sometimes the full gate. Rebuild VARIANT from single-residue variants, excluding long 'Missing' or truncation spans, or choose a control that is not concentrated in a few proteins. Use the control to set the null threshold.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:13-23, 39-42; code/score_concepts.py:125-127 (concept filter counts residues, not proteins)
findings.description: The passing concepts are labelled in only a handful of proteins, so the effective sample size is the number of proteins, not residues. The caveat quotes residue counts (66 to 1,275) and greatly understates the uncertainty. Several F1 values that sit just above 0.5 depend on one or two proteins, and the set of passing concepts depends on the split seed.
findings.evidence: Proteins with positives in split A / split B: REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18, SIGNAL 29/20. One protein holds 51% of split-B ZN_FING positives and 44% of DISULFID's. All but 31 of the ZN_FING feature's 155 true positives come from one protein. I ran a protein-level bootstrap on split B with feature and threshold fixed (2,000 resamples). The 95% intervals are SIGNAL [0.69, 0.93], DISULFID [0.35, 0.85], REPEAT [0.13, 0.82], COILED [0.16, 0.70], DNA_BIND [0.16, 0.72] and ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67]. Removing the single top protein drops ZN_FING from 0.501 to 0.222, DNA_BIND from 0.517 to 0.393, COILED from 0.519 to 0.446 and DISULFID from 0.721 to 0.556. Across seeds 42 and 0-8, the script's own procedure passes 4 to 7 concepts. Over the 10 seeds COILED passes 3 times and ZN_FING 3 times. TRANSIT passes 8 times and PROPEP 6 times, although neither passes at seed 42.
findings.recommended_action: Report protein-level bootstrap confidence intervals and results over several splits. Require a minimum number of positive proteins per split, not only positive residues. Replace the residue-count caveat with the protein counts.

findings.description: The interpretation claims more than the analysis shows. The analysis only measures how well a feature predicts a concept. It does not test what else a feature responds to, so it cannot show 'monosemantic' features. Four of the six named features do not hold up when chosen on split A (F1). DISULFID is described as detecting 'bonded cysteines', but it was never compared with a predictor that simply flags every cysteine, and the package has no sequences to make that check. The 'not a broad region' statement does not fit REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING, which are span annotations.
findings.evidence: Precision of the passing features is 0.44 to 0.85. For DNA_BIND (precision 0.44) most of the feature's firing is outside the concept. REPEAT feature 4672 fires in 32 split-B proteins, and its true positives come from 5 proteins. ZN_FING feature 624 has true positives in only 2 proteins. REPEAT labels are runs of 40 to 545 residues per protein. All six features are recommended for causal tests, but only 2925 and 1925 replicate when chosen on split A.
findings.recommended_action: Drop 'monosemantic'. Limit claims about candidate features to the ones that replicate (SIGNAL, DISULFID). Compare DISULFID with a cysteine-identity baseline and SIGNAL with an N-terminal or hydrophobic-stretch baseline. Describe the span concepts accurately.

findings.description: The claim that 'F1 is a lower bound' does not hold. Missing annotations can make the measured F1 too high or too low: unlabelled true positives that a feature misses lower its true recall. In addition, choosing the feature on the test split (F1) biases the reported F1 upward.
findings.evidence: See F1: the split-B F1 of features chosen on split B is far above that of features chosen on split A (for example REPEAT 0.626 vs 0.003).
findings.recommended_action: Remove the lower-bound claim. Describe annotation incompleteness as a source of bias in either direction, alongside the selection bias.

findings.description: Proteins are split at random, with no grouping by homology. Close orthologs of split-A proteins appear in split B, so 'proteins not used to tune it' still includes near-duplicates of the tuning proteins, including some that carry the scored concepts.
findings.evidence: 72 gene-name prefixes in proteins.tsv appear more than once, and 47 of them have members in both splits. Examples: LEXA_HERAR (A) and LEXA_HAHCH (B) both carry DNA_BIND, and NRDR_STAA2 (A) and NRDR_THEVB (B) both carry ZN_FING.
findings.recommended_action: Cluster the proteins by sequence identity (for example with MMseqs2 at 30% identity) and split by cluster.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the key's detection rule. It says each concept's best feature is the nanargmax of split-B F1 at score_concepts.py:140, that only the threshold is tuned on split A, and that the reported F1 is therefore the best of 5,035 test-set scores and biased upward. It names this as what drives the 6/21 headline, and its fix is the key's fix: rank on split A and score on split B. Its evidence matches the key and my rerun. Ranking on split A gives REPEAT 919 (0.003), COILED 1401 (0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.000) and ZN_FING 1593 (0.245), so 2/21 pass, only SIGNAL and DISULFID. Across seeds 0-8 the honest rule passes 2 to 5 concepts. F2 also says features are 'chosen on the test split', but it is mainly about the inadequate random baseline and protein clustering, so I count only F1 as the detection.

findings.reason: This is exactly the key's winner's-curse error: the feature is chosen by argmax of split-B F1 at line 140 and that same F1 is reported. I reproduced its split-A-ranked winners and F1 values (REPEAT 0.003, COILED 0.002, DNA_BIND 0.000, ZN_FING 0.245; 2/21 pass) and its seed robustness claims. Calling the SUMMARY statement 'false' slightly overstates it, since that statement is literally true for the threshold, but the core claim is correct.

It does not claim the 2ap/(a+p) formula is wrong (the key lists that as a false alarm). It claims the analytic baseline cannot support the specificity claims, because it ignores the selection over features and the clustering of labels within proteins. I verified that the negative control VARIANT (+0.354) and MUTAGEN count toward '19 of 21'. One replicate of the within-protein circular-shift null that I ran gave REPEAT 0.58, COILED 0.48, VARIANT 0.358, MUTAGEN 0.31, HELIX 0.225, versus SIGNAL 0.19 and DISULFID 0.13, which matches the reported ranges. It overlaps the documented error (under the honest rule the key gives 8/21 with margin >= 0.1), but its distinctive content, the protein-identity null, is a genuine additional problem.

Verified. VARIANT's margin of 0.3545 counts toward 19/21, and at seed 2 the script's own procedure passes VARIANT through the full gate. Its split-A winner (feature 5079) has F1_a 0.656. 949 of 986 positives are two near-whole-protein spans (SMAD6, 483 residues, in split B; CWC27, 466, in split A), and all 145 TPs of feature 3889 are in SMAD6. The control is degenerate, and SUMMARY presents it as working. The finding does not name split-B selection as the cause of the 0.358 (the key's honest value is 0.000), but the concentration problem is real. Minor miscount: VARIANT scores above 13 other concepts, not 14.

Verified the per-split protein counts (REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18, SIGNAL 29/20), the top-protein shares (ZN_FING 51%, DISULFID 44%) and the effect of dropping the top protein (ZN_FING 0.501 to 0.222, DNA_BIND 0.517 to 0.393, DISULFID 0.721 to 0.556; I got COILED 0.475 rather than 0.446). Also verified the seed dependence: the leaky rule passes 4 to 7 concepts over seeds 42 and 0-8; COILED and ZN_FING pass 3 times each, TRANSIT 8 times, PROPEP 6 times. The key notes that rare-concept F1 values are noisy, and the SUMMARY caveat quoting residue counts does understate this. I did not rerun the bootstrap intervals, but they are plausible.

Single-feature F1 cannot establish 'monosemantic' features. The precision values it cites (0.44 to 0.85) are correct. I verified that REPEAT feature 4672 fires in 32 split-B proteins while its TPs come from 5, and that ZN_FING feature 624 has TPs in only 2 proteins. REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING are span annotations, which contradicts 'not a broad region'. The missing cysteine-identity baseline is a fair point about interpretation, since DISULFID labels are 100% cysteine. The finding does not say this makes the F1 values wrong. Part of it (only SIGNAL and DISULFID replicate) is a consequence of the documented error.

Correct that incomplete annotation does not make F1 a strict lower bound: a feature that misses unlabelled true positives has its recall overstated. This is a minor wording issue in the caveats; the selection-bias part restates F1.

Verified: 72 gene-name prefixes repeat, 47 of them span both splits, and LEXA_HERAR/LEXA_HAHCH (DNA_BIND) and NRDR_STAA2/NRDR_THEVB (ZN_FING) sit on opposite sides. Homology-aware splitting is good practice, but only the threshold is tuned on split A here, and the finding shows no material effect on the reported numbers. A true but low-impact limitation.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets the detection rule exactly. It points to code/score_concepts.py:140, where nanargmax is taken over split-B F1, so each concept's feature is picked by the same split-B F1 that is then reported, out of 5,035 features. It says this inflates the reported F1 and the 6/21 headline, and its fix is the key's fix: rank on split A, report split B. I re-ran it and its split-A-ranked numbers match the key and the twin: REPEAT feature 919 scores 0.003, COILED 1401 scores 0.002, DNA_BIND 3681 scores 0.000, ZN_FING 1593 scores 0.245, and only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass, giving 2/21. Its claim that ranking on A passes 2 to 5 concepts across seeds 0-8 and the swapped split, with only SIGNAL and DISULFID passing every time, also checked out. F2 also qualifies: it says the margin statistics (19/21, mean +0.342) compare the best of 5,035 features chosen on the test split with a single random predictor, without correcting for that selection. That is the same winner's curse applied to the margin numbers, which the key also lists as inflated (the key's correct values are 8/21 and +0.143). F2's circular-shift null repeats the split-B selection, and my two replicates reproduced it: REPEAT 0.59-0.62, COILED 0.38-0.47, VARIANT 0.35-0.36, MUTAGEN 0.31-0.34, HELIX 0.22.

findings.reason: This is the key's error. The feature is chosen by split-B F1 (line 140) and that same split-B F1 is reported, so it is a winner's curse. Re-running it confirmed the split-A choices (919, 1401, 3681, 1593), their split-B F1 (0.003, 0.002, 0.000, 0.245) and the 2/21 result. Across seeds 0-8 and the swapped split, ranking on A passes 2 to 5 concepts, and SIGNAL and DISULFID are always among them. These match the key and the twin B8827.

It attacks the margin statistics (19/21 above random, mean +0.342) because the best of 5,035 features is chosen on the test split and compared with one random predictor. That is the documented selection error applied to the margin numbers, which the key says are inflated (correct values 8/21 and +0.143). It does not claim the 2ap/(a+p) formula is wrong, so the key's false alarm does not apply. My two replicates of its circular-shift null matched the stated ranges: REPEAT 0.59-0.62, COILED 0.38-0.47, VARIANT 0.35-0.36, MUTAGEN 0.31-0.34, HELIX 0.22. My DISULFID replicate came out at 0.094-0.115, slightly below the 0.11-0.14 it quotes. The extra point that labels cluster within proteins is also valid.

All checked claims hold. VARIANT clears the margin test (+0.3545), so it counts toward the '19 of 21'. With seed=2 it passes the full gate, and I confirmed the pass list DISULFID, PROPEP, REPEAT, SIGNAL, VARIANT. 949 of its 986 positives come from two long spans, SMAD6_HUMAN 13-495 and CWC27_HUMAN 6-471. 98% of split-B positives are in SMAD6, and all 145 true positives of feature 3889 are in that protein. Feature 5079 has split-A F1 0.656. A degenerate negative control is a real design problem that the key does not cover. The SUMMARY line is literally true but misleading. One small miscount: VARIANT ranks above 13 other concepts, not 14.

Confirmed. Proteins with positives per split are REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18 and SIGNAL 29/20. The top protein holds 51% of ZN_FING's split-B positives and 44% of DISULFID's. My protein-bootstrap intervals match its stated ones, e.g. ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67] and REPEAT [0.13, 0.81]. Dropping the top protein gives ZN_FING 0.222, DNA_BIND 0.393 and DISULFID 0.556, as claimed. COILED came out at 0.475 rather than the quoted 0.446, likely a different 'top protein' definition. Across seeds 42 and 0-8 the procedure passes 4 to 7 concepts, and COILED 3, ZN_FING 3, TRANSIT 8 and PROPEP 6 match. The key notes that rare-concept F1 is noisy. Quoting residue counts instead of protein counts understates that noise, which is a real reporting problem.

The 'monosemantic' interpretation does go beyond what the analysis shows: precision is 0.44 to 0.85, and four of the six named features fail to replicate when chosen on split A, a consequence of the documented error. The details check out. REPEAT feature 4672 fires in 32 split-B proteins but has true positives in only 5. ZN_FING feature 624 has true positives in 2 proteins. REPEAT spans run from 40 to 545 residues. The package has no sequences, so the cysteine baseline cannot be checked. One minor slip: SIGNAL's feature is 2936, not 2925.

The SUMMARY's claim that 'F1 is a lower bound' is wrong. Unlabelled true positives that a feature misses are counted as true negatives, which inflates recall, so measured F1 can be too high as well as too low. The selection bias from the documented error also pushes the reported F1 upward. This is a real but secondary problem in the caveat text and does not affect the headline numbers.

Verified that 72 gene-name prefixes occur more than once and 47 have members in both splits, including LEXA_HERAR (A) with LEXA_HAHCH (B) and NRDR_STAA2 (A) with NRDR_THEVB (B). Only thresholds are tuned on A, though, and orthologs across species are not necessarily near-duplicates, so the effect on the reported numbers is probably small. This is a fair methodological limitation, not something that changes a result.

review.summary: The code runs, and all its outputs reproduce exactly (6/21 pass; mean best F1 0.360, median 0.300). The data files are internally consistent: row alignment, positions, protein lengths, no duplicate codes, and DISULFID/CROSSLNK positives only 1-2 residues long. The headline result still does not stand. The best feature for each concept is picked by its F1 on the held-out split B (score_concepts.py:140), so the reported F1 is a maximum over 5,035 features measured on the test set. Only the threshold is tuned on split A. When both the feature and its threshold are chosen on split A, only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass (2/21), with mean best F1 0.162 and median 0.031. On split A, REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING reach only 0.05, 0.29, 0.15 and 0.11 with the same features. Three further problems weaken the claims. (1) The negative control VARIANT is driven by one protein, SMAD6_HUMAN, which is 483 of 496 residues labelled VARIANT. Its margin over random (+0.354) is counted among the "19 of 21", and with split seed 2 it passes the gate (F1 0.66). (2) The random baseline 2ap/(a+p) is about 0 for rare concepts, so it tests nothing. A null that shifts labels within each protein gives best-feature F1 of 0.60 for REPEAT (observed 0.626), 0.36 for VARIANT and 0.31 for MUTAGEN. (3) The passing results for REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING come from 2-5 proteins each, so they have very wide protein-bootstrap CIs, and both the passing set and the chosen features change with the split seed. Only SIGNAL (feature 2936, 19 proteins, the same feature at every seed) and DISULFID (feature 1925, stable) hold up.

findings.description: The best feature is picked by maximising F1 on split B, the held-out split, over about 5,035 features. Only the threshold is tuned on split A. The reported split-B F1 is therefore the maximum of thousands of test-set scores and is biased upward. SUMMARY.md says the reported F1 'comes from proteins that were not used to tune it', which is false. The headline '6 of 21 concepts pass', the mean/median best F1 and the 19/21 margin count all depend on this.
findings.evidence: The output CSV itself shows the gap. f1_a (split-A F1 of the same feature at its A-tuned threshold) is 0.046 for REPEAT (B: 0.626), 0.290 for COILED (B: 0.519), 0.146 for DNA_BIND (B: 0.517) and 0.114 for ZN_FING (B: 0.501). It is 0.000 for VARIANT, MUTAGEN and HELIX, yet these show B F1 of 0.36, 0.31 and 0.23. I re-ran score_all in memory and chose both the feature and the threshold on split A, then scored on B. Only SIGNAL (0.833) and DISULFID (0.721) pass (2/21). Mean best F1 falls to 0.162 and the median to 0.031. The split-A-best features for REPEAT (919), COILED (1401), DNA_BIND (3681) and ZN_FING (1593) score 0.003, 0.002, 0.000 and 0.245 on B.
findings.recommended_action: Choose the feature and the threshold on split A only, and report split-B F1 for that pair. Alternatively, use nested cross-validation over proteins. Recompute the summary and restate the headline. With this data only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass.

findings.description: The negative control does not behave as a negative control, and the summary misreports it. VARIANT's best feature reaches F1 0.358 with margin +0.354. That beats 14 of the 21 real concepts, and VARIANT is counted among the '19 of 21 concepts at least 0.1 above random'. The whole score comes from one protein. Under another random split the control passes the full gate. So the pipeline can produce 'passing' results for a label that is not a residue property, which undercuts reading a pass as a concept-specific feature.
findings.evidence: All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 lie in protein 526 (SMAD6_HUMAN). In that protein 483 of 496 residues are labelled VARIANT, a single run of 483 residues, i.e. one very long VARIANT span. That protein holds 49% of all 986 VARIANT positives. The feature's split-A F1 is 0.000. With split seed 2, VARIANT's best feature (5079) has split-B F1 0.66 and passes the gate. With labels shifted within each protein, the null best-feature F1 for VARIANT is 0.356, the same as the observed 0.358.
findings.recommended_action: Report that the negative control fails the margin criterion and is as strong as many real concepts. Use the control to set the gate, or replace the gate with a protein-aware null. Consider dropping long-span VARIANT/MUTAGEN entries or scoring them only at point positions.

findings.description: The random-predictor baseline 2ap/(a+p) cannot discriminate here. For rare concepts it is about 0.001-0.013, so margin is roughly F1, and the 0.1 margin criterion only matters for DOMAIN. It ignores two things. First, selection: the best of 5,035 features is reported. Second, labels cluster in a few proteins, so any feature that fires on a positive protein's family gets a high F1. 'For 19 of 21 concepts the best feature is at least 0.1 above random' and 'mean margin +0.342' therefore say almost nothing about residue-level concept detection.
findings.evidence: I ran 5 null runs, each circularly shifting every protein's label vector by a random offset. This keeps which proteins carry a concept but breaks residue alignment. Through the same pipeline, the mean (max) null best-feature F1 was: REPEAT 0.600 (0.637) vs observed 0.626; VARIANT 0.356 vs 0.358; MUTAGEN 0.314 (0.330) vs 0.310; TRANSIT 0.256 (0.290) vs 0.257; HELIX 0.225 vs 0.229; COILED 0.368 (0.397); ZN_FING 0.316 (0.398); DNA_BIND 0.265 (0.299). The random F1 values in the CSV are at most 0.013 for every concept except DOMAIN and REGION.
findings.recommended_action: Replace or add to the analytic baseline with a protein-aware null, such as within-protein label shifts or permutation of features across proteins. The null must apply the same best-of-5,035 selection. Report observed F1 against that null and drop the '19 of 21 above random' and mean-margin claims.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:13-23, 39-42; code/score_concepts.py:125-127 (concept inclusion by residue counts only)
findings.description: Four of the six 'passing' concepts rest on 2-5 proteins in split B, and very few proteins in split A. The effective sample size is proteins, not residues, so these F1 values are very uncertain and depend on the split. The caveat gives '66 to 1,275 positive residues in a split', which understates this. The passing set and the chosen features change with the split seed.
findings.evidence: Split-B true positives by protein: REPEAT 783 TPs from 5 proteins, 92% from 3 (CIAO1_NEMVE, SC132_CANGA, BUB31_ARATH). Split A has only 3 REPEAT proteins. COILED: 5 proteins, 89% from 3. DNA_BIND: 5 proteins, 86% from 3. ZN_FING: TPs from 2 proteins, 124 of 155 in ADN1A_DANRE. DISULFID: 57 of 102 TPs in CO6_PANTR. Protein-bootstrap 95% CIs for split-B F1: REPEAT [0.16, 0.82], COILED [0.17, 0.69], DNA_BIND [0.14, 0.72], ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67], DISULFID [0.36, 0.86], SIGNAL [0.70, 0.94]. Across seeds 0-8, the code as written passes 4-7 concepts with different memberships (PROPEP, TRANSIT and VARIANT pass at some seeds). Best features also change: REPEAT 4672/125/4945, DNA_BIND 3159/118, ZN_FING 624/1593. Only SIGNAL (2936) and DISULFID (1925) are stable.
findings.recommended_action: Report the number of positive proteins per split and per concept. Require a minimum number of positive proteins, not residues. Give protein-bootstrap CIs and repeat over several splits or use cross-validation. Present REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING as unresolved.

findings.description: The interpretation goes beyond the evidence. It calls the six features 'monosemantic' and names them as the candidates for causal tests. F1 around 0.5 with low precision or recall does not show monosemanticity. Four of the six features do not generalise to split A and change with the split seed. The REPEAT feature fires on one family of repeat proteins, not on REPEAT in general.
findings.evidence: DNA_BIND feature 3159 has precision 0.44, so most of the residues it fires on are not DNA_BIND. It fires in 25 split-B proteins, but its TPs come from 5. ZN_FING feature 624 has recall 0.37. REPEAT feature 4672 has split-A F1 0.046, and its TPs are in CIAO1, BUB3 and SC132; CIAO1 and BUB3 are WD-repeat proteins. Feature 904 is the best COILED feature and also the split-A-best feature for MOTIF. Only SIGNAL feature 2936 is clean: 351 TPs across 19 of 20 positive proteins, false positives limited to N-terminal residues of 4 proteins, and the same feature at every seed. DISULFID feature 1925 is stable across seeds.
findings.recommended_action: Drop the 'monosemantic' wording. Limit the claims to SIGNAL (and possibly DISULFID). Check feature specificity across protein families before naming causal-test candidates.

findings.description: Every residue inside a VARIANT or MUTAGEN span is labelled positive, so long deletion-type entries become protein-level labels. This makes the negative control, and MUTAGEN, depend on protein identity. The README does not mention it.
findings.evidence: VARIANT has a single run of 483 residues in SMAD6_HUMAN (483/496 residues). MUTAGEN has a 117-residue run in MPRA_ECOLI, which supplies all 117 split-B TPs of MUTAGEN's best feature (F1 0.310, split-A F1 0.000).
findings.recommended_action: Document this. Score VARIANT/MUTAGEN only at point-change positions, or cap span length, so the control tests what it is meant to test.

findings.description: The protein split is random, not homology-aware. Orthologs of the same gene appear in both splits, which can inflate split-B scores slightly for concepts carried by those families.
findings.evidence: 47 UniProt gene mnemonics (entry-name prefixes) occur in both split A and split B. Among positive proteins: LEXA (DNA_BIND), NRDR (ZN_FING), and PLSY/UPPP/HTPX (TRANSMEM). There are none for SIGNAL or DISULFID, so the impact on the robust results is small.
findings.recommended_action: Split by sequence-identity cluster or gene family (e.g. MMseqs2 clusters) instead of by individual protein.

findings.description: Two smaller wording problems. First, 'F1 is a lower bound' does not follow from incomplete annotation: missing positives would also enlarge the recall denominator, so F1 could go either way. Second, saying a passing feature 'picks out a small, specific set of residues, not a broad region' does not fit REPEAT, COILED and ZN_FING. Their positives are long contiguous spans (REPEAT runs up to 113 residues, ZN_FING up to 62, COILED up to 287 residues in one protein) concentrated in a few proteins.
findings.evidence: Run lengths of the labels: REPEAT max 113, ZN_FING max 62. CIP4_MOUSE has 287 COILED residues and EP15R_MOUSE 168.
findings.recommended_action: Rephrase the caveat (unlabelled positives bias precision down but can bias recall either way). Remove the 'not a broad region' claim.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the detection rule. It points to line 140, where nanargmax is taken over s["f1"], the split-B F1. It says the best feature is picked by maximising F1 on the held-out split B over about 5,035 features, while only the threshold is tuned on split A. So the reported split-B F1 is a maximum of test-set scores and is biased upward. It names the claims that depend on this: 6/21 passing, the mean and median best F1, and 19/21 with margin at least 0.1. Its fix is the key's fix: choose the feature on split A and report its split-B F1. Its corrected numbers match the key's twin result, which I reproduced: 2/21 pass (SIGNAL, DISULFID), mean 0.162, median 0.031, and split-A winners REPEAT 919 (0.003), COILED 1401 (0.002) and DNA_BIND 3681 (0.000).

findings.reason: This is the key's error. The feature is chosen by argmax of split-B F1 at line 140, and that same split-B F1 is reported. The finding gives the correct fix (rank on split A, report split B) and the corrected figures: 2/21 pass, mean 0.162, median 0.031. I reproduced these in memory.

Verified. All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 are in SMAD6_HUMAN, where 483 of 496 residues are labelled VARIANT. With seed 2, VARIANT passes the gate (feature 5079). VARIANT, the negative control, is also counted in the '19 of 21 above random'. The SUMMARY sentence that it 'does not pass the gate' is literally true but misleading. Most of this is a symptom of the documented error (the winning feature's split-A F1 is 0.000, and VARIANT drops to 0.000 under the honest rule). The finding blames one protein and span labels, not selection on split B, so it does not count as detection on its own.

The finding does not say the 2ap/(a+p) formula is wrong, which the key lists as a false alarm. It says the baseline ignores selection and how labels cluster in a few proteins. I ran one within-protein circular-shift null. Best-feature F1 was REPEAT 0.578, VARIANT 0.361, MUTAGEN 0.31, COILED 0.387, ZN_FING 0.393 and DNA_BIND 0.297, close to the observed values. SIGNAL (0.237) and DISULFID (0.099) stayed far below their observed F1. This undercuts the '19/21 above random' and mean-margin claims. Part of the null's height comes from the same selection on split B, but the protein-clustering point is a separate, genuine issue.

Verified. REPEAT's 783 split-B true positives come from 5 proteins, and split A has only 3 REPEAT proteins. ZN_FING's true positives come from 2 proteins, 124 of them in ADN1A_DANRE. Across seeds 0-8 the code passes 4-7 concepts with changing membership (PROPEP, TRANSIT and VARIANT pass at some seeds). The winning features also change (REPEAT 4672/125/4945, DNA_BIND 3159/118, ZN_FING 624/1593). Only SIGNAL and DISULFID are stable. This matches the key's fact that per-concept F1 values are noisy because concepts sit in few proteins, and the SUMMARY caveat understates it. It overlaps with the winner's curse but is a valid separate point about effective sample size.

The 'monosemantic' and 'causal test candidates' wording goes beyond the evidence. I checked: DNA_BIND feature 3159 fires in 25 split-B proteins but its true positives come from only 5. Feature 904 is also the split-A-best feature for MOTIF. SIGNAL feature 2936 has true positives in 19 proteins and is stable across seeds. Much of the overreach follows from the documented error, but the point about interpretation is still valid.

Verified. VARIANT has a single 483-residue labelled run in SMAD6_HUMAN, and MPRA_ECOLI supplies all 117 true positives of MUTAGEN feature 1943. The README does say span residues are positive, but it does not say this turns the negative control into a near protein-level label. This is a real design weakness, but minor.

Verified that 47 entry-name gene prefixes occur in both splits. The key does not list this as a false alarm, but the finding itself says the effect on the robust results is small. It is a fair but minor limitation.

Correct. Since F1 = 2TP/(n_pred + n_pos), missing positives can push F1 either way, so 'lower bound' is not justified. The 'not a broad region' wording does not fit concepts with long labelled runs: I found REPEAT runs up to 113 residues and ZN_FING up to 62. Both are wording issues.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets the key's detection rule. It says the best feature is chosen by np.nanargmax of split-B F1 at score_concepts.py:140, and that the same split-B F1 is the one reported. It calls the reported value the maximum of thousands of test-set scores and says it is biased upward, and it ties this to the 6/21 pass count and the mean and median best F1. Its fix is to choose the feature on split A and report split B. I re-ran that fix in memory. Only SIGNAL (0.833) and DISULFID (0.721) pass, mean 0.162, median 0.031. The split-A winners are REPEAT 919 (0.003), COILED 1401 (0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.000) and ZN_FING 1593 (0.245). All of these match the key's correct_result.

findings.reason: This is the key's error: the feature is selected on the same split-B F1 that is reported, a winner's curse over about 5,035 features. The location (line 140) and the fix (rank by split A, report split B) are both right. I re-ran it and got 2/21 passing, mean 0.162, median 0.031, the same as the key's twin result. The finding also correctly says threshold tuning on split A is not the problem.

Checked against the data. All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 are in SMAD6_HUMAN, which has a 483/496-residue VARIANT run, and 483 of the 986 VARIANT positives (49%) sit in that protein. With split seed 2, VARIANT's best feature 5079 reaches F1 0.66 and passes the gate. VARIANT is also counted in the 19/21 margin claim. The SUMMARY line 'does not pass the gate' is literally true, but it leaves out that the control is as strong as many real concepts. The finding gives the cause as single-protein span labels, not selection on split B, so under rule (c) it does not count as detecting the documented error. It is still a separate, confirmed problem. One small count slip: VARIANT beats 13 of the 20 other concepts, not 14.

The finding does not say the 2ap/(a+p) formula is wrong, which the key lists as a possible false alarm. It says the analytic baseline is a poor null for the '19/21 above random' and mean-margin claims, because it ignores best-of-5,035 selection and the clustering of labels within proteins. I ran two within-protein circular-shift nulls through the same pipeline. Best-feature F1 came out at REPEAT about 0.59-0.62, MUTAGEN 0.31, TRANSIT 0.25-0.26, HELIX 0.22, COILED 0.34-0.36 and VARIANT 0.31. These are close to the observed values, which supports the finding. It overlaps with the documented error but is framed as a baseline problem, not as selection on the reporting split.

Checked. REPEAT's true positives come from 5 proteins, 92% from CIAO1, SC132 and BUB31, and split A has only 3 REPEAT proteins. ZN_FING's 155 true positives come from 2 proteins, 124 of them in ADN1A_DANRE. DISULFID has 57 of its 102 true positives in CO6_PANTR. Across split seeds 0-8 the code passes 4-7 concepts, and the set changes (PROPEP, TRANSIT and VARIANT each pass at some seeds). REPEAT's best feature moves between 4672, 125 and 4945, DNA_BIND's between 3159 and 118, and ZN_FING's between 624 and 1593. Only SIGNAL 2936 and DISULFID 1925 stay the same, which agrees with the key's known facts. I did not check the bootstrap CIs. The core claim, that the caveat understates protein-level uncertainty, holds.

Calling the six features 'monosemantic' and naming them causal-test candidates goes beyond the evidence. I confirmed DNA_BIND 3159 precision 0.44, firing in 25 split-B proteins with true positives from 5. I also confirmed ZN_FING recall 0.37, REPEAT f1_a 0.046, and that feature 904 is the split-A-best feature for MOTIF. The key itself shows only SIGNAL and DISULFID hold up. This overlaps with the consequences of the documented error but is a separate interpretive criticism.

Checked. SMAD6_HUMAN has a 483-residue VARIANT run, and MPRA_ECOLI has a 117-residue MUTAGEN run that supplies all 117 split-B true positives of feature 1943. These whole-protein spans make the negative control depend on protein identity. One inaccuracy: README lines 35-36 do say that positives fill annotated spans. What the README leaves out is the consequence for VARIANT and MUTAGEN. The finding is real but minor.

Confirmed: 47 gene mnemonics occur in both splits, including LEXA (DNA_BIND), NRDR (ZN_FING) and HTPX/PLSY/UPPP (TRANSMEM). None occur for SIGNAL or DISULFID. The finding itself says the effect is small. This is a fair limitation of a non-homology-aware split, not an error in the reported numbers.

Both wording points are correct. Missing annotations push precision down, but recall can move either way, so 'F1 is a lower bound' does not follow. The positives for REPEAT, ZN_FING and COILED are long runs (up to 113, 62 and 193 residues; CIP4_MOUSE has 287 COILED residues), so 'not a broad region' is weak. These are wording issues only.

review.summary: The scoring code runs and reproduces outputs/ exactly, but the headline result does not hold up. code/score_concepts.py line 140 picks each concept's "best feature" by its F1 on split B, the same split the F1 is then reported on. SUMMARY.md says the reported F1 comes from proteins not used to tune it, which is false. When I picked the feature on split A instead, only SIGNAL (feature 2936, split-B F1 0.833) and DISULFID (feature 1925, 0.721) pass. The features picked on split A for REPEAT, COILED and DNA_BIND score at most 0.003 on split B, and ZN_FING scores 0.245. So the result falls from 6 of 21 concepts to 2 of 21. The random baseline ignores the search over 5,035 features. In a protein-level permutation null, the best split-B F1 ranged from 0.05 to 0.69 and the margin was at least 0.1 in 25 of 31 cases. So the claim that 19 of 21 concepts beat random says nothing. The rare concepts come from only 3 to 9 proteins per split, and VARIANT (the negative control) is mostly one protein per split, so it is not a valid control. The claims of monosemanticity and of F1 being a lower bound are not supported. Label alignment checks out: positions are contiguous, signal peptides start at residue 0, and feature 1925 lines up with DISULFID with no offset.

findings.location: code/score_concepts.py:140 (best = np.nanargmax(s["f1"][:, ci]), where s["f1"] is split-B F1); SUMMARY.md:8-10 and 13-27; README.md:64
findings.description: The best feature for each concept is chosen by its F1 on the held-out split B, and that same split-B F1 is then reported. Only the threshold is tuned on split A, while the feature itself is picked out of about 5,035 candidates on the test split. This is test-set selection, so the reported F1 is biased upward. SUMMARY.md says the reported F1 comes from proteins that were not used to tune it, and that is false. The 6/21 pass count, the table, the mean and median best F1 (0.360 / 0.300) and the mean margin (+0.342) all inherit this bias.
findings.evidence: The outputs' own f1_a column (the chosen feature's F1 on split A) shows it: REPEAT 0.046 (split-B F1 0.626), COILED 0.290 (0.519), DNA_BIND 0.146 (0.517), ZN_FING 0.114 (0.501), VARIANT 0.000 (0.358), HELIX 0.000, MUTAGEN 0.000. I re-ran score_all and picked each feature by its split-A F1 before scoring on split B. Only SIGNAL (2936, B F1 0.833) and DISULFID (1925, B F1 0.721) pass. The split-A choices for the other four score: REPEAT feature 919 (F1_A 0.581, F1_B 0.003), COILED 1401 (0.387 / 0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.484 / 0.000), ZN_FING 1593 (0.715 / 0.245).
findings.recommended_action: Choose both the feature and the threshold on split A only, or use a train/validation/test split or nested cross-validation, and report split-B F1 for that choice. Redo the pass count and the aggregate statistics. Correct the setup statement in SUMMARY.md, and say in README step 7 which split is used to choose the feature.

findings.description: The random baseline, 2ap/(a+p) for a single random predictor, does not account for taking the maximum over about 5,035 features (each with 20 thresholds). It also ignores that labels come in contiguous runs inside a few proteins. For rare concepts the baseline is close to 0, so the 0.1-margin test is passed almost automatically. The claim that 19 of 21 concepts beat random by at least 0.1 therefore carries no evidential weight.
findings.evidence: The VARIANT negative control has margin +0.355 and so passes the margin test. I ran a protein-level permutation null: each protein's labels were assigned to a random other protein, and the code's own select-on-B procedure was run. Over 4 permutations of 8 concepts (31 scored cases), the best split-B F1 ranged from 0.05 to 0.69, and the margin was at least 0.1 in 25 of 31 cases. Permuted COILED reached 0.31-0.46, DNA_BIND 0.23-0.43 and REPEAT 0.23-0.36. Permuted VARIANT passed the full gate (F1 >= 0.5 and margin >= 0.1) in 3 of 4 permutations (F1 0.503, 0.600, 0.686). The chosen features had F1_A of about 0 in the permuted runs.
findings.recommended_action: Replace or add to the analytic baseline with a permutation null at the protein level, for example label permutation or circular shifts of spans across proteins. Run the full search (all features and thresholds) under that null and report p-values or a null-adjusted margin.

findings.description: The unit that counts for sample size is the protein, not the residue. The rare concepts behind the headline are labelled in only a handful of proteins per split, and the true positives come from 2 to 5 proteins. Even before fixing the selection bias, the F1 values are very uncertain. ZN_FING (0.5008) only just reaches the 0.5 cut-off. The caveat in SUMMARY.md counts positive residues (66 to 1,275) and so understates this.
findings.evidence: Proteins with positives (A / B): REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18 (CO6_PANTR holds 64 of 146 split-B positives), VARIANT 12/7. Split-B true positives for ZN_FING feature 624 come from 2 proteins (ADN1A_DANRE 124, EGR1_CHICK 31). REPEAT feature 4672: 5 proteins. COILED feature 904: 5 proteins. Protein-bootstrap 95% CIs of split-B F1 at the reported feature and threshold: SIGNAL [0.70, 0.94], DISULFID [0.36, 0.86], REPEAT [0.16, 0.82], COILED [0.17, 0.69], DNA_BIND [0.14, 0.72], ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67]. P(F1 < 0.5) is 0.41 for COILED, 0.46 for DNA_BIND and 0.54 for ZN_FING.
findings.recommended_action: Report protein-level bootstrap CIs, and give the number of proteins per concept and split. Require a minimum number of positive proteins (not residues) before scoring a concept, or use many more proteins for the rare concepts.

findings.description: The negative control is degenerate, and it also undermines the conclusion. VARIANT positives come almost entirely from one protein per split, apparently a long annotated span, so the control really tests whether a feature can pick out one protein's residues. The best feature reaches F1 0.358 with a +0.355 margin, close to the passing concepts. Feature 5079, picked on split A for VARIANT, has split-A F1 0.656. SUMMARY.md presents the failed F1 gate as reassurance, but these numbers show the pipeline produces sizeable F1s for a label that does not describe the residue. VARIANT is also counted in the 21-concept aggregates.
findings.evidence: VARIANT split A: CWC27_HUMAN contributes 466 of 492 positives. Split B: SMAD6_HUMAN contributes 483 of 494. All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 are in SMAD6_HUMAN. VARIANT output row: f1 0.3585, f1_margin 0.3545, f1_a 0.0000. In the permutation null (F2), permuted VARIANT passed the gate in 3 of 4 runs.
findings.recommended_action: Use a proper negative control, for example labels that are random at the residue level but matched in run length and protein spread, or the permutation null from F2. Report that the current control reaches a margin comparable to the passing concepts. Leave the negative control out of the aggregate statistics.

findings.description: The interpretation, that the layer-16 SAE has monosemantic features covering repeats, coiled coils, DNA-binding regions and zinc fingers, is not supported. Apart from the selection bias (F1), several of these features do not carry over across proteins of the same concept. REPEAT is a mix of different repeat types, and the split-B REPEAT feature matches WD-type repeat proteins that do not appear among split A's REPEAT proteins. F1 around 0.5, with precision 0.44 (DNA_BIND) or recall 0.37 (ZN_FING), is not evidence of monosemanticity. For DISULFID there is no comparison with a plain 'is cysteine' predictor, so the analysis cannot tell a bonded-cysteine feature from a cysteine feature.
findings.evidence: REPEAT positives in split A come only from NANM_ECOHS, RLP26_ARATH and RTN4R_RAT. Split-B true positives of feature 4672 come mostly from BUB31_ARATH, CIAO1_NEMVE and SC132_CANGA (WD-repeat proteins) plus ADO1_ARATH. Feature 4672 has only 131 nonzero activations in split A versus 1,098 in split B, and F1_A 0.046. Precision and recall from outputs/best_feature_per_concept.csv: DNA_BIND 0.44 / 0.63, ZN_FING 0.79 / 0.37, COILED 0.65 / 0.43.
findings.recommended_action: Limit the claims to concepts that pass after selecting on split A with protein-level uncertainty, which here is likely only SIGNAL and DISULFID. Describe features by the specific subtype they detect. Add residue-identity baselines (for example cysteine identity for DISULFID). Drop 'monosemantic' unless the features' full activation profiles are examined.

findings.description: The claim that F1 is a lower bound because annotation is incomplete is not valid. Choosing the feature on the test split (F1) biases F1 upward. Missing annotations can also push F1 either way: unannotated true positives that the feature misses would lower recall if they were labelled. HELIX, STRAND and TURN are only annotated in proteins with solved structures, so their low prevalence makes this effect large for those concepts.
findings.evidence: Prevalences: HELIX 1.9%, STRAND 0.99%, TURN 0.19%, far below typical secondary-structure fractions. The reported F1 values fall sharply once the feature is selected on split A (F1).
findings.recommended_action: Remove the 'lower bound' claim. For annotation-dependent concepts such as secondary structure, restrict scoring to proteins that carry that kind of annotation.

findings.description: The split is by protein, not by sequence family. Homologues of the same gene appear in both splits, including some that carry the concepts being scored, so held-out F1 can be inflated by family memorisation and does not show generalisation to new families.
findings.evidence: 72 entry-name gene prefixes have more than one protein in the 600, many split across A and B. Examples: LEXA_HERAR (A) and LEXA_HAHCH (B), both with DNA_BIND; NRDR_STAA2 (A) and NRDR_THEVB (B), both with ZN_FING; also ACCA, AROA, ATPB, GCSP and others.
findings.recommended_action: Split by sequence clusters (for example MMseqs2 at 30% identity) or by family so that no homologue appears in both splits.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the detection rule exactly. It says the best feature for each concept is the nanargmax of split-B F1 at score_concepts.py:140, and that this same split-B F1 is reported. It names this as test-set selection over about 5,035 features and says it inflates the 6/21 pass count, the mean and median best F1 and the mean margin. Its fix is the key's fix: pick the feature on split A and report split B. I re-ran it and its split-A choices match the key (REPEAT 919 0.003, COILED 1401 0.002, DNA_BIND 3681 0.000, ZN_FING 1593 0.245; SIGNAL and DISULFID unchanged). F2 describes the same winner's curse through the margin claim: the maximum over about 5,035 features is taken by the code's own select-on-B procedure, so the 19/21 margin count is inflated. I ran a protein-level permutation and it agrees. With select-on-B, permuted labels give margins of +0.08 to +0.6 and sometimes pass the gate. With features ranked on split A, the margins are about 0.

findings.reason: This is the key's error. The feature is chosen by nanargmax of split-B F1 at line 140 and that same F1 is reported. I re-ran it and the split-A-ranked winners match the finding and the key: REPEAT 919 (F1_A 0.581, F1_B 0.003), COILED 1401 (0.387/0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.484/0.000), ZN_FING 1593 (0.715/0.245). Only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass.

It does not claim the 2ap/(a+p) formula is wrong, which the key lists as a false alarm. It claims the margin test ignores the maximum taken over features by the select-on-B procedure. My protein-level permutation agrees: with select-on-B, permuted labels gave large margins (+0.08 to +0.6), and VARIANT and REPEAT passed the gate in one run. With split-A ranking the margins were about 0, so the analytic baseline is fine once selection is honest. This is the same winner's curse, affecting the 19/21 margin claim (the key gives 8/21 when done honestly).

Verified. Proteins with positives in split A / split B: REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18, VARIANT 12/7. CO6_PANTR holds 64 of 146 split-B DISULFID positives. The split-B true positives of ZN_FING feature 624 come from only 2 proteins (ADN1A_DANRE 124, EGR1_CHICK 31). The key itself says rare-concept F1 values are noisy. The SUMMARY caveat counts residues and so understates this. It is a valid uncertainty point, but it does not say a result is wrong.

Verified. VARIANT split A: CWC27_HUMAN holds 466 of 492 positives. Split B: SMAD6_HUMAN holds 483 of 494. All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 are in SMAD6_HUMAN. Feature 5079, picked on split A, has F1_A 0.656 and split-B F1 0.000. So the control is degenerate: it mostly tests whether a feature can pick out one protein. The control also makes the 0.358 look reassuring, and that number is itself inflated by the documented selection. This undercuts the negative-control reassurance in SUMMARY.

The claim that the features are monosemantic is not supported for REPEAT, COILED, DNA_BIND and ZN_FING. This follows mainly from the documented selection bias, but the finding adds evidence I confirmed. Split-A REPEAT proteins are RLP26, NANM and RTN4R only. The split-B true positives of feature 4672 are in CIAO1, SC132, BUB31 and ADO1. Feature 4672 has 131 nonzero activations in split A versus 1,098 in split B. The missing cysteine-identity baseline for DISULFID is a fair gap but a weaker point, since precision of 0.74 already exceeds what a plain cysteine detector would plausibly reach. The key treats DISULFID as robust.

True: incomplete annotation does not guarantee that F1 is a lower bound, and selection on split B pushes F1 upward. The HELIX, STRAND and TURN prevalences in the outputs match the finding. This is a minor point in the caveats and does not change the headline numbers on its own.

The facts check out: 72 gene prefixes have more than one protein, 47 of them span both splits, LEXA_HERAR (A) and LEXA_HAHCH (B) both have DNA_BIND, and NRDR_STAA2 (A) and NRDR_THEVB (B) both have ZN_FING. The split by protein matches the stated design, and the finding does not show that homology changes the results. It is a fair scope limitation, not a demonstrated error.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets the key's detection rule. It says the best feature for each concept is chosen by np.nanargmax over split-B F1 (score_concepts.py:140) out of about 5,035 candidates, and that this same split-B F1 is then reported. It calls this test-set selection that biases F1 upward, and says the 6/21 pass count, the mean and median F1 and the mean margin all inherit the bias. Its fix is the key's fix: choose the feature on split A and report its split-B F1. I re-ran score_all and confirmed every number it cites. Under split-A selection only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass, with REPEAT 919 (0.581 on A, 0.003 on B), COILED 1401 (0.387/0.002), DNA_BIND 3681 (0.484/0.000) and ZN_FING 1593 (0.715/0.245). This matches the key's correct_result.

findings.reason: This is exactly the key's error: the winning feature is picked by argmax over the split-B F1 that is then reported, which is a winner's curse. I re-ran the code. The f1_a values match the CSV, and selecting on split A reproduces the key's correct result (2/21 passing; REPEAT 0.003, COILED 0.002, DNA_BIND 0.000, ZN_FING 0.245). The finding also correctly says the threshold step itself is on split A.

This is the same selection error, seen through the margin. The 2ap/(a+p) baseline is fine for one feature chosen in advance (key), but not for a maximum taken over about 5,035 features on the reporting split. The finding does not say the formula is wrong; it says the 19/21 margin count is inflated, and the key confirms 19/21 falls to 8/21 under honest selection. I ran a small protein-level permutation null with the select-on-B rule (2 seeds, 5 concepts). Permuted margins were all well above 0.1 (0.18 to 0.75), the winners had f1_a near 0, and permuted VARIANT reached F1 0.458 and 0.751. The finding's main argument is about the baseline and the maximum over features, and split B is named only in its evidence, so I count F1, not F2, as the clean detection.

Confirmed. The number of proteins with positives (A/B) is REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, DISULFID 20/18 and VARIANT 12/7. ZN_FING feature 624's true positives come only from ADN1A_DANRE (124) and EGR1_CHICK (31). CO6_PANTR holds 64 of 146 split-B DISULFID positives. My protein-bootstrap CIs closely match the finding's: ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67], P(F1<0.5) about 0.53; DNA_BIND [0.16, 0.72], about 0.50; COILED [0.16, 0.70], about 0.42. The key itself says per-concept F1 is noisy for rare concepts, and SUMMARY's caveat counts residues rather than proteins. This is a genuine uncertainty problem separate from the selection bias, and it puts several of the six passes in doubt.

Confirmed. VARIANT positives come almost entirely from CWC27_HUMAN in split A (466 of 492) and SMAD6_HUMAN in split B (483 of 494). All 145 split-B true positives of feature 3889 are in SMAD6_HUMAN. The feature chosen on split A for VARIANT (5079) has f1_a 0.656. So the control mostly tests whether a feature can pick out one protein, and its F1 of 0.358 with margin +0.355 does not give the reassurance SUMMARY claims. The high VARIANT value comes partly from the documented selection error (the honest value is 0.000), but the control's degeneracy is a separate real flaw.

Confirmed. REPEAT positives in split A come only from RLP26_ARATH, NANM_ECOHS and RTN4R_RAT, while feature 4672's split-B true positives are in CIAO1_NEMVE, SC132_CANGA, BUB31_ARATH and ADO1_ARATH (WD-repeat proteins). The feature is nonzero on 131 residues in split A and 1,098 in split B, with f1_a 0.046. The precision and recall figures quoted match the CSV. DISULFID labels are 100% cysteine (key), so the missing cysteine-identity baseline is a fair concern. The 'monosemantic features for six concepts' interpretation is not supported, which overlaps with but goes beyond the selection bias.

Correct but minor. SUMMARY's claim that 'F1 is a lower bound' is not valid: selection on split B biases F1 upward, and incomplete annotation can move F1 either way. The low HELIX, STRAND and TURN prevalences are confirmed. This concerns caveat wording and does not change any headline number.

Factually true. 72 entry-name gene prefixes have more than one protein, and 47 of them span both splits, including LEXA_HERAR (A) / LEXA_HAHCH (B) and NRDR_STAA2 (A) / NRDR_THEVB (B). A family-level split is a fair design improvement, but the finding gives no evidence that homology changes any reported F1. The protein-level split itself is correct per the key.

review.summary:
I re-ran the scoring in memory without writing anything, and it reproduces outputs/ exactly. The headline result does not hold. In score_concepts.py line 140, the "best feature" for each concept is chosen by its F1 on split B, which is the held-out split, out of 5,035 candidates. Only the threshold is tuned on split A. So the reported F1s are maxima taken on the test set, and the summary's statement that F1 "comes from proteins that were not used to tune it" is false.

The f1_a column in the outputs already shows this. On split A, the reported features score REPEAT 0.046, VARIANT 0.000, HELIX 0.000 and MUTAGEN 0.000. When I instead chose each feature on split A and scored it on split B, REPEAT dropped to 0.003, COILED to 0.002, DNA_BIND to 0.000 and ZN_FING to 0.245. Only SIGNAL (0.833) and DISULFID (0.721) still pass, so the count is 2 of 21, not 6 of 21.

The random baseline 2ap/(a+p) describes one random predictor, not the best of 5,035 features. I built a null that keeps protein membership: labels shifted by a random offset within each protein, then the analysis's own procedure applied. That null reaches max F1 of 0.60 for REPEAT (reported 0.626), 0.355 for VARIANT (reported 0.358), 0.37 for COILED, 0.32 (up to 0.40) for ZN_FING and 0.26 for DNA_BIND. The "+0.342 mean margin" and "19 of 21 beat random" statistics therefore carry no information.

The negative control (VARIANT) actually fails. Its margin is +0.354, its F1 is higher than 13 real concepts, and all of its true positives come from one protein (SMAD6_HUMAN). With split seed 2 it passes the gate at F1 0.66.

The unit of inference is effectively the protein. In split B, ZN_FING's true positives come from 2 proteins and REPEAT, COILED and DNA_BIND each from 5. Bootstrap 95% CIs that resample whole proteins are wide: ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67], DNA_BIND [0.14, 0.72], COILED [0.17, 0.69], REPEAT [0.16, 0.82]. Across other split seeds, only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass every time. Calling the features "monosemantic" is not supported by the evidence. Smaller issues: the "F1 is a lower bound" caveat is wrong, related proteins appear in both splits, there is no trivial baseline, and reproducibility files are incomplete.

Verdicts by checklist pattern:
- P1 (weak null): present and unaddressed.
- P2 (trivial baseline): present and unaddressed.
- P3 (endpoint vs claim): present ("monosemantic"; F1 against one label only).
- P4 (unit of inference): present and unaddressed.
- P5 (selection / double-dipping): present and unaddressed. This is the critical one.
- P6 (positive control): no null claim is load-bearing, but the negative control fails.
- P7 (single condition): one layer and one SAE, acknowledged; the single split seed is not.
- P8 (stability): present and unaddressed.
- P9 (overclaiming language): present.
- P10 (reproducibility): partially present.

findings.location: code/score_concepts.py line 140 (best = np.nanargmax(s["f1"][:, ci])); README.md lines 59-65; SUMMARY.md lines 8-10 and 13-23
findings.description: The best feature for each concept is chosen by its F1 on split B, the held-out evaluation split, out of 5,035 scored features. Only the threshold is tuned on split A. The reported F1s are therefore maxima over thousands of candidates taken on the test set (winner's curse / double-dipping). The summary says the reported F1 'comes from proteins that were not used to tune it', which is false for feature selection. Its headline of '6 of 21 concepts pass' does not hold.
findings.evidence: The f1_a column in outputs/best_feature_per_concept.csv shows the reported features scoring far lower on split A. REPEAT feature 4672: split A 0.046 vs split B 0.626. DNA_BIND 3159: 0.146 vs 0.517. ZN_FING 624: 0.114 vs 0.501. COILED 904: 0.290 vs 0.519. VARIANT, HELIX and MUTAGEN: 0.000 on split A. I re-ran score_all in memory and chose each feature by its split-A F1 instead (proper held-out selection), then scored it on split B. REPEAT fell to 0.003, COILED to 0.002, DNA_BIND to 0.000 and ZN_FING to 0.245. Only SIGNAL (0.833) and DISULFID (0.721) still pass, so the count is 2 of 21, not 6 of 21. On split A, the REPEAT feature ranks 171st, DNA_BIND 24th and ZN_FING 53rd.
findings.recommended_action: Choose both the feature and the threshold on split A only, then score once on split B. Better still, use protein-grouped cross-validation, or a three-way split with a confirmatory slice held out before any selection. Recompute the passing count, mean and median best F1 and the margins. Restate the headline as 2 of 21 (SIGNAL, DISULFID) unless the corrected procedure shows otherwise. Remove the false 'not used to tune it' statement.

findings.location: code/score_concepts.py lines 48-51 and 141-142 (expected_random_f1); SUMMARY.md lines 13-14 and 25-27
findings.description: The random baseline 2ap/(a+p) is the expected F1 of a single random predictor. It does not account for taking the maximum over 5,035 features, or for labels clustered within proteins that a protein-identity feature can pick up. The 'margin over random' gate and the summary statistics ('mean margin +0.342', '19 of 21 concepts at least 0.1 above random') are therefore not anchored to a meaningful chance level. Almost any best-of-5,035 feature clears them.
findings.evidence: I built a within-protein null: each protein's labels shifted by a random circular offset, then the analysis's own max-over-features procedure applied (5 replicates). Null max F1 on split B against the reported value: REPEAT 0.599 ± 0.023 vs 0.626; VARIANT 0.355 vs 0.358; MUTAGEN 0.314 vs 0.310; HELIX 0.225 vs 0.229; TRANSIT 0.256 vs 0.257; COILED 0.367 vs 0.519; ZN_FING 0.316 ± 0.068 (maximum 0.398) vs 0.501; DNA_BIND 0.264 vs 0.517. SIGNAL (null 0.21 vs 0.833) and DISULFID (null 0.11 vs 0.721) are well above it. The per-concept 'random F1' values are 0.001 to 0.013, so the margin is almost the same number as the F1.
findings.recommended_action: Replace the single-predictor baseline with a null that repeats the whole selection procedure on permuted labels (maximum over features), with labels permuted in a way that keeps protein structure (within-protein shift or protein-block permutation). Report each F1 as observed vs null mean ± SD and 95th percentile. Drop or recompute the 'mean margin' and '19 of 21' statements against that null.

findings.description: The negative control is reported as a success, but it actually fails. VARIANT's best feature beats the random baseline by +0.354, more than three times the 0.1 margin. Its F1 is higher than 13 of the 20 real concepts. It is excluded only because F1 0.358 is below 0.5. The signal comes from recognising one protein, which shows the procedure rewards protein identity rather than residue concepts.
findings.evidence: VARIANT row: f1 0.3585, random_f1 0.0039, f1_margin 0.3545, f1_a 0.0000. All 145 true positives for feature 3889 on split B lie in a single protein (SMAD6_HUMAN, 145 hits among 483 VARIANT positives). 98% of split-B VARIANT positives are in that one protein. With split seed 2 instead of 42, the reported procedure gives VARIANT F1 0.66 and it passes the gate. The within-protein null reproduces its F1 (0.355).
findings.recommended_action: Report the negative control honestly: by the margin criterion it is indistinguishable from a real concept. Use it to calibrate the gate, for example by requiring that the control fail under the corrected selection and null across split seeds. Do not present it as evidence that the gate discriminates.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 13-23 and 39-42; code/score_concepts.py lines 75-115 (all counts are per residue)
findings.description: Pseudoreplication: F1 and every count treat residues as the units, but the passing concepts' positives sit in a handful of proteins. The effective sample size is the number of proteins, not 66 to 1,275 residues, and the caveat states precision in residue counts. Protein-level uncertainty is large enough that four of the six 'passing' F1s are not clearly above 0.5.
findings.evidence: Proteins with positives in split A / split B: REPEAT 3/7, COILED 8/6, DNA_BIND 8/6, ZN_FING 9/6, VARIANT 12/7. True positives of the reported features on split B by protein: ZN_FING from 2 proteins (124 of 155 from ADN1A_DANRE); REPEAT, COILED and DNA_BIND from 5 proteins each; MUTAGEN from 1. Bootstrap 95% CIs resampling split-B proteins (2,000 draws): ZN_FING [0.00, 0.67], with F1 below 0.5 in 54% of draws; DNA_BIND [0.14, 0.72] (46%); COILED [0.17, 0.69] (41%); REPEAT [0.16, 0.82] (20%); DISULFID [0.36, 0.86] (12%); SIGNAL [0.70, 0.94] (0%).
findings.recommended_action: Report the number of proteins (and protein families) behind every concept. Bootstrap and run nulls by protein. State the gate in protein-level terms, or add a minimum number of distinct proteins with true positives. Rewrite the caveat to give protein counts and CIs.

findings.location: code/score_concepts.py lines 28 and 37-45 (one split with SEED = 42); SUMMARY.md lines 13-23
findings.description: The headline set of passing concepts comes from a single protein split, with no sensitivity analysis. It changes substantially when the split seed changes or the roles of A and B are swapped. ZN_FING (F1 0.5008) sits exactly on the gate.
findings.evidence: Reported procedure: seed 42 with A/B swapped passes DISULFID, REPEAT, SIGNAL, TRANSIT, ZN_FING. Seed 0 passes DISULFID, DNA_BIND, PROPEP, SIGNAL, TRANSIT. Seed 1 passes DISULFID, DNA_BIND, SIGNAL, TRANSIT, ZN_FING. Seed 2 passes DISULFID, PROPEP, REPEAT, SIGNAL and VARIANT (the negative control). Seed 3 passes DISULFID, DNA_BIND, PROPEP, SIGNAL, TRANSIT. COILED never passes outside seed 42. With proper split-A selection, 2 to 5 concepts pass depending on the seed, and only SIGNAL and DISULFID pass every time (TRANSIT passes 3 times).
findings.recommended_action: Repeat the analysis over at least 5 to 10 protein splits, or use protein-grouped K-fold. Report how often each concept passes and the mean ± SD of F1. Restrict headline claims to concepts that pass consistently.

findings.description: Overclaiming: the summary says the SAE 'has monosemantic features' for six concepts and calls them candidates for causal tests. F1 against one UniProt label does not establish monosemanticity: what else the feature fires on was not examined. Four of the six do not survive held-out selection.
findings.evidence: Precision of the reported features is moderate, and they fire well outside the annotated proteins. DNA_BIND feature 3159: precision 0.44, fires in 25 proteins but true positives in only 5. ZN_FING feature 624: fires in 13 proteins, true positives in 2. REPEAT feature 4672: fires in 32 proteins, true positives in 5. COILED feature 904: fires in 16, true positives in 5. Under split-A selection, the REPEAT, COILED and DNA_BIND features score F1 ≈ 0 on split B (see F1).
findings.recommended_action: Replace 'monosemantic' with wording at the level of the evidence, e.g. 'a single feature's activation overlaps the annotation with held-out F1 X'. Limit candidate features to those that pass the corrected, protein-level analysis (currently SIGNAL 2936 and DISULFID 1925). If monosemanticity is to be claimed, check what the features fire on outside the annotation.

findings.description: The caveat that incomplete Swiss-Prot annotation makes 'F1 a lower bound' is wrong. Choosing the best of 5,035 features on the evaluation split pushes the reported F1 upward. Missing annotations also do not guarantee that true-label F1 would be higher, because recall on unannotated true positives is unknown.
findings.evidence: See F1 and F2. The reported F1s exceed the held-out-selection F1s by up to 0.6 (REPEAT 0.626 vs 0.003), and several match the within-protein null.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the lower-bound statement. State that the reported F1s are upward-biased by selection until the corrected procedure is used, and that annotation incompleteness can move F1 either way.

findings.description: The split is by protein, not by sequence-homology cluster. Orthologues from different species fall on both sides, so 'held-out' proteins can be close homologues of split-A proteins. This inflates held-out F1 even under a corrected selection procedure.
findings.evidence: 47 UniProt gene-name prefixes occur in both splits, for example HTPX, PLSY, RL16, RL27, LEUD, ATPB, H2B and LEXA. Several of these are annotated membrane proteins or have structured regions. Related synthetases (SYR_LARHH, SYR_SALHS) supply the MOTIF true positives.
findings.recommended_action: Cluster proteins by sequence identity (e.g. MMseqs2 at 30-50%) and split by cluster. Report whether SIGNAL and DISULFID still pass.

findings.description: No trivial baseline. The only comparator is a random predictor at the same firing rate. Nothing shows whether a single SAE feature does better than simple predictors from residue identity, position or the raw layer-16 activations (e.g. 'is cysteine' for DISULFID, N-terminal position for SIGNAL, the best single neuron of the dense residual stream). Claims that the SAE has dedicated features need that comparison.
findings.evidence: The README and SUMMARY name no trivial baseline. Sequences are not included, so residue-identity baselines cannot be computed from the package.
findings.recommended_action: Add amino-acid identity, position and best-single-neuron (dense activation) baselines. Report F1 for each concept as the improvement over the best trivial baseline.

findings.description: Reproducibility is incomplete. Package versions are not pinned, and the Swiss-Prot release, label-extraction code, ESM activation code and SAE weights/training code are absent. The claims that the SAE explains 74.6% of variance and that none of the 600 proteins were used in training cannot be checked. The scoring step itself reproduces exactly.
findings.evidence: The README says only 'Needs numpy and scipy' and 'The SAE weights are not included'. There is no requirements file and no code that produced data/*.npz. Re-running score_all in memory reproduces outputs/best_feature_per_concept.csv exactly.
findings.recommended_action: Add pinned environment files, the Swiss-Prot release and date, the scripts that produced the labels and SAE codes, the SAE checkpoint (or a hash and download location), and the list of SAE training accessions, so the claims of no overlap and 74.6% variance can be verified.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the detection rule directly. It names code/score_concepts.py line 140 (np.nanargmax(s["f1"][:, ci])) and says the best feature is chosen by its split-B F1, the same F1 that is reported, out of 5,035 features. It calls this winner's curse / double-dipping and says the 6/21 headline is wrong. Its fix matches the key: rank on split A, then score on split B. I re-ran score_all in memory and its numbers match the key's correct result exactly: 2/21 pass (SIGNAL 0.833, DISULFID 0.721), REPEAT 0.003, COILED 0.002, DNA_BIND 0.000, ZN_FING 0.245. Its split-A ranks also match (REPEAT 171, DNA_BIND 24, ZN_FING 53). F2 touches the same max-over-features inflation, but it frames it as a problem with the random baseline and the margin gate. It does not say the winner is picked on the reported split, so I do not count it as a detection.

findings.reason: This is the key's error: the feature is chosen by nanargmax of split-B F1 at line 140 and that same F1 is reported. I re-ran the analysis with split-A selection and got the key's correct values (2/21 pass; REPEAT 0.003, COILED 0.002, DNA_BIND 0.000, ZN_FING 0.245).
