F2 is confirmed: the expression null's binary search hits its upper bound of s = 20. This contradicts the key's statement that every null is matched to its own linear circ-R2. F5's dimension dependence is also confirmed. Neither of these is a documented error, because the key has none.

findings.reason: Only part of this finding reproduced. I built the same 4-D loop (cos phi, sin phi, cos 2phi, sin 2phi) at scGPT settings (d = 512, noise matched to circ-R2 0.892). With almost no noise it gives an out-of-plane angle of 26.0 deg and planarity 0.805, matching the review and close to the flat-null mean of 25.6. So the statistic does depend on whitening and is not monotone in non-planarity. A half-amplitude 2nd harmonic was detected 5/5, also matching. But the main 'little power' claim (only 1/5 runs above the null 95th percentile of 29.23) did not reproduce. In my 11 matched-noise runs, 8 exceeded 29.23 (values 30.8, 31.7, 29.4, 31.5, 31.6, 31.6, 27.0, 29.21, 31.2, 30.2, 27.5), about 70% power. The real values sit below the null in all three representations, which hints at a conservative isotropic-noise null; for expression that is partly the F2 bug. The key calls the low power a stated limitation, and SUMMARY already says the result is a failure to reject, not proof of flatness. Whether Conclusion 3 'cannot stand' therefore stays undecided.

Confirmed by re-running flat_null for seed 100 on the expression data. The binary search goes to lo every step, ends at s = 19.99996 (the bound is 20) and gives null linear circ-R2 0.952 against the real 0.929. Its out-of-plane angle is 18.879 deg, exactly the stored draw. With the bound widened to 60, the search matches at s about 23.0 (R2 0.927), and the out-of-plane angle rises to 23.0 deg (seed 100) and 21.9 deg (seed 101). Both are well above the real 17.9. So the expression null (17.9 +- 1.4) and p = 0.571 in the table are wrong, and the README's statement that noise is matched is false for expression. This contradicts one of the key's 'known true facts'. The 'not rejected' verdict still holds and gets stronger (real < null).

Reproduced exactly on the 2,000 shared cells (linear circ-R2 by number of whitened PCs). Geneformer: 0.844 (20), 0.892 (50), 0.902 (200). scGPT: 0.896, 0.913, 0.919. Expression: 0.935, 0.932, 0.920. At 200 PCs, expression vs scGPT is 0.920 vs 0.919, so the gap of 0.039 in Conclusion 2 largely comes from the fixed 20-PC, alpha = 10 setup. The expression-Geneformer gap shrinks from 0.091 to 0.018. The numbers as computed are correct, and the key's checks (CV seeds, bootstrap) cover only the 20-PC setup. But the size of the expression advantage and the models' decodability depend on the dimension, which the summary does not mention. The review's tuned RidgeCV result (expression still slightly best) means the ranking may survive while the gap sizes do not.

Correct in substance. phi = atan2(u, v), where u and v are linear projections of z-scored marker expression, so the gradient of phi lies in span(a, b), which is a 2-plane. I checked that the two marker PCs are almost linear in the 20 whitened expression PCs (5-fold CV R2 0.98 and 0.93; scGPT 0.93 and 0.85; the review's numbers differ a little). So in expression the tangent field is close to planar by construction, and the expression 'flat circle' result carries no information. SUMMARY does not say this. This is not the key's 'marker label as an error in itself' false alarm, because it names a specific consequence for the geometry test. It does not make any number or the 'not rejected' verdict wrong; it limits how they can be read.

The numbers reproduced (5 PCs: scGPT linear 0.490 vs kNN 0.592, Geneformer 0.322 vs 0.366, expression 0.638 vs 0.711; at 200 PCs scGPT kNN 0.378). But the kNN-over-linear flip happens only at 5 PCs, where both readouts do far worse than linear at 20. As the key notes, kNN on the unwhitened 20 PCs is still below linear (scGPT 0.836 < 0.892). No kNN setting I tested reaches linear at 20+ PCs. So 'linear readout is enough' still holds in practice. The logical point that an untuned kNN is a weak nonlinear benchmark is fair but minor, and the key lists 'kNN worse' as a measured result, not an error.

True. With 20 draws, np.percentile(.., 95) interpolates at order position 18.05, so a real value between the 19th and 20th order statistics would be 'rejected' while p = 2/21 = 0.095. That makes the rule inconsistent with the stated p, but it does not apply to any current result (all p >= 0.57). Trivial.

Confirmed: np.expm1(emb).sum(1) has min 7447, median 9137 and max 9573, not 10,000. So the README's 'log(1 + CP10k) of all 6,546 genes' is inaccurate; CP10k was evidently computed on a larger gene set before subsetting. This is a provenance and documentation slip with negligible effect on the z-scored labels.

verdicts.reason: I re-ran the test and the power limitation is real. Using scGPT phi, d=512, the package's own flat_null-style binary search to linear circ-R2 0.892, and the package's loop_tangents/turning_stats, here is how often each loop exceeded the stored scGPT null 95th percentile (29.23 deg). (1) Equal-amplitude 4-D loop (cos phi, sin phi, cos 2phi, sin 2phi): 8 of 15 draws, angles 25.7-32.7 deg. (2) Saddle: 3 of 5. (3) Half-amplitude 2nd harmonic: 5 of 5, angles 34-39 deg. A near noise-free 4-D loop gives an out-of-plane angle of 26.2 deg and planarity 0.803, about the scGPT null mean (25.6 deg, 0.799). A 4-D loop whose 2nd harmonic has twice the amplitude gives 11-15 deg, well below the flat null. So the one-sided out-of-plane statistic is not monotone in non-planarity and cannot detect some strongly non-planar loops. This does not make Conclusion 3 wrong, for four reasons. (a) SUMMARY.md presents it only as a failure to reject ('This is a failure to reject with 20 null draws, not proof that the loop is exactly flat'), and every number matches outputs/*.json. (b) The package's own total-turning statistic separates the real data from the non-planar loops the finding uses. scGPT real total turning is 588 deg against a null of 613+-35. My simulated 4-D loops gave 701-741 deg (1:1) and 721-732 deg (1:2), so the real loop does not look like these alternatives; the substance of 'consistent with a flat loop' holds. (c) The 'null not calibrated / flatter than a flat circle in all three' claim is not supported. The null is a proper flat-circle null with p = (#>=real+1)/21, and the real values fall inside the null spread: scGPT 22.7 vs 25.6+-2.3, Geneformer 34.2 vs 35.7+-2.4, expression 17.94 vs a null mean of 17.9 (not below it). p values of 0.905, 0.762 and 0.571 are ordinary under the null. (d) The answer key lists 'low power' and 'null mis-calibrated' as false alarms. At most this is a wording and limitation point (the hedge mentions only the number of draws, not the statistic's blind spot), not a load-bearing error. The 'critical' rating and 'heading cannot stand' overstate it.

review.summary:
I reviewed B4328 (cell-cycle phase decodability and loop flatness in scGPT, Geneformer and expression for K562 control cells) against all ten checklist patterns, and re-ran parts of the code inline without writing any files. The decodability numbers reproduce: same-cell linear circ-R2 is 0.896, 0.844 and 0.935 for scGPT, Geneformer and expression, and stays within ±0.003 across CV seeds. The shared-cell gaps are statistically solid (paired bootstrap 95% CI: expression minus scGPT [0.031, 0.050]; scGPT minus Geneformer [0.038, 0.066]).

The geometry conclusion is the main problem.
- **P6, P1, P9 (critical):** the flat-circle test has no positive control. When I planted non-planar loops into the real scGPT noise, they were never rejected and produced out-of-plane angles no higher than flat loops. So 'the loop fits a flat circle' (conclusion 3) cannot stand.
- **P3, P5 (major):** the expression row is flat by construction. The phase label is the angle within a fixed 2-D projection of marker-gene expression, and the expression tangents' best-fit plane matches that projection.
- **Code bug (major):** the noise search for the expression null hits its upper limit of 20, so its null is not matched. The reported null (17.9 ± 1.4, p = 0.571) is wrong; a properly matched null gives about 22–24 degrees, which makes p ≈ 1.
- **P8 (major):** 'kNN does worse in all three, so a linear readout is enough' only holds at 20 whitened PCs. At 5 PCs kNN beats linear in every representation.

Minor issues:
- **P2, P3:** the advantage of expression over scGPT disappears once the marker genes that define the label are removed. The summary partly acknowledges this.
- **P8:** there are no confidence intervals and no sweep over the number of PCs (Geneformer circ-R2 runs from 0.58 to 0.89 depending on that number).
- **P7:** results come from a single cell line, a single layer per model and a single noise model.
- **Marker list:** it uses outdated gene names, so two markers present in the data are missed.
- **P10:** reproducibility gaps, including no code for producing the embeddings and an expression normalisation that does not match its description.

P4 is clean for the within-dataset decodability claims, and conclusion 4 (the evidence is correlational) is appropriately hedged.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 30-32 (Conclusion 3) and table lines 15-17; code/cc_geometry.py lines 81-98 (turning_stats) and 102-118 (flat_null)
findings.description: The bold claim 'The loop fits a flat circle' rests on failing to reject a test whose power was never checked (no positive control, P6). The test statistic cannot tell flat loops from clearly non-planar ones. The null uses isotropic Gaussian noise, which is not calibrated to the real data's noise. So failing to reject says nothing, and the hedge 'not proof that the loop is exactly flat' does not address power (P1, P9).
findings.evidence: Planted loops with real noise: I took the scGPT embedding, removed its phase harmonics 1-4 by regression, and added a loop (cos φ, sin φ, b·cos 2φ, b·sin 2φ)·A, scaled so linear circ-R2 = 0.892 (the real value). Out-of-plane angle over 5 seeds each: flat (b=0) 24.2 ± 2.5 deg; non-planar b=1 22.4 ± 2.2; b=2 14.6 ± 1.0. Rejection rate against the stored null p95 (29.2 deg) was 0/5 for both b=1 and b=2. Under the analysis's own isotropic noise model, b=0.5 and b=1 were rejected, but b=2 gave 12.8-13.7 deg, well below the flat-null mean of 25.6, and was not rejected. The statistic therefore falls as non-planarity grows. Matching on linear circ-R2 also lowers the null's noise for strongly non-planar loops. In all three representations the real value sits below the null mean (p = 0.905, 0.762, 0.571; below about 1.0 once F3 is corrected), which shows the null does not match the real noise structure.
findings.recommended_action: Add a positive-control battery: plant non-planar loops of several shapes and strengths into the real residual noise and report detection power. Build the null from the real residual noise rather than isotropic Gaussian noise. Use a statistic that increases with non-planarity, for example the variance of the phase-binned centroid trajectory outside its best-fit 2-plane, compared with a matched null. Until then, restate Conclusion 3 as 'no detectable departure from planarity with a test of unknown or low power', not 'the loop fits a flat circle'.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md line 30 ('In all three representations'); code/cc_common.py lines 63-79 (phase_angle); README.md lines 34-36
findings.description: The expression result is flat by construction. φ is defined as atan2 of PC2/PC1 of z-scored marker-gene expression, so the direction that best reads out φ always lies in that fixed 2-D marker plane. The regression 'tangents' therefore recover the plane that defines the label. More generally, the 'loop' is a parameterization imposed on the data (every cell gets an angle), not a structure the analysis tested. So the planarity of expression, and arguably the 'loop' framing itself, is circular (P3, P5).
findings.evidence: Marker PC1/PC2 can be predicted from the expression 20 whitened PCs with R² = 0.956. The principal angles between the best-fit plane of the expression sector tangents and the label-defining marker plane are 5.3 and 11.6 deg. Mean tangent angle to the marker plane is 19.4 deg, against a reported out-of-plane angle of 17.9. In the marker plane, 14.8% of cells lie within half the median radius, and the radius histogram shows no central gap, so the analysis assumes a ring rather than showing one.
findings.recommended_action: Drop expression from the 'flat circle in all three' claim, or label it explicitly as planar by construction. For the model representations, check whether planarity simply reflects the planar definition of the label: use a label not defined as an angle in a fixed linear plane (for example a pseudotime fitted on non-marker genes, or held-out markers), and check that the data actually form a ring before testing loop geometry.

findings.location: code/cc_geometry.py line 110 (lo, hi = 0.0, 20.0) and lines 111-118; outputs/cc_geometry_expr.json flat_null; SUMMARY.md line 17; README.md lines 54-56
findings.description: For the expression representation (6,546 columns), the binary search on noise never brackets the target: circ-R2 stays above the real 0.929 even at the upper bound of 20, so every expression null draw uses noise of about 20. The expression null therefore has less noise than documented ('noise set by binary search so that its linear circ-R2 matches the real one'). The reported expression null mean, SD and p are wrong.
findings.evidence: Seed 100 search trace: s=10 → 0.991, 15 → 0.977, 17.5 → 0.968, 18.75 → 0.959, ... final s = 20.0, final null circ-R2 = 0.952 vs target 0.929. Re-running with the upper bound raised to 60, the matched noise is s ≈ 23.0 (circ-R2 0.920-0.927), and the null out-of-plane angles for seeds 100-102 are 22.1, 24.4 and 23.2 deg. The stored capped draws are 18.9, 18.3 and 17.7. The real expression value of 17.9 deg falls below all matched draws, so p ≈ 1, not 0.571, and the null is about 23 deg, not 17.9 ± 1.4.
findings.recommended_action: Raise or adapt the upper bound (for example scale it with sqrt(d), or expand it until circ-R2 falls below the target) and assert that the search brackets the target. Recompute the expression null and replace the expression row of the table (null 17.9 ± 1.4, p 0.571). Report the achieved null circ-R2 for each representation.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 24-25 (Conclusion 1: 'kNN does worse in all three representations, so a linear readout is enough'); code/cc_common.py lines 19, 95-101 (DIM=20, whitening); code/cc_geometry.py line 53 (k=15)
findings.description: The finding that kNN beats linear nowhere comes from one hyperparameter setting (20 PCs, each scaled to unit variance, k = 15). Whitening gives the noise components the same weight as the signal components in kNN distances, so kNN gets worse as the number of PCs grows. At lower dimensions kNN matches or beats the linear readout. Even where kNN does worse, that does not show a linear readout is 'enough' (P8).
findings.evidence: Same 2,000 cells, linear vs whitened kNN: at 5 PCs, scGPT 0.490 vs 0.592, Geneformer 0.322 vs 0.366, expression 0.638 vs 0.711 (kNN higher in all three). At 10 PCs, scGPT 0.883 vs 0.854 (unwhitened kNN 0.834), Geneformer 0.581 vs 0.571, expression 0.925 vs 0.894 (unwhitened 0.914). At 50 PCs, Geneformer 0.892 vs 0.590. The gap depends on dimension and whitening rather than on the shape of the representation.
findings.recommended_action: Sweep the number of PCs (for example 5/10/20/50), run kNN both with and without whitening, and tune k by nested CV. Report the worst case. Remove or restrict the claim 'kNN does worse in all three, so a linear readout is enough' to the settings where it holds.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 26-29 (Conclusion 2); README.md line 22; code/cc_common.py lines 63-79
findings.description: Expression's advantage over scGPT comes entirely from the 87 marker genes that define the label. The summary acknowledges a 'built-in advantage' but never runs the obvious fair comparison (expression without the marker genes). So 'Expression does better than both models' and 'they do not add to it' rest on a circular comparator (P2, P3).
findings.evidence: Linear circ-R2 on the shared 2,000 cells: expression with the 87 markers removed scores 0.899 at 20 PCs (full expression 0.935, scGPT 0.896). At 50 PCs scGPT is 0.913 vs 0.896 for expression without markers. Against the non-circular baseline, scGPT ties or slightly exceeds expression; Geneformer stays lower.
findings.recommended_action: Report expression-without-markers (and ideally a held-out marker split) as the trivial baseline, and phrase Conclusion 2 relative to it, for example 'scGPT matches non-marker expression; Geneformer is lower'.

findings.description: The headline circ-R2 values and the differences between representations are single point estimates: no CIs, no bootstrap, and one fixed number of PCs (P8). Geneformer's value in particular depends strongly on the number of PCs, which changes the size of the scGPT-Geneformer gap.
findings.evidence: Geneformer linear circ-R2 is 0.581 at 10 PCs, 0.844 at 20 and 0.892 at 50; the scGPT-Geneformer gap shrinks from 0.052 at 20 PCs to 0.021 at 50. My paired bootstrap at 20 PCs (1,000 resamples) gives expression − scGPT [0.031, 0.050] and scGPT − Geneformer [0.038, 0.066], so the ranking holds, but none of this is reported.
findings.recommended_action: Report bootstrap 95% CIs for each circ-R2 and each paired difference, plus a sweep over the number of PCs with the worst case.

findings.description: All findings come from one cell line (K562, a cancer line), one layer per model (layer 11 of 12 vs 11 of 18, so different relative depths), one noise model for the null and 20 null draws. The conclusions are worded generally ('Phase can be read linearly from both models', 'The loop fits a flat circle') with no held-out condition (P7).
findings.evidence: README data table: one dataset and a single layer per model. The null p-value resolution is 1/21 = 0.048, and the 95th percentile is estimated from 20 draws.
findings.recommended_action: Qualify the conclusions as specific to K562 and layer 11, or add at least one other layer or depth and one other dataset or cell type. Use more null draws (for example 200) for the percentile threshold.

findings.description: The Tirosh marker lists use outdated gene names. Two markers present in the data under their current names are missed (MLF1IP = CENPU, HN1 = JPT1), so the label uses 37/43 S and 50/54 G2M genes instead of 38 and 51. The effect on the label is small, but the reported marker counts reflect a matching error, not real absence.
findings.evidence: Missing S genes include MLF1IP; missing G2M genes include HN1 and FAM64A. 'CENPU' and 'JPT1' are present in the genes of expr_k562.npz.
findings.recommended_action: Map the old names to current HGNC symbols (MLF1IP→CENPU, HN1→JPT1, FAM64A→PIMREG) and recompute the labels, or state the omission.

findings.description: Reproducibility gaps (P10). There is no code that produced the scGPT and Geneformer embeddings (tokenization, binning, layer extraction, pooling) and no pinned package versions. The expression normalization does not match its description: it is said to be log(1 + counts per 10,000) of all 6,546 genes, but the rows do not sum to 10,000 after back-transformation, so normalization used a larger, undocumented gene set.
findings.evidence: expm1(emb) row sums range from 7,447 to 9,573 (median 9,137), not 10,000. README line 26: 'The embeddings were computed once, earlier'. README line 82 lists only 'numpy, scikit-learn' with no versions.
findings.recommended_action: Include the embedding-extraction scripts and the checkpoint identifiers, pin package versions (requirements.txt or environment.yml), and document the normalization accurately (which gene set the totals were computed over).

grade_a.detection_reason: The key marks B4328 as clean (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. One finding (F3) does describe a real implementation bug that the key does not cover. I confirmed it by running the package code. In flat_null, the binary search for expression (d = 6,546) never brackets the target. For seed 100, every step returns null circ-R2 above 0.929, and the noise saturates at s = 19.99996 with circ-R2 of about 0.952. Re-running with the upper bound raised to 60 gives matched s of about 23.0, circ-R2 of 0.920 to 0.926, and null out-of-plane angles of 22.1 and 24.4 deg for seeds 100 and 101. The stored capped draws are 18.9 and 18.3. So the expression null mean (17.9 +- 1.4) and p (0.571) are wrong. The verdict, however, is unchanged (still not rejected, with p near 1).

findings.reason: This is a power and overreach critique of Conclusion 3, and the key lists both as false alarms. It treats the low power from 20 draws as load-bearing and claims the null is mis-calibrated because it uses isotropic noise. The key also says a P9 overreach finding against this summary is a false alarm. SUMMARY.md already calls the result 'a failure to reject with 20 null draws, not proof that the loop is exactly flat'. The point that the best-fit-plane statistic can miss loops dominated by a higher harmonic is a fair design limitation, but it is not an error in the reported results.

Confirmed by running the code. For expression, the binary search in flat_null hits hi = 20: every step from s = 10 to 19.9999 gives circ-R2 above the 0.929 target, and the final value is 0.952. With a wider bracket, the matched noise is about 23 and the null out-of-plane angles are 22.1 and 24.4 deg (seeds 100 and 101), against the stored 18.9 and 18.3. So the expression null mean, SD and p in the table are wrong, which contradicts the README and the key's claim that the noise is matched. The 'not rejected' verdict still holds, because p moves toward 1.

The numbers check out: at 5 PCs on the shared cells, linear vs kNN is 0.490 vs 0.592 for scGPT, 0.322 vs 0.366 for Geneformer and 0.638 vs 0.711 for expression. But both readouts are poor at 5 PCs. The best readout in every case is linear at 20 or more PCs, and the key notes kNN stays below linear at 20 PCs with or without whitening. 'kNN does worse in all three representations' is correct for the stated design, so the conclusion is not overturned. This is a robustness caveat.

The key lists 'treating the use of a marker-defined label as a load-bearing error in itself' as a false alarm: the label is the stated design. Expression being close to the marker plane follows from that design, the summary already notes expression's built-in advantage, and the numbers are correct. Calling the 'loop' framing circular is an interpretive point, not an error.

The numbers check out: expression with the 87 marker genes removed gives a linear circ-R2 of 0.899 on the shared cells, against 0.896 for scGPT. SUMMARY.md already says the label gives expression a built-in advantage and that the models do not add to it. That statement still holds against the marker-free baseline. A useful extra analysis, but not an error.
No CIs are reported, which is true. But the key's own bootstrap and seed checks, and the review's own bootstrap, show the ranking holds. This is a reporting-completeness point.

The limits on generality (one cell line, one layer, 20 draws) are real but are disclosed in the README and SUMMARY. The key lists treating the 20-draw power limit as a load-bearing error as a false alarm. This is a scope caveat.

Confirmed: CENPU and JPT1 are present in genes, while MLF1IP, HN1 and FAM64A/PIMREG are absent. So the old marker names miss 2 available markers. The README already reports '37 of 43' and '50 of 54' found. The label is the defined target and is recomputed exactly. The effect is small.

Confirmed: expm1(emb) row sums range from 7,447 to 9,573 (median 9,137), not 10,000, so the README's normalization description is inaccurate. The missing embedding-extraction code is disclosed, and the key lists this as a false alarm if presented as invalidating the results. This is a documentation and reproducibility point.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key (status 'clean', error null) has no documented error, so error_detected is null. I re-ran package code and confirmed two real problems that the key does not list. (a) F3: for expression (d=6,546) the noise binary search in flat_null never brackets the target. Tracing seed 100: s goes 10 (0.991), 15 (0.977), 17.5 (0.968), ... then sticks at 19.9999 with circ-R2 about 0.952 against the real 0.929. With hi=60 the matched noise is s=23.05 (circ-R2 0.927) and the null out-of-plane angle is 23.0 deg, against the real 17.9. So the stored expression null (17.9 +- 1.4, p 0.571) is under-noised, and the key's statement that the null is matched to each representation's own circ-R2 is false for expression. For scGPT and Geneformer, circ-R2 at s=20 is 0.41 and 0.64, so those two searches do bracket the target. The not-rejected verdict for expression still holds. (b) F1: the out-of-plane statistic does not rise steadily as the loop gets less flat. I planted loops (cos, sin, b cos2, b sin2) in the scGPT width, matched to circ-R2 0.892. With isotropic noise, b=0 gave about 25 deg, b=0.5 gave 33-35, b=1 gave 28-30 and b=2 gave 12-14. With the real residual noise, b=0 to 1 all fell in 21-28 and b=2 gave 13-16. So the test has little or even inverted power against some clearly non-planar loops, which the summary's '20 draws' hedge does not cover. I also confirmed the factual parts of F2, F4, F5, F8 and F9 on the data.

findings.reason: I confirmed this by simulation. The mean out-of-plane statistic falls for strongly non-planar loops: b=2 gives 12-16 deg against about 25 deg for a flat loop, under both isotropic and real residual noise. With real residual noise, b=0.5 and b=1 cannot be told apart from flat. So 'The loop fits a flat circle' rests on a test whose power against plausible non-planar shapes is low or inverted. The summary's hedge only mentions the 20 draws. Some sub-claims are overstated. Failing to reject is not entirely uninformative: under the isotropic model b=0.5 is detected. The 'real value below null mean in all three' argument is weak. For flat loops the isotropic null is roughly consistent with real noise for scGPT.

Confirmed by running the code. For expression the binary search on noise never brackets the target. Trace for seed 100: s converges to the cap of 20, where null circ-R2 is about 0.952 against the target 0.929. With hi=60 the matched s is 23.05, circ-R2 0.927, and the null out-of-plane angle is 23.0 deg. The reported expression null (17.9 +- 1.4) and p=0.571 are therefore wrong; the real 17.9 would sit below the matched null, giving p near 1. This contradicts the key's claim that the noise is matched for every representation. The not-rejected verdict is unchanged. The scGPT and Geneformer searches do bracket the target (circ-R2 at s=20 is 0.41 and 0.64).

All numbers verified: marker PCs predicted from the 20 whitened expression PCs with R2=0.956; principal angles between the tangent plane and the marker plane 5.3 and 11.6 deg; mean tangent angle 19.4 deg; 14.8% of cells within half the median radius. Because phi is the angle in a linear 2-D projection of expression, near-planarity for expression is close to built in. The summary never says this when it claims 'in all three representations'. The key's known facts and listed false alarms don't cover this point. It mainly weakens the expression row; the model results are not shown to be wrong, so it is not load-bearing. The broader 'loop framing is circular' point overlaps the known fact that the phase order is imposed.

The numbers check out: at 5 PCs kNN beats linear in all three (0.490/0.592, 0.322/0.366, 0.638/0.711), and at 10 PCs linear is ahead. So 'kNN does worse' holds for the stated 20-PC design only. Conclusion 1 is not overturned: the best linear readout (0.892/0.844/0.929 at 20 PCs) beats every kNN value the reviewer reports, and the key confirms kNN stays below linear with or without whitening at 20 PCs. This is a robustness caveat, not evidence that the claim is wrong.

Verified: expression without the 87 markers scores 0.899 on the 2,000 shared cells, against scGPT 0.896. That is a useful extra baseline. But the summary already says expression has a built-in advantage because the label is built from marker expression, and 'the models do not add to it' still holds against non-marker expression. Per the key, the baseline is not played down.

It is true that no CIs are given and that Geneformer's value depends on the number of PCs (0.581 at 10 PCs). The key and the reviewer's own bootstrap both show the ranking is robust (expression minus scGPT 95% CI 0.031-0.050). This is a reporting nicety.

A generic caveat: one cell line, one layer, 20 draws. The summary is scoped to K562 and layer 11, and the p-floor of 0.048 is stated in the code and README. The key lists low power from 20 draws as a non-load-bearing, stated limitation.

Verified that MLF1IP, FAM64A and HN1 are missing while their current names CENPU and JPT1 are present (PIMREG is absent). Only two markers are lost to old names; the label is otherwise as documented and recomputes exactly. The problem is real but trivial.

Verified: expm1 row sums are 7,447-9,573 (median 9,137), not 10,000, so the README's normalization description is inaccurate. Package versions are not pinned. The missing embedding code is already stated in the README, and the key says fixed embeddings are not an error. This is a documentation and reproducibility point only.

grade_c.detection_reason: The key marks B4328 as clean (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. I checked every finding against the package by running code. F3 (the expression null's noise search never brackets the target) and F1 (the out-of-plane statistic is not monotonic in non-planarity) are real problems not in the key. F2 is a real but non-load-bearing interpretive point. F4 is a false alarm. The rest are minor.

findings.reason: Confirmed with the package's own isotropic flat_null construction at scGPT width (d=512, matched to linear circ-R2 0.892, seeds 100-102). Planted loop (cos, sin, b·cos2φ, b·sin2φ)·A gave out-of-plane angles of b=0: 23.5/26.7/25.1; b=0.5: 30.4/33.4/33.3; b=1: 35.0/32.3/28.7; b=2: 14.2/14.0/12.2 deg. A strongly non-planar loop therefore scores well below a flat one (geometrically about atan(1/4)), so the statistic is not monotonic and fails to see some non-planarity. This is a limitation of the statistic itself, not the '20 draws' power limit that the key treats as non-load-bearing, and the summary's hedge covers only the 20 draws. Together with F3, the claim that the null is calibrated is also weaker than the key states. I did not verify the real-noise positive-control numbers. The reported non-rejection is computed correctly, but the bold 'The loop fits a flat circle' is overstated.

Confirmed by tracing flat_null for expression (d=6546), seed 100. Every bisection step ends with circ-R2 above the target 0.929 (s=10→0.991, 15→0.977, 17.5→0.968, ..., final s≈19.99996 with circ-R2 about 0.952), so the search never brackets and every expression null draw uses noise at the cap of 20. With hi=60 the matched s is 23.05 (circ-R2 0.920) and the null out-of-plane angle is 22.1 deg, against the stored 18.88 and the real 17.9. The reported expression null (17.9 ± 1.4) and p = 0.571 are therefore wrong, and the README's claim that the noise is matched is false for expression. This contradicts the key's 'null is matched' fact and its possible-false-alarm entry. Non-rejection still holds (p becomes about 1), so the conclusion's direction survives, but headline table numbers are wrong.

The numbers reproduce. Marker PC1/PC2 can be predicted from the expression 20 whitened PCs with R² 0.956. The principal angles between the expression tangent plane and the marker plane are 5.3 and 11.6 deg, and the mean tangent angle to the marker plane is 19.4 deg. 14.8% of cells lie within half the median radius. Mathematically, the gradient of atan2(p2, p1) lies in span(∇p1, ∇p2), so expression's planarity is largely built in. The summary does not say this, though the key notes that the label and its order are imposed. The finding makes the expression part of Conclusion 3 uninformative rather than wrong, so it is not load-bearing.

The 5-PC and 10-PC numbers reproduce exactly (5 PCs: scGPT 0.49 vs 0.592, Geneformer 0.322 vs 0.366, expression 0.638 vs 0.711; 10 PCs: 0.883 vs 0.854, 0.581 vs 0.571, 0.925 vs 0.894). However, linear beats kNN in all three at 10, 20 and 50 PCs, and per the key also with unwhitened PCs at 20. kNN wins only at 5 PCs, where neither readout recovers the phase. The claim that Conclusion 1 is an artifact of whitening or dimension is not supported, and the key lists kNN-related objections as false alarms.

Verified: with the 87 markers removed, expression scores 0.899 at 20 PCs and 0.896 at 50, against scGPT 0.896 on the shared cells. The summary already says expression has a built-in advantage because the label comes from marker expression, and 'models do not add to it' stays consistent. The finding is a useful extra baseline, but the key treats the marker-defined label as the stated design.

There are no CIs and only one PC setting. The reviewer's own bootstrap matches the key (expression − scGPT 0.031-0.050) and the ranking holds. The key confirms the gap is not noise. This is a reporting improvement, not an error.
Generalization limits (one cell line, one layer, 20 draws) are true, but the README and summary state K562 and layer 11, and the key treats the 20-draw power limit as stated and non-load-bearing.

Verified: MLF1IP, HN1 and FAM64A are missing, while CENPU and JPT1 are present in expr genes (PIMREG is absent). Two markers are missed because of outdated names. This is true but has minimal effect on the label, and the README reports the counts accurately.

Verified: expm1(emb) row sums range from 7,447 to 9,573 (median 9,137), not 10,000, so the README's normalization description is inaccurate. Embedding-extraction code is absent, as the README states, and versions are not pinned. These are documentation and reproducibility nits that do not affect the results.

review.summary:
I reran the code with the package interpreter. My inline checks wrote nothing to the folder. All stored numbers reproduce exactly: circ-R2, turning statistics, the p-values, the phase labels (phase_check) and the shared-cell table. The decodability numbers barely move across CV seeds (+-0.003), and shuffled labels give a circ-R2 of about -0.03, so circ-R2 is properly anchored to chance.

The headline geometric claim, SUMMARY Conclusion 3 ("The loop fits a flat circle"), cannot stand.
- The method does not measure where the cells' loop goes. Its "loop tangents" are within-sector ridge decoding directions.
- When I measure the loop directly, using the 12 sector centroids of the cells, it is clearly non-planar in all three representations. Planarity is 0.70 (scGPT), 0.77 (Geneformer) and 0.70 (expression), against 0.91-0.95 under the analysis's own flat-circle null. The out-of-plane structure replicates across random half-splits of the cells; in the null it does not.
- The tangent test is also underpowered. A planted non-planar loop with a 27-degree out-of-plane tangent was never detected (0 of 3).
- The verdict depends on the number of sectors. With 8 sectors, the real scGPT angle exceeds every null draw.
- The expression null is not noise-matched as the README says. The noise search hits its upper bound of 20, and the null's circ-R2 is still 0.951 against a target of 0.929.

The decodability claims (Conclusions 1-2) hold in direction but are fragile.
- The gaps between expression and the models depend strongly on the fixed 20-component reduction. On the shared 2,000 cells the scGPT gap shrinks from 0.039 to 0.001 at 200 components, and the Geneformer gap from 0.091 to 0.018. Geneformer's 0.844 is largely an artefact of that bottleneck.
- Expression without the 87 label-defining marker genes scores 0.895, the same as scGPT's 0.892.
- scGPT's 1,200-gene input window covers only about 48% of the expressed marker-gene entries.
- So "the models do not add to it" cannot be tested with this label.
- "kNN worse, so a linear readout is enough" reverses at 5 components and depends on the whitening step.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1 (null anchoring): circ-R2 is clean. The flat null is present and unaddressed (miscalibrated, and unmatched for expression).
- P2 (trivial baseline): expression is used as the baseline; the marker circularity is present but acknowledged.
- P3 (endpoint vs object): present and unaddressed. The tangent metric measures decoding directions, not the loop's geometry, and the label is built from expression.
- P4 (unit of inference): clean for a single cell line.
- P5 (selection / input window): present and unaddressed (scGPT's 1,200-gene window).
- P6 (positive control): present and unaddressed. None was run, and my own control shows low power.
- P7 (generalization): one cell line and one layer per model; a minor scope issue.
- P8 (stability): present and unaddressed. Number of components and number of sectors were not swept, and the verdict changes with them.
- P9 (language): Conclusion 3's heading asserts the null result; Conclusion 4 is well hedged.
- P10 (reproducibility): runtime is documented, but package versions are not pinned and the embedding and cell-selection code is missing.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:30-32 (Conclusion 3) and results table lines 13-17; code/cc_geometry.py:61-78 (loop_tangents), 81-98 (turning_stats); README.md:48
findings.description: The claim "The loop fits a flat circle" in all three representations is contradicted when the loop is measured directly. The test never measures where the cells' loop goes. Its 'tangent' in each sector is the ridge-regression coefficient of phase offset on the 20 whitened components. That is a decoding (backward) direction, not the tangent of the loop the cells trace (E[X | phase]). The loop itself, built from the centroids of the cells in each of the 12 phase sectors in the same 20-component whitened space, leaves its best-fit 2-plane far more than the analysis's own flat-circle null allows.
findings.evidence:
Sector-centroid loop, analysis's own prep and the 12 sectors.

Share of the loop's energy in its best 2-plane, real vs flat null (flat_null, seeds 100-109, 10 draws):
- scGPT: 0.703 vs mean 0.953, min 0.942.
- Geneformer: 0.774 vs mean 0.930, min 0.914.
- Expression: 0.695; null centroid planarity is about 0.93-0.95 in the other two.

Absolute squared singular values of the centroid loop:
- scGPT: real [9.67, 7.21, 3.82, 2.17] vs null [9.88, 7.82, 0.40, 0.20].
- Geneformer: real [8.75, 6.08, 2.56, 0.64] vs null [9.01, 7.57, 0.64, 0.32].
- Expression: real [10.37, 7.59, 4.05, 2.32].
The in-plane loop is the same size as in the null, but there are 2-4 extra dimensions of real, non-noise variation.

Random half-splits of the cells: the out-of-plane residuals correlate r = 0.78 (scGPT), 0.40 (Geneformer) and 0.77 (expression), vs about 0.0 in the null. So the non-planarity is reproducible structure, not centroid noise. A linear map such as the whitening keeps a planar curve planar, so this non-planarity is not created by the whitening.
findings.recommended_action: Withdraw or reverse Conclusion 3. Measure the loop geometry directly, e.g. sector centroids or a principal curve of E[X | phase], and compare it with the flat-circle null, reporting null mean +- SD. If the decoding-direction statistic is kept, describe it as the planarity of the phase-decoding gradient, not of the loop. Rename the claim to match what is measured.

findings.description: A null finding ("not rejected" in all three representations) is reported without a positive control, and the test turns out to have little power. The verdict also depends on the arbitrary choice of 12 sectors. The real out-of-plane angle lies below the null mean in all three representations. This suggests the isotropic-noise null is not calibrated to the real data's noise structure, which makes the test conservative.
findings.evidence:
Positive control: a planted non-planar loop (cos, sin, a*cos2phi, a*sin2phi) with 512 dimensions, noise matched to linear circ-R2 0.89, and the real scGPT phi. Flat-null 95th percentile = 29.3 deg (10 draws).
- a = 0.25 (true tangent out-of-plane angle 26.6 deg): measured 28.5, 27.5, 24.0 deg; 0 of 3 detected.
- a = 0.5 (45 deg): 3 of 3 detected.

Sensitivity sweep for scGPT, 6 null draws each:
- 8 sectors: real 15.8 vs null 13.7 +- 0.7, max 15.0; the real value exceeds every null draw (p = 1/7, the minimum possible).
- 16 sectors: real 32.5 vs null 35.7 +- 1.2; p = 1.0.
- 50 components: real 35.7 vs null 34.4 +- 1.4; p = 0.29.
- 10 components: p = 0.86.

At the defaults the real angle lies below the null mean: 22.7 vs 25.6, 34.2 vs 35.7, 17.9 vs 17.9.
findings.recommended_action: Add a planted-ground-truth positive control at each representation's real signal-to-noise and report the smallest out-of-plane deviation the test can detect. Sweep the number of sectors (e.g. 8/12/16) and components (10/20/50) with 20 or more null draws each, and report the worst case. Calibrate the null to the real residual covariance rather than isotropic noise. State the result as "no detectable deviation above the detection limit X", not as a fit.

findings.description: The size of the gaps between expression and the two models depends strongly on the fixed reduction to 20 principal components. No sweep was run. Geneformer's 0.844 and the gaps of 0.04 and 0.09 on the same 2,000 cells are artefacts of the 20-component bottleneck. With more components the models nearly catch up, while expression peaks at 20.
findings.evidence:
Linear circ-R2 on the shared 2,000 cells (Geneformer label), as scGPT / Geneformer / expression:
- 10 components: 0.883 / 0.581 / 0.925
- 20 components: 0.896 / 0.844 / 0.935
- 50 components: 0.913 / 0.892 / 0.932
- 100 components: 0.916 / 0.895 / 0.928
- 200 components: 0.919 / 0.902 / 0.920

The expression - scGPT gap goes from 0.039 to 0.001, and expression - Geneformer from 0.091 to 0.018. On its own 2,000 cells, Geneformer is 0.322 at 5 components, 0.581 at 10, 0.844 at 20 and 0.892 at 50.

CV-seed variability at a fixed number of components is only +-0.003, so the instability comes from the hyperparameter, not from sampling.
findings.recommended_action: Report decodability over a sweep of the number of components (or without PCA, using ridge with a CV-tuned alpha), giving each representation's best value and worst-case gap. Restate Conclusion 2 with these ranges. In particular, Geneformer's decodability should not be quoted as 0.844 without stating that it is limited by the 20-component setting.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:27-29 ("The models keep the phase signal; they do not add to it"); README.md:20 (scGPT input top 1,200 genes); code/cc_common.py:54-91 (label from expression)
findings.description: "They do not add to it" cannot be tested with this design. The target is defined from the same expression matrix used as the baseline, so a model that carried extra or cleaner phase information would be penalised, not rewarded. Expression's whole advantage comes from the 87 marker genes that define the label. scGPT's input is also truncated to each cell's top 1,200 genes, which removes about half of the marker-gene expression the label is built from. The deficit therefore may reflect input truncation rather than what the model learned.
findings.evidence:
Expression with the 87 marker genes removed: linear circ-R2 = 0.895 at 20 components, essentially equal to scGPT's 0.892 (expression with all genes: 0.929).

Of the nonzero marker-gene entries per cell (mean 48.5 of 87), only 48% fall inside the cell's top-1,200 expression window that scGPT receives. Cells express a median of 3,078 genes. Ties at low counts make this approximate.
findings.recommended_action: Remove or soften "they do not add to it". Report the marker-free expression baseline alongside the models. State that scGPT never sees about half of the label-defining marker expression. To test whether models add information, use a phase target that does not come from the same expression, e.g. FUCCI, held-out markers, or a label built from genes excluded from all inputs.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:23-25 (Conclusion 1: "kNN does worse in all three representations, so a linear readout is enough"); code/cc_geometry.py:53 (k = 15), code/cc_common.py:95-101 (whitening)
findings.description: That kNN does worse than linear is specific to one setting: 20 whitened components with k = 15. With fewer components it reverses, and without whitening kNN does better. The inference also does not follow: a weaker kNN with fixed k does not show that a linear readout captures all the decodable phase information.
findings.evidence:
- 5 components, whitened: kNN beats linear for scGPT (0.588 vs 0.486) and Geneformer (0.366 vs 0.322).
- 20 components: scGPT kNN is 0.807 whitened vs 0.836 unwhitened (linear 0.892).
- 50 components: scGPT kNN is 0.792 whitened vs 0.839 unwhitened.
- Changing k from 15 to 50 shifts kNN by up to 0.08.
findings.recommended_action: Report the linear and kNN comparison across numbers of components, whitened vs unwhitened, and several values of k. Rephrase as "at 20 whitened components, a linear readout outperforms kNN (k = 15)" rather than "a linear readout is enough".

findings.location: code/cc_geometry.py:110-118 (binary search bounds lo, hi = 0, 20); README.md:54-56; SUMMARY.md:17 (expression row)
findings.description: For expression (6,546 dimensions), the flat-circle null is not matched to the real linear circ-R2, contrary to the README. The noise binary search hits its upper bound of 20 and the null stays cleaner than the real data. So the reported expression null (17.9 +- 1.4) and p = 0.571 come from a mis-specified null. The not-rejected decision would likely not change, since a properly matched, noisier null would give larger out-of-plane angles.
findings.evidence: Seed 100, d = 6546: noise s = 10 gives null circ-R2 0.991; s = 19.99 (the bound) gives 0.951. The target is the real value of 0.929. Signal scale per plane axis is about sqrt(d/2), roughly 57, so the noise needed is above 20. scGPT and Geneformer nulls match within about 0.01 (0.883 vs 0.892; 0.853 vs 0.844).
findings.recommended_action: Scale the search bound with sqrt(d), or normalise the signal per plane axis rather than per entry. Check and report each null's achieved circ-R2 against the target, then rerun the expression null.

findings.description: Single condition: one cell line (K562 control cells), one layer per model (layer 11, chosen without justification), and one cell-selection and CV seed. Conclusions are worded as properties of "both models" in general.
findings.evidence: Only layer 11 of scGPT (12 layers) and of Geneformer (18 layers) was analysed. The summary has no sweep over layers, datasets or cell types.
findings.recommended_action: Scope the claims explicitly to K562 and layer 11, or add a layer sweep and at least one held-out cell type or dataset.

findings.description: Reproducibility gaps. Package versions are not pinned (only "numpy, scikit-learn"). The code that computes the embeddings and selects the 3,000 control cells and the 2,000-cell Geneformer subset is not included, and model checkpoints and source-file versions are not identified precisely enough to regenerate the inputs.
findings.evidence: The README says the embeddings "were computed once, earlier" and that the model weights are not in the package. There is no requirements or environment file, and no description of how the 2,000-cell subset was chosen. Its phase mix (25/40/35%) and genes-per-cell (3,116 vs 3,133) match the full set, which suggests the subset is representative.
findings.recommended_action: Add pinned package versions, the embedding-extraction and cell-selection scripts, and checkpoint identifiers or hashes.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. I re-ran checks on the package data. They confirm two genuine problems that the key does not list. F1 (load-bearing): the sector-centroid loop is clearly non-planar compared with the flat-circle null. F6 (minor): the expression null's noise search hits its upper bound, so that null is not matched to the real circ-R2.

findings.reason: I confirmed this by re-running on the package with the same prep and 12 sectors. Planarity of the sector-centroid loop: scGPT real 0.703 vs flat_null seeds 100-105 0.942-0.963 (mean 0.953); Geneformer real 0.774 vs 0.914-0.936 (mean 0.928); expression real 0.695. Squared singular values: scGPT real [9.67, 7.21, 3.82, 2.16] vs null mean [10.11, 7.91, 0.31, 0.20]. In random half-splits the out-of-plane residuals correlate 0.73-0.82 (scGPT), 0.36-0.58 (Geneformer) and 0.74-0.81 (expression), vs about 0 in the null. So the loop the cells trace, E[X|phi], reproducibly leaves its 2-plane far more than a flat circle does. The package's statistic uses within-sector ridge coefficients, which are decoding directions, not the loop's tangent. It therefore misses this, and Conclusion 3 ('the loop does not leave its best-fit 2-plane more than a flat circle does') is contradicted by a direct measurement. The key does not cover this. It is not one of its false alarms: the finding does not say the code is wrong, it says the statistic does not measure what the claim names.

Low power is already stated as a limitation: the summary calls the result 'a failure to reject with 20 null draws, not proof', and the README gives the p floor. The key lists '20 draws give low power' as a load-bearing claim and 'null mis-calibrated' among its false alarms. The 8-sector result (p = 1/7 with 6 draws) is not a rejection, and the other settings do not reject either. The positive-control idea is reasonable, but the finding does not show that any headline number is wrong. The confirmed non-planarity belongs to F1.

Confirmed. Shared-cell linear circ-R2, scGPT / Geneformer / expression: 10 PCs 0.883 / 0.581 / 0.925; 20 PCs 0.896 / 0.844 / 0.935; 50 PCs 0.913 / 0.892 / 0.932; 100 PCs 0.916 / 0.895 / 0.928; 200 PCs 0.919 / 0.902 / 0.920. The expression - scGPT gap shrinks from 0.040 to 0.001, and Geneformer's 0.844 is held down by the 20-PC limit. However, expression still matches or beats both models at every setting, and the reported numbers are correct for the stated design. So the direction of Conclusion 2 survives; only the size of the gap depends on the setting. This is a genuine robustness problem, not a refutation.

The numbers check out: marker-free expression gives 0.895; about 47% of a cell's nonzero marker entries fall inside its top-1,200 genes; median 3,078 genes per cell. But the summary already says expression has a built-in advantage because the label comes from marker expression. The key treats this framing, including 'they do not add to it', as correct, and lists treating the marker-defined label as a load-bearing error among its false alarms. Whether models could add phase information that this label cannot reward is a fair point about wording and scope. It does not show that a stated result is wrong.

True. At 5 PCs kNN beats linear: on the shared cells scGPT 0.592 vs 0.490 and Geneformer 0.366 vs 0.322. At the stated 20-PC design kNN is below linear in all three representations, whitened or not, as the key says. The finding does not claim a bug. 'So a linear readout is enough' is a mild overstatement of wording.

Confirmed by tracing flat_null for expression, seed 100. Every binary-search step gives circ-R2 above the target 0.929, so s converges to the bound of 20 (final s = 19.99996), and the null's achieved circ-R2 is 0.952 vs the real 0.929 (s = 30 would give 0.818). So the expression null is not matched as the README, and the key's known true fact, describe it. This is a real but minor problem. A properly matched, noisier null would probably give larger null angles, so the not-rejected decision would not change.
A scope limitation: one cell line, one layer, one seed. True, but it does not make any reported result wrong, and the summary describes the setup (K562, layer 11).

Reproducibility nits: unpinned package versions, and no embedding-extraction or cell-selection code. The README says the embeddings are given and not recomputed. The key lists 'results invalid because the embeddings cannot be regenerated' as a false alarm, and this finding does not claim that. The package's outputs reproduce.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key marks B4328 as clean (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule says a load-bearing finding is a false alarm unless the verifier confirms it by running code. I ran checks with the package interpreter, and several findings held up as real problems outside the key. F1: the sector-centroid loop is clearly non-planar compared with the flat null, and the half-split check shows the structure is reproducible. F6: in the expression null, the noise binary search hits its upper bound, so the null does not reach the real circ-R2. F3: the gaps between expression and the models shrink as the number of PCs grows. F2: the positive control shows the test has low power.

findings.reason: Reproduced with package code, using the 12 sector centroids in the 20 whitened PCs. Share of energy in the best 2-plane: scGPT real 0.703 vs null 0.94-0.96 (seeds 100-103); Geneformer real 0.774 vs null 0.91-0.93. Squared singular values: scGPT real [9.67, 7.21, 3.82, 2.16] vs null about [9.9, 7.8, 0.4, 0.2]. Half-split correlation of the out-of-plane residuals: real 0.71-0.77 (scGPT) and 0.29-0.42 (Geneformer), vs about 0 in the null. So the loop the cells trace leaves its 2-plane far more than a flat circle does. The tangent statistic is a per-sector ridge decoding coefficient, as the README describes, and it misses this. That undermines the wording of Conclusion 3 ('The loop fits a flat circle'). The key's facts cover only the tangent-based test and its p values, which are correct as computed. They do not address this construct-validity issue.

Confirmed on the shared 2,000 cells. Linear circ-R2 (scGPT / Geneformer / expression): 10 PCs 0.883/0.581/0.925; 20 PCs 0.896/0.844/0.935; 50 PCs 0.913/0.892/0.932; 200 PCs 0.919/0.902/0.920. The expression-minus-scGPT gap falls from 0.039 to 0.001, and Geneformer's deficit at 20 PCs is largely due to the PC setting. The ranking never reverses, but the size of the Conclusion 2 gaps, and expression beating scGPT at all, depend on the 20-PC choice. The key's robustness checks vary only the KFold seed and use a bootstrap, not the number of PCs.

Confirmed by tracing flat_null for expression with seed 100. The binary search ends at s = 19.99996, the upper bound of 20, and gives a null circ-R2 of 0.952 against the target 0.929. Geneformer (0.853 vs 0.844) and scGPT (0.883 vs 0.892) are matched. So the README's claim that the null is matched (also in the key's facts) fails for expression. The not-rejected verdict is unlikely to change, because a noisier null would give larger out-of-plane angles.

I reproduced the positive control: a planted cos2phi component with a = 0.25 (26.6 deg true out-of-plane angle) at scGPT's SNR gave 25.7 and 28.6 deg, below the null 95th percentile of 29.2, so it was not detected. With a = 0.5 it gave 35.9 and 37.2, which was detected. So the statistic has limited power beyond the acknowledged 20-draw floor. SUMMARY.md already says this is a failure to reject and not proof of flatness, so the result is not overturned. The finding's suggestion that the isotropic null is miscalibrated or conservative is speculative and matches one of the key's listed false alarms. The 8-sector p of 1/7 is not significant.

The marker-free expression baseline reproduces: 0.895 vs 0.929 with markers, about equal to scGPT's 0.892. My top-1,200 marker coverage came out at about 63% with ties included, not 48%, though ties make this approximate. But SUMMARY.md already says expression has a built-in advantage because the label comes from marker expression, and the key lists 'they do not add to it' as appropriate correlational wording. This is a wording and interpretation point, not an error.

Confirmed that at 5 whitened PCs kNN beats linear: scGPT 0.588 vs 0.486, Geneformer 0.366 vs 0.322. At the stated 20-PC design, kNN is below linear in every representation, whitened or not (key fact). 'So a linear readout is enough' is a slightly loose inference, which makes this a scope and wording issue.
True that one cell line and one layer were used, and SUMMARY.md states K562 and layer 11. This is a scope caveat, not an error.

True that package versions are not pinned and the extraction and selection scripts are absent. The README says the embeddings are fixed inputs, and the key says that is acceptable. This is a reproducibility nicety.

review.summary: I reviewed the analysis against all ten checklist patterns. I re-ran its key pieces inline: one stored null draw per model reproduces exactly (seed 100: 24.749, 34.52, 18.879 deg), and so do the real out-of-plane angles. The decodability numbers are stable across CV seeds (scGPT 0.892-0.893, expr 0.929-0.931). Two findings are critical, and both concern headline conclusion 3, "The loop fits a flat circle." (a) A direct measure contradicts it. In all three representations, 23-31% of the energy of the loop of 12 sector means lies outside its best-fit 2-plane, against 4-9% in the analysis's own flat-circle null draws. This holds for 8, 12 and 16 sectors and after regressing out genes detected. (b) The tangent-based test has no demonstrated power and is not monotone in true non-flatness. A planted, strongly non-flat loop (second harmonic, amplitude 1.0) gets p=0.73 and is not rejected. Major findings: (1) for expression, the flat null is not noise-matched, because the binary search hits its upper bound (null circ-R2 0.95-0.96 vs 0.929). (2) The "expression beats both models" result comes entirely from the marker genes that define the label: without those 87 genes, expression scores 0.895, level with scGPT at 0.892. (3) The decodability numbers, especially Geneformer's, depend strongly on the fixed 20-PC truncation. Minor findings: an unfair kNN comparison, the marker-proxy label and a depth correlation, a rejection rule that disagrees with the reported p, a single dataset/layer/seed, and gaps in reproducibility and documentation. Checklist verdicts: P1, partly clean (circ-R2 is anchored to 0, and a shuffled label gives about -0.03), but the flat null is weak and miscalibrated for expression. P2, present: expression is the baseline but is contaminated by the label genes. P3, minor (the label is a marker proxy). P4, clean (one cell line, unit = cells; PCA is fit before CV, which is negligible). P5, present (label-gene leakage into the expression comparator; depth not residualized). P6, present and unaddressed (critical). P7, present (minor). P8, present (PC dimension, kNN preprocessing, no CIs). P9, present: "fits a flat circle" and "do not add to it" overclaim, though conclusion 4 is properly hedged. P10, minor gaps.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 30-32 (Conclusion 3); code/cc_geometry.py lines 61-98 (loop_tangents, turning_stats); README.md lines 10-11, 48-57
findings.description: The headline answer to Question 2 ('The loop fits a flat circle' in all three representations) is contradicted by a direct measure of the loop. The test statistic used is the mean out-of-plane angle of ridge-regression gradient directions estimated within 12 phase sectors, and it mostly reflects estimation noise. The curve the cells actually trace is the conditional mean of the representation as phase varies, and that curve clearly leaves its best-fit 2-plane, much more than the analysis's own flat-circle null allows.
findings.evidence: I took the 12 sector means of the 20 whitened PCs (prep), centred them, and computed the share of SVD energy outside the top-2 plane. Real data: scGPT 0.297, Geneformer 0.226, expr 0.305. flat_null draws (seeds 100-104, same calibration as the pipeline): scGPT 0.037-0.058, Geneformer 0.064-0.086, expr 0.040-0.042. With 8/12/16 sectors the results are scGPT 0.244/0.297/0.310 vs null max 0.028/0.058/0.076, and expr 0.268/0.305/0.334 vs null max 0.025/0.042/0.059. The excess survives regressing out genes detected per cell (scGPT 0.311, Geneformer 0.233, expr 0.325). A harmonic fit agrees: in scGPT, adding cos/sin(2*phi) adds singular values 880 and 198 beyond the first-harmonic plane, against about 25 and 20 in the null. For a truly flat loop, sector means stay in the plane, as the null confirms.
findings.recommended_action: Withdraw or reverse Conclusion 3. Test flatness on the conditional-mean loop (sector means or a harmonic fit) against the flat null, and report the off-plane share with its null mean, SD and p. Restate the answer to Q2 as 'the loop leaves a single 2-plane (off-plane share about 0.23-0.31 vs null at most 0.09)'. Then characterise where the extra dimension comes from.

findings.location: code/cc_geometry.py lines 81-98 and 102-118 (turning_stats out_of_plane_deg, flat_null); SUMMARY.md lines 30-32; README.md lines 54-57
findings.description: There is no positive control, and the out-of-plane test has no demonstrated power. Its response to real non-flatness is not even monotone, so the three non-rejections (p 0.905, 0.762, 0.571) carry no information about flatness. The null also matches only linear circ-R2, using isotropic Gaussian noise, which is a weak null family for anisotropic embedding noise.
findings.evidence: Positive control in the scGPT setting (d=512, the real phi, noise s=9). I planted the loop (cos phi, sin phi, a*cos 2phi, a*sin 2phi)@A and ran the pipeline's own procedure: circ_r2, loop_tangents, turning_stats, then flat_null calibrated to the planted representation's linear circ-R2. At a=0.5: oop 38.1 vs null 28.9+-2.6 over 10 draws, p=0.091. At a=1.0, which is far more non-flat (sector-mean off-plane share about 0.47): oop 33.3 vs null 36.4+-2.9, p=0.727, NOT rejected. Without null recalibration, a=1.5 gives an oop of about 21-25 deg, the same as the flat-circle null for scGPT (25.6+-2.3).
findings.recommended_action: Add a planted-ground-truth positive-control battery: several non-flatness amplitudes, run through the same calibration and the same 20-draw null, with power reported for each. Use a statistic that rises monotonically with non-flatness, such as the sector-mean off-plane share. Do not present non-rejection as support for flatness until the test detects planted non-flat loops of realistic size.

findings.location: code/cc_geometry.py line 110 (lo, hi = 0.0, 20.0) and lines 111-118; README.md lines 54-56; outputs/cc_geometry_expr.json
findings.description: For the expression representation (d=6,546), the binary search for the null's noise level hits its upper bound of 20. The null is therefore less noisy than the real data, and its linear circ-R2 does not match, contrary to the README's description of the null as matched. The achieved null circ-R2 is never checked or saved.
findings.evidence: I replicated flat_null(seed 100) for expr. Every bisection step stays above the target (s=10: 0.991, 15: 0.977, 17.5: 0.968, 18.75: 0.959, 19.375: 0.958, 19.69: 0.954). The final s is 19.84 and gives null linear circ-R2 0.956 against the real 0.929. Seeds 100 and 101 give 0.952 and 0.953. For scGPT and Geneformer, the achieved null circ-R2 lands within about 0.01 of target (0.883-0.895 vs 0.892; 0.836-0.861 vs 0.844).
findings.recommended_action: Scale the search bound with sqrt(d), or search on the SNR in the signal plane. After calibration, assert that the null's circ-R2 is within a tolerance of the target, store the achieved value per draw, and re-run the expr null.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 26-29 (Conclusion 2) and line 19; data/expr_k562.npz; code/cc_common.py lines 54-79
findings.description: 'Expression does better than both models' and 'the models ... do not add to it' come from target leakage. The phase label is atan2 of a linear projection of the 87 marker genes, and those genes are columns of the expression representation. Once they are removed, expression is no better than scGPT. The summary mentions the 'built-in advantage' but never quantifies it, and still states the comparison as a conclusion. Whether the models 'add' anything cannot be tested in this design, because the target is defined from expression.
findings.evidence: Inline, using the same prep and circ_r2: expression without the 87 marker genes gives linear circ-R2 0.895 and kNN 0.833. Expression with the markers gives 0.929 / 0.858. scGPT gives 0.892 / 0.807. The 87 marker genes alone give a linear circ-R2 of 0.965.
findings.recommended_action: Use expression with the label-defining marker genes removed as the trivial baseline. Report the deltas (scGPT about -0.003, Geneformer lower) and restate Conclusion 2: on non-marker genes, expression and scGPT decode the marker-defined phase about equally. Drop 'they do not add to it', or rephrase it as untestable against a target built from expression.

findings.location: code/cc_common.py line 19 (DIM = 20) and lines 95-101 (prep); SUMMARY.md lines 15-19 and 23-25
findings.description: The reported decodability numbers depend heavily on the single, unswept choice of 20 whitened PCs, most of all for Geneformer. No confidence intervals or sensitivity range are given. The Geneformer value and the scGPT-Geneformer gap are artefacts of the truncation point.
findings.evidence: Linear circ-R2 at 5/10/20/50 whitened PCs: Geneformer 0.322/0.581/0.844/0.892; scGPT 0.486/0.877/0.892/0.911; expr 0.641/0.921/0.929/0.929. The scGPT-Geneformer gap shrinks from 0.048 at 20 PCs to 0.019 at 50. CV-seed variation is negligible (scGPT 0.8916-0.8929 over 5 seeds), so the PC dimension is the main source of instability.
findings.recommended_action: Report decodability over a sweep of PC dimensions (e.g. 10/20/50/all), or tune the dimension inside nested CV. Add bootstrap 95% CIs, and paired CIs for the model-vs-model and model-vs-expression differences on the shared 2,000 cells. State the worst case in the summary.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 24-25 (Conclusion 1, 'kNN does worse ... so a linear readout is enough'); code/cc_geometry.py lines 48-57
findings.description: The inference that a linear readout is enough rests on one kNN setting (k=15) applied in whitened PC space. Whitening gives the roughly 18 non-phase dimensions the same weight as the phase plane, which handicaps kNN. A single handicapped nonlinear readout doing worse does not show that the representation is linearly organised or that linear is enough.
findings.evidence: kNN (k=15) on the unwhitened top-20 PCs: scGPT 0.836 (vs 0.807 whitened), expr 0.912 (vs 0.858), Geneformer 0.596 (vs 0.663). k=50 whitened gives scGPT 0.793 and expr 0.854. Linear still leads, but the reported gaps (-0.085, -0.071) depend on the preprocessing.
findings.recommended_action: Sweep k and the preprocessing (whitened vs unwhitened, PC dimension) for kNN, or use a stronger nonlinear readout (e.g. a small MLP or kernel ridge). Restate the claim as 'linear readout matches or beats kNN under these settings'.

findings.location: code/cc_geometry.py lines 166-168; README.md lines 56-57; SUMMARY.md table p column
findings.description: The rejection rule (real value above np.percentile(null, 95), with interpolation) is not equivalent to the reported p = (#null >= real + 1)/21. The flat circle can be declared rejected while the reported p is about 0.09. With 20 draws, p also has very coarse resolution (minimum 0.048).
findings.evidence: In my positive-control run (10 null draws, planted a=0.5), the code's rule returned rejected=True while p=0.091. With 20 draws, a real value that beats only 19 of 20 nulls gives p=2/21=0.095 but can still exceed the interpolated 95th percentile.
findings.recommended_action: Base the decision on p <= 0.05, or on a non-interpolated order statistic. Use more null draws (e.g. 200 or more) so that p is resolved.

findings.location: code/cc_common.py lines 4-12 and 63-79; SUMMARY.md lines 5-6 and 23-29
findings.description: The endpoint is a marker-derived proxy angle (atan2 of the top two PCs of the Tirosh marker z-scores), not an independent measurement of cell-cycle phase. It also co-varies with library complexity, and none of the readouts are residualised for that. The claims use the word 'phase' as if it were ground truth.
findings.evidence: Mean genes detected per cell: G1 2,769, S 3,149, G2M 3,341. Spearman correlation of genes detected with cos(phi) is -0.42, and genes detected alone decodes phi with circ-R2 0.21 (kNN).
findings.recommended_action: Say that the target is a marker-defined pseudo-phase. Report decodability after residualising the representations for genes detected / depth. If possible, validate against an independent phase reference.

findings.description: All findings come from one cell line (K562 controls), one layer per model (layer 11), one checkpoint each and one CV/null seed family. Yet the conclusions are worded generically ('Phase can be read linearly from both models', 'The loop fits a flat circle').
findings.evidence: Only layer 11 of scGPT and of Geneformer was analysed. No other layer, dataset or cell type was tested, and no held-out condition was used.
findings.recommended_action: Qualify the claims as specific to K562 and layer 11, or add a layer sweep and at least one held-out dataset.

findings.description: Reproducibility and documentation gaps. The code that extracted the embeddings (layer choice, pooling, scGPT binning) is not included. Package versions are not pinned. The README says the expression matrix is log(1+CP10K) 'of all 6,546 genes in the source file', but the data contradict this.
findings.evidence: The expm1 row sums of expr_k562.npz emb range from 7,447 to 9,573, not 10,000. So normalisation used a larger gene set than the 6,546 genes provided. The README lists only 'numpy, scikit-learn' with no versions, and states 'The embeddings were computed once, earlier' with no script.
findings.recommended_action: Include the embedding-extraction script, or document its exact parameters and commit. Pin package versions. Correct the description of the normalisation.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' and its error is null, so there is no documented error to detect. I re-ran checks on the package to grade the findings. Three findings point to real problems the key does not cover. (a) For expression, the noise search in the flat null hits its upper bound. (b) The out-of-plane test fails to detect a planted non-flat loop. (c) In the pipeline's own whitened space, the conditional-mean loop leaves its 2-plane much more than the null does.

findings.reason: Reproduced exactly. Off-plane share of the 12 sector means in the whitened 20-PC space: scGPT 0.297 and Geneformer 0.226. The pipeline's own flat_null draws (seeds 100-104) give 0.037-0.058 and 0.064-0.086. Using 8 or 16 sectors gives the same result. For scGPT the excess holds without whitening too: 0.157 vs a null of 0.020-0.026. For Geneformer it does not: unwhitened, the real value is 0.022 vs a null of 0.044-0.055, so the claim is weaker there than stated. A direct measure of the loop shows it leaving its 2-plane more than a flat circle with matched noise, at least for scGPT, and the planted-loop control in F2 shows the pipeline's statistic lacks power. Together these undercut the headline of Conclusion 3 ('The loop fits a flat circle'). This goes beyond the key's '20 draws give low power' false alarm.

Confirmed with my own seed. I planted a loop with harmonics 1 and 2 (d=512, the real phi, s=9) and recalibrated flat_null to it (10 draws). At a=0.5: out-of-plane 35.7 vs null 28.6+-2.7, p=0.091. At a=1.0, a much less flat loop: 33.9 vs 37.3+-2.7, p=0.818, not rejected. Matching the null on linear circ-R2 gives it more noise when the loop is non-planar, so the statistic is not monotone in non-flatness. This is a real lack of power that the 20-draw p floor does not explain. The non-rejections therefore give little support to Conclusion 3.

Confirmed by replicating the bisection for flat_null(expr, seed 100). Every step stays above the target (s=10: 0.991 ... s=19.92: 0.955), so the noise level converges to the upper bound of 20. At that noise the null's circ-R2 is about 0.953, against a real 0.929. So the expression null is not matched as the README claims, and the key's 'matched' fact is wrong for expression. Not load-bearing: at matched noise (s about 23, circ-R2 0.928) the null out-of-plane angle rises to about 22 deg vs the real 17.9, which strengthens the stated non-rejection.

The numbers reproduce: expression without the 87 markers gives 0.895 linear / 0.833 kNN, and the markers alone give 0.965. But SUMMARY Conclusion 2 already says expression has a built-in advantage because the label is a projection of marker expression. True: comparing to the interpolated 95th percentile can reject while p = 2/21 = 0.095. My own positive control produced rejected=True with p=0.091. It has no effect on the reported results: nothing was rejected, and the p values are 0.57-0.91.

The numbers reproduce: genes detected per cell are 2,769 / 3,149 / 3,341 for G1 / S / G2M, and the Spearman correlation with cos(phi) is -0.423. Under the key's rule, a load-bearing finding counts as a false alarm unless running code on the package confirms it. I ran inline checks for F1 and F2. In all three representations the conditional-mean loop (12 sector means of the 20 whitened PCs) has much more energy outside its best-fit 2-plane than the package's own flat_null gives: scGPT 0.297 vs 0.046-0.058, Geneformer 0.226 vs 0.070-0.086 (null seeds 100-102), and expr 0.305 vs 0.040-0.042 (expr null as reported by the reviewer; I did not re-run it). findings.reason: Confirmed by running code. The 12-sector-mean off-plane energy share is scGPT 0.297 and Geneformer 0.226 in the real data, against 0.046-0.058 and 0.070-0.086 in the package's own flat_null (seeds 100-102).
