review.summary: The pipeline runs cleanly and its outputs reproduce. Re-running dataset.py in memory gives a label matrix and prot_index identical to outputs/residue_labels.npz, and a concept summary identical to concept_summary.json. Every number in the SUMMARY table and text matches. The data checks also passed: corpus and flat-file accessions, entry names, ID-line lengths and order all agree; no feature falls outside its sequence; every DISULFID endpoint is a cysteine; isoform-specific features (e.g. 'Q13555-2:325') are correctly skipped; and CA_BIND/METAL/NP_BIND really are absent from the file. The problems are in what the labels mean, not in the arithmetic. (1) The variation negative control clears the 1e-3 floor only because of long 'Missing' deletion spans, which cover almost whole proteins in a handful of entries. Counting single-residue or short (<=10 residue) features only, both VARIANT and CONFLICT fall below the floor, so Conclusion 3 cannot stand. (2) HELIX, STRAND and TURN are annotated in only 307 of the 5,000 proteins. Unannotated proteins are labelled negative, so scoring treats about 94% of the corpus's helices and strands as true negatives, even though their structure is simply unknown. (3) The residue-count floor ignores how few proteins the positives come from. It admits concepts concentrated in a few proteins and drops ACT_SITE, which is spread over 928 proteins. (4) Fuzzy ends are handled inconsistently: '1..?' becomes a single residue, and '?..N' is dropped even though the docstring says fuzzy bounds are resolved to their numeric part. The impact is small.

findings.location: code/dataset.py lines 170-180 (all non-bond ranges labelled in full, including VARIANT/CONFLICT 'Missing' spans); SUMMARY.md lines 33, 37, 57, 66 (Conclusion 3)
findings.description: The negative control is in place only because whole deleted segments count as 'variant' residues. VARIANT and CONFLICT ranges are expanded to every residue in the span, so a few long 'Missing (in disease X)' or 'Missing (in Ref. 1)' features supply most of the positives. Without those spans, neither key reaches the 1e-3 floor and no variation key would be scored. The positives that remain are mostly near-whole-protein blocks from a handful of entries. A feature that just tracks protein identity or a protein region could score well on them, which defeats the point of a negative control.
findings.evidence: VARIANT has 640 parsed features, 609 of them single residues. The 25 features longer than 10 residues cover 5,881 positions (with overlap). Single-residue VARIANT features alone give 591 positive residues (prevalence 3.7e-4); features of 10 residues or fewer give 607 (3.8e-4). Both are below the 1e-3 floor (1,606 residues), against the reported 3,243 (2.0e-3). Five proteins hold 61% of VARIANT positives and ten hold 85%. Within single proteins, 483 of 496 residues of O43541 are labelled VARIANT (via 'VARIANT 14..496 Missing'), as are 356/386 of Q86V24 and 335/358 of Q8IYM1. CONFLICT: single-residue features give 910 residues (5.7e-4) and features of 10 residues or fewer give 1,298 (8.1e-4), against the reported 1,860. The difference comes from spans such as 'CONFLICT 149..282 Missing (in Ref. 1)' (P21506) and 'CONFLICT 301..440' (Q9NVD3).
findings.recommended_action: Define the variation concepts as point positions. Either keep only single-residue or substitution features, or drop 'Missing' deletions and multi-residue replacements. Then recompute VARIANT and CONFLICT prevalence. If they fall below the floor, state that no negative control passes the floor. In either case, also check concentration by protein (top-k protein share) before calling the control 'in place'. Revise Conclusion 3 and the variation bullet.

findings.location: code/dataset.py lines 140-182 (build_label_matrix sets every unannotated residue to False); SUMMARY.md lines 22, 30, 35, 49, 61-62
findings.description: For HELIX, STRAND and TURN, a missing label means 'unknown', not 'negative'. Swiss-Prot gives these keys only to entries with a PDB structure. The label matrix nevertheless marks every residue of the other proteins as negative. A perfect helix or strand detector would therefore be scored with a huge false-positive rate, and precision/F1 for these three 'scored' concepts measures structure coverage rather than the concept. This undercuts the claims that these concepts are scored and that the label set is 'usable' for stable per-residue F1. A similar but weaker incompleteness affects other annotation-dependent keys.
findings.evidence: Only 307 of the 5,000 proteins (109,518 residues) carry any HELIX, STRAND or TURN feature. Within those proteins, HELIX prevalence is 0.288, STRAND 0.169 and TURN 0.025. Across the full corpus, as reported, they are 0.0197, 0.0115 and 0.0017. So about 93-94% of the corpus's helix and strand residues are labelled negative.
findings.recommended_action: Restrict scoring of the secondary-structure concepts to proteins that have structure annotation, using a per-concept protein mask in the outputs. Alternatively, derive secondary structure for all proteins, e.g. with DSSP on PDB or AlphaFold models. Report prevalence within the evaluable subset, and add a caveat to SUMMARY's secondary-structure bullet and Conclusion 1.

findings.location: code/build_labels.py line 32 and line 76 (MIN_PREVALENCE applied to residue counts); SUMMARY.md lines 55-56, 61-62
findings.description: The floor counts residues, not proteins. Conclusion 1 says the 21 scored concepts have enough positives for 'stable per-residue F1', but several of them come from few proteins: ZN_FING and DNA_BIND (99 proteins each), TRANSIT (73), REPEAT (112), COILED (117), and VARIANT, which is effectively a few proteins (see F1). These positives are highly correlated within proteins, so the effective sample size is far below the residue count. Meanwhile ACT_SITE, a key the code calls one of 'the highest-value targets', is spread over 928 proteins yet is excluded for being 72 residues short of the floor. The statement 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' is thus a product of the residue-only rule, not of a lack of stable data.
findings.evidence: Top-10-protein share of positives: VARIANT 0.85, ZN_FING 0.37, PROPEP 0.37, COILED 0.32, CONFLICT 0.31, DNA_BIND 0.30, TRANSIT 0.25, REPEAT 0.23. ACT_SITE: 1,534 residues in 928 proteins, top-10 share 0.04. The floor is 1e-3 x 1,606,104, about 1,606 residues.
findings.recommended_action: Add a minimum number of distinct proteins to the inclusion rule (or use one alongside the residue rule), and report per-concept protein counts in concept_summary.json. review.summary:
I re-ran the label build in memory. It reproduces outputs/residue_labels.npz exactly (labels, keys and prot_index all match). Every number in SUMMARY.md matches the outputs and the log. The corpus and the flat file agree on accession, entry name, length and order. The 876 proteins without labels genuinely have no concept keys (875 of them carry only CHAIN-type features). The three legacy keys (CA_BIND, METAL, NP_BIND) really are absent from the file. Disulfide and cross-link bonds are correctly labelled at their two endpoints. Features tied to a specific isoform are correctly skipped.

The problems are in what the labels mean. The main one: VARIANT clears the 1e-3 floor only because the code fills the whole span of 27 multi-residue "Missing" deletion/truncation variants. These supply 2,711 of its 3,243 positive residues, and 10 proteins supply 85% of them. Labelled as point variants only, VARIANT falls to 3.7e-4, below the floor. That changes the bolded headline count from 21 to 20 and undermines conclusion 3 about the negative control.

Further issues:
- Secondary-structure keys are treated as negative in the 93% of residues from proteins that have no structure annotation.
- The floor counts residues, not independent proteins, so "stable F1" is not supported.
- Fuzzy '?' end positions are handled wrongly, which undercounts TRANSIT.
- REGION is mostly "Disordered" regions but is reported as domain architecture.
- One log message is misleading.

findings.location: code/dataset.py lines 170-180 (range fill applied to every non-bond key, including VARIANT/CONFLICT/MUTAGEN); SUMMARY.md lines 9, 33, 57, 61-66
findings.description: VARIANT clears the prevalence floor only because multi-residue 'Missing' (deletion/truncation) variants are expanded to every residue they span. A variant like SMAD6 14..496 'Missing' marks a truncated region, not a variant residue, yet the whole region becomes VARIANT-positive. Without these ranges VARIANT is far below the 1e-3 floor. The bolded headline '21 of the 31 concepts clear the floor' should therefore be 20. Conclusion 3 ('negative control is in place, with two of the three variation keys scored') does not stand. The VARIANT negative control would mostly measure whether a feature fires on large stretches of about 10 human proteins (e.g. SMAD6, MYBPP, FBX11, PAQR2, SEP12, ARRC), not on variant sites.
findings.evidence: In parse_features output, VARIANT has 640 features: 609 single residues and 24 longer than 20 residues (max 483; summed span 6,508). In the flat file, 27 multi-residue VARIANT features have a /note starting 'Missing'. They cover 2,711 of the 3,243 positive residues (84%). Excluding them leaves 602 residues, prevalence 3.75e-4 (below 1e-3). Concentration: VARIANT positives come from 141 proteins; the top protein holds 15%, the top 5 hold 61% and the top 10 hold 85%. SMAD6_HUMAN alone has 13 nested 'Missing' ranges ending at 496. CONFLICT has the same problem on a smaller scale: without its 13 'Missing' ranges it drops from 1,860 to 1,662 residues (1.03e-3), only just above the floor. MUTAGEN loses 315 of its 1,109 residues.
findings.recommended_action: For the variation keys, label only the substituted position(s), or exclude 'Missing' and other deletion/truncation ranges (they can be parsed from the /note). Then recompute prevalences, the number of scored concepts and the negative-control set. Revise the headline count and conclusion 3. Consider requiring a minimum number of distinct proteins per concept.

findings.location: code/dataset.py lines 140-182 (an unannotated residue becomes a negative); SUMMARY.md line 49 and conclusion 1 (lines 61-62)
findings.description: HELIX/STRAND/TURN exist only for the few proteins that have experimental structures. Every residue of every other protein is labelled not-helix, not-strand and not-turn. In downstream per-residue F1, a feature that correctly fires on helices in unannotated proteins is counted as a false positive. Its precision, and hence F1, becomes meaningless. The 2% 'prevalence' of HELIX reflects annotation coverage, not biology. The summary nonetheless says these concepts are scored with 'stable per-residue F1'.
findings.evidence: Only 307 of the 5,000 proteins (109,518 residues, 6.8% of the corpus) carry any HELIX/STRAND/TURN feature. Within those proteins, HELIX prevalence is 0.288, STRAND 0.169 and TURN 0.025. Corpus-wide the figures are 0.0197, 0.0115 and 0.0017. So about 93% of residues are 'negatives' only because no annotation exists.
findings.recommended_action: Score the secondary-structure concepts only on proteins that have structure annotation (supply a per-concept evaluation mask), or derive secondary structure from structures (DSSP) for all proteins. State this caveat in the summary. Apply the same reasoning to any concept where a missing annotation does not mean absence.

findings.location: code/build_labels.py line 32 and line 76 (MIN_PREVALENCE floor on residue counts); SUMMARY.md lines 55-56 and 61-62
findings.description: The 1e-3 floor counts positive residues, not independent proteins or features. Long range-type annotations from a few proteins clear it easily, while sparse site annotations spread over many proteins do not. So 'enough positives for stable per-residue F1' is not shown. It is also arbitrary that catalytic residues are 'not tested' while concepts with much less independent support are scored.
findings.evidence: ACT_SITE (1,534 residues from 928 proteins) is excluded. VARIANT (141 proteins, 85% of positives from 10), TRANSIT (73 proteins), ZN_FING (99 proteins) and DNA_BIND (99 proteins) are scored. Residues within one protein are strongly correlated, so their count overstates the effective sample size.
findings.recommended_action: Base the floor on the number of distinct proteins or features (or both), or estimate F1 uncertainty with a protein-level bootstrap. Then revisit whether ACT_SITE should be scored. Soften the 'stable F1' claim until that is done.

findings.location: code/dataset.py line 87 (_FT_RE) and lines 129-133; docstring lines 99-100

'1..?' fails the optional end group, so end is set equal to start and a whole transit peptide or propeptide becomes a single residue. '?..124' fails the regex and is silently dropped. findings.location: code/dataset.py line 43 (REGION in the 'domain' group); SUMMARY.md lines 46-47

review.summary: The pipeline is internally consistent. Re-running parse_features and build_label_matrix reproduces outputs/residue_labels.npz exactly. Every count in SUMMARY.md matches build_log.txt and concept_summary.json. Corpus and flat file agree in accessions, entry names, order and lengths. VARIANT and CONFLICT clear the 1e-3 floor only because of a few long 'Missing' (truncating-variant or deletion) ranges: 79% of VARIANT positives come from 21 features in 9 human proteins. Counted as sites, both keys fall below the floor. The scored count would drop from 21 to 19, and the claim that the negative control is in place would fail. (2) VARIANT is not a valid negative control in any case: 96.5% of its positives are in human proteins, which make up 4.7% of residues, and disease variants sit at functionally important positions. (3) Missing annotation is treated as a negative. Only 307 of 5,000 proteins have any secondary-structure annotation; within them HELIX prevalence is 29%, against 2% overall. This caps HELIX/STRAND/TURN precision and F1, and 876 proteins have no labels at all. (4) The prevalence floor, not the number of proteins, decides which biology is tested. ACT_SITE (928 proteins) misses the floor by 72 residues, while VARIANT, ZN_FING and DNA_BIND (99 to 141 proteins, concentrated in a few) pass. No F1-stability analysis backs the 'stable F1' claim. findings.location: code/dataset.py:170-180 (build_label_matrix range filling, applied to VARIANT/MUTAGEN/CONFLICT); SUMMARY.md:9, 31-35 (table rows 16 and 20), 57, 66
findings.description: Variation features that span a range are expanded to every residue in the range. Most VARIANT residues come from 'Missing' annotations: truncating (nonsense) or deletion variants that UniProt writes as start..C-terminus. Each one labels hundreds of downstream residues as 'variant'. VARIANT and CONFLICT clear the 1e-3 floor only because of these few long ranges. So the headline '21 of the 31 concepts clear the floor', the scored negative-control set and Conclusion 3 all rest on this artefact.
findings.evidence: I recomputed with the package's own functions, keeping only features no longer than 50 residues. VARIANT: 3,243 -> 696 positives (4.3e-4); counted as point sites, 591 (3.7e-4). CONFLICT: 1,860 -> 1,506 (9.4e-4); as point sites, 910. Both fall below the floor of 1,606 residues. 21 VARIANT features longer than 50 residues, in 9 human proteins, give about 2,547 of the 3,243 positives (79%). Examples: SMAD6_HUMAN has 13 nested 'Missing' ranges ending at residue 496 (14..496, 42..496, ...), so 483 of its 496 residues are VARIANT-positive (15% of all VARIANT positives). MYBPP_HUMAN 518..984 (467), PAQR2_HUMAN 31..386, SEP12_HUMAN 24..358. For CONFLICT, three ranges (SETD4_HUMAN 301..440, ZNF10_HUMAN 149..282, PQIA_ECOLI 338..417; 354 residues) push it over the floor. The top three proteins hold 40% of VARIANT positives and 19% of CONFLICT positives.
findings.recommended_action: Define variation concepts at the variant site: label only the first residue of a 'Missing' or truncating range, or label point substitutions only. Then recompute prevalence. Report that, under a site definition, VARIANT and CONFLICT fall below the floor (19 scored concepts, no negative control). Revise the headline count, the variation-group bullet and Conclusion 3 accordingly, or choose a different negative-control design.

findings.description: VARIANT is a poor negative control even apart from F1. Swiss-Prot VARIANT entries are mostly human disease or polymorphism annotations. They sit at functionally constrained residues, which PLMs are known to track (zero-shot variant-effect prediction). They are also almost entirely in human proteins, so any feature that tracks species or protein identity would score on them. MUTAGEN sites are chosen by experimenters because they are functional. A positive F1 on these concepts would therefore not show that a feature is spurious, so 'the negative control is in place' overstates what the controls can show.
findings.evidence: 96.5% of VARIANT-positive residues are in Homo sapiens proteins, which make up 4.7% of corpus residues. VARIANT positives come from only 141 proteins, and the top three (SMAD6, MYBPP, PAQR2) hold 40.3%. CONFLICT positives are 36% human.
findings.recommended_action: Use a control that the model is not expected to track. Options: CONFLICT point sites only, or label sets made by shuffling or randomly placing positions within proteins while matching residue type and prevalence. At least, report VARIANT as a confounded control, not a clean negative, and stratify it by organism.

findings.location: code/dataset.py:156-181 (all unlabelled residues default to False); SUMMARY.md:49, 61-62
findings.description: Absence of an FT annotation is treated as a true negative. That is not valid for concepts that are only annotated when evidence exists. HELIX, STRAND and TURN come only from PDB structures, so they exist for a small minority of proteins. Residues in every other protein are labelled non-helix or non-strand whatever their real structure. Per-residue precision and F1 for these concepts are therefore capped far below what a perfect detector would score. Downstream conclusions that no SAE feature tracks secondary structure would be artefacts. The same problem applies, less severely, to incompletely annotated concepts such as DOMAIN, REGION, MOD_RES and BINDING, and to the 876 proteins (17.5%) with no concept labels at all.
findings.evidence: Only 307 of 5,000 proteins (109,518 residues, 6.8%) carry any HELIX, STRAND or TURN annotation. Within those proteins, HELIX prevalence is 0.288 and STRAND 0.169; corpus-wide they are 0.0197 and 0.0115. A perfect helix detector firing on roughly 29% of all residues would reach precision of about 0.07 and F1 of about 0.13 against these labels. 4,124 of 5,000 proteins have at least one positive label, so 876 contribute only negatives.
findings.recommended_action: For coverage-dependent concepts, score only within proteins that carry annotation of that type: for example, restrict HELIX/STRAND/TURN to the 307 structure-annotated proteins, ideally only within resolved PDB regions. Alternatively, carry an explicit 'unknown' mask in the npz. Report prevalence within annotated proteins next to corpus-wide prevalence, and qualify the 'label set is usable' conclusion.

findings.description: The scoring floor is a corpus-wide prevalence cut. The noise in a concept's F1 depends on how many independent positives it has, which is better measured by proteins or features than by prevalence. The cut decides which biology is tested, and nothing supports the claim that the 21 retained concepts have 'enough positives for stable per-residue F1'. ACT_SITE is excluded although it is spread over 928 proteins, and it misses the floor by 72 residues. Several included concepts rest on far fewer proteins and are concentrated in a handful. 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' follows from this threshold choice, not from the data.
findings.evidence: ACT_SITE has 1,534 residues in 928 proteins (no protein above 6); the floor is 1,606.1 residues. Included concepts rest on fewer proteins: VARIANT 141 proteins (top 3 = 40%), ZN_FING 99 (top 3 = 16%), DNA_BIND 99, TRANSIT 73, REPEAT 112, COILED 117. No F1-variance or bootstrap analysis is present.
findings.recommended_action: Base inclusion on the number of positive proteins or features, and/or a bootstrap estimate of F1 variance over proteins. Run a sensitivity check around the floor. findings.description: Features with an unknown end ('N..?') are collapsed to a single residue at N, because the optional end group fails to match '?'. Transit peptides and propeptides annotated as '1..?' end up as single-residue labels.
findings.evidence: The raw file contains 'FT   TRANSIT 1..?' (5 times), 'FT   PROPEP 1..?' (1) and 'FT   DISULFID 4..?' / '20..?'; each becomes one labelled residue. findings.description: Three of the 31 columns (CA_BIND, METAL, NP_BIND) cannot have positives in the current flat-file format, yet they are counted in the '21 of 31' denominator and kept as concepts. findings.recommended_action: Drop the dead columns or report '21 of 28 populated keys'. Consider splitting BINDING by the /ligand qualifier (e.g. metal ions vs nucleotides vs other) to restore the intended binding concepts.

review.summary:
I reviewed B4481 against all ten checklist patterns. The arithmetic holds up. I re-ran load_corpus, parse_features and build_label_matrix in memory with nothing written to disk. The labels, keys and prot_index arrays match outputs/residue_labels.npz exactly, and concept_summary.json matches too. Every number in the SUMMARY tables matches the JSON. All 5,000 corpus accessions are primary accessions in the flat file, with the same order, names and lengths, and no FT range runs past its sequence. Parsed feature counts per key equal the raw FT line counts, except for isoform-specific locations (e.g. "P29310-3:149"), which are correctly skipped, and a handful of fuzzy "?" ends.

The problems are in what the labels mean and in the summary's three conclusions:
- **Conclusion 3 (critical):** the 'negative control' does not stand. VARIANT clears the floor only because of about 25 long "Missing" truncation spans, and 96% of its positives sit in human proteins. CONFLICT clears the floor only through long-span entries.
- **Conclusion 1 (major):** HELIX/STRAND/TURN treat 'no PDB structure' as 'negative'. The claim 'enough positives for stable F1' counts residues, not proteins. Which concepts pass the floor is unstable under a protein-level bootstrap, and ACT_SITE's exclusion depends on that knife-edge.
- **Conclusion 2 (major):** DISULFID positives are 100% cysteine, so residue identity alone predicts them.
- **Concept definitions (major):** DOMAIN and REGION are mixtures of hundreds of note types, and most labels are themselves sequence-model predictions.

Checklist verdicts:
- **P1** present, unaddressed. Per-concept chance F1 is not reported; it ranges from 1e-4 to 0.245.
- **P2** present, unaddressed. No residue-identity or position baseline: DISULFID is all Cys, CARBOHYD 94% Asn, SIGNAL is N-terminal, COMPBIAS is composition by definition.
- **P3** present, unaddressed. Mixed concepts, labels that are computational predictions, and missing annotation treated as negative.
- **P4** present, unaddressed. The unit is residues, but positives cluster in a few proteins and homologs: 36 identical sequences and 2,588 proteins sharing a gene mnemonic.
- **P5** present, unaddressed. The prevalence floor favours long-span keys and drops point-site keys. VARIANT and CONFLICT pass only through long spans.
- **P6** present, minor. The label set has no positive-control concept.
- **P7** present. The concept set comes from one 5,000-protein sample and one release; covered under P8.
- **P8** present, unaddressed. A single 1e-3 threshold, and the count of 21 is not stable under resampling.
- **P9** present. Wording such as 'usable', 'stable', 'negative control is in place' and 'PLMs should NOT track these' goes beyond the evidence.
- **P10** minor. No sampling script or seed, no release number, no environment file. The outputs do reproduce exactly from the shipped code.

findings.description: The variation 'negative control' is not valid. VARIANT and CONFLICT clear the 1e-3 floor only because of long multi-residue spans, mostly 'Missing' truncation and deletion variants. VARIANT is confounded with species and protein identity. Disease variants also sit by design at conserved, functional positions, which PLMs are known to track (the basis of ESM-1v-style variant scoring). So the premise in dataset.py:44 that 'PLMs should NOT track these' is wrong for VARIANT, and is wrong by construction for MUTAGEN, whose targets are chosen at known functional sites. The claim 'The negative control is in place, with two of the three variation keys scored' cannot stand.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the parsed features. VARIANT has 640 features, 609 of them single residues. Single-residue positives give prevalence 3.7e-4 (591 residues), below the floor. 2,636 of the 3,243 positives (81%) come from multi-residue spans of up to 483 residues. Examples: 13 'Missing' spans in SMAD6_HUMAN (483, 455, 422 ... residues), plus MYBPP_HUMAN (467), PAQR2_HUMAN (356) and SEP12_HUMAN (335). The top protein holds 15% of VARIANT positives and the top 5 hold 61%. 96% of VARIANT positive residues are in human proteins, which are only 4.7% of corpus residues. Under a protein-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) the VARIANT prevalence 95% CI is [9.2e-4, 3.4e-3]. CONFLICT reaches only 5.7e-4 from single-residue features and 8.1e-4 from features of 10 residues or fewer. It passes the floor (1.16e-3) only through spans of up to 140 residues, such as 'Missing (in Ref. 1)' in ZNF10_HUMAN and a 140-residue segment in SETD4_HUMAN. CONFLICT stays above the floor in only 85% of bootstrap resamples.
findings.recommended_action: Do not use VARIANT or MUTAGEN as negative controls. If a variation control is kept, restrict it to single-residue entries and drop 'Missing' and other span annotations. Restrict its negatives to human proteins, or match the control on species and protein, and report its prevalence after those changes. It will likely fall below the floor. A better negative control is a label permutation within each protein that preserves run length, or a random-position concept matched on prevalence and run length. Restate Conclusion 3 accordingly.

findings.description: The matrix treats absence of an annotation as a negative label. This is invalid for concepts that are annotated only on a subset of proteins. HELIX, STRAND and TURN come from PDB structures and exist only for proteins with a solved structure. Every residue in the other ~94% of proteins is labelled 'not helix'. Per-residue precision and F1 for these concepts will therefore be dominated by unlabelled true helices and strands, and the reported prevalences are not biological prevalences. The same problem applies in part to VARIANT (curated almost only for human proteins) and to annotations inferred 'by similarity'. Conclusion 1 ('The label set is usable') does not hold for these concepts.
findings.evidence: Only 307 of 5,000 proteins (6.8% of residues) carry any HELIX/STRAND/TURN annotation, and all of it is ECO structure evidence. Within those proteins HELIX prevalence is 0.289, STRAND 0.169 and TURN 0.025. Across the full matrix the values are 0.0197, 0.0115 and 0.0017. A perfect helix detector would therefore have per-residue precision capped at about 0.07 against these labels.
findings.recommended_action: Add a per-concept 'evaluable' mask, for example proteins with any secondary-structure feature for HELIX/STRAND/TURN, and score only within it. Report prevalence and positives inside the evaluable set. Alternatively, derive secondary structure for every protein from structures or predicted structures, such as DSSP on AlphaFold models. Document the annotation-completeness assumption for every concept.

findings.description: The prevalence floor and the 'stable per-residue F1' claim use residues as the inference unit. Positives are, however, clustered within proteins and within homolog families. The 1e-3 cut-off is a single fixed value applied to one 5,000-protein sample, and which concepts pass it is not stable. No F1-stability analysis supports 'enough positives for stable per-residue F1'. The floor also ranks concepts in a way unrelated to stability. ACT_SITE (1,534 residues in 928 proteins) is excluded, so 'catalytic residues are not tested'. Meanwhile concepts drawn from far fewer independent proteins are kept: TRANSIT (73 proteins), DNA_BIND and ZN_FING (99 each), COILED (117) and VARIANT (141, with 61% of residues in 5 proteins).
findings.evidence: In a protein-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples), the number of concepts at or above 1e-3 was 21 in 73% of resamples, 20 in 18%, 22 in 7% and 19 in 1.5%. P(prevalence >= 1e-3) was 0.09 for ACT_SITE, 0.956 for MOD_RES and 0.846 for CONFLICT. ACT_SITE's CI is [9.0e-4, 1.02e-3] and MOD_RES's is [9.8e-4, 1.27e-3]. The corpus is redundant: 36 sequences are identical duplicates, and 2,588 proteins share a gene mnemonic with another corpus entry (e.g. ATPA x16, CYB x14, RS7 x14). Many PTM and site labels are propagated 'by similarity' (54% of DISULFID and 58% of MOD_RES features carry ECO:0000250).
findings.recommended_action: Report positives as 'n residues over m proteins over k homolog clusters'. Base the scoring floor on the number of independent proteins or clusters, not residue prevalence, or justify it with a simulation showing F1 variance against positive count. Report a sweep of at least three floor values and the concepts that pass under resampling. Cluster the corpus (e.g. MMseqs2 at 30-50% identity) and resample or split by cluster downstream. Restate 'catalytic residues are not tested' as a consequence of an arbitrary threshold, not a property of the data.

findings.description: Several of the largest 'concepts' mix many unrelated annotation types, and most labels are outputs of other sequence-based predictors rather than measured properties. The project asks whether single SAE features match 'known residue-level properties'. Here DOMAIN pools 553 distinct domain types, and half of REGION is MobiDB-lite 'Disordered' predictions. A feature that is monosemantic for one domain family cannot reach high recall on DOMAIN. Agreement with TRANSMEM, DOMAIN, COILED or ZN_FING largely measures agreement with HMM, profile or TM predictors run on the same sequences, which is a circularity problem. This is an endpoint–object mismatch the write-up does not acknowledge.
findings.evidence: DOMAIN has 553 distinct /note values; the largest (Radical SAM core, tr-type G, Protein kinase, ABC transporter) each cover about 4% of DOMAIN residues. REGION has 455 distinct notes, and 'Disordered' covers 51% of REGION span-residues. COMPBIAS evidence is 100% ECO:0000256 (automatic), with 7 composition classes. Share of features with ECO:0000255 (sequence analysis) evidence: DOMAIN 99%, COILED 98%, ZN_FING 98%, TRANSMEM 89%, DNA_BIND 87%, SIGNAL 83%, ACT_SITE 79%, BINDING 73%.
findings.recommended_action: Split composite keys into specific concepts, e.g. DOMAIN by domain name or InterPro ID and REGION 'Disordered' versus named regions. Then apply the floor to those concepts. Tag each label with its evidence class and provide an experimental- or structure-evidence-only version. In the write-up, describe the endpoint as agreement with UniProt annotations, many of them computational predictions, not as 'known properties'.

findings.description: No trivial baseline is provided, and several scored concepts can be read off residue identity or sequence position. Conclusion 2 says 'PTM biology enters the scoring through DISULFID and MOD_RES'. But DISULFID labels are a subset of cysteines, so a pure 'is-Cys' token feature already scores high F1. MOD_RES is dominated by S/T/Y/K. SIGNAL, TRANSIT and PROPEP are N-terminal, and COMPBIAS is composition by definition. Without a residue-identity or position baseline, or labels conditioned on residue type, downstream F1 cannot separate PTM or targeting biology from amino-acid-identity features.
findings.evidence: 100% of DISULFID positives are Cys. Cys makes up 1.33% of corpus residues. The 'residue == C' predictor reaches F1 = 0.183 on DISULFID, against 0.0027 for an all-on predictor. CARBOHYD positives are 94% Asn. MOD_RES positives are 84% S/T/Y/K. A 'position < 20' predictor reaches F1 = 0.144 on SIGNAL (all-on 0.0115) and 0.026 on TRANSIT (all-on 0.0037).
findings.recommended_action: For every concept, ship trivial-baseline F1 values: best single amino acid, best N- or C-terminal window, and local composition. Downstream, report ΔF1 over the best trivial baseline. For residue-restricted concepts, evaluate within the eligible residue type, e.g. DISULFID among Cys, CARBOHYD among N-x-S/T sequons, MOD_RES among S/T/Y/K.

findings.description: The summary does not anchor each concept to a chance level. Scored concepts span about 125-fold in prevalence (0.00112 to 0.140), and the F1 a constant or random feature achieves scales with prevalence. F1 values across concepts and layers will not be comparable without a per-concept chance baseline.
findings.evidence: All-on F1 = 2p/(1+p): DOMAIN 0.245, REGION 0.156, TOPO_DOM 0.096, TRANSMEM 0.082, and down to about 0.0022 for MOD_RES. For DOMAIN, the all-on baseline beats every single-amino-acid and positional predictor (best 0.142).
findings.recommended_action: Add chance F1 (all-on, and a random feature matched to the concept's firing rate) to concept_summary.json and to the SUMMARY table. Require downstream claims to be stated relative to it, or against a permutation null that preserves run length within each protein.

findings.description: A range with an unknown end ('N..?') is silently collapsed to a single residue, and an unknown start ('?..N') is dropped. The docstring (lines 99-100) says fuzzy bounds are 'resolved to their numeric part'. In practice a transit peptide or propeptide of unknown length is labelled as residue 1 only. The rows still look like valid labels, so no error is visible.
findings.evidence: Flat-file lines 'FT   TRANSIT         1..?' (5 entries, e.g. lines 2173, 58319, 120224, 145839, 150268) and 'FT   PROPEP          1..?' (line 76526) each produce one positive residue. 'FT   TRANSIT         ?..124' (line 150270) is dropped. Parsed TRANSIT features number 74, against 75 raw FT lines.
findings.recommended_action: Drop features with unknown bounds, or flag them and infer the end from the adjacent CHAIN or PEPTIDE start. Count and log every fuzzy-bound case.

findings.description: n_accessions_with_ft and the log line '4,124/5,000 corpus accessions carry >=1 FT annotation' are mislabelled. Every entry has FT lines (CHAIN etc.); the 4,124 counts accessions with at least one of the 31 concept keys. The abort guard at line 54 uses this count as an accession-matching check, so it mixes up 'no concept annotation' with 'accession parsing broken'. Separately, the headline '21 of the 31 concepts' counts three columns (CA_BIND, METAL, NP_BIND) that cannot be non-empty in the current format. It is effectively 21 of 28.
findings.evidence: awk over the flat file shows 5,000 ID entries, and all 5,000 have at least one FT line. All 5,000 corpus accessions are primary accessions in the file. The legacy keys have 0 FT lines.
findings.recommended_action: Rename the field to n_accessions_with_concept_key. Base the abort guard on the number of corpus accessions found in the flat file. Remove the retired keys from ALL_FT_KEYS, or report the fraction as 21 of 28 usable keys.

findings.description: Reproducibility scaffolding is incomplete. The code that sampled the 5,000-protein corpus and cut down the flat file is missing, along with its random seed. The Swiss-Prot release number is not given, only 'downloaded July 2026'. No environment or version file is included. The concept set depends on this one sample (see F3), so the sampling must be reproducible. The labels themselves do reproduce exactly from the shipped code and data.
findings.evidence: I re-ran parse_features and build_label_matrix in memory: labels, keys and prot_index are identical to outputs/residue_labels.npz, and concept_summary matches the JSON. No requirements.txt or environment.yml exists, and there is no sampling script and no seed.
findings.recommended_action: Add the corpus-sampling and flat-file subsetting script with its seed, the UniProt release identifier (e.g. 2026_0x) and a pinned environment (numpy version).

findings.description: The label set has no positive-control concept. The downstream scoring will produce null results, for example concepts with no matching SAE feature, and with no planted concept known to be encoded those nulls cannot be interpreted.
findings.evidence: All 31 columns are UniProt FT keys. None is a known-answer concept such as amino-acid identity, which ESM-2 SAEs are known to encode.
findings.recommended_action: Add positive-control columns, e.g. one per amino-acid identity and a synthetic concept planted into the activations. Confirm the scoring pipeline recovers them before interpreting negative or near-chance results.

The top VARIANT protein holds 14.9% of positives and the top 5 hold 60.6%, e.g. SMAD6_HUMAN 'Missing' spans such as 14..496. 96% of VARIANT positives are in human proteins, which make up 4.7% of residues. The key lists this exact point as a possible false alarm: unannotated residues are treated as negatives, and HELIX/STRAND/TURN exist only for proteins with a solved structure. The key calls it a real limitation of UniProt ground truth but a caveat, not a load-bearing error. The key states that the 1e-3 floor and the 5,000-protein sample size are design choices stated in the README, and that claiming they are errors is a false alarm. The finding's bootstrap and clustering points describe sensitivity to a design choice, not an error. The data confirm the main facts. DOMAIN has about 550-580 distinct notes, and 'Disordered' is the dominant REGION note. COMPBIAS evidence is 100% ECO:0000256. I reproduced the numbers. DISULFID positives are 100% Cys, and an 'is-Cys' predictor reaches F1 = 0.183 against 0.0027 for all-on. MOD_RES positives are 84% S/T/Y/K and CARBOHYD positives 94% Asn. review.summary:
I re-ran the pipeline in memory without writing any files. The saved outputs reproduce exactly: the label matrix, keys, prot_index and every count in SUMMARY.md and build_log.txt match. Protein order, ID-line lengths and entry names in the flat file all agree with the corpus. Coordinates are correct: every DISULFID residue is a cysteine, and 94% of CARBOHYD residues are asparagine. The only FT lines the parser skips are isoform-prefixed ones, which is the right behaviour.

The problems are in how the labels are defined and in the claims SUMMARY.md makes from them.

1. **Variation keys and the negative control.** Variation features with a range are filled across the whole range. As a result, VARIANT and CONFLICT clear the 1e-3 floor only because of long "Missing" truncations and sequence-conflict segments. About 82% of VARIANT positives come from 31 range features. SMAD6_HUMAN alone gives 15%, and the top 10 proteins give 85%. If only point positions are counted, VARIANT drops to 3.7e-4 and CONFLICT to 5.7e-4. With either point-only or start-position labelling, the headline count would be 19 rather than 21, and the summary's claim that "the negative control is in place" would not hold.

2. **Missing annotation is treated as a negative.**
   - HELIX, STRAND and TURN are annotated in only 307 of 5,000 proteins. Within those proteins HELIX covers 28.8% of residues, against 2.0% across the corpus.
   - The other 876 proteins carry none of the 31 keys, so all their residues count as negatives.
   - Per-residue F1 for these concepts is therefore capped by how much of the corpus is annotated.

3. **The scoring floor is fragile and uses the wrong unit.** The floor is a residue-level prevalence and is set at a single value. At 5e-4 the scored set is 23 concepts; at 2e-3 it is 16. In a protein-level bootstrap, exactly 21 concepts are scored in only 73% of resamples. The floor admits VARIANT (141 proteins, highly concentrated) and excludes ACT_SITE (928 proteins, missing the floor by 4.5%). So the statement "catalytic residues are not tested" comes from where the threshold was set, not from a real lack of data.

4. **The large concepts are mixed and mostly computer-predicted.**
   - REGION: about 67% of its features are MobiDB-lite "Disordered" predictions.
   - COMPBIAS: 100% automatic composition rules.
   - DOMAIN: 99.5% sequence-analysis evidence (ECO:0000255).

Smaller issues:
- DISULFID can be recovered almost from amino-acid identity alone (a "residue is C" predictor reaches F1 0.79 within annotated proteins), so the claim that PTM biology enters the scoring through DISULFID needs that baseline.
- Locations with an unknown end ("1..?") are cut to a single residue, and those with an unknown start ("?..N") are dropped, although the docstring says unresolvable entries are skipped.
- PROPEP is grouped as "targeting".
- The corpus contains duplicate and homologous sequences, which the floor and later scoring treat as independent.
- Reproducibility: no UniProt release number, no corpus-sampling script or seed, no pinned versions, and one log line is mislabelled.

findings.location: code/dataset.py:170-180 (range fill applied to VARIANT/CONFLICT/MUTAGEN; only BOND_KEYS at line 52 get special handling); SUMMARY.md:9, 57, 66; README.md:20
findings.description: Variation-group features are labelled by filling the whole FT range, as if each were a region concept. Many VARIANT, MUTAGEN and CONFLICT ranges are 'Missing' truncations or replaced sequence segments that span hundreds of residues. These residues are not variant positions. VARIANT and CONFLICT clear the 1e-3 floor only because of these ranges, so the headline count of 21 scored concepts and Conclusion 3 ('The negative control is in place') rest on the label rule, not on how often variants actually occur. The VARIANT 'concept' also amounts to C-terminal blocks of about 10 human proteins. An SAE feature that tracks protein or region identity could score well on it, so it does not work as a negative control. Disease-variant positions are also enriched at conserved residues that PLMs are known to track, which further undermines the control.
findings.evidence: There are 31 VARIANT range features. Point-only VARIANT positions number 591 (prevalence 3.68e-4), so ranges supply at least 2,652 of the 3,243 positives (82%). SMAD6_HUMAN alone has 13 overlapping 'Missing' variants (e.g. 14..496) giving 483 residues (14.9%). The top 10 proteins account for 84.8% of VARIANT positives (141 proteins in total), and 550 of 641 VARIANT lines are from human entries. CONFLICT: point-only 910 (5.67e-4); start-only 1,045 (6.51e-4); ranges of 10 residues or fewer 1,298 (8.08e-4). All are below the floor, and 148 range features (e.g. SETD4_HUMAN 301..440) supply about half its positives. In a protein-level bootstrap the VARIANT prevalence 95% CI is 0.00092-0.00336.
findings.recommended_action: Label variation keys at the variant position: the start residue, or point features only, and drop or flag 'Missing' and segment-replacement features. Recompute the prevalences and the scored-concept count, which comes to 19 under point labelling. Restate Conclusion 3: with correct labelling no variation key clears the floor. Either lower or justify the floor for the control, or choose a different negative control, such as a residue-shuffled or position-permuted pseudo-concept matched to each real concept's prevalence and run length.

findings.location: code/dataset.py:156-181 (labels initialised to False for all residues of all proteins); SUMMARY.md:6, 49, 61-62
findings.description: A missing annotation is treated as a confirmed negative. For HELIX, STRAND and TURN this matters most, because Swiss-Prot gives them only for the roughly 6% of proteins that have PDB structures. Every helix in the other proteins is labelled negative, so corpus-wide prevalence and any per-residue precision or F1 mostly reflect annotation coverage, not the concept. The same applies, less severely, to MOD_RES, DISULFID, BINDING and ACT_SITE, which are incompletely annotated. The 876 proteins with no concept key contribute only negatives. Conclusion 1 ('the label set is usable ... stable per-residue F1') and the plain 'Secondary structure ... all scored' statement leave this out.
findings.evidence: 307 of 5,000 proteins (6.8% of residues) have any HELIX, STRAND or TURN label. Within those proteins HELIX = 0.288, STRAND = 0.169 and TURN = 0.025. Across the corpus the figures are 0.0197, 0.0115 and 0.0017. A perfect helix detector would therefore reach precision of only about 0.02/0.29, roughly 7%. Within-protein vs corpus prevalence for other keys: DISULFID 0.0207 vs 0.0013 (352 proteins); TRANSMEM 0.277 vs 0.043; MOD_RES 0.0074 vs 0.0011.
findings.recommended_action: For each concept, store a per-protein 'annotated' mask, i.e. proteins with at least one feature of that key or group, and score only within annotated proteins. Report prevalence both within annotated proteins and across the corpus. For secondary structure, use DSSP on PDB or AlphaFold structures for the whole corpus instead of FT HELIX/STRAND/TURN. State in SUMMARY.md that unannotated residues are not true negatives.

findings.description: Which concepts get scored depends on a single residue-prevalence cut of 1e-3. That threshold was not sensitivity-tested, and it is computed in the wrong unit. The stated reason, that rarer concepts give noisy F1, depends on the number of independent positives (proteins), not on residue prevalence. The rule keeps VARIANT, whose positives come from very few proteins, and drops ACT_SITE, which is spread over many proteins and misses the floor by 4.5%. So 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' is an artefact of the threshold, and 'enough positives for stable per-residue F1' was never checked.
findings.evidence: Threshold sweep: 23 concepts at 5e-4 (adds ACT_SITE and MUTAGEN), 21 at 1e-3, 16 at 2e-3 (drops TRANSIT, TURN, DISULFID, CONFLICT and MOD_RES; VARIANT 2.019e-3 and MOTIF 2.031e-3 survive by under 2%). In a protein-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) the number of scored concepts ranges from 19 to 23, and exactly 21 occur in 73% of resamples. P(clears floor): CONFLICT 0.85, MOD_RES 0.96, VARIANT 0.97, ACT_SITE 0.09. ACT_SITE: 1,534 positives in 928 proteins, top-10 share 3.7%, bootstrap CI 0.00090-0.00102. VARIANT: 3,243 positives in 141 proteins, top-10 share 85%, CI 0.00092-0.00336.
findings.recommended_action: Base the eligibility rule on independent units, for example at least N proteins carrying the concept plus a cap on single-protein share, or on a bootstrap CI of F1 for a reference feature. Report a 3-point sweep and a protein-level bootstrap of membership in SUMMARY.md. Either include ACT_SITE or say plainly that its exclusion depends on the threshold.

findings.location: code/dataset.py:43 (domain group: DOMAIN, REGION, COMPBIAS, ...); SUMMARY.md:17-19, 22, 46-47
findings.description: The largest concepts are mixed and mostly come from automatic sequence predictions. REGION, the second largest concept, is mainly MobiDB-lite 'Disordered' predictions mixed with assorted named regions ('G1', 'Interaction with X'). COMPBIAS is computed entirely by an automatic sequence-composition rule. DOMAIN pools every domain family into one binary concept, almost all from sequence-analysis profiles. Scoring SAE features against these measures agreement with other sequence-based predictors, not with 'known residue-level properties'. A truly monosemantic feature for one family, such as a kinase domain, would get a low F1 against the pooled DOMAIN concept. SUMMARY.md presents these as the bulk of the biology ('Domain architecture is the bulk of the labelled residues') and does not mention their provenance.
findings.evidence: REGION notes: 1,508 of about 2,251 features are '"Disordered"', and 1,506 carry evidence ECO:0000256 (automatic). COMPBIAS: 1,849 of 1,849 are ECO:0000256 ('Basic and acidic residues', 'Polar residues', 'Low complexity', ...). DOMAIN: 1,502 of 1,510 are ECO:0000255 (sequence analysis). TRANSMEM: 2,905 of 3,275 are ECO:0000255, with only 56 experimental.
findings.recommended_action: Split REGION into disorder and named-region concepts, and split DOMAIN by family (from the /note or InterPro ID), or score per family. Record each concept's evidence breakdown, and add an experimental-evidence-only variant where counts allow. In SUMMARY.md, describe REGION and COMPBIAS as predictor outputs, not curated biology.

findings.description: Conclusion 2 says PTM biology enters the scoring through DISULFID, but DISULFID positives are exactly a subset of cysteines. An SAE feature that detects cysteines would score high on DISULFID without any knowledge of bonding. No trivial baseline (amino-acid identity) is given for this or for other residue-type-specific concepts (CARBOHYD to Asn, CROSSLNK to Lys, MOD_RES to Ser/Thr/Lys, LIPID to Cys).
findings.evidence: All 2,154 DISULFID residues are C. A 'residue is C' predictor gives F1 = 0.183 across the corpus, and P = 0.648, R = 1.0, F1 = 0.787 within DISULFID-annotated proteins. CARBOHYD: 94% N (recall 0.94 for 'is N'). CROSSLNK: 82% K. LIPID: 71% C.
findings.recommended_action: Ship a per-concept amino-acid-identity baseline F1 with the label set, and require later SAE scores to beat it (delta-F1). Alternatively, define the negatives for these concepts as the same residue type, e.g. bonded vs unbonded cysteines, and say so in SUMMARY.md.

findings.description: Ranges with an unknown end ('1..?') are reduced to a single residue at the start position. Ranges with an unknown start ('?..124') fail the regex and are dropped silently. The docstring says unresolvable entries are skipped, which describes neither behaviour accurately. This mostly affects TRANSIT and PROPEP, which are targeting concepts close to the floor.
findings.evidence: The subset contains TRANSIT '1..?' ×5, PROPEP '1..?' ×1, REGION '<1..?1' and TRANSIT '?..124' (Q9SM43, dropped). The '1..?' transit peptides each add only residue 1.
findings.recommended_action: Treat '?' bounds explicitly: skip the feature, or flag it and exclude it from that concept's negatives. Log the number affected and fix the docstring.

findings.description: PROPEP (propeptides removed during maturation) is grouped under 'targeting'. The per-group statement 'Targeting: SIGNAL, PROPEP and TRANSIT are all scored' overstates targeting coverage. PROPEP is also highly concentrated in a few proteins.
findings.evidence: PROPEP: 4,913 residues in 124 proteins; top-10 proteins = 36.6% of positives; maximum feature length 259.
findings.recommended_action: Move PROPEP to a processing or maturation group, or rename the group, and update the By-group text.

findings.description: Prevalences and the later per-residue scoring treat residues, and the proteins they come from, as independent. The corpus contains exact duplicate sequences and many orthologs (e.g. 1108L_ASFK5 and 1108L_ASFM2 are near-identical with identical FT tables). This inflates the effective number of positives and will inflate the precision of later F1 estimates.
findings.evidence: 36 exact duplicate sequences; 2,588 of 5,000 entries share an entry-name gene prefix with at least one other entry (3,079 distinct prefixes).
findings.recommended_action: Cluster the corpus by sequence identity (e.g. MMseqs2 at 30-50%), report counts per cluster, and use clusters as the bootstrap or CV unit in later scoring.

findings.description: The setup cannot be fully reproduced: no UniProt release number (only 'downloaded July 2026'), no corpus-sampling script or seed (the analysis rests on a single random sample of 5,000), no pinned package versions or environment file, and no script that builds the flat-file subset. The log line '4,124/5,000 corpus accessions carry >=1 FT annotation' is mislabelled: all 5,000 have FT lines (e.g. CHAIN), and 4,124 is the count with at least one of the 31 concept keys. Because of this, the <50% ABORT check cannot tell a parse failure apart from an absence of concept keys.
findings.evidence: The flat-file subset has 5,032 CHAIN lines across the 5,000 entries; 876 entries have only non-concept keys. No requirements.txt or environment.yml exists, and no sampling code is in code/.
findings.recommended_action: Record the UniProt release (e.g. 2026_0x) and file checksum, add the sampling and subsetting script with its seed, and pin numpy and Python versions. Fix the log message, and add a separate check that every corpus accession was found in the flat file.
