Withdraw or restate Conclusion 3, and drop MUTAGEN from the negative-control framing.

findings.location: code/dataset.py lines 159-181 (every unannotated residue is set False); SUMMARY.md lines 49 and 61-62
findings.description: A missing annotation is treated as a true negative. This is most serious for HELIX, STRAND and TURN, which Swiss-Prot gives only for proteins with a solved 3D structure. In 94% of proteins, every helical or strand residue is labelled negative. The labels therefore mean 'annotated helix in a protein that has a PDB structure', not 'is a helix'. Per-residue precision and F1 against them cannot measure whether a feature detects secondary structure, yet the summary calls these concepts usable for stable F1. The 876 proteins with no concept annotation at all (177,736 residues, 11%) are also counted as all-negative for every concept.
findings.evidence: Only 307 of 5,000 proteins (6.8% of residues) have any HELIX, STRAND or TURN label: HELIX 294 proteins, STRAND 286, TURN 240. Within the annotated proteins HELIX covers 29.7% of residues, but the global prevalence is 1.97%. If unannotated proteins have similar helix content, a perfect helix detector would get precision of about 31.6k/480k, roughly 0.07, and F1 of about 0.12. Every HELIX feature line has experimental (non-ECO:0000255/256) evidence, which confirms the labels come from structures.
findings.recommended_action: Restrict each concept's scoring to proteins where that annotation type exists: for HELIX/STRAND/TURN, only structure-annotated proteins, or use DSSP on AlphaFold/PDB models for all proteins. Report prevalence within annotated proteins next to the global prevalence. Flag concepts where absence does not mean negative, and qualify Conclusion 1 for them.

findings.location: code/build_labels.py lines 32 and 76; README.md line 19; SUMMARY.md lines 9, 40, 55-56 and 61-62
findings.description: Which concepts get scored is decided by one global residue-prevalence cutoff. The cutoff sits on a knife edge for several keys and does not measure what it is meant to guard against (noisy F1). ACT_SITE, with 1,534 positives spread over 928 proteins, is excluded. Concepts with far fewer independent proteins, or with positives concentrated in a few proteins, are included. The claim that catalytic residues are 'therefore not tested' follows from this arbitrary rule, not from lack of data. The set of 21 concepts is also not stable across resamples of the corpus.
findings.evidence: ACT_SITE prevalence is 9.55e-4 (needs 1,606 positives; has 1,534) from 928 proteins, and its top-10 proteins hold 4% of positives. Included concepts: MOD_RES 1,802 positives; CONFLICT 1,860; VARIANT from 141 proteins with 85% in the top 10; TRANSIT 73 proteins; DNA_BIND and ZN_FING 99 proteins each. Bootstrap over proteins (2,000 resamples) gives P(prevalence >= 1e-3) of 0.09 for ACT_SITE, 0.85 for CONFLICT, 0.96 for MOD_RES and 0.96 for VARIANT. No sensitivity sweep of the floor is reported.
findings.recommended_action: Base inclusion on the number of independent proteins or annotation instances, or on a power or F1-variance criterion, rather than global residue prevalence. Report a 3-point sweep, for example 5e-4, 1e-3 and 2e-3, and the protein-bootstrap CI of each concept's prevalence. Score ACT_SITE, or state explicitly that its exclusion is threshold-driven. Restate 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' accordingly.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 61-62; code/dataset.py lines 185-200 (concept_summary reports residue counts only)
findings.description: The claim that 21 concepts 'have enough positives for stable per-residue F1' counts residues. Residues are not independent: positives come as contiguous spans within a protein, proteins are clustered by homology, and the corpus has exact duplicate sequences. The relevant unit is the protein or homology cluster, and no protein-level n or stability estimate is given. No F1-stability analysis supports the word 'stable'.
findings.evidence: ZN_FING has 6,187 residues from 99 proteins, with the top 10 holding 37%. PROPEP has 4,913 residues from 124 proteins (top 10: 37%). COILED has 10,953 from 117 (top 10: 32%). DNA_BIND has 5,220 from 99. INTRAMEM has 263 from 8 proteins. The corpus has 35 groups of identical sequences (for example AAEA_SALDC/AAEA_SALTI and ATPA_ECO7I/ATPA_ECODH), and identical pairs disagree on 8 concept columns. concept_summary.json has no per-concept protein count.
findings.recommended_action: Add n_proteins (and ideally n_clusters at about 30-50% identity) per concept to concept_summary.json and to the summary table. Back 'stable F1' with a protein- or cluster-level bootstrap of F1 for a reference feature, or soften the wording. Deduplicate or cluster the corpus before scoring.

findings.location: README.md lines 6-7 and 9-15; code/dataset.py lines 31-46; SUMMARY.md lines 44-46
findings.description: The concepts are framed as 'known residue-level properties of proteins'. The largest concepts by residue count are mostly outputs of sequence-based predictors (UniProt evidence codes ECO:0000255/0000256: profile/HMM domains, MobiDB-lite disorder and composition bias, Coils, TM predictors), not experimentally established properties. Agreement between SAE features and these labels partly measures recovery of other sequence predictors. Several concepts also mix unlike biology: TOPO_DOM combines cytoplasmic, extracellular and lumenal segments; BINDING now combines metal, nucleotide and small-molecule sites after the legacy keys were retired; REGION is half 'Disordered'. Separately, '21 of 31' counts three keys that cannot have positives.
findings.evidence: By residues: DOMAIN 91% ECO:0000255/256; COILED 97%; TRANSMEM 88%; COMPBIAS 100% computed composition classes ('Basic and acidic residues' 30%, 'Low complexity' 23%, 'Polar residues' 20%, ...); REGION 51% 'Disordered'. TOPO_DOM: Extracellular 28%, Cytoplasmic 23%+12%, Lumenal 10%+5%. CA_BIND, METAL and NP_BIND have zero FT lines in the file, so 28 concepts are possible, not 31.
findings.recommended_action: State in README and SUMMARY which concepts are curated or experimental and which are predicted, for example by splitting on evidence code. Treat the predictor-derived concepts as a separate tier. Split TOPO_DOM by side and BINDING by /ligand class, or note that they are heterogeneous. Report '21 of 28 non-empty concepts'.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 52-54 and 63-65; code/dataset.py lines 171-175 (bond endpoints)
findings.description: There is no trivial residue-identity baseline per concept. Some scored concepts are close to amino-acid identity, so a 'PTM' match can come from residue type alone. DISULFID positives are all cysteines, and MOD_RES is half serine. The summary presents DISULFID and MOD_RES as how 'PTM biology enters the scoring' without saying that a single-amino-acid detector already scores well on DISULFID.
findings.evidence: Residue identity at labelled positions: DISULFID 2,154/2,154 Cys; CARBOHYD 746/794 Asn; MOD_RES 914/1,802 Ser. A 'fires on every Cys' detector gets DISULFID F1 = 0.183 (precision 0.10, recall 1.00), the highest best single-amino-acid F1 of any scored concept (others ≤ 0.113).
findings.recommended_action: Add a best-single-amino-acid (and position-in-protein) baseline F1 per concept to concept_summary.json. Report downstream concept F1 as the gain over that baseline. For DISULFID, consider scoring against all cysteines as the background.

findings.description: Ranges whose end is unknown ('1..?') are reduced to a single residue at the start position (end = start). The docstring says entries with no resolvable position are skipped. Each such transit peptide or propeptide becomes a one-residue label at residue 1. Ranges with an unknown start ('?..124') are dropped, so the two cases are handled inconsistently.
findings.evidence: Locations that are not plain numbers include 'N..?' (11 lines) and '?..N' (8). The concept keys affected are 5 TRANSIT '1..?', 1 PROPEP '1..?' and 2 DISULFID 'N..?'. My rebuild that skips these gives TRANSIT 2,941 vs 2,946 and PROPEP 4,912 vs 4,913. The numerical effect is negligible.
findings.recommended_action: Skip ranges with an unresolvable endpoint, or flag them in a column, as the docstring describes. Keep single-endpoint handling only for bond keys.

findings.description: The code says per-residue precision/recall/F1 is computed 'as InterPLM does'. As far as I recall, InterPLM computes recall per annotated domain or instance (a domain counts as recovered if any residue fires), not per residue, for multi-residue concepts. If the downstream scorer uses per-residue recall, results will not be comparable with InterPLM, and long-span concepts (DOMAIN, REGION, TOPO_DOM) will get systematically lower recall than point concepts.
findings.evidence: build_label_matrix keeps only a flat per-residue boolean matrix. Instance or domain identity is discarded (overlapping ranges are OR-ed), so instance-level recall cannot be computed from residue_labels.npz.
findings.recommended_action: Check the scoring definition against the InterPLM method. Either store instance IDs per concept so domain-level recall can be computed, or remove the 'as InterPLM does' equivalence claim.

findings.description: Reproducibility gaps. The script that sampled the 5,000-protein corpus, and its seed, are missing. The script that made the flat-file subset is missing. The Swiss-Prot release number is not recorded (only 'downloaded July 2026'). No package versions are pinned. The activation extractor is not included. The README says row alignment with the activation cache matters for 'every downstream number', but the only check is that the total row count matches (line 60). Per-protein lengths, BOS/EOS stripping and ordering are not checked against the cache.
findings.evidence: There are no requirements or environment files. build_labels.py asserts only labels.shape[0] == n_res. My own checks show the labels are internally consistent: corpus order equals flat-file order, all lengths match the ID lines, DISULFID positions are 100% Cys and SIGNAL always starts at residue 1. Alignment with the actual activation cache cannot be verified from this package.
findings.recommended_action: Add the corpus-sampling and subset-extraction scripts with their seed, record the UniProt release (for example 2026_03), pin the numpy version, and store per-protein lengths or accessions with the activation cache. Assert per-protein agreement (prot_index and lengths) when labels and activations are joined.

review.summary:
I reviewed B4481 (Swiss-Prot residue concept labels for scoring ESM-2 SAE features) against all ten checklist patterns. The label computation itself is correct. I rebuilt the labels independently from the flat file and they match the npz exactly for 28 of 31 columns; the other three differ by 1 to 5 residues because of how '?'-bounded ranges are parsed. Corpus order, sequence lengths, accessions and residue identities at labelled sites (DISULFID all Cys, CARBOHYD mostly Asn, SIGNAL always at residue 1) are consistent, and the headline counts (4,124/5,000 annotated; 21 concepts at or above 1e-3) are reproduced.

The problems are in what the labels mean and how the summary uses them:
- **Negative control (critical, P1/P3/P6):** Conclusion 3 cannot stand. VARIANT is scored only because 'Missing' truncation ranges label whole C-terminal tails of a few human proteins: 82% of its residues come from such ranges, 85% from 10 proteins, and 96% from human proteins. Using point variants only, VARIANT and CONFLICT both fall below the floor. MUTAGEN is 8x enriched at functional sites.
- **Missing annotation treated as negative (major, P3):** HELIX, STRAND and TURN exist only for 307 structure-annotated proteins (6.8% of residues), so these labels cannot measure secondary-structure detection.
- **Concept selection (major, P5/P8):** The prevalence floor is knife-edge and not tied to F1 stability. ACT_SITE (928 proteins) is excluded, while concepts with far fewer independent proteins are kept, and CONFLICT, MOD_RES and VARIANT are not stably included under a protein bootstrap.
- **Wrong inference unit (major, P4):** The 'stable F1' claim counts residues rather than proteins or homology clusters, and the corpus has 35 duplicate-sequence groups.
- **Concepts are mostly predictor outputs (major, P3/P9):** Most large concepts come from sequence predictors, several are heterogeneous, and three of the 31 keys are structurally empty.
- **Minor:** No residue-identity baseline (P2; a Cys detector already gets DISULFID F1 = 0.18); unknown-end ranges collapsed to one residue; the InterPLM-equivalence wording is questionable; reproducibility gaps (P10).

Pattern verdicts: P1 present and unaddressed (no chance or matched null; variation null invalid); P2 present and unaddressed; P3 present and unaddressed; P4 present and unaddressed; P5 present and unaddressed; P6 partial (no alignment or positive-control checks were done, though my checks pass); P7 present and unaddressed (single 5k sample, threshold decisions sample-dependent); P8 present and unaddressed (no sweep or CI); P9 present ('known properties', 'negative control in place', 'stable F1'); P10 present (sampling and extraction scripts, release number and package versions missing).

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect and error_detected is null. I ran code to check the findings. None shows a load-bearing error in how the labels are built or in the summary's numbers. One finding (F1) raises a real interpretive problem: on the data, the scored VARIANT 'negative control' is mostly 'Missing' truncation tails of a few human proteins.

findings.reason: I confirmed this by running code. VARIANT has 3,243 positives from 141 proteins. The top 10 proteins hold 84.8% of them, and 96.5% are in human proteins (175 human proteins in the corpus). SMAD6_HUMAN alone has 13 'Missing' ranges of the form N..496, and MYBPP_HUMAN has 518..984. Counting point positions only gives VARIANT 591 (3.7e-4) and CONFLICT 910 (5.7e-4), both below the floor. MUTAGEN residues fall in ACT_SITE/BINDING/SITE/ZN_FING/DNA_BIND 16.2% of the time against a 2.0% base rate. The key does say that filling VARIANT/CONFLICT ranges is correct label construction, so the recommendation to use point positions only conflicts with the key. The core point still holds and is not in the key: the scored 'negative control' is essentially a few human protein tails, so Conclusion 3 ('negative control is in place') is a weak and possibly misleading control. It is an interpretive problem, not a label-construction bug.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm. Treating unannotated residues as negatives (HELIX/STRAND/TURN exist only for proteins with a solved structure) is a real limitation of UniProt ground truth, to be graded as a caveat, not as a load-bearing error. The numbers check out: 307 proteins (6.8% of residues) have any secondary-structure label, and HELIX covers about 29% of residues within them.

The finding attacks the 1e-3 prevalence floor and the resulting set of 21 concepts as arbitrary. The key says the floor is a design choice stated in the README, and that ACT_SITE (9.6e-4) is truly just below it. The supporting data are accurate: ACT_SITE has 928 proteins with 3.7% of positives in the top 10. But claiming the floor or the concept selection is an error is a listed false alarm. 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' is accurate under the stated rule.

The protein counts and concentration figures check out: ZN_FING 99 proteins, COILED 117, PROPEP 124, INTRAMEM 8. The corpus has 35 groups of identical sequences, which disagree on 7 concept columns in my check (the finding says 8). The word 'stable' is not backed by any analysis, so this is a fair wording caveat. It shows no error in the labels or the numbers.

The evidence-code shares check out: DOMAIN 91%, COILED 97% and TRANSMEM 88% of residues come from ECO:0000255/256 (sequence-predicted) annotations. Pointing out that many concepts are predicted rather than experimental is a fair interpretive caveat. The SUMMARY already explains why CA_BIND/METAL/NP_BIND are empty, and the key confirms they are correctly empty, so '21 of 28 non-empty' is only a wording nitpick.

Verified: all 2,154 DISULFID positives are Cys, a 'fires on every Cys' detector gets F1 0.183, and the best single-amino-acid F1 for every other scored concept is 0.113 or lower. Adding a residue-identity baseline is a reasonable suggestion for the downstream scoring. The labels are correct (key fact), so this is a minor caveat.

The key states that an unknown end ('1..?') is read as the start position only, and that fuzzy and unresolvable records touch 77 of 40,063 concept records with no change to any conclusion. The finding itself says the effect is negligible. The small mismatch between the docstring and the code is true but trivial.

This concerns how the downstream scoring compares with InterPLM's recall definition (per domain vs per residue), and that scoring is outside this package. It touches only a docstring claim. It does not affect the labels or the summary numbers, and the finding hedges its own claim.

These are reproducibility gaps: no sampling script, no release number, no pinned package versions. The finding itself confirms the labels are internally consistent and does not claim the rows are misaligned, which the key says they are not. True but minor.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key's status is "clean" and its error field is null, so there is no documented error to detect and error_detected is null. I reran the label parsing from the flat file to check what the findings claim. Reported counts match within small differences. For example, I find 7 concept columns where duplicate sequences disagree, against the 8 F4 reports, and 28.8% helix coverage within annotated proteins, against 29.7% in F2. No finding shows an error in label construction or in the summary's numbers. F2 (unannotated residues counted as negatives) and F3 (the arbitrary 1e-3 floor) match items on the key's list of possible false alarms. F7 matches the fuzzy-bound handling the key says touches only 77 records and changes no conclusion.

findings.reason: I confirmed the evidence by running code. VARIANT has 3,243 positives but only 591 point positions (prevalence 3.7e-4). Its top 10 proteins hold 85% of positives and 96% are in the 175 human proteins. SMAD6 'Missing' ranges such as 14..496 dominate. CONFLICT excluding 'Missing' ranges is 1.03e-3, and 16.2% of MUTAGEN residues fall in functional sites against a 2.0% base rate. The key says filling VARIANT/CONFLICT ranges is correct construction, so the recommendation to use point positions only is not a construction fix. The key says nothing on whether these keys make a valid negative control. A control made mostly of deleted tails from about 10 human proteins, plus the doubtful premise that PLMs ignore variant or mutagenesis sites, really does weaken Conclusion 3. Calling it 'critical' and saying the conclusion 'does not hold' overstates this.

The facts are correct: 307 proteins (6.8% of residues) carry HELIX, STRAND or TURN, and 876 proteins (177,736 residues) have no concept label. The key lists 'unannotated residues treated as negatives (HELIX/STRAND only for solved structures)' as a real limitation to treat as a caveat, not as a detection or a load-bearing error. The finding's 'major' framing goes beyond that.

This is a critique of the 1e-3 floor. The key lists 'claiming the 1e-3 floor ... is an error' as a false alarm, because the floor is a design choice stated in the README. The key also confirms that ACT_SITE (9.6e-4) is truly just below the floor, so the summary's statement that catalytic residues are not tested is accurate under the stated rule. The protein counts are correct (ACT_SITE has 928 proteins), but no reported result is wrong.

The counts are correct: ZN_FING has 99 proteins with the top 10 holding 37%, INTRAMEM has 8 proteins, and there are 35 groups of identical sequences. I find 7 disagreeing columns, not 8. Residues are not independent, and 'stable F1' is unsupported wording. Still, every scored concept spans at least 73 proteins and the duplicates are 0.7% of the corpus. This is a statistical caveat or wording point, not an error in the package.

Confirmed: by residues, DOMAIN is 91% ECO:0000255, COILED 97%, TRANSMEM 88% and COMPBIAS 100% ECO:0000256. CA_BIND, METAL and NP_BIND have zero FT lines. So the largest concepts largely come from sequence predictors rather than being experimentally 'known' properties. That is a real interpretive caveat the package does not mention. The finding does not claim that the count of 21 is wrong. '21 of 28 non-empty' is a style suggestion.

Confirmed: all DISULFID positives are Cys, a 'fires on every Cys' detector gets F1 = 0.183, 746 of 794 CARBOHYD positives are Asn, and 914 of 1,802 MOD_RES positives are Ser. These facts match the key and show nothing wrong with the labels. Adding a residue-identity baseline is a reasonable suggestion for downstream scoring, not a problem in this stage.

Confirmed: 5 TRANSIT, 1 PROPEP and 2 DISULFID records of the form 'N..?' are read as their start only, and '?..N' records are skipped. The key describes exactly this handling and says it changes no conclusion. The finding itself calls the effect negligible. The mismatch with the docstring is a small documentation point.

This concerns a docstring remark comparing the method to InterPLM. InterPLM does compute recall at the domain level for multi-residue concepts, so 'as InterPLM does' is loose. Scoring happens downstream and is not part of this package, and no result here depends on it.

These are reproducibility and documentation gaps: the sampling script, the UniProt release number and package versions are missing. The finding explicitly says the labels are internally consistent and does not claim any misalignment, which the key confirms is absent. These are true but minor.

grade_c.detection_reason: The key marks B4481 as clean, with no documented error, so there is nothing to detect. I rebuilt the label matrix from the package code and it matched outputs/residue_labels.npz exactly. Every summary number is correct. Most of the review's own numbers check out against the data: VARIANT has 591 point positions, its top 10 proteins hold 85% of positives, 96% are human, 307 proteins carry secondary-structure labels, ACT_SITE spans 928 proteins, there are 35 groups of duplicate sequences, and a fires-on-every-Cys detector gets DISULFID F1 of 0.183. But none of the findings shows a load-bearing error in how the labels were built or in the summary's numbers. The three findings that claim a headline is wrong (F1, F2 and F3) rest on points the key covers. Filling VARIANT and CONFLICT ranges residue by residue is correct. Unannotated residues counted as negatives is a known caveat. The 1e-3 floor is a design choice stated in the README.

findings.reason: The numbers are right. The package code rebuilds a VARIANT count of 3,243 with only 591 point positions. The top 10 proteins hold 85% of positives and 96% are human. SMAD6 14..496 is a 'Missing' variant, and MUTAGEN is enriched about 8x at functional sites. But the key says VARIANT and CONFLICT ranges are real contiguous stretches, so filling them residue by residue is correct. The fix the review proposes (point positions only) goes against that. Conclusion 3 only says that two variation keys clear the floor and are used as the control, and that is true. MUTAGEN is not scored, so its enrichment does not affect any conclusion. Calling the negative control invalid is an interpretive overreach, not an error in label construction.

The numbers are right: 307 proteins (6.8% of residues) carry HELIX, STRAND or TURN, and about 29% of residues inside those proteins are helix. But the key says that treating unannotated residues as negatives is a real limitation of using UniProt as ground truth, not an error in label construction. It tells graders to treat this as a caveat, neither a detection nor a load-bearing error. The 876 proteins with no concept labels are also a known true fact in the key.

ACT_SITE does sit at 9.55e-4 and spans 928 proteins, and other included concepts cover fewer proteins. But the key lists 'claiming the 1e-3 floor is an error' as a possible false alarm, because the floor is a design choice stated in the README. It also says ACT_SITE and MUTAGEN are genuinely just below the floor. 'Catalytic residues are therefore not tested' is literally true under the stated rule.

The facts are confirmed: ZN_FING and DNA_BIND each come from 99 proteins, INTRAMEM from 8, and there are 35 groups of identical sequences. But this only challenges the soft word 'stable' in the README's design rationale. INTRAMEM is not scored, and duplicate sequences are normal in a uniform Swiss-Prot sample. No label or number is wrong. It is reasonable advice to report protein counts, not an error.

The evidence-code point is real: DOMAIN, COILED and COMPBIAS evidence lines are almost all ECO:0000255/256, while HELIX evidence is experimental. TOPO_DOM and BINDING are also heterogeneous. That is a caveat on how to interpret the concepts, not an error in the package. The summary already states that CA_BIND, METAL and NP_BIND are empty legacy keys, and the key confirms the count of 21 is correct, so '21 of 28' is only wording.

Confirmed: a fires-on-every-Cys detector gets DISULFID F1 = 0.183, MOD_RES has 914 serines out of 1,802 positives, and CARBOHYD is mostly Asn (consistent with the key). A residue-identity baseline is a useful suggestion for the downstream scoring stage. It does not show an error in this package.

The key itself documents that '1..?' is read as the start position and that this has a negligible effect on 77 of 40,063 records. The finding admits the effect is negligible, and the parse_features docstring mentions handling '?'. It is a trivial documentation inconsistency.

InterPLM does use domain-level recall for multi-residue concepts, so the docstring's 'as InterPLM does' is loosely worded. But the scoring happens downstream and is not in this package. The finding is hedged and does not affect any label or summary number.

The reproducibility gaps are real: the sampling script, the UniProt release number and pinned package versions are missing. But the finding does not claim misalignment, and the key confirms rows are aligned and in corpus order. These are minor provenance suggestions.

review.summary:
I reran code/sign_test.py in memory without writing any files. It reproduces outputs/run_log.txt exactly, and every number quoted in SUMMARY.md matches the outputs. I found no computational bug. The problems are in how the numbers are interpreted and attributed.

1. The conclusion ("direct causal regulatory interactions", "validated wiring diagram", "ground truth") cannot stand. In K562 there is no association across all 8,358 edges (OR 0.99) or in the top 50% (OR 1.09). A Perturb-seq knockdown measures total downstream effects, which include indirect ones, so it cannot show that an edge is direct.
2. The edge-level evidence is weak.
   - K562 fails the test that shuffles signs only within each TF (p=0.065). A Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio pooled within TFs is 1.51 (95% CI 0.91-2.51) and is not significant at any |dE| cutoff from 50% to 98%.
   - RPE1 rests entirely on MYC. Without MYC, the top-10% OR is 1.64 (p=0.42) and the within-TF OR is 1.10 (p=0.91). The TF-resampled interval (0.71-14.25) includes 1. So the claim that the result "holds in both cell lines" fails.
3. The headline test statistics treat edges as independent: the Fisher p-values, the across-edge shuffle and the edge-level bootstrap of balanced accuracy. Under a TF-cluster bootstrap, the RPE1 balanced-accuracy interval becomes [0.458, 0.771], which includes chance.
4. The signs are not DoRothEA's own. 99.5% of the signed rows carry a CollecTRI source, against 0.04% of rows without CollecTRI. In practice the test uses CollecTRI's signs merged in by OmniPath, on the roughly 7% of DoRothEA edges that CollecTRI also covers.
5. Smaller issues:
   - In K562, activation targets go down only 49.6% of the time, so the stated prediction holds only for inhibition edges.
   - The level A vs D comparison has no statistical test and is confounded by which TFs contribute the edges.
   - The baselines are not real benchmarks: the random-sign score is a single draw, and "always predict down" is mechanically tied to the database sign's own score.
   - Ranking by |dE| favours noisy profiles from few cells and TFs with no sign of being knocked down. This does not overturn the result but undermines interpretation 2.

findings.description: The conclusion that CRISPRi 'confirms DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions' and that the signed network is 'a validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth' is not supported. (a) Perturb-seq measures the transcriptome about a week after knockdown. It captures total effects, direct and indirect (other TFs, cell-cycle or cell-state shifts), so agreement in sign cannot show that an edge is direct. (b) In K562 most scored edges show no association at all. Any agreement exists only in a top-10% |dE| subset chosen after looking at three strata, and even there it is not significant at the edge level once TF composition is held fixed (see F2). The conclusion goes far beyond 836 of 8,358 edges in one line and a single-TF effect in the other.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt, K562: all edges OR 0.99 (Fisher p 0.89, TF CI 0.87-1.13); top 50% OR 1.09 (p 0.31); only the top 10% (836 edges) has OR 2.31. Within-TF shuffle p = 0.065 (K562). Across |dE| cutoffs from 50% to 98%, the Mantel-Haenszel OR pooled within TFs in K562 is never significant (0.95-2.31, p 0.10-0.57). Nothing in the code separates direct from indirect effects.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the claims about direct causation, 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. Restate the result as: modest agreement in sign for large responses, mostly at the between-TF level in K562 and driven by MYC in RPE1, with no association across most edges. If directness matters, add binding or timing evidence (for example ChIP, or early time points).

findings.description: The claim that the result replicates in both cell lines does not hold. In RPE1 the whole top-10% effect, including the within-TF test it 'passes', comes from one TF, MYC. The within-TF test only has information from the 9 TFs that have both classes, not the 26 TFs quoted. In K562 the within-TF test fails. So neither line shows edge-level sign agreement that survives control for TF clustering, beyond a single TF.
findings.evidence: RPE1 top 10%: MYC alone has 8 of 9 inhibition edges up versus 18 of 73 activation edges up (OR 24.4, p 3e-4). Without MYC: table [[43,47],[9,6]], OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42. Mantel-Haenszel OR within TFs is 4.24 (p 0.003) with MYC and 1.10 (CI 0.22-5.49, p 0.91) without it. sign_rpe1.json gives n_tfs_with_both_classes = 9. The TF-resampled CI (0.71-14.25) and a TF-cluster-robust logistic fit (p = 0.054) are both non-significant. K562: within-TF shuffle p 0.065; Mantel-Haenszel within TF 1.51 (0.91-2.51), p 0.097.

review.summary:
The code reproduces its own outputs. An independent recomputation of the scored edges matched all 8,358 K562 and 1,866 RPE1 edges, with identical signs and dE within 2e-8, and every number in SUMMARY.md matches run_log.txt and the JSON files. The problems are in what the summary concludes from those numbers.

1. The headline claims ("CRISPRi confirms DoRothEA edges as direct causal regulatory interactions", "validated wiring diagram ... ground truth") do not follow from the data:
   - Across all edges K562 shows no association (OR 0.99), and top-50% shows none either (OR 1.09).
   - Even in the top 10%, K562 activation edges are at chance (50.4% go up). These are 86% of the edges.
   - Edge-level agreement in K562 fails the within-TF null (p = 0.065).
   - A knockdown response cannot separate direct from indirect regulation.
2. The "replication" in RPE1 rests on one TF. Without MYC, the top-10% OR falls from 4.06 to 1.64 (Fisher p = 0.42, within-TF p ≈ 0.63). The TF-resampled intervals for both the OR and the balanced accuracy include chance.
3. The signs being tested are mostly not DoRothEA's own. In the OmniPath table, 20,208 of the 20,242 signed rows also come from other curated resources, mainly CollecTRI and TRRUST. DoRothEA-only edges are almost never signed.
4. The quoted confidence intervals and p-values treat edges as independent, so they are too narrow.
5. The level A vs D claim is untested and, in RPE1, confounded with MYC.
6. Smaller issues: the random baseline is a single random draw; cell counts are ignored; the reason given for the null all-edge result is untested; trivial baselines that beat the database sign are left out.

findings.description: The summary concludes that CRISPRi 'confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions' and that the signed network is 'a validated wiring diagram' usable as 'ground truth'. Neither claim is supported. (1) A pseudo-bulk knockdown response includes indirect, downstream effects, so it cannot show that an edge is direct. (2) Most edges show no agreement at all. (3) The overall accuracy is modest. (4) Agreement at the level of individual edges is not established in K562 (see F3).
findings.evidence: K562 all edges: OR 0.99, Fisher p 0.89, TF-resampled CI 0.87-1.13. K562 top 50%: OR 1.09, CI 0.90-1.31 (run_log.txt). Only the top-10% stratum, 836 of 8,358 edges, shows an association. Top-10% balanced accuracy is 0.599 in K562, and 0.547 when balanced over the observed up/down classes. K562 top-10% activation edges: 364 up / 358 down (acc_activating 0.496); level D activation 0.442. K562 within-TF shuffle p = 0.065 (null median 1.76). No analysis in the code separates direct from indirect effects.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the 'direct causal' and 'ground truth / validated wiring diagram' language. At most, say that in the largest-response stratum, inhibition-labelled targets go up more often than activation-labelled ones. Most edges and all activation edges show no measurable agreement, and the design cannot tell direct regulation from indirect.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 47-49 (Interp. 1), 53-56 (Interp. 3), 62-63 (Interp. 6), 67-68 (Conclusion 'in two cell lines ... OR 4.1')
findings.description: The RPE1 result, presented as replication in a second cell line, depends entirely on one TF, MYC. MYC supplies 82 of 187 top-10% edges and 8 of the 17 inhibition edges that went up. With MYC removed, the association disappears. The summary mentions MYC's share but never tests what happens without it, and still says 'the result holds in both cell lines'.
findings.evidence: RPE1 top 10%, recomputed from outputs/edges_rpe1.csv. With all TFs: OR 4.06 (table 61/102, 17/7). Without MYC: table 43/47, 9/6, OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42. Rerunning stratum_stats on the data without MYC gives within-TF p ≈ 0.63, across-edge p ≈ 0.27, TF-bootstrap CI [0.50, 6.5]. Balanced accuracy without MYC: 0.561. MYC on its own: activation 18 up / 55 down, inhibition 8 up / 1 down. Even with MYC, the TF-resampled OR CI is 0.71-14.25, and a TF-cluster bootstrap of balanced accuracy gives [0.459, 0.768].
findings.recommended_action: Report a leave-one-TF-out analysis (at least without MYC). State that RPE1 does not independently replicate the effect beyond MYC. Drop 'holds in both cell lines' and the cross-line OR 4.1 headline, or qualify them.

findings.description: Interpretation 1 rests on the across-edge shuffle ('both well above the across-edge shuffle'). That null ignores TF-level confounding: TFs labelled mainly as repressors whose knockdown raises expression broadly. In K562 most of the OR is between-TF. The within-TF null, which the code's own docstring calls the test of edge-level information, is not significant. The conclusion still treats the edges as confirmed.
findings.evidence: K562 top 10%: within-TF null median 1.76, 95th percentile 2.31 (equal to the observed value), p = 0.065; the same with seeds 1 and 2 (0.0655, 0.065). Only 37 of 151 TFs have both classes. Edges of TFs with a single label class give OR 4.2, versus 1.99 for edges of mixed-class TFs. The Mantel-Haenszel OR within mixed TFs is 1.51. Taking the top 10% of |dE| within each TF instead of pooled gives OR 1.29 (K562) and 1.64 (RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Make the within-TF (or a TF-stratified, e.g. Mantel-Haenszel or mixed-model) analysis primary. State plainly that K562 gives no significant edge-level evidence. Remove 'well above the shuffle' as headline support.

findings.description: The claim that the database's 'activation/inhibition edges' are confirmed does not hold for activation edges. These are 86% of the scored edges. In K562 they do not move in the predicted direction more often than chance, even in the top-10% stratum. Any signal comes from 114 inhibition edges.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt, K562 top 10%: activation 364 up / 358 down (acc_activating 0.496); level D activation accuracy 0.442 (more activation targets go up than down); level A 0.559. K562 MYC activation targets in the top 10%: 59 up / 73 down. Inhibition: 80 up / 34 down.
findings.recommended_action: Report agreement separately by sign class. State that activation labels show no agreement in K562 at any stratum and that support is limited to inhibition labels.

findings.location: README.md line 5 and line 19; SUMMARY.md lines 1, 5, 58, 67-68

Edges coming only from DoRothEA are almost never signed. The analysis therefore tests mostly CollecTRI/TRRUST-derived signs on a selected ~7% subset of DoRothEA edges, not 'DoRothEA's label'. Conclusions about 'the signed DoRothEA network' do not carry over to DoRothEA as a whole.

Only 34 signed rows are DoRothEA-only, against 246,154 unsigned DoRothEA-only rows. Of the K562 scored edges, 99.8% have a non-DoRothEA source, most often CollecTRI2 (8,014) and ExTRI2_CollecTRI2 (5,738).

findings.description: The 'random sign' baseline is one random draw, not its expectation (0.5). The reported values of 0.453 and 0.406 are sampling noise below chance, which makes the database sign look better relative to 'random' than it is.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt: the random baseline's CIs [0.403, 0.501] (K562) and [0.307, 0.511] (RPE1) are centred well below 0.5. The expected balanced accuracy of a random sign is 0.5 by construction.

findings.description: Cell counts per profile (7 to 894 cells) are never used. Guide profiles are averaged without weights, and the |dE| strata ignore measurement precision. Noisy profiles with few cells are therefore over-represented in the 'top 10%' stratum.
findings.evidence: K562: 9.3% of top-10% edges come from TFs with fewer than 50 cells, against 1.5% of all edges; median cells 123 (top) vs 188 (rest). Ranking by dE*sqrt(cells) instead gives OR 2.2 (K562) and 4.76 (RPE1), so the headline ORs barely change, but the strata definition is not precision-aware.
findings.recommended_action: Weight guide averaging by cell count. Define strata on a precision-scaled statistic, or report this as a sensitivity analysis.

findings.description: The null result across all edges is called 'expected' because near-zero changes are noise. That explanation is not tested. Other explanations are plausible: ineffective knockdowns, or TFs not expressed in the cell line. No knockdown-efficacy or expression filter is applied. Separately, pooled |dE| strata mostly select TFs with strong effects rather than strong edges.

findings.recommended_action: Filter or stratify by observed knockdown of the TF and by TF expression. Reword Interpretation 2 as a hypothesis.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's documented error is the causal and validation overreach in SUMMARY.md: Interpretation 4 says CRISPRi 'confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions', and the Conclusion calls the signed network a 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. F1 names these exact claims and gives every reason the detection rule accepts. (1) A knockdown response includes indirect and downstream effects, and nothing in the package separates direct from indirect. (2) Agreement is modest and appears only in the top 10%: all-edge OR 0.99 in K562, and balanced accuracy 0.599. (3) The K562 within-TF shuffle gives p = 0.065. F3 points at the Conclusion (lines 67-68) treating the edges as confirmed. It argues reason (3): the K562 within-TF null is not significant, so edge-level agreement is not shown. Both meet the rule. F2 attacks the 'holds in both cell lines' claim (Interpretation 6), which overlaps part of the key's error. But it rests mainly on MYC dominance and does not challenge the direct-causal or validated-network wording, so I count it separately as a real robustness problem.

findings.reason: This is the key's planted error: the 'direct causal' and 'validated wiring diagram / ground truth' claims at Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion. F1 gives detection reasons (1) knockdowns measure total effects, (2) agreement is modest and limited to the top 10% (K562 all-edge OR 0.99, balanced accuracy 0.599), and (3) the K562 within-TF p is 0.065. All the numbers it cites match run_log.txt.

Recomputed: with MYC removed, RPE1 top 10% has a 43/47 and 9/6 table, OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF p 0.63, across-edge p 0.27, TF-bootstrap CI [0.50, 6.46]. These match the key's leave-one-TF-out figure of 1.64. So the 'holds in both cell lines' replication (Interpretation 6) rests on a single TF. The SUMMARY states MYC's share but never tests removing it. This overlaps the key's Interpretation 6 overreach, but its core argument is MYC dependence. It does not challenge the direct-causal or validated-network claim, so I do not count it as the documented detection.

This is detection reason (3). Interpretation 1 relies on the across-edge shuffle, while the K562 within-TF null (median 1.76, p 0.065) does not show edge-level agreement, yet the Conclusion treats the edges as confirmed. Verified: single-class TFs give OR 4.2 versus 1.99 for mixed-class TFs, and the Mantel-Haenszel OR within the 37 mixed TFs is 1.51. The key's known facts agree that about two thirds of the log OR comes from each TF's label mix. It does not claim clustering was ignored; it says the conclusion overrides the within-TF result.

Verified: K562 top-10% activation edges split 364 up / 358 down, and K562 MYC activation targets split 59 up / 73 down. The 'activation/inhibition edges confirmed' claim therefore has no support for activation labels in K562. The key lists the inhibition-class pattern as a true description, not an error on its own, and it is not enough for detection. Used here against the conclusion, it is a genuine, confirmable limitation.

Verified in dorothea_omnipath.tsv.gz: 20,242 rows are signed, but only 34 of 246,188 DoRothEA-only rows carry a sign. 99.8% of the K562 scored edges list a non-DoRothEA source, and 99.3% include CollecTRI. The tested signs are therefore OmniPath-merged signs on a subset of DoRothEA edges, not DoRothEA's own mode of regulation. This is a real attribution and scope issue. It does not change any reported number.

It is true that the Fisher p, the across-edge shuffle and the within-class balanced-accuracy bootstrap treat edges as independent. However, the package computes and SUMMARY.md reports the TF-resampled OR intervals and the within-TF shuffle for every stratum. The key lists 'clustering ignored' as a false alarm. What remains is a presentation point, and the substantive part is already covered by F3.
Interpretation 5 is descriptive and already notes the small counts (20 and 7 inhibition edges). Asking for a test and noting that MYC dominates level A in RPE1 are fair but minor points.
The key's known facts confirm the random baseline is a single draw (0.453 / 0.406). The SUMMARY states that chance is 0.5, and the OR is the main statistic. The point is true but trivial.

Cell counts are indeed unused, and guide averaging is unweighted. But the finding itself reports that a precision-scaled ranking leaves the ORs essentially unchanged (2.2 and 4.76), and the key lists guide averaging as a stated choice. This is a sensitivity suggestion, not a defect.

Calling the all-edge null 'expected' is an untested gloss, and that small point is fair. But the finding's claim of 'weak or absent knockdown for many TFs' conflicts with the key: own-gene responses are negative for 97-98% of measurable TFs (11 of 297 positive by the finding's own count). It gives all three reasons in the detection rule. (1) A pseudo-bulk knockdown includes indirect and downstream effects, so it cannot show an edge is direct. (2) The all-edge OR is 0.99 with CI 0.87-1.13, agreement appears only in the top 10%, and balanced accuracy is modest at 0.599. (3) The K562 within-TF p is 0.065. It argues reason (3): the within-TF null is not significant in K562 (p = 0.065, null 95th percentile 2.31, equal to the observed OR), so edge-level agreement is not shown. I reproduced F3's numbers: 37 of 151 TFs have both classes, single-class TF OR 4.2 vs mixed 1.99, Mantel-Haenszel OR 1.51.

findings.reason: This is the planted overreach, at the exact location the key gives (Interp. 4 and Conclusion). Its target, however, is the replication claim, not the direct-causal or validated-network claim, and the key says MYC dominance and replication critiques alone do not count as detection. So I count it as a related real problem, not the documented error.

It targets Conclusion lines 67-68 ('the conclusion still treats the edges as confirmed') and Interp. 1, and argues reason (3): the K562 within-TF shuffle (p 0.065) leaves edge-level agreement unshown. I verified: within-TF q95 2.314 equals the observed OR, 37 of 151 TFs have both classes, single-class TF OR 4.2 vs mixed 1.99, MH OR 1.51. The within-TF top-10% OR came out 1.25 / 1.44 in my run, against the 1.29 / 1.64 cited, depending on how the quantile is defined. That gap is small and does not change the point.

The key treats this split as a description of the table, though, and says the inhibition-class pattern on its own does not count. However, the TF-resampled OR interval and the within-TF shuffle are computed and reported for every stratum, and the key lists 'clustering ignored' as a false alarm. This finding adds little beyond F3 and the documented error, and the main OR is unaffected. The shared-target count (221) did not match my count (355 edges whose target appears more than once), which is a minor discrepancy.

Interp. 5 is descriptive and already states that it rests on 20 and 7 inhibition edges. I verified that 62% of RPE1 level-A top-10% edges are MYC, and that 4 of the 7 level-A inhibition edges are MYC. The finding is true, but it is a small caveat on a secondary claim.

The key states that the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni over the six line-by-stratum tests (4.6e-4 and 0.020). verdicts.reason: The counts in the finding are correct. I checked them against outputs/edges_k562.csv: K562 top-10% activation edges go 364 up / 358 down (accuracy 0.496, binomial p 0.85), level D activation 230 up / 182 down (0.442), level A 109 / 138 (0.559), MYC activation 59 up / 73 down, and inhibition 80 up / 34 down. The conclusion drawn from them is not. It assumes a 50% chance level, which the data contradict. Among strong responses (|dE| >= 0.166), K562 non-target genes go up 58.5% of the time (1.11M non-DoRothEA TF x gene pairs). For the same TFs' non-targets the expected up fraction is 0.633 for activation-edge TFs and 0.641 for inhibition-edge TFs. Activation targets are well below that: Mantel-Haenszel OR 0.59 against same-TF non-targets, p = 5.6e-11 over 129 TFs (0.65, p = 9e-7 without MYC). Inhibition targets do not differ significantly from their background (MH OR 1.34, p = 0.17). So the claim that 'any signal comes from 114 inhibition edges' is not supported. Against a proper reference, the activation class carries the clearer shift in K562. The recommended statement ('activation labels show no agreement... support is limited to inhibition labels') would put a new wrong claim into the summary. Also, SUMMARY.md already reports the per-class up fractions (0.501 / 0.502 / 0.504 for K562 activation), so nothing is hidden. The answer key treats this inhibition-class pattern as a description of the table, not an error (the pattern also failed on four other datasets in the source project). The conclusion at lines 67-70 does overreach, but for other reasons: knockdowns measure total (direct plus downstream) effects, the agreement is modest and limited to the top decile, and the within-TF result is weak. The finding does not make any of these arguments.

review.summary:
I re-ran sign_test.py in memory without writing any files, and its output matches outputs/run_log.txt line for line. The edge tables also match the data. Every number quoted in SUMMARY.md matches the outputs, so the problems are in what the summary concludes from them.

- **"Direct causal" and "ground truth" go too far.** The conclusion says CRISPRi confirms DoRothEA edges as direct causal interactions and that the network can serve as ground truth. Perturb-seq cannot separate direct from indirect effects, and across all edges K562 shows no agreement at all (OR 0.99).
- **The K562 result fails the analysis's own edge-level test.** The within-TF shuffle gives p = 0.065.
- **The RPE1 result comes from one TF.** With MYC removed, the top-10% OR is 1.64 (Fisher p = 0.42, within-TF p = 0.63), and the TF-resampled interval already includes 1. So the "holds in both cell lines" claim cannot stand.
- **Activation edges show nothing in K562.** These are 83% of edges, and their targets go up and down at coin-flip rates in every stratum. The positive OR rests on 114 inhibition edges.
- **The balanced-accuracy intervals ignore clustering by TF.** Resampling TFs instead of edges gives an RPE1 interval of [0.456, 0.771], which includes chance (0.5).
- **No check that the knockdown worked.** About half the K562 TFs (214 of 429) are not in the measured genes, so the knockdown cannot be checked. Several top contributors show no knockdown or come from tiny profiles (e.g. 7 cells). Profiles are averaged without weighting by cell count.

The smaller issues concern the baselines, the level A vs D claim, the source of the signs and the choice of the top-10% stratum.

findings.description: The summary says CRISPRi "confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions" and calls the signed network "a validated wiring diagram" that "can serve as ground truth". The data cannot support either claim. A Perturb-seq pseudo-bulk profile, measured days after the knockdown, shows total downstream effects; direct and indirect regulation look the same. The design also never tests causality or directness. It only tests whether the sign agrees with the direction of change, and that agreement appears only in the top 10% of |dE|.
findings.evidence: Across all scored edges K562 shows no association: OR 0.99, Fisher p 0.89, balanced accuracy 0.499 [0.486, 0.513] (run_log.txt, 'all' rows). The only non-null stratum is 836 of 8,358 K562 edges and 187 of 1,866 RPE1 edges, out of 20,048 signed DoRothEA edges. Nothing in the code separates direct from indirect effects.
findings.recommended_action: Drop the "direct causal" and "validated wiring diagram / ground truth" wording. At most, say that among the largest knockdown responses the annotated sign is modestly associated with the direction of change, and that this does not show the regulation is direct.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 47-49, 53-54, 62-63, 67-68; outputs/run_log.txt K562 '|dE| top 10%' 2x2 row
findings.description: The script describes the within-TF sign shuffle as the test where "only edge-by-edge information is tested" (sign_test.py lines 19-22). The K562 headline fails it. Most of the observed OR (2.31) is reproduced by shuffling signs within each TF (null median 1.76). So in K562 the association is between a TF's overall mix of labels and its overall response, not between edge-specific labels and target responses. The summary still counts K562 as a confirmation, and Interpretation 1 relies on the across-edge shuffle, which ignores clustering.
findings.evidence: K562 top 10%: within-TF null median 1.76, one-sided p = 0.0650. Without MYC, within-TF p = 0.114 (my rerun of stratum_stats). Two-sided Fisher p is computed treating edges as independent, although many edges share a TF: MYC alone contributes 138 of the 836 edges.
findings.recommended_action: State that K562 does not show edge-level sign information (within-TF p = 0.065). Present any K562 association as TF-level. Make a clustered test (within-TF shuffle or TF bootstrap) the primary inference rather than Fisher or the across-edge shuffle.

findings.description: The RPE1 result comes almost entirely from one TF, MYC. Only 9 of the 26 TFs in the RPE1 top-10% stratum have both activation and inhibition edges, and MYC supplies 82 of 187 edges. Without MYC there is no association. The within-TF p = 0.0025 therefore reflects one TF, not '26 TFs'. The TF-resampled interval (0.71-14.25) already includes 1. Replication 'in two cell lines' cannot stand.
findings.evidence: My rerun of stratum_stats on RPE1 top 10% without MYC: table act 43 up / 47 down, inh 9 up / 6 down; OR 1.64; Fisher p 0.42; within-TF null median 1.64, p 0.63; TF bootstrap 0.50-6.46. MYC alone: act 18/55, inh 8/1, OR 24.4. Level A in RPE1 is also mostly MYC (43 of 69 edges; 4 of 7 inhibition edges).
findings.recommended_action: Report the RPE1 result as essentially a single-TF (MYC) observation. Add a leave-one-TF-out analysis and report which TFs carry the signal. Remove 'the result holds in both cell lines'.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 47-48 and 58 ('Removing the TF moves its annotated targets the way DoRothEA says it should'); run_log.txt K562 'act' accuracy column
findings.description: In K562 the activation label shows no agreement in any stratum. Activation targets go down no more often than they go up, even among the largest responses. Activation edges are 83% of K562 edges (6,903 of 8,358). The OR > 1 rests entirely on the 114 inhibition edges in the top-10% stratum, which themselves fail the within-TF test (F2). The general statement that knockdown moves annotated targets the way DoRothEA says is therefore false for most edges.
findings.evidence: K562 accuracy of the database sign on activation edges: 0.499 (all), 0.498 (top 50%), 0.496 (top 10%). Top-10% activation targets: 364 up vs 358 down.
findings.recommended_action: Report agreement separately for the activation and inhibition classes, and say that K562 activation edges show no sign agreement. Narrow the claim to what the inhibition class shows, with clustering taken into account.

findings.description: The 95% intervals for balanced accuracy resample edges within each class and ignore clustering by TF, so they are too narrow. The '*' flag in the log and the intervals quoted in the summary overstate precision. For RPE1, an interval that resamples TFs includes chance (0.5).
findings.evidence: Summary gives 0.667 [0.564, 0.763] for RPE1 and 0.599 [0.553, 0.645] for K562. A TF-cluster bootstrap of the same statistic (4,000 resamples) gives RPE1 [0.456, 0.771] (includes 0.5) and K562 [0.550, 0.647]. The script's own TF-resampled OR interval for RPE1 is also 0.71-14.25.
findings.recommended_action: Resample TFs for the balanced-accuracy intervals, as the code already does for the OR, and update the summary's intervals and significance flags.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 70-87 (load_response) and 162-169 (edge scoring); README Method step 1; SUMMARY.md lines 50-52
findings.description: There is no check that the knockdown worked, and cell numbers are ignored. Edges are scored for TFs whose knockdown cannot be verified, or plainly failed, or that are probably not expressed in the cell line. Profiles are averaged without weighting by num_cells_filtered, which the data folder provides but the code never uses. Because |dE| is larger for profiles with fewer cells, the top-|dE| strata are enriched for noisy profiles and for TFs whose knockdown did nothing. This leaves the explanation in Interpretation 2 ('the sign of a near-zero change is mostly measurement noise') untested, and the all-edge null is mixed with ineffective knockdowns.
findings.evidence: K562: 214 of 429 scored TFs are not among the measured genes, so their knockdown cannot be checked; 233 of 836 top-10% edges come from them (e.g. ESR1, 41 edges; SOX2, 31 edges from a 7-cell profile). MYC's own-gene response in K562 is z = -0.03 (no detectable knockdown), yet it supplies 138 top-10% edges. Spearman rho between |dE| and cell count: -0.25 (K562), -0.19 (RPE1). The result changes materially with a knockdown filter: K562 top 10% restricted to TFs with own-gene z < -0.3 gives OR 5.8 (58 TFs); TFs not measured give OR 1.18.
findings.recommended_action: Filter knockdowns on on-target reduction (the own-gene value before it is set to missing) and on expression of the TF. Weight or filter profiles by cell count. Rank responses by a standardised effect (dE times sqrt(cells), or a per-profile z) rather than raw |dE|. Re-run all strata.

findings.description: The 'random sign' baseline is a single random draw, not an expected value or a null distribution. In RPE1 it lands well below chance (0.406), which makes the database sign look better than it is. The 'always predict down' baseline, balanced over database classes, is tied to the database-sign score by construction and has no independent meaning as a comparator. Quoting either in the summary is misleading: chance is 0.5.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt top-10% random: 0.4534 (K562), 0.4059 (RPE1), each from one rng.choice draw. Always-down: 0.397 and 0.459. In RPE1 top 50%, always-down (0.603) beats the database sign (0.534), which the summary does not mention.
findings.recommended_action: Drop these baselines from the summary, or replace the random baseline with the mean and quantiles of many draws (equivalently, the sign-shuffle null).

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 38-39 and 61 (level A vs level D)
findings.description: 'Level A edges score higher than level D' is presented as showing that higher-confidence signs are more accurate. No test was run. In K562 the accuracy on inhibition edges is the same at both levels; the gap comes only from activation-edge accuracy. In RPE1, level A is dominated by MYC.
findings.evidence: K562 top 10%, inhibition accuracy: level A 14/20 (0.70) vs level D 58/85 (0.68), Fisher p = 1. Activation accuracy: 138/247 vs 182/412. RPE1 level A: 43 of 69 edges and 4 of 7 inhibition edges are MYC. Without MYC, RPE1 level D balanced accuracy is 0.43.
findings.recommended_action: Test the level difference with clustering taken into account, report it per class, or drop the claim.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 49-60 (load_signed); README Data table; SUMMARY.md title and Conclusion
findings.description: The 'DoRothEA sign' tested is not DoRothEA's own mode of regulation. It is OmniPath's is_stimulation / is_inhibition, which pools signs across resources and comes almost entirely from CollecTRI. Some scored edges also have no consensus sign in OmniPath. Conclusions about 'DoRothEA's activation/inhibition edges' are therefore misattributed.
findings.evidence: 8,296 of 8,358 scored K562 edges (and 1,828 of 1,866 RPE1 edges) list CollecTRI2 in 'sources'. 513 K562 edges (6%) and 78 RPE1 edges have consensus_stimulation = consensus_inhibition = False but are scored as signed.
findings.recommended_action: Describe the sign as OmniPath's merged sign (mostly CollecTRI). Optionally re-run with consensus signs only, or with DoRothEA's native mode-of-regulation column.

findings.description: The headline uses the top-10% stratum, the one stratum that shows an effect out of three per line (six in all). The cutoff is not justified in advance, and there is no correction for multiple strata and tests. Combined with F2 and F3, this adds to the risk that the headline is a selected result.
findings.evidence: K562 all / top 50%: OR 0.99 / 1.09 (n.s.). RPE1 top 50%: Fisher p 0.14. Only the top-10% rows are carried into the Conclusion.
findings.recommended_action: Pre-specify the threshold, or show agreement as a continuous function of |dE| (or of a standardised effect) with a clustered test, and correct for multiple comparisons.

review.summary:
I re-ran code/sign_test.py in memory without writing any files. It reproduces outputs/sign_*.json and edges_*.csv exactly, and every number in SUMMARY.md matches the log and the JSON. The problems are in inference and interpretation, not arithmetic.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1 (weak null): present and unaddressed. Interpretation 1 cites the across-edge shuffle. K562 fails the stricter within-TF null (p=0.065).
- P2 (trivial baseline): present and unaddressed. The baselines used are degenerate. A target-only baseline beats the database sign on raw accuracy.
- P3 (endpoint mismatch): present and unaddressed. A knockdown response measures total effect, direct plus indirect, yet the summary claims "direct causal" interactions.
- P4 (wrong inference unit): partly addressed. The TF-level bootstrap and within-TF null exist, but the Fisher p-values and balanced-accuracy CIs are edge-level.
- P5 (selection): present. The top-10% |dE| cut preferentially picks noisy low-cell profiles and dominant TFs. There is no filter for knockdown efficacy or TF expression.
- P6 (positive control): absent. The "no agreement across all edges" result is explained as noise without a check. It changes when TFs that were not knocked down are removed.
- P7 (single condition): present. The RPE1 result disappears without MYC.
- P8 (stability): present. Three strata only, and the claim rests on the most favourable cut. A sweep shows K562 never passes the within-TF null.
- P9 (overreach): severe. "Confirms", "direct causal", "validated wiring diagram" and "ground truth" are used.
- P10 (reproducibility): no correctness impact. The run is deterministic and reproduces exactly; versions are not pinned.

The headline conclusion cannot stand as written. The two-cell-line confirmation rests on one K562 stratum that fails the within-TF null and one RPE1 result driven by a single TF. The direct-causal / ground-truth language is not supported by this design.

findings.description: The summary claims that CRISPRi 'confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions, not correlations' and that the signed network is 'a validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth for the direction of regulation'. A knockdown response is a total effect (direct plus indirect). The test only checks whether the sign agrees, given that an edge exists; it never tests whether the edge exists or acts directly. And the agreement is absent in 90% of K562 edges.
findings.evidence: Across all K562 edges OR = 0.99 (Fisher p 0.89) and the top-50% OR = 1.09. In the K562 top-10% stratum, activation edges (722 of 836) go down only 49.6% of the time, i.e. at chance. Overall raw accuracy of the database sign there is 0.524. My check: non-target genes of the same knockdown cross the top-10% |dE| threshold at 8.0% vs 10.2% for annotated targets in K562 (6.0% vs 11.3% in RPE1). So most large responses among targets are not edge-specific, which fits generic or indirect effects. Only 20,048 of ~278k DoRothEA rows are signed. 91% of level-A rows are signed vs ~5% of level-D rows, so 'DoRothEA edges' generalises far beyond the subset tested. No binding data, direct-effect filter or time-resolved data is used.
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion at the evidence level. For example: 'for the ~10% largest knockdown responses, inhibition-labelled targets are more often up-regulated than activation-labelled targets; this is consistent with the DoRothEA sign for a subset of edges'. Drop 'direct', 'causal', 'confirms', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. State that the activation label carries no information in K562, and that only the signed subset was tested.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 49, 53-56, 62-63, 67-68 (claims that the result holds in both cell lines; conclusion 'in two cell lines (top-10% OR 2.3 and 4.1)')
findings.description: The two-line replication does not hold at the TF level, which is the right unit. K562 fails the within-TF null. The RPE1 result is carried almost entirely by one TF (MYC), and its TF-resampled interval includes 1.
findings.evidence: K562 top-10%: within-TF null median 1.76, observed 2.31, p = 0.065. RPE1 top-10%: TF-bootstrap 95% CI 0.71-14.25. My re-analysis without MYC (105 edges, 15 inhibition, 25 TFs): OR 1.64, across-edge p 0.27, within-TF p 0.62. A TF-cluster bootstrap of the RPE1 top-10% balanced accuracy gives [0.459, 0.769], which includes 0.5; the summary reports the edge-level [0.564, 0.763]. Both lines come from one study and one assay.
findings.recommended_action: Report a leave-one-TF-out analysis, especially without MYC, and TF-level CIs for every headline number. Restate the finding as 'not significant against the within-TF null in K562; in RPE1 driven by MYC'. Remove 'holds in both cell lines' unless a TF-level test supports it.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 33 and 47-49; code/sign_test.py lines 118 and 121
findings.description: Interpretation 1 anchors the headline ORs to the across-edge sign shuffle and the edge-level Fisher test. Both ignore that edges cluster within TFs. The stricter within-TF null shows that most of the K562 OR comes from TF-level composition (TFs with more inhibition labels have more up-responses overall), not from edge-specific sign information.
findings.evidence: K562 top-10%: across-edge null median 1.02 (p 0.0005) vs within-TF null median 1.76 (p 0.065). The within-TF null's 95th percentile (2.314) equals the observed OR. The Fisher p = 7.7e-5 treats 836 edges from 151 TFs as independent.
findings.recommended_action: Make the within-TF null (or a TF-level test) the primary comparison for every headline claim, and report the Fisher/across-edge p only as secondary. Name the null family next to each p-value in the summary.

findings.description: The balanced-accuracy 95% intervals come from resampling edges within each database class. TFs, the non-exchangeable unit, are ignored, so the intervals are too narrow (pseudoreplication). The same applies to the starred 'CI > 0.5' flags in the log.
findings.evidence: RPE1 top-10%: reported edge-level CI [0.564, 0.763] vs TF-cluster bootstrap CI [0.459, 0.769], which includes chance. In RPE1, 82 of 187 top-10% edges come from MYC.
findings.recommended_action: Resample by TF, as in tf_bootstrap_ci, for the balanced-accuracy intervals. Report n edges / n TFs / n inhibition edges with every interval.

findings.description: The baselines are degenerate and no meaningful simple comparator is given. 'Always predict down' and a single random draw are not chance anchors. A target-only predictor that ignores the TF entirely beats the database sign. The summary also omits strata where 'always down' equals or beats the database sign.
findings.evidence: Top-10% raw accuracy of the database sign: 0.524 (K562) and 0.636 (RPE1). Predicting each target's direction from the sign of its mean response across all other knockdowns gives 0.632 and 0.668. The random-sign 'baseline' is one draw (0.453, 0.406; RPE1 CI 0.307-0.511), so its value is noise. In RPE1, always-down balanced accuracy equals the database sign across all edges (0.5416 vs 0.5416) and beats it in the top-50% stratum (0.603 vs 0.534).
findings.recommended_action: Report a permutation-based chance distribution for balanced accuracy, ideally within-TF. Add a trivial target-level and TF-level direction baseline. Report the database sign's increment over those baselines, and state the strata where it adds nothing. Avoid 'predicts the direction' for K562, where the activation label is at chance.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 70-87 and 162-169 (no knockdown/expression filter; guide_info unused); SUMMARY.md lines 50-52
findings.description: The analysis never checks whether the TF is expressed in the cell line or actually knocked down, and never uses the cell counts in *_guide_info.csv. Guides are averaged without weighting. As a result, noise from TFs that were not knocked down dilutes the 'all edges' result. Interpretation 2's explanation ('expected: the sign of a near-zero change is mostly measurement noise') is never tested, and the alternative explanation is not considered. Ranking by |dE| also favours low-cell, noisy profiles.
findings.evidence: In K562, 214 of 429 scored TFs have no measured own-gene column, i.e. they were probably not expressed. They supply 233 of 836 top-10% edges and 50 of 114 inhibition edges, with OR 1.18 (p 0.74), vs OR 3.37 for TFs whose own gene is measured. Restricted to measured TFs, the K562 top-10% passes the within-TF null (OR 3.27, null median 1.76, p 0.017). For TFs with own-gene z < -0.4, K562 all-edge OR is 1.44 (p 0.012); RPE1 is mixed at that cut (OR 0.91). MYC in K562 has own-gene z = -0.03 yet supplies 138 top-10% edges. Spearman(cells, |dE|) = -0.25 in K562; median cells 123 in the top 10% vs 185 overall. The SOX2 profile has 7 cells and supplies 31 top-10% edges. TFs with a <50-cell guide make up 16.6% of top-10% edges vs 7.8% overall.
findings.recommended_action: Filter on, or stratify by, on-target knockdown (own-gene z) and TF expression in each line. Weight or filter profiles by num_cells_filtered, or rank by a variance-scaled statistic. Re-report all strata, and either test or drop the 'near-zero noise' explanation.

findings.description: The headline rests on one post hoc response-magnitude cut (top 10% of pooled |dE|), selected on the outcome magnitude, out of three strata. There is no sensitivity sweep and no multiplicity correction. The pooled cut also concentrates the stratum on a few large-effect TFs.
findings.evidence: My sweep (within-TF null p; TF-bootstrap CI): K562 top 30/20/15/10/5/3% give p = 0.19/0.14/0.15/0.06/0.20/0.27, so the within-TF null is never passed and 10% is the most favourable cut. RPE1 TF-bootstrap CIs include 1 at every cut from top 50% to top 3%. MYC supplies 138/836 (K562) and 82/187 (RPE1) top-10% edges. Six line×stratum tests are reported without correction.
findings.recommended_action: Report a threshold sweep with the worst case. Use per-TF or variance-scaled thresholds. Correct for the multiple strata, or pre-register one. Restrict claims to the threshold range where the TF-level test holds; on present evidence there is none in K562.

findings.description: 'Level A edges score higher than level D' is stated without a test. K562 shows no monotone confidence trend, and the RPE1 contrast is dominated by MYC.
findings.evidence: K562: TF-bootstrap CI for bal(A) - bal(D) is [-0.05, 0.18]; inhibition-edge accuracy A 14/20 vs D 58/85 (Fisher p = 1.0). K562 levels B (0.844) and C (0.658), omitted from the summary, both exceed A (0.629). RPE1: 43 of 69 level-A edges are MYC edges.
findings.recommended_action: Report all levels with TF-clustered CIs and a formal comparison. Hedge or drop the A > D statement.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 5, 58, 67-69; README.md data table (dorothea_omnipath.tsv.gz); code/sign_test.py lines 49-67
findings.description: The summary treats the labels as 'DoRothEA's' signs. In the OmniPath export, though, is_stimulation/is_inhibition is a merged attribute whose supporting resources include CollecTRI, TRRUST, SIGNOR and others. Those resources were curated mostly outside K562/RPE1, and the curation context is not stated.
findings.evidence: The sources column of the signed rows is dominated by entries such as CollecTRI2 (19,661), ExTRI2_CollecTRI2 and TRRUST. 91% of level-A rows are signed vs 5-8% of level B-D rows. The analysis tests only this curated, literature-backed subset (7.2% of rows).
findings.recommended_action: State the provenance of the sign labels and that the tested set is the literature-signed subset. Tag the curation context, and do not generalise to DoRothEA as a whole or to unsigned edges.

This is a fair provenance and wording caveat ('DoRothEA's signs' are a merged OmniPath attribute), but it is a minor presentation point.

grade_c.detection_reason: F1 targets Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion (SUMMARY.md 57-60, 67-70): 'confirms ... direct causal regulatory interactions', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. It gives reason (1): a knockdown response is a total effect (direct plus indirect), so the design cannot show an edge is direct. It also gives reason (2): there is no agreement across all K562 edges (OR 0.99, p 0.89), and the activation label is at chance in the K562 top 10%. It asks for the wording to be downgraded. That meets the rule cleanly. F2 targets the Conclusion's 'confirms ... in two cell lines (top-10% OR 2.3 and 4.1)' and Interpretation 6. It gives reason (3): K562 fails the within-TF null (p 0.065), and the RPE1 TF-resampled CI 0.71-14.25 includes 1. It uses MYC dominance to support reason (3), not as a standalone point. That also meets the rule. I re-ran checks with the package code and data. F2's numbers hold: without MYC, OR 1.64 on 105 edges (15 inhibition, 25 TFs); across-edge p 0.27; within-TF p 0.62. The TF-cluster bootstrap of RPE1 balanced accuracy is about [0.458, 0.773]. F1's figures for activation edges going down (358/722) and for raw accuracy (0.524) also hold.

findings.reason: Targets the planted overreach directly: 'confirms direct causal', 'validated wiring diagram', 'ground truth' in Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion. It gives key reason (1) (total effect, direct plus indirect, with nothing that separates them) and reason (2) (K562 all-edge OR 0.99; activation label at chance in the top 10%). Supporting numbers check out: 358/722 activation edges go down, raw accuracy is 0.524, 20,242 of 278,677 rows are signed, and 91% of level-A rows vs about 5% of level-D rows are signed. One side figure is off: I get about 8.4% non-target threshold crossing in RPE1, not the 6.0% stated. This does not affect detection.

Attacks the Conclusion's 'in two cell lines (top-10% OR 2.3 and 4.1)' and Interpretation 6 (part of the key's error location) using reason (3). K562 within-TF p is 0.065, and the RPE1 TF-resampled CI 0.71-14.25 includes 1. MYC dominance is used to argue reason (3), which the rule allows. Verified: without MYC, OR 1.64 (43/47 vs 9/6), across p 0.27, within-TF p 0.62. The TF-cluster bootstrap CI for RPE1 balanced accuracy is about [0.458, 0.773], which includes 0.5. It also notes that both lines come from one study.

Argues that Interpretation 1 ('predicts', line 47) rests on the across-edge shuffle and Fisher test, while the within-TF null shows that most of the K562 OR comes from each TF's label mix. That is true: the key's own facts say about 2/3 of the log OR is reproduced by the TF label mix. The key lists line 47 'predicts' as part of the same overreach, and this is reason (3). The finding does not target Interpretation 4/Conclusion or the validated/ground-truth wording, so on its own it does not meet the detection rule. It does not claim the analysis ignored clustering, so it is not the 'clustering ignored' false alarm.

True: the balanced-accuracy CIs (code lines 202-208) resample edges within each database class and ignore TF clustering. With a TF-cluster bootstrap, the RPE1 top-10% CI widens to about [0.458, 0.773], which includes 0.5, while SUMMARY.md quotes [0.564, 0.763]. The K562 CI still excludes 0.5 under TF resampling ([0.548, 0.643]). Not in the key. It does not overturn a headline on its own, because the TF-resampled OR interval is already reported.

The target-only baseline numbers reproduce (0.632 / 0.668 vs database-sign raw accuracy 0.524 / 0.636). But that is a data-driven comparator scored on raw accuracy, and the OR, which is the main statistic, already measures what the label adds. Always-down below 0.5, the single random draw, and RPE1 always-down matching or beating the database sign all follow from the tables and are in the run log. The key lists these as possible false alarms. The suggestion for permutation-based chance baselines is reasonable but minor.

Verified: there is no expression or knockdown filter and guide_info is unused. 214 of 429 K562 TFs have no own-gene column; their top-10% edges (233, 50 inhibition) give OR 1.18. Measured TFs give OR 3.37, within-TF p about 0.01. MYC's own-gene z in K562 is -0.03. Spearman(cells, |dE|) is -0.25. The median cell count is 123 in the top 10% vs 185 overall. SOX2 has 7 cells and 31 top edges. This does not claim the test is invalid, so it is not the key's false alarm. It is consistent with the key fact that filtering raises the OR. It is a genuine omission that weakens Interpretation 2's untested noise explanation, but it does not threaten the headline. If anything it would strengthen the sign association.

The core premise, that the headline rests on a post hoc single cut with no multiplicity correction, is contradicted by the key's facts. The strata select on |dE| only, all three are reported, and the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni over the six tests. My sweep also shows the K562 Fisher-level association is significant and grows steadily across all cuts from top 30% to top 3% (p 0.005 to 7.7e-5). So the result is not a threshold artifact. The sweep numbers it gives are accurate: the K562 within-TF p is never below 0.05 at any cut, and the RPE1 TF CIs include 1 at every cut. That repeats the already-disclosed TF-level weakness, which is the documented error's reason (3). It is not a new threshold-selection problem.

True but minor: Interpretation 5 (level A > D) is untested. K562 inhibition accuracy is A 14/20 vs D 58/85 (no difference). K562 levels B (0.844) and C (0.658) exceed A and are left out of the summary. 43 of 69 RPE1 level-A top edges are MYC. Interpretation 5 is a secondary claim and already notes the small inhibition counts.

Verified: in the OmniPath export the sign attributes are merged across resources. Almost all signed rows list CollecTRI/TRRUST sources (20,136 of 20,242 contain 'CollecTRI'). Only 7.3% of rows are signed, and 91% of level-A rows are signed vs 5-8% of levels B-D. This is a fair provenance and scope caveat but does not change any result.

review.summary:
I reviewed B4668 (does the DoRothEA activation/inhibition sign predict the direction of CRISPRi knockdown responses in the Replogle K562 and RPE1 data) against all ten checklist patterns. I re-ran code/sign_test.py in memory without writing any files, and its log matches outputs/run_log.txt exactly. Every number quoted in SUMMARY.md matches the outputs. The problems are in how the results are interpreted and in which nulls, baselines and inference unit the claims rest on.

The main claims cannot stand:
(a) The causal language is unsupported: "CRISPRi confirms DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions" and "validated wiring diagram / ground truth" (P3, P9). Knockdown responses mix direct and indirect effects, edge existence was never tested, and the sign has no predictive value for about 90% of K562 edges (OR 0.93).
