(b) The "holds in both cell lines" claim fails (P4, P7). K562 fails the within-TF null (p = 0.065) at every threshold from 2% to 50%. The RPE1 result comes entirely from MYC: without MYC, OR = 1.64, Fisher p = 0.42, within-TF p = 0.62. RPE1's TF-resampled confidence interval also includes 1.

Further problems, by checklist pattern:
- P1/P4: the headline rests on the across-edge shuffle and Fisher p, which treat edges as independent. The balanced-accuracy interval is bootstrapped over edges; resampled by TF, the RPE1 interval includes chance.
- P6: there is no check that the knockdown worked. In K562, MYC's own expression is unchanged (dE = -0.03), yet MYC supplies 138 of the 836 top-10% edges. Keeping only TFs with a confirmed knockdown changes the K562 within-TF result.
- P2: the baselines are degenerate ("always down" and one random draw). A TF-level baseline that ignores the database sign matches the database sign's balanced accuracy in K562.
- P8/P5: the odds ratio depends on the threshold, the headline is the best of three nested strata, and ranking by raw |dE| favours profiles with few cells.
- Minor: the claim that level A edges beat level D is untested and selective. Package versions and the data-cutting script are missing (P10).

findings.description: Overreach (P3/P9). The summary says CRISPRi 'confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions' and that the signed network is 'a validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth for the direction of regulation'. The analysis supports none of this. (1) A pseudo-bulk knockdown response averaged over many cells captures direct and indirect (downstream) effects; nothing here separates direct targets (no ChIP-seq, no time course). (2) Only the sign of edges assumed to exist was tested. No test checks that DoRothEA targets respond more than non-targets, so edge existence is not 'validated'. (3) Agreement is limited to a subset of edges: across all edges the K562 OR is 0.99, and K562 activation edges, 86% of the headline stratum, are at chance even in the top 10%. (4) The curation context of the DoRothEA edges (many level-D, inferred or from other cell types) is not matched to K562/RPE1.
findings.evidence: run_log: K562 all edges OR 0.99 (Fisher p 0.89; TF-bootstrap CI 0.87-1.13). My recomputation over the bottom 90% of K562 edges by |dE| (7,522 edges) gives OR 0.926. K562 top 10%: 'act 0.496', i.e. 364 up / 358 down for activation edges (frac up 0.504). Within-TF null p = 0.065. code/sign_test.py scores only sign agreement on DoRothEA edges (lines 163-169); there is no comparison with non-target genes.
findings.recommended_action: Remove 'direct', 'causal', 'confirms', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. Restate the claim as: in the largest-|dE| decile, inhibition-labelled edges go up more often than activation-labelled edges, which is consistent with the sign labels for a minority of edges; for most edges the sign does not predict the direction of the knockdown response. If edge validity is to be claimed, add a test of target vs non-target response magnitude, and use ChIP-seq or a time-resolved design for any 'direct' claim.

findings.description: The claim that 'the result holds in both cell lines' is not supported (P7/P4). K562 does not pass the within-TF null. The RPE1 signal comes entirely from one TF, MYC: removing MYC eliminates it. In RPE1 only 9 of 26 TFs have both edge classes, so the within-TF test there is mainly a MYC test. Each line fails one of the two TF-aware tests (K562 the within-TF shuffle; RPE1 the TF-resampled CI), so neither line gives TF-level confirmation. The summary reports MYC's 44% share but never checks whether the result survives without MYC.
findings.evidence: My recomputation on outputs/edges_rpe1.csv, top 10%: with all TFs, OR 4.06. Without MYC: n = 105, 15 inhibition edges, OR 1.64, Fisher p = 0.42, within-TF p = 0.62, TF-bootstrap CI 0.51-6.46. Leave-one-TF-out: dropping MYC gives OR 1.64; dropping any other TF leaves OR 3.5-5.4. RPE1 TF-bootstrap CI 0.71-14.25 (run_log) includes 1, and so does every threshold I swept (2%-50%). K562 within-TF p = 0.065 at the top 10% and 0.07-0.74 at thresholds of 2%, 5%, 15%, 20%, 30% and 50%.
findings.recommended_action: Report leave-one-TF-out results (at least without MYC) for both lines, and state that the RPE1 effect depends on MYC. Drop 'holds in both cell lines' and 'in two cell lines'. Present K562 as not passing the within-TF test, and RPE1 as a single-TF result whose TF-level interval includes 1. Add a held-out condition with more TFs before making a generalisation claim.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 47-49 (Interpretation 1), 26-29 (Fisher p column), 33; code/sign_test.py lines 118 and 121
findings.description: The headline significance is anchored to the weakest null, and edges are treated as the unit of inference (P1/P4). Interpretation 1 rests on 'well above the across-edge shuffle', and the table shows Fisher p values; both treat edges as independent. But edges cluster within TFs: 836 edges from 151 TFs in K562 and 187 from 26 in RPE1, with large global per-TF effects. The within-TF null has a median of 1.76 in K562, so most of the apparent OR is explained by TF-level composition. Only the TF-aware tests are appropriate, and they do not agree (see F2). Fisher p values (two-sided) and permutation p values (one-sided) are also mixed in one table.
findings.evidence: run_log K562 top 10%: across-edge null median 1.02 (p = 0.0005), but within-TF null median 1.76 and q95 2.314, essentially equal to the observed 2.31 (p = 0.065). Fisher p = 7.7e-5 vs within-TF p = 0.065. Only 37 of 151 K562 TFs and 9 of 26 RPE1 TFs have both classes (sign_*.json n_tfs_with_both_classes).
findings.recommended_action: Make the within-TF null and the TF-cluster bootstrap the primary inference. Give the number of TFs and the number of mixed-class TFs next to every claim, and report Fisher and across-edge p values only as edge-level supplements. Alternatively, fit a GLM with standard errors clustered by TF that adjusts for each TF's global response direction.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 83-86 (own-gene response set to NaN), README.md Method step 1; SUMMARY.md Interpretations 1-3
findings.description: There is no positive control and no check that the knockdown worked (P6). The script discards each TF's response in its own gene instead of using it to confirm the knockdown. TFs with no measurable knockdown, TFs not expressed in the cell line, and profiles with very few cells all enter the test, so many 'edges' are pure noise. This dilutes the K562 result and makes the K562 null result (all edges) uninterpretable. It also changes the conclusion: keeping only TFs with a confirmed knockdown, the K562 within-TF test passes.
findings.evidence: From data/k562_tf_knockdown_response.csv.gz: MYC's own-gene dE = -0.03 (one profile, 99 cells), i.e. no knockdown. Yet MYC supplies 138 of the 836 K562 top-10% edges and 70 of the 267 level-A top-10% edges. 187 K562 top-10% edges come from TFs whose own dE > -0.2, and 233 from TFs whose own gene is not measured (e.g. ESR1, SOX2, CEBPA; SOX2 = one 7-cell profile). GATA1 (erythroid) is scored in RPE1. Restricting to own dE < -0.3: K562 top-10% (re-thresholded) OR 5.96, within-TF p = 0.001, TF-bootstrap CI 3.06-20.6; all such K562 edges OR 1.19.
findings.recommended_action: Add a knockdown-efficacy filter, pre-registered rather than tuned on the result (e.g. own-gene z below a cutoff, or the release's knockdown QC). Report how many TFs and edges are excluded, and use on-target knockdown as the positive control. Exclude TFs not expressed in the cell line, and rerun all strata.

findings.description: There is no meaningful trivial baseline (P2). The comparators are 'always predict down' and one random sign draw. Scored as balanced accuracy over database classes, 'always down' is guaranteed to look bad whenever inhibition targets go up, so it is not an informative floor. The random baseline is a single draw: 0.453 and 0.406 are reported as if they were chance levels, but its expected value is 0.5. The natural simple comparator is a TF-level predictor that ignores the edge's sign and predicts each target's direction from the TF's overall response; it is not run. In K562 it matches the database sign.
findings.evidence: My recomputation on the top 10%: predicting each edge's direction from the majority direction of that TF's large-|dE| non-target genes gives balanced accuracy 0.614 in K562 (database sign 0.599) and 0.601 in RPE1 (database sign 0.667). The run_log 'random' rows show 0.4534 and 0.4059 in one draw each. Logistic regression with TF-clustered standard errors: the inhibition label keeps an effect in K562 (coef 0.87, p < 0.001) but is only marginal in RPE1 (p = 0.056).
findings.recommended_action: Replace the random-draw baseline with its expectation (0.5) or a distribution of draws. Add the TF-global-direction baseline and report the database sign's improvement over it, with a TF-clustered interval. State plainly that a sign-free TF-level predictor reaches the same balanced accuracy in K562.

findings.description: The negative results are understated or explained away (P9: own the negatives). Interpretation 1 says the database sign 'predicts the direction of the strongest responses', but in K562 the effect comes only from inhibition edges (114 of 836). Activation edges, 86% of the stratum, are at chance. Interpretation 2 explains the all-edge null post hoc ('expected... measurement noise') without testing it. In RPE1, the database sign does no better than always predicting down in the all-edges stratum, and worse than always-down in the top-50% stratum; this is not mentioned.
findings.evidence: run_log K562 top 10%: activation accuracy 0.496 (364 up / 358 down). K562 bottom-90% OR 0.926 and 10-50% band OR 0.944 (my recomputation). RPE1 all: database sign balanced accuracy 0.5416 = always-down 0.5416. RPE1 top 50%: database sign 0.534 vs always-down 0.603.
findings.recommended_action: State as findings that the activation label carries no directional information in K562 at any stratum, and that for most edges the sign is uninformative. Show the RPE1 always-down comparison. Test the noise explanation (e.g. stratify by |dE|/SE or by cell count) instead of asserting it.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 40 and 183-184 (strata on raw |dE|); SUMMARY.md lines 14-15, 47-49, 68 ('top-10% OR 2.3 and 4.1')
findings.description: The headline numbers depend on the threshold and come from the most favourable of three nested strata, with no multiplicity correction (P8/P5). The OR rises steadily with the |dE| cutoff, so 'OR 2.3 and 4.1' describe the chosen cutoff rather than the data. The strata also rank by raw mean z (|dE|), which does not account for how many cells are behind each profile. Profiles with few cells have noisier means, so they are over-represented in the top stratum. There is no minimum cell count (profiles with 7 cells are included), and guide profiles are averaged without weighting by cell count.
findings.evidence: My threshold sweep for K562: OR 1.09 / 1.38 / 1.63 / 1.86 / 2.31 / 2.50 / 4.11 at the top 50 / 30 / 20 / 15 / 10 / 5 / 2%. RPE1: 1.33 → 7.00 over the same thresholds. The TF-aware tests never pass together at any threshold. TFs with fewer than 50 cells supply 9.3% of K562 top-10% edges vs 1.5% of all edges. Median cells per TF: 123 for top-10% edges vs 185 for all edges. Profiles have as few as 7 cells (k562_guide_info.csv).
findings.recommended_action: Pre-specify one threshold or report the full sweep, with the worst case in the summary. Stratify by a noise-scaled statistic (dE·sqrt(cells), or the release's own p values), set a minimum cell count, and weight guide averages by cell count. Correct for the multiple strata and lines tested.

findings.description: The balanced-accuracy confidence intervals come from resampling edges within each class, ignoring clustering by TF (P4). The RPE1 interval quoted as excluding chance does not exclude it once TFs are resampled, which also casts doubt on the '*' significance markers in the log.
findings.evidence: Reported RPE1 top-10% interval [0.564, 0.763]; my TF-cluster bootstrap (2,000 resamples) gives [0.457, 0.771]. K562: reported [0.553, 0.645], TF-cluster [0.548, 0.643].
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap balanced accuracy by TF, as is already done for the OR, and update the summary. RPE1 balanced accuracy is not distinguishable from 0.5 at the TF level.

findings.description: The claim that level A edges score higher than level D is untested and selectively reported. In K562, levels B (0.844) and C (0.658) both exceed A (0.629) but are left out, so there is no monotone confidence trend. Level A in RPE1 is mostly MYC, and level A in K562 includes 70 MYC edges from a profile with no knockdown.
findings.evidence: K562 level A minus level D balanced accuracy = 0.067, TF-cluster bootstrap CI [-0.05, 0.185], which includes 0. In RPE1, MYC supplies 43 of 69 level-A edges and 4 of 7 level-A inhibition edges. run_log K562 level B 0.8438 (4 inhibition edges), C 0.6581.
findings.recommended_action: Report all levels with TF-clustered intervals and test the A vs D difference. Drop or qualify Interpretation 5 (K562: not significant; RPE1: MYC-driven).

findings.location: README.md lines 21-28 (data cutting) and 62 (dependencies); README line 19 (OmniPath download)
findings.description: Reproducibility scaffolding is incomplete (P10). The code that cut the response matrices from the full Replogle release (row/column selection, removal of non-finite genes, handling of duplicate names) is not included. Package versions are not pinned, and the OmniPath/DoRothEA table is identified only by its download month, with no version. The analysis script itself does reproduce the logged results exactly.
findings.evidence: There is no preprocessing script or requirements/environment file in the folder. My in-memory re-run of sign_test.py reproduced run_log.txt with zero differing lines.
findings.recommended_action: Add the extraction script, a requirements file with versions, the OmniPath and DoRothEA versions or query, and the source release file names and checksums.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the key's detection rule. It targets Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion: the 'direct causal regulatory interactions', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth' claims. It gives reason (1): a pseudo-bulk knockdown response includes direct and indirect/downstream effects, and there is no ChIP-seq or time course to separate them. It gives reason (2): the K562 all-edge OR is 0.99, and agreement holds only for a subset (the top decile). It also notes that edge existence is never tested. F2 also counts. It targets Interpretation 6 and the Conclusion sentence ('confirms ... direct causal regulatory interactions in two cell lines'), which the key lists as part of the planted overreach. It argues reason (3): the K562 within-TF shuffle p is 0.065, the RPE1 TF-resampled interval of 0.71-14.25 includes 1, and the RPE1 OR drops to 1.64 without MYC. So neither line gives TF-level confirmation. I recomputed all of F2's numbers: OR without MYC 1.64, within-TF p about 0.59, TF-bootstrap interval about 0.52-6.7, other leave-one-TF-out ORs 3.52-5.41, and 9 of 26 TFs carrying both classes.

findings.reason: This is the planted causal/validation overreach (SUMMARY 57-60, 67-70). It gives key reason (1), indirect/downstream effects with no ChIP or time course, and reason (2), K562 all-edge OR 0.99 with agreement only in the top decile. Its supporting numbers match the run log and my recomputation (K562 bottom 90% OR 0.926; activation edges 364 up / 358 down).

It targets Interpretation 6 and the 'in two cell lines' Conclusion, which the key lists as part of the error location. It argues key reason (3): K562 fails the within-TF shuffle and the RPE1 TF-resampled interval includes 1. I confirmed the MYC dependence: RPE1 top-10% OR without MYC is 1.64, with a non-significant within-TF test and TF interval. Dropping any other single TF leaves OR 3.52-5.41. The RPE1 TF interval includes 1 at every threshold, and only 9 of 26 RPE1 TFs carry both classes.

This is one facet of the key's overreach: line 47 ('predicts') is listed as the same overreach. It argues that Interpretation 1's significance rests on edge-level tests (Fisher, across-edge shuffle), while the within-TF null (median 1.76 vs observed 2.31, p 0.065) reproduces most of the K562 OR. That is key reason (3). It does not target the direct-causal, validated or ground-truth claim, so it does not meet the detection rule by itself. Its wording that edges are 'treated as the unit of inference' is overstated, because the summary table does report the TF-aware tests.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm ('knockdown efficiency was not checked so the test is invalid'). Own-gene responses are negative for 97-98% of the TFs where this can be checked, and dropping weak knockdowns raises the OR. The reviewer's numbers are accurate: K562 MYC own-gene dE is -0.032; 187 top-10% edges come from TFs with own dE above -0.2 and 233 from TFs whose own gene is not measured; filtering to own dE below -0.3 gives OR 5.96 with within-TF p 0.001. But this cuts in favour of the analysis. The claim that the K562 results are 'uninterpretable' or noise-driven is not a real defect, and a post hoc filter that strengthens the result does not correct the summary's claims.

Confirmed in code/sign_test.py lines 202-208: the balanced-accuracy bootstrap resamples edges within each class, not TFs. A TF-cluster bootstrap gives about [0.47, 0.77] for RPE1 top 10%, which includes 0.5, while SUMMARY line 35 quotes [0.564, 0.763]. The key covers TF clustering only for the OR tests. This affects a secondary statistic, not the headline OR.

I verified that a sign-free TF-level predictor (majority direction of each TF's large non-target responses) reaches balanced accuracy 0.614 in K562, against 0.599 for the database sign, and 0.601 in RPE1 against 0.667. This is a fair point that the always-down and single-random-draw baselines are weak comparators. It does not claim a bug, so it is not the listed false alarm. It largely restates the TF-composition effect that the reported within-TF shuffle already captures, and the reviewer's own logistic regression keeps a significant label effect in K562.

Confirmed. The K562 level B (0.844) and C (0.658) balanced accuracies exceed level A (0.629) and are left out of the summary. The K562 A-minus-D difference of 0.067 has a TF-bootstrap interval of about [-0.05, 0.18], which includes 0. In RPE1, MYC supplies 43 of 69 level-A edges and 4 of 7 level-A inhibition edges. So Interpretation 5 is untested and partly MYC-driven. It is a secondary claim.

The facts are correct: K562 top-10% activation accuracy is 0.496, K562 bottom-90% OR is 0.926, Interpretation 2's noise explanation is asserted without a test, and RPE1 all-edge database sign equals always-down (0.5416). But SUMMARY already reports the 50% activation rate and the all-edge null. The key lists the RPE1 always-down and top-50% comparison as a non-issue (it is in the run log, and the OR is in SUMMARY). This is mainly a criticism of emphasis.

The threshold sweep (K562 OR 1.09 to 4.11) and the over-representation of few-cell profiles in the top stratum (9.3% vs 1.5% of edges from TFs with fewer than 50 cells) are verified. However, all three strata are reported, the strata select on |dE| only, and the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni correction over the six tests. So the multiplicity and cherry-picking concerns do not overturn anything. Noise from few-cell profiles would bias toward OR = 1, not inflate it. The suggestion to scale by noise is reasonable but minor.

It is true that the package has no extraction script and no pinned versions. But the key confirms the data are an exact subset of the release, and the script reproduces the outputs byte for byte. This is a reproducibility-hygiene point only.

grade_b.detection_reason:
F1 clearly meets the detection rule. It quotes the exact overreach in Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion ('confirms ... direct causal regulatory interactions', 'validated wiring diagram', 'ground truth'). It gives reason (1): a pseudo-bulk knockdown captures direct and indirect downstream effects, and nothing here separates them. It also gives reason (2): the all-edge K562 OR is 0.99, agreement is confined to the top decile, and the bottom-90% OR is 0.926. Its K562 within-TF p of 0.065 further supports reason (3).

F2 also meets the rule, but only through one facet of the planted error. It targets the Conclusion's 'in two cell lines' and Interpretation 6, which the key names as part of the overreach. It argues reason (3) with the key's numbers: K562 within-TF p is 0.065, and the RPE1 TF-resampled CI of 0.71-14.25 includes 1. It uses MYC dominance only to support reason (3) (without MYC, OR 1.64), which the rule allows.

I re-ran checks on outputs/edges_*.csv. They confirm F2's numbers: no-MYC RPE1 OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF p about 0.61, TF-bootstrap CI about 0.5-6. They also confirm the K562 bottom-90% OR of 0.926.

findings.reason: This is the planted P9 overreach (key reasons 1 and 2, plus 3). It names the claims in Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion ('direct causal', 'validated wiring diagram', 'ground truth'). It states that a knockdown captures direct plus downstream effects with no way to separate them, and that agreement is absent across all K562 edges (OR 0.99). The supporting numbers are correct: activation edges are 86% of the top decile (722/836) at 364 up / 358 down, I recomputed the bottom-90% OR as 0.926, and within-TF p is 0.065.

It targets Interpretation 6 and the Conclusion's 'in two cell lines', both part of the key's error location, and argues reason (3): K562 fails the within-TF test and the RPE1 TF-level interval includes 1. All quantitative claims check out. RPE1 without MYC: OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF p about 0.61, TF-bootstrap CI about 0.5-6. The RPE1 TF CI includes 1 at every threshold from 2% to 50%. K562 within-TF p is 0.075-0.76 across the threshold sweep, never below 0.05. Only 9 of 26 RPE1 TFs carry both classes. MYC dominance is used to support reason (3), not on its own.

Interpretation 1 does rest its claim on the across-edge shuffle ('well above the across-edge shuffle') and on edge-level Fisher p. The key lists line 47 ('predicts') as the same overreach and notes that about two thirds of the K562 log OR is reproduced by the TF label mix (within-TF null median 1.76, q95 about 2.31). F3 does not claim TF clustering is ignored; it acknowledges the TF-aware tests exist and argues they should be primary, so it avoids the listed false alarm. It does not point at the causal/validation claim, so on its own it does not meet the detection rule. The mixing of one-sided and two-sided p values is a minor sub-point.

This is confirmed. The balanced-accuracy CI resamples edges within each class (code lines 202-208), ignoring TF clustering, unlike the OR interval. My TF-cluster bootstrap gives RPE1 top-10% [0.457, 0.771], which includes 0.5 (reported: [0.564, 0.763]), and K562 [0.548, 0.643], matching the finding. The issue is real but concerns a secondary statistic. The summary already reports the TF-resampled OR interval including 1 for RPE1.

The main point is confirmed. A sign-free predictor that takes each TF's majority direction among large-|dE| non-target genes reaches balanced accuracy 0.614 in K562 (database sign 0.599) and 0.601 in RPE1 (database sign 0.667). So in K562 the label adds nothing over TF-level response direction, in line with the within-TF null. F5 does not claim that always-down below 0.5 or the single random draw is a bug, which would be a listed false alarm. It only calls them uninformative baselines, which is fair but minor. I did not verify the logistic-regression sub-claim.

The facts are true: the K562 MYC own-gene dE is -0.032; 187 top-10% edges come from TFs with own dE > -0.2 and 233 from TFs whose own gene is unmeasured; the own<-0.3 filter gives OR 5.96, within-TF p about 0.002, CI about 3.2-20.7. It sits close to the key's listed false alarm ('knockdown efficiency not checked so the test is invalid'): the key states that 97-98% of measurable knockdowns have a negative own-gene response, and filtering raises the OR. F4 argues the result is diluted, not invalid, and its numbers match the key's. 'No check that knockdown worked' and 'K562 all-edge null uninterpretable' overstate the issue. It is a reasonable QC suggestion that would, if anything, strengthen the result, and does not reveal an error.

The threshold sweep is confirmed: K562 OR 1.09/1.38/1.63/1.86/2.31/2.50/4.11 and RPE1 1.33 to 7.00. The few-cell over-representation is also confirmed: TFs with fewer than 50 cells supply 9.3% vs 1.5% of edges, median 123 vs 185 cells, and the smallest profile has 7 cells. However, all three strata are reported, the strata select on |dE| only, and per the key the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni over the six tests. The 'most favourable stratum, no multiplicity correction' framing is overstated. Noise scaling is a reasonable refinement, not an error.

Partly true: K562 top-10% activation edges are at chance (0.496), so 'predicts' is generous, and the noise explanation in Interpretation 2 is untested. But the summary does own the negatives: it states K562 shows no agreement across all edges, gives the weak RPE1 all-edge OR with its interval, and reports the shrunken K562 within-TF margin. The point that RPE1 always-down equals or beats the database sign and is 'not mentioned' matches the key's listed false alarm. Both values are in the run log and follow arithmetically from the tables (inhibition split 122/122; top-50% stratum OR 1.33 reported).

This is true but minor. The summary omits levels B and C (0.844 and 0.658 in K562). My TF-cluster bootstrap of the K562 A-minus-D difference gives [-0.05, 0.18], which includes 0. In RPE1, MYC supplies 43 of 69 level-A edges and 4 of 7 level-A inhibition edges (confirmed). The summary already hedges with 'on 20 and 7 inhibition edges'. The RPE1 A-minus-D difference does exclude 0 at the TF level ([0.15, 0.54]).

This is accurate: the package has no extraction script and no pinned package versions, and the OmniPath table is identified only by download month. These are reproducibility-scaffolding gaps only. The finding itself correctly notes that sign_test.py reproduces the logged outputs exactly.

grade_c.detection_reason: F1 clearly meets the detection rule. It targets Interpretation 4 (SUMMARY.md:57-60) and the Conclusion (67-70), quoting 'confirms ... direct causal regulatory interactions', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. It gives reason (1): a pseudo-bulk knockdown response includes direct and indirect (downstream) effects, and no ChIP-seq or time course separates them. It also gives reason (2): the K562 all-edge OR is 0.99 and agreement is confined to a subset of edges. It asks for the wording to be downgraded. F2 also meets the rule, though less centrally. It targets Interpretation 6 and the Conclusion's 'confirms ... in two cell lines', both part of the key's error location, and uses reason (3) with the key's own numbers: K562 within-TF p = 0.065, and an RPE1 TF-resampled interval of 0.71-14.25 that includes 1. It uses MYC dependence to support reason (3), which the rule allows, not on its own.

findings.reason: This is the planted overreach, at the exact location the key gives (Interpretation 4 and Conclusion). It cites reason (1), total vs direct effects with nothing to separate them, and reason (2), all-edge K562 OR 0.99 with agreement only in the top decile. The numbers it cites match the run_log, and I reproduced the bottom-90% OR of 0.926.

It attacks the 'holds in both cell lines' / 'in two cell lines' part of the Conclusion and Interpretation 6, which the key lists as part of the error, using reason (3). I verified: RPE1 without MYC gives n = 105, 15 inhibition edges, OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF p about 0.61 and TF-bootstrap about 0.51-6.2. The K562 within-TF test fails at the other thresholds (I got p 0.14-0.75, against the stated 0.07-0.74, a small discrepancy). 'Eliminates' slightly overstates an OR of 1.64, but the substance is right.

Its point is that Interpretation 1 ('predicts ... well above the across-edge shuffle') leans on edge-level tests while the TF-aware tests are weak: K562 within-TF null median 1.76 vs observed 2.31, p = 0.065. That is the key's reason (3) applied to SUMMARY.md:47, which the key lists as 'the same overreach'. The evidence matches the run_log and JSON. It is not counted as a detection because it does not target the direct-causal / validated-network claim. The phrase 'edges treated as unit of inference' borders on the key's false alarm that clustering is ignored, but the body acknowledges that both TF-aware tests are reported. Mixing two-sided Fisher p and one-sided permutation p in one table is documented in the README and trivial.

Verified: MYC's own-gene dE in K562 is -0.032 (one profile), yet MYC supplies 138 of 836 top-10% edges (70 of 267 at level A). 187 top-10% edges come from TFs with own dE > -0.2 and 233 from TFs whose own gene is unmeasured. GATA1 contributes 29 RPE1 edges. Restricting to own dE < -0.3 gives K562 top-10% OR 5.96, within-TF p about 0.002, TF CI about 3.1-16. The finding does not claim the test is invalid (the key's false alarm). It says the result is diluted and conservative, which agrees with the key's known fact that dropping weak knockdowns raises the OR. So the missing knockdown QC is a genuine but non-overturning gap. 'Pure noise' and 'uninterpretable' overstate it, and the -0.3 cutoff is post hoc.

The new substantive point is verified. A sign-free baseline that predicts each edge from the majority direction of the TF's large-|dE| non-target genes gives balanced accuracy about 0.613 in K562 (database sign 0.599) and about 0.595 in RPE1 (stated 0.601; database 0.667). This shows TF-level composition, which agrees with the within-TF null. The remarks that always-down is uninformative and that the random baseline is a single draw are true, but the key treats them as arithmetic or disclosed, not errors. The finding does not claim a bug.

The facts are true but already visible in the SUMMARY table or the run_log. K562 top-10% activation edges at 0.504 up is a description of the table, and the key says the inhibition-class pattern alone is not the error. RPE1 always-down tying or beating the database sign at all edges and top 50% is in the run_log, and the key lists calling it hidden as a possible false alarm. The point that the noise explanation in Interpretation 2 is asserted rather than tested is fair but minor.

The threshold sweep is verified (K562 OR 1.09 to 4.11, RPE1 1.33 to 7.00), and so are the cell-count facts: under-50-cell TFs supply 9.3% of top-10% edges vs 1.5% of all, median 123 vs 185 cells, minimum 7 cells. But all three strata are reported, the strata select on |dE| only, the dependence on response size is stated in Interpretation 2, and the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni over six tests (key). Noisier few-cell profiles would dilute sign agreement, not create it. The 'most favourable stratum / no multiplicity correction' concern does not change the headline.

Confirmed in code (lines 202-208): the balanced-accuracy intervals resample edges within each database class and ignore TF clustering. My TF-cluster bootstrap gives RPE1 [0.461, 0.774], which includes 0.5, and K562 [0.548, 0.643], matching the finding. So the quoted RPE1 balanced-accuracy interval [0.564, 0.763] is anti-conservative. Impact is limited because the TF-resampled OR interval (0.71-14.25) is already reported and is the main statistic.

Interpretation 5 is literally true (level A 0.629 > D 0.562 in K562; 0.863 > 0.564 in RPE1) and it states the small inhibition counts. Omitting levels B and C (both above A in K562) and having no formal A-vs-D test are fair but minor points about a secondary claim. The MYC share of RPE1 level A is a true caveat.

True: there is no extraction script and no pinned versions. But the README describes the cut, the key confirms the data are an exact unchanged subset of the release, and the analysis reproduces. This is a minor reproducibility-scaffolding point.

review.summary:
I reviewed the DoRothEA-sign vs CRISPRi Perturb-seq analysis (B4668) against all ten checklist patterns, re-running checks inline on the shipped data and outputs. Every number quoted in SUMMARY.md matches run_log.txt and the JSON outputs, and the code does what the README says. I found no arithmetic bugs: the OR orientation, the within-TF shuffle and the TF bootstrap are all implemented correctly. The problems are in inference and in the claims.

Verdicts by pattern:
- P1 (weak null): present and unaddressed. The headline relies on the edge-level Fisher test and the across-edge shuffle. Under the stricter TF-aware tests K562 does not pass (within-TF p=0.065; Mantel-Haenszel by TF OR 1.51, 95% CI 0.91-2.51).
- P2 (trivial baseline): present. The baselines given score below chance, and no TF-matched background is shown.
- P3 (endpoint mismatch): present and unaddressed. The summary reads a total knockdown response as proof of direct causal edges.
- P4 (pseudoreplication): present. Fisher p values and balanced-accuracy intervals are computed per edge. A per-TF interval for RPE1 balanced accuracy includes 0.5.
- P5 (selection / confounding): present. The pooled top-10% cut is dominated by a few high-effect TFs, and between-TF composition drives much of the pooled OR.
- P6 (positive control): absent. Whether the TF was actually knocked down is never checked. Non-expressed TFs (ESR1, SOX2) and MYC with an own-gene response of -0.03 in K562 are scored anyway.
- P7 (generalisation): the claim that the result holds in two cell lines fails because the RPE1 result depends on MYC alone (without MYC: OR 1.64, p=0.42, within-TF p=0.64).
- P8 (stability): the effect is threshold-dependent with no multiplicity correction. The TF-stratified OR in K562 is not significant at any threshold.
- P9 (overreach): severe. The summary says "confirms ... direct causal regulatory interactions" and "validated wiring diagram ... ground truth", and buries the null result for activation edges.
- P10 (reproducibility): minor gaps. The script that cut the data is missing, package versions are not pinned, and the OmniPath version is not recorded.

findings.description: P3/P9 endpoint mismatch and causal overreach. The summary concludes that CRISPRi 'confirms that DoRothEA edges are direct causal regulatory interactions, not correlations' and that the signed network is 'a validated wiring diagram' that 'can serve as ground truth'. A Perturb-seq pseudo-bulk z-score taken days after CRISPRi measures the total effect of a knockdown, direct plus indirect, so sign agreement cannot show that an edge is direct. Only an aggregate association was tested, never individual edges. The association appears only in the top 10% of |dE| (836 of 8,358 edges in K562, 187 of 1,866 in RPE1); across all edges K562 shows OR 0.99. Also, only about 7% of DoRothEA rows carry a sign (20,048 signed pairs out of ~278k rows), and DoRothEA is a context-free resource not curated for K562 or RPE1.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt: K562 all-edge OR 0.99 (Fisher p 0.89); top-50% OR 1.09 (p 0.31). DoRothEA file: 257,029 rows are neither stimulation nor inhibition, 16,766 stimulation-only, 3,476 inhibition-only. No directness filter (ChIP, time course) is applied anywhere in code/sign_test.py.
findings.recommended_action: Restate the conclusion at the level of evidence: 'in the strongest-responding edges, DoRothEA inhibition labels are enriched for up-regulation after TF knockdown, consistent with the annotated sign (total, not direct, effect)'. Remove 'direct causal', 'confirms', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. Say explicitly that edges were not validated one by one and that most edges show no agreement.

findings.description: P1/P4/P5: the K562 headline (top-10% OR 2.31) does not survive TF-aware nulls. The pooled OR mixes edges across TFs, so TFs that carry many inhibition labels and also tend to up-regulate genes overall inflate it. The script's own within-TF shuffle has a null median of 1.76 and gives p = 0.065 (not significant), yet the summary says the observed value 'beats it' and treats the across-edge shuffle as the reference ('both well above the across-edge shuffle'). A Mantel-Haenszel OR stratified by TF, which I computed from edges_k562.csv, is not significant at any |dE| threshold. The TF-resampled interval 1.51-3.57 does not answer this, because resampling whole TFs keeps the between-TF composition effect in every resample.
findings.evidence: run_log: K562 top 10% within-TF null median 1.76, q95 2.314 (equal to the observed value), p 0.0650. My Mantel-Haenszel by TF on the top-10% edges: OR 1.51 (95% CI 0.91-2.51), p = 0.13 on 27 informative TFs. Other thresholds: top 30% OR 1.14 (0.88-1.48); top 20% 1.21 (0.87-1.70); top 5% 1.42 (0.71-2.84); top 2% 2.31 (0.66-8.08). Against a TF-matched background, strongly responding genes of these TFs go up 61-62% of the time, against 50% for activation edges and 70% for inhibition edges.
findings.recommended_action: Make the within-TF or TF-stratified (Mantel-Haenszel / conditional logistic) test the primary test, and report that K562 does not pass it at alpha = 0.05. Drop 'well above the across-edge shuffle' as the main support, and remove K562 from the claim that the result is confirmed in two cell lines.

findings.description: P4/P7: the RPE1 result depends on a single TF (MYC), so 'the result holds in both cell lines' cannot stand. MYC supplies 82 of the 187 top-10% edges and 9 of the 24 inhibition edges, and its own 2x2 table is nearly perfect (inhibition 8 up / 1 down). With MYC removed, the effect and the within-TF test both vanish. The TF-resampled 95% interval (0.71-14.25) already includes 1, and the within-TF 'pass' rests on 9 mixed-sign TFs, mostly MYC. RPE1 is also the essential-gene screen from the same study and pipeline (58 TFs), not an independent, representative held-out condition.
findings.evidence: I re-ran stratum_stats on the RPE1 top-10% edges without MYC: n=105, 15 inhibition edges, OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF shuffle p 0.64, TF bootstrap CI 0.50-6.55. With MYC, leave-one-TF-out ORs are 3.5-4.0 (p < 0.01), so MYC is the only TF whose removal changes the result. MYC top-10% table: activation 18 up / 55 down, inhibition 8 up / 1 down.
findings.recommended_action: Report a leave-one-TF-out sensitivity analysis, state that the RPE1 signal comes from MYC, and remove the claim that the result 'holds in both cell lines'. If generalisation is to be claimed, add an independent screen or cell type with a broad TF set.

findings.location: code/sign_test.py line 118 (Fisher test) and lines 202-208 (balanced-accuracy bootstrap); SUMMARY.md lines 22-29, 34-35
findings.description: P4 pseudoreplication. The Fisher p values in the headline table and the 95% intervals for balanced accuracy treat edges as independent. Edges share TFs (e.g. MYC contributes 138 of 836 top-10% edges in K562 and 82 of 187 in RPE1), and the balanced-accuracy bootstrap resamples edges within each class instead of resampling TFs. The precision reported is therefore overstated. For RPE1, a TF-cluster bootstrap interval for balanced accuracy includes chance.
findings.evidence: Reported edge-level interval for RPE1 top-10% balanced accuracy: [0.564, 0.763]. My TF-cluster bootstrap (2,000 resamples): [0.458, 0.771]. For K562 it is [0.549, 0.644], similar. K562 top 10%: edge-level Fisher p 7.7e-5 against a TF-stratified Mantel-Haenszel p of 0.13.
findings.recommended_action: Resample by TF for every interval and replace edge-level Fisher p values with TF-stratified or cluster-robust tests. Give the inference unit explicitly (edges / TFs) for every number in the summary.

findings.description: P9 negative result understated. 'Removing the TF moves its annotated targets the way DoRothEA says it should' is not supported for activation edges, which are the large majority. In K562, even in the top 10%, activation targets go down only 49.6% of the time, no different from chance, and level-D activation edges go the wrong way more often than the right way. All of the edge-level accuracy above 0.5 comes from 114 (K562) and 24 (RPE1) inhibition edges. In RPE1 the 62.6% down-rate for activation edges matches what an 'always down' predictor gets, reflecting the global down-bias of RPE1 knockdowns.
findings.evidence: K562 top 10%: activation 364 up / 358 down (binomial p = 0.85 vs 0.5); level D activation accuracy 0.442 (n=412, binomial p = 0.02, wrong direction). The always-down predictor gets the same activation accuracy as the database sign in both lines (0.496 K562, 0.626 RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Report accuracy by class prominently and say plainly that activation labels alone show no better-than-chance edge-level agreement in K562. Restrict any positive statement to inhibition-labelled edges, compared against a TF-matched background.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 50-52 (Interpretation 2); code/sign_test.py line 40 (STRATA) and line 183
findings.description: P8/P5 threshold dependence and post-hoc stratum choice. The claim exists only in the top-10% stratum. K562 shows nothing at 'all' or 'top 50%'. RPE1 is non-monotonic: 'all' OR 1.40 (p 0.015), top 50% OR 1.33 (p 0.14). About 6 stratum-by-line tables, each with several tests, are reported with no multiplicity correction. The explanation offered ('expected: the sign of a near-zero change is noise') is never tested, for example against a significance-based cut using the cell counts. The pooled quantile also lets high-effect TFs dominate the stratum, so 'top 10%' partly selects on TF identity.
findings.evidence: Threshold sweep for the K562 pooled OR: 0.99 (all), 1.09 (50%), 1.38 (70%), 1.63 (80%), 1.86 (85%), 2.31 (90%), 2.50 (95%), 4.11 (98%). The TF-stratified Mantel-Haenszel OR is not significant at any of these (p 0.13-0.41 for 70-98%).
findings.recommended_action: Pre-specify the threshold or show the full sweep with the TF-stratified statistic and the worst case. Correct for the number of strata and lines tested, and restrict claims to the range where the TF-aware test is stable (for K562, none).

findings.location: code/sign_test.py lines 84-86 (own-gene response set to NaN); README.md lines 33-34; SUMMARY.md lines 50-52
findings.description: P6: no positive control or knockdown-efficacy check. The script masks each TF's response in its own gene and never verifies that the knockdown happened or that the TF is expressed. Many knockdowns cannot carry signal: TFs not expressed in K562 (own gene not among the measured genes) are scored, and some contribute many top-10% edges. The all-edges null (OR 0.99) is therefore uninterpretable; dilution by ineffective knockdowns is an untested alternative to 'near-zero changes are noise'.
findings.evidence: K562: own gene measured in only 297 of 672 profiles, and only 64 profiles have own-gene z < -0.5. ESR1 and SOX2 (own gene not measured; the SOX2 profile has 7 cells) contribute 72 of the 836 top-10% edges. MYC own-gene z = -0.03 yet contributes 138 top-10% edges. CEBPA (own gene not measured) supplies 12 of the 114 inhibition edges. Edges from TFs with an unmeasured own gene (40% of K562 edges) show OR 0.87 over all edges and 1.19 (p 0.58) in their top 10%.
findings.recommended_action: Add a knockdown-efficacy filter (own-gene z below a threshold, or TF expressed in the cell line) and report results with and without it. Add a positive control with known strong targets (e.g. GATA1/TAL1 in K562) to show the pipeline detects sign agreement when it exists.

findings.description: P2: weak and misleading baselines. The 'random sign' baseline is a single random draw (0.453 and 0.406) rather than its expected value of 0.5. The 'always predict down' baseline scored over database classes falls below 0.5 by construction. Both make the database sign look further above baseline than it is. The summary also leaves out that always-down equals the database sign in RPE1 over all edges (0.5416 vs 0.5416) and beats it in the top 50% (0.603 vs 0.534). The natural trivial baseline, the up-rate of all strongly responding non-target genes for the same TFs, is missing.
findings.evidence: run_log RPE1: all edges, database sign 0.5416 = always-down 0.5416; top 50%, always-down 0.6034 vs database sign 0.5342. TF-matched background up-rate in the top 10%: K562 0.61-0.62, RPE1 0.57-0.59.
findings.recommended_action: Report chance as 0.5 (or the mean over many random draws) and add a TF-matched non-edge background. Express the effect as the margin over that background.

findings.description: The claim that 'Level A edges score higher than level D' has no test and is confounded by TF composition. MYC makes up 43 of 69 level-A edges in RPE1 and 70 of 267 in K562. Accuracy on inhibition edges does not differ between levels, so the difference comes from activation edges, where level D in K562 is below chance.
findings.evidence: K562 inhibition accuracy at level A is 0.70 vs 0.68 at level D (Fisher p = 1.0); RPE1 inhibition A vs D p = 0.11. Level A in RPE1 has 7 inhibition edges, 4 of them from MYC.
findings.recommended_action: Test the level difference with a TF-stratified model and report it as exploratory, noting how few inhibition edges each level has and how many come from MYC.

findings.description: Guide profiles are averaged without weighting, and the cell counts in *_guide_info.csv are never used. Because dE is a mean z-score, profiles with few cells are much noisier, so the |dE| strata partly select noisy profiles. A sensitivity check suggests the headline ORs are fairly robust to this, but the analysis neither documents nor controls it.
findings.evidence: K562 correlation between log(cells) and profile SD: -0.75. 9.3% of top-10% edges come from TFs with < 50 cells, against 1.5% of all edges. Ranking by |dE|*sqrt(cells) instead gives OR 2.20 (K562) and 4.76 (RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Weight profiles by cell count when averaging, or stratify on a precision-scaled statistic, and report the result.

findings.description: P10 reproducibility gaps. The script that cut the response files from the full Replogle release (row and column selection, removal of non-finite genes, handling of duplicate names) is not included. Package versions are not pinned, and the OmniPath/DoRothEA download is identified only by month, with no version or query.
findings.evidence: The only code file is code/sign_test.py. The README says 'Needs numpy, pandas and scipy' with no versions, and 'downloaded August 2026' with no release identifier.
findings.recommended_action: Include the data-preparation script, a requirements file with pinned versions, and the OmniPath query/version (or a checksum of the DoRothEA file).

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 clearly detects the error. It targets Interpretation 4 (SUMMARY.md:57-60) and the Conclusion (67-70), quoting 'direct causal', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. It meets reason (1): a Perturb-seq knockdown measures the total effect, direct plus indirect, so sign agreement cannot show an edge is direct. It also meets reason (2): agreement appears only in the top 10% of |dE|, and K562 has OR 0.99 across all edges. Its recommended rewording matches the key's correct result. F2 and F3 also point at the Conclusion lines 67-68 and at Interpretation 6 ('holds in both cell lines'). Both argue reason (3), that support weakens once edges are grouped by TF. F2 uses the K562 within-TF shuffle (p 0.065), backed by a Mantel-Haenszel test I reproduced: OR 1.51, CI 0.91-2.51. F3 uses the RPE1 TF-resampled CI that includes 1, and shows the RPE1 result collapses without MYC (OR 1.64, p 0.42, within-TF p about 0.63). F3 also notes that both screens come from the same study. Both therefore support detection under reason (3).

findings.reason: This is the planted causal and validation overreach. It names the Interpretation 4 / Conclusion claims and gives reason (1): a knockdown measures total direct-plus-indirect effects, and nothing separates direct edges. It gives reason (2): the effect is limited to the top 10%, with K562 all-edge OR 0.99. Its supporting numbers check out: 278,677 DoRothEA rows, of which 257,029 are unsigned, 16,766 stimulation-only and 3,476 inhibition-only.

The key's error includes that the K562 within-TF shuffle (median 1.76, p 0.065) leaves edge-level agreement unshown, and F2 argues exactly this against the 'two cell lines' conclusion (lines 67-68). I reproduced its Mantel-Haenszel numbers by TF: top 10% OR 1.51 (0.91-2.51) on 27 informative TFs, p 0.126 with continuity correction. Its other thresholds also match: 1.14 at 30%, 1.21 at 20%, 1.42 at 5%, 2.31 at 2%.

F3 attacks Interpretation 6 and the Conclusion's two-line support using reason (3): the RPE1 TF-resampled CI includes 1, and the result depends on MYC. It also makes the key's same-study point (c). I verified the numbers without MYC: n=105, 15 inhibition edges, OR 1.64, Fisher p 0.42, within-TF p about 0.63, bootstrap CI about 0.50-6.5. The MYC table (activation 18 up/55 down, inhibition 8/1) is also correct. One small inaccuracy: the other leave-one-TF-out ORs range from 3.52 to 5.41, not 3.5-4.0.

This is technically true. The Fisher p values and balanced-accuracy CIs are edge-level, and I reproduced F4's TF-cluster bootstrap of RPE1 balanced accuracy at 0.457-0.771. However, the summary already reports TF-resampled OR intervals and within-TF shuffles for every stratum, so TF clustering is not ignored (the key lists that claim as a false alarm). This adds little beyond F2 and F3.

The raw facts are correct: K562 top-10% activation edges are 364 up / 358 down, and level D activation accuracy is 0.442. However, the claim that activation labels show no agreement rests on comparing to 0.5. Against a TF-matched background, which the review itself advocates (I get about 0.62 up, edge-weighted, in K562), activation targets at 0.50 up do move in the annotated direction. The key treats the inhibition-class pattern as a disclosed description of the table, and the summary table shows the 0.504.

The threshold sweep numbers are correct, but the core charges of post-hoc strata and missing multiplicity correction are contradicted by the key. The strata are fixed in code and select on |dE| only, all three strata are reported for both lines, and the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni across six tests. Threshold dependence is already disclosed in Interpretation 2, and the TF-stratified part repeats F2.

The key lists 'knockdown efficiency not checked' as a false alarm. Own-gene responses are negative for 97-98% of measurable TFs, and dropping weak knockdowns raises the top-10% OR (4.05 K562 / 7.26 RPE1). Several of F7's facts are true: 297 of 672 profiles have the own gene measured, 64 profiles are below -0.5, MYC's K562 own z is -0.03, and ESR1+SOX2 contribute 72 top-10% edges. Even so, the claimed invalidating problem does not hold.

It is true that the random-sign baseline is a single draw and that always-down falls below 0.5 by construction. The key explains both, as well as the RPE1 0.5416 tie and the top-50% always-down result, which appear in the run log. F8 does not claim a bug, and the OR remains the main statistic. This is a fair but minor presentation point.

Its numbers are correct: MYC supplies 43 of 69 level-A edges in RPE1 and 70 of 267 in K562, and K562 inhibition accuracy is 0.70 at level A vs 0.68 at level D. The level A vs D comparison is untested, but it is a secondary claim, and the summary already notes the small inhibition counts.

Averaging guides is a stated choice that matches the source loader. The correlation between log cell count and profile SD is -0.75, as F10 says, but F10 itself reports that the headline ORs are robust to precision weighting. This is a minor sensitivity note.

These are true reproducibility gaps: there is no data-cutting script, package versions are not pinned, and the OmniPath download is identified only by month. The README does describe the cut, and the key confirms the data are an exact subset, so this is a trivial documentation point.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 is a clear detection under the key's rule. It points at Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion ('direct causal regulatory interactions', 'validated wiring diagram', 'ground truth'). It gives reason (1): a Perturb-seq z-score measures the total effect, direct plus indirect, so sign agreement cannot show an edge is direct. It also gives reason (2): agreement appears only in the top 10%, with K562 all-edge OR 0.99. F2 also meets the rule through reason (3). It targets the 'confirmed in two cell lines' Conclusion (lines 67-68) and argues that K562 edge-level agreement is not shown once TF is accounted for (within-TF p = 0.065, null median 1.76). I confirmed its Mantel-Haenszel figure: OR 1.51 [0.91-2.51] on 27 informative TFs, not significant. F3 also meets reason (3) for RPE1. It cites the TF-resampled interval 0.71-14.25, which includes 1, shows that MYC alone carries the effect (OR 1.64 without MYC, confirmed), and attacks Interpretation 6 and the Conclusion. One detail in F3 is slightly off: with MYC kept in, the other leave-one-TF-out ORs run from 3.52 to 5.41, not 3.5 to 4.0.

findings.reason: Names the planted overreach exactly: Interpretation 4 and the Conclusion's 'direct causal', 'validated wiring diagram' and 'ground truth'. It gives key reason (1) (knockdown measures total, not direct, effect) and reason (2) (association only in the top 10%; K562 all-edge OR 0.99). Its numbers match the run log.

Facet (3) of the documented error: the K562 within-TF shuffle (median 1.76, p 0.065) leaves edge-level agreement unshown, so K562 should not count toward the 'confirmed in two cell lines' Conclusion. I verified its TF-stratified Mantel-Haenszel numbers: top 10% OR 1.51 [0.91, 2.51] on 27 TFs, and the sweep 1.14 / 1.21 / 1.42 / 2.31 is not significant at any threshold. Not the 'clustering ignored' false alarm, because it engages with the reported within-TF null.

Facet (3) of the error applied to RPE1 and to Interpretation 6 / Conclusion: the TF-resampled interval 0.71-14.25 includes 1, and the result rests on MYC. Verified: MYC has 82/187 edges and 9/24 inhibition edges, with table act 18/55 and inh 8/1; without MYC the OR is 1.64, and MYC is the only TF whose removal kills the effect. It also notes that both screens come from the same study. Small inaccuracy: the other leave-one-out ORs range 3.52-5.41, not 3.5-4.0.

Correct that the Fisher p values and the balanced-accuracy bootstrap are edge-level. A TF-cluster bootstrap of RPE1 balanced accuracy is about [0.449, 0.772], which includes 0.5. However, the summary table already reports the TF-resampled OR interval and the within-TF null for every stratum, so this is a presentation nuance rather than an unhandled clustering problem. The key lists 'clustering ignored' as a false alarm.

Verified: K562 top-10% activation edges split 364 up / 358 down (binomial p 0.85), and level-D activation is 182/412 correct (p 0.02, wrong direction). So the sentence 'removing the TF moves its annotated targets the way DoRothEA says' is unsupported for most edges, and the OR is driven by the inhibition class. The key treats the inhibition pattern as a table description, not the planted error, but the interpretive overstatement it points to is real.

Strata select on |dE| only and all strata are reported. The multiplicity concern is moot because the top-10% Fisher p values survive Bonferroni over the six tests (key fact). The untested 'near-zero is noise' explanation and the threshold dependence are minor, and its TF-stratified sweep (verified) duplicates F2.

The facts are accurate (297 of 672 profiles have the own gene measured; MYC own-gene z -0.03 in K562; ESR1/SOX2 not measured). But the key lists 'knockdown efficiency not checked' as a false alarm: own-gene responses are negative for 97-98% of measurable TFs (I reproduced 97.4% / 98.0%), and restricting to efficient knockdowns raises the top-10% OR to 4.05 / 7.26. It also raises the all-edge OR only modestly (1.14 / 1.62). So the claimed threat to validity does not hold.

True that the random baseline is a single draw and always-down falls below 0.5 by construction. The RPE1 always-down equality and the top-50% result are in the run log. The key lists these as non-bugs, so this is presentational only.

Interpretation 5 (level A beats level D) is untested and confounded. Verified: MYC supplies 43 of 69 level-A edges in RPE1 and 70 of 267 in K562. Inhibition accuracy A vs D does not differ (K562 14/20 vs 58/85, Fisher p 1.0; RPE1 p 0.11). This is a secondary claim.
Unweighted averaging of guides is a stated choice that matches the source loader (key false-alarm list), and the finding itself reports that the headline ORs are robust to weighting by cell count.
True that the data-cut script, pinned versions and an OmniPath version are absent. The README documents the cut and the data reproduce exactly, so this is a minor reproducibility note.

verdicts.reason: The finding's counts are correct, but the conclusion it draws from them does not hold up. I re-checked against outputs/edges_*.csv. In K562 top 10%, activation edges go 364 up / 358 down (binomial p = 0.85); level-D activation accuracy is 0.442 (n = 412, p = 0.02); RPE1 activation down-rate is 0.626. The finding's own evidence is weaker than it looks. (1) The claim that 'always-down' matches the database sign on activation edges is true by construction, because the database predicts 'down' for every activation edge, so it shows nothing. (2) 0.5 is the wrong benchmark, because large responses are not symmetric. Among the top-10% responses of the scored TFs, only 41.4% (K562) and 47.5% (RPE1) of all genes go down. Against each TF's own non-target genes the expected down-rate is 0.374 (K562) and 0.286 (RPE1). So activation targets (0.496 / 0.626) go down more often than background. (3) The comparison the finding itself recommends, a TF-matched background, reverses its diagnosis. I compared annotated targets with the same TF's non-targets at |dE| above the top-10% threshold, within each TF (Mantel-Haenszel). For activation targets going down, the OR is 1.62 in K562 (TF-bootstrap 1.19-2.10; 1.46 without MYC) and 2.76 in RPE1 (1.34 without MYC). For inhibition targets going up, it is 1.45 in K562 and 1.0 in RPE1. So 'activation labels show no better-than-chance agreement in K562' is wrong, and restricting positive statements to inhibition edges is not supported, since RPE1 inhibition edges show no excess over background. (4) The 'global down-bias of RPE1 knockdowns' does not explain the top 10%: large responses there are 47.5% down overall and 28.6% for TF-matched genes. (5) Nothing is understated: SUMMARY.md reports the per-class up-fractions in its table and in Interpretation 1 ('against 50% (K562) and 37% (RPE1)'). The answer key also treats the activation/inhibition pattern as a description of the table, not an error. Lines 58-60 and 67 do overreach, but for reasons this finding does not give: a knockdown measures total (direct plus downstream) effects, agreement appears only in the top 10% (K562 all-edge OR 0.99), and the K562 within-TF shuffle gives p = 0.065. Its own argument would replace the summary's claim with a different wrong one.

review.summary: The code runs and reproduces every number in outputs/ and SUMMARY.md (43 genes, circular correlation 0.9832, median 15.1 deg, mean 16.5 deg). The headline inference does not hold. The gene-by-gene agreement test cannot tell a matching continuous phase from a crude or noisy one. The 43 Whitfield genes fall into two tight groups (S/G1-S genes near 30-90 deg and G2/M genes near 120-165 deg), so the circular correlation mostly records which group a gene is in. Three checks show this. A 3-state categorical phase (G1/S/G2M set to fixed angles) gives 0.982. Adding N(0, 60 deg) noise to every RPE1 cell's angle still gives 0.981. Shuffling peaks within each group gives a null mean of 0.80. Part of the agreement is built in: 31 of the 43 compared genes are the Tirosh markers used to build both PCAs and to set direction and origin. The direction is forced (K562 was flipped), and the S peak is pinned at 45 deg in both lines. The differences that remain are systematic, not random. All 20 S-phase genes peak later in RPE1 (median +20 deg) and 19 of 22 G2/M genes peak earlier, so the S-to-G2M arc is compressed in RPE1. This contradicts the 'same ruler' and 'same gene order' claims. Two other pieces of evidence do not support their claims: R near 0 also comes out of random-gene PCA, and nothing backs the 'not across batch or platform' statement. Minor issues: the Whitfield reference phases are never used, there is a non-cycling gene (AURKAIP1), the module scoring departs from Scanpy, the 'peak' estimator depends on cell density, and there is no uncertainty estimate. Robustness checks that passed: renormalising K562 to panel totals or restricting RPE1 to the K562 panel changes almost nothing (corr 0.982/0.983), and the G1 cluster sits at about 286 deg in both lines.

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py lines 87-96 (circ_corr_deg on per-gene peaks); SUMMARY.md lines 24, 32-37
findings.description: The headline statistic (circular correlation +0.983 of per-gene peak phases) cannot test whether the RPE1 continuous phase means the same thing as the K562 one. The Whitfield genes form two clusters (S/G1-S near 30-90 deg, G2/M near 120-165 deg), so the correlation mostly measures whether S and G2/M cells sit in different directions. Conclusions 1-3 ('almost perfectly correlated', 'valid as a transfer target') rest on this number and cannot stand.
findings.evidence: All checks were rerun inline with the analysis's own functions. (a) Replacing each line's continuous phase with a 3-state categorical label (G1=280, S=45, G2M=145 deg, from the Tirosh scores) gives circ corr 0.982 and a median |diff| of 8.3 deg, which looks better than the real result. (b) Adding per-cell N(0,30/60/90 deg) noise to the RPE1 theta gives 0.982 / 0.981 / 0.963. (c) Squeezing RPE1's 0-180 deg arc by a factor of 0.5 still gives 0.95. (d) Shuffling RPE1 peaks within the S and G2M gene groups gives a null mean of 0.799 (95th percentile 0.850). Within-group correlations are only 0.874 (S, n=20) and 0.888 (G2M, n=22).
findings.recommended_action: Drop the pooled circular correlation as evidence of equivalence, or report it next to the within-group permutation null and the categorical-phase baseline. Use a test that can detect distortions of the continuous scale: per-group (within S, within G2M) agreement, per-gene offsets with bootstrap CIs, and a check that the label locates known within-phase transitions. Then restate conclusions 1-3.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py lines 61-78 (PCA on Tirosh markers, flip so G2M follows S, rotate S peak to 45 deg); SUMMARY.md lines 14-18, 34-35
findings.description: Several 'agreements' are imposed by the method rather than found in the data. Both lines' phases are built from the same Tirosh S/G2M marker genes. The direction is forced so that G2M follows S, and the S-score peak is rotated to exactly 45 deg. 31 of the 43 compared Whitfield genes are these same markers. The S peak of 45.0/45.0, the shared direction ('runs in the same direction as the K562 one'), and an S-G2M separation below 180 deg are all guaranteed by construction. They are presented as findings.
findings.evidence: phase_agreement.json: K562 flipped=true (rotation 135.9 deg), RPE1 flipped=false (rotation 124.9 deg). s_peak_deg is 45.0 in both, which equals the s_at_deg anchor. Compared genes that are also Tirosh markers: 31/43. The only non-marker genes are AURKAIP1, BUB1B, CCNA2, CCNB1, CDT1, DHFR, E2F1, MCM3, MCM7, PLK1, PTTG1 and RFC4.
findings.recommended_action: Say in the summary that direction and origin are set by construction. Do not report the S peak as a check. Validate on genes that were not used to build or orient the phase (e.g., hold out the Tirosh markers, or use an independent periodic gene list) and report agreement on that held-out set.

findings.description: The K562-vs-RPE1 differences are systematic, not scatter. Every S-phase gene peaks later in RPE1 and nearly every G2/M gene peaks earlier, so the RPE1 S-to-G2M arc is compressed relative to K562. This contradicts 'judged against the same ruler'. A perfect K562-trained readout would show phase-dependent errors of about 10-30 deg on RPE1 from the label mismatch alone. The claim 'the gene order around the circle in RPE1 is the same as the order in K562' is also false.
findings.evidence: Signed RPE1 minus K562 difference: S/G1-S genes 20/20 positive (sign test p=1.9e-6), range +5 to +47, median about +20 deg. G2M genes 19/22 negative, median about -10 deg. S-G2M separation is 108.8 vs 97.1 deg. Kendall tau of peak order (excluding AURKAIP1) is 0.84, with 70 of 861 gene pairs discordant. For example, CDC45 moves from 44.3 to 91.0 deg, past DHFR, TYMS and MCM7; GINS2 moves from 28.8 to 64.6 deg. Median |diff| is 20.1 deg for S genes and 9.9 deg for G2M genes.
findings.recommended_action: Report the signed per-group offsets and the arc compression. Either remove the claims of the same ruler and same order, or add a calibration step (e.g., a common reference mapping or monotone warping between the lines) before using RPE1 phase as ground truth. Then quantify how much transfer error the label mismatch alone would cause.

findings.description: 'Phase concentration R near 0' is cited as evidence that cells spread around the circle and that each line gives a usable cell-cycle circle. R near 0 is nearly guaranteed for the angle of mean-centred PCA scores, whatever genes are used. The cells are in fact not spread evenly around the circle.
findings.evidence: PCA on 90 random genes gives R = 0.058, 0.057, 0.029, 0.070, 0.032 (K562) and 0.047, 0.078, 0.042, 0.054, 0.042 (RPE1), the same range as the reported 0.079/0.043. Theta histogram in 30-deg bins: the 270-300 bin holds 468 (K562) and 729 (RPE1) of 3,000 cells. The 180-270 arc holds only 297 and 217 cells.
findings.recommended_action: Remove R as evidence of a cycle. Instead report the angular density, the placement of Tirosh-labelled G1/S/G2M cells around the circle, and the variance explained relative to a random-gene null.

findings.location: README.md lines 38-41 and SUMMARY.md lines 38-39 (conclusion 4); data/*.h5ad
findings.description: The claim that RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform, so the transfer 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform', is unsupported. The two lines were profiled in separate Replogle et al. 2022 screens. The files supplied here were also processed differently, so cell line is confounded with batch and processing.
findings.evidence: K562 was normalised to 10,000 before the panel was cut (per-cell panel totals 7,447-9,573). RPE1 was normalised after cutting (exactly 10,000). The panels differ (6,546 vs 8,749 genes; the K562 PCA uses 87 marker genes, RPE1 uses 93). Cell IDs are re-indexed integers in K562 but barcodes with GEM-group suffixes (-34, -42, -55) in RPE1, which points to different processing pipelines. No analysis in the folder tests for batch effects.
findings.recommended_action: Remove or soften the batch/platform claim. State that cell line is confounded with screen and batch, and harmonise processing (same gene panel, same normalisation) before the transfer test.

findings.description: The Whitfield 'known peak phases' are only used as a gene list and never as a reference, although the README presents them as known peak phases. Neither line's phase is checked against them. Both lines put G2/M genes at about 140 deg against reference values of about 180-220 deg. The list also contains AURKAIP1, which shows no cycling signal in either line. No per-gene amplitude filter removes it, and it produces the largest discrepancy (52.5 deg).
findings.evidence: Circular correlation with the Whitfield values is 0.88 (K562) and 0.84 (RPE1). The CDK1/TOP2A/CCNB1 peaks are 115-160 deg in the data against 170-210 deg in WHITFIELD_PEAK. AURKAIP1 has resultant length 0.073 (K562) and 0.065 (RPE1) and is detected in 97% of cells, so it is a flat, non-cycling gene. Its peaks are 352.9 vs 45.4 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Either use the reference phases as an external calibration (and report agreement per line), or describe them as only a gene list. Add a per-gene amplitude threshold and drop genes that do not cycle, such as AURKAIP1. Check the hand-entered reference values against the source.

findings.description: The per-gene 'peak' is an expression-weighted circular centroid over all cells. It depends on how cells are distributed around the circle, not only on when the gene is expressed. That distribution differs between the lines, so part of the per-gene differences reflects different cell densities rather than different gene timing. No uncertainty (bootstrap CIs) is reported for the per-gene peaks, the median difference or the correlation.
findings.evidence: Cell counts per 30-deg bin differ between lines, e.g. 120-150 deg: 328 (K562) vs 527 (RPE1); 270-300 deg: 468 vs 729. A cell-level bootstrap (phase held fixed) gives a median |diff| 95% interval of about 10.8-16.5 deg, which the summary does not report.
findings.recommended_action: Estimate peaks with density-corrected binned means or a smoothed expression-vs-phase curve and its argmax. Report bootstrap CIs, ideally re-estimating the phase inside each bootstrap.

findings.description: score_genes is described as Scanpy-style but departs from Scanpy. The control pool is not purged of the gene set itself. The number of controls is (genes in bin) x 50 rather than a fixed number per bin, so in some bins the whole bin, including the markers, becomes the control set. This only affects which top-200 cells are used for orientation and anchoring, but the description is inaccurate.
findings.evidence: In K562, 1 of 18 S bins and 1 of 17 G2M bins take the entire 262-gene bin as controls. In RPE1, 3 of 15 G2M bins take the entire 350-gene bin. Pools are np.where(bins == b) with no exclusion of idx.
findings.recommended_action: Exclude the gene set from the control pool and sample a fixed ctrl_size per bin, as Scanpy does, or correct the README description.

findings.description: The mean absolute difference is 16.5 deg (phase_agreement.json) but is printed and summarised as 16 deg, because Python's '.0f' rounds half to even.
findings.evidence: phase_agreement.json gives mean_abs_diff_deg 16.5; run_log.txt and SUMMARY.md give '16 deg'.
findings.recommended_action: Report 16.5 deg, or round consistently (to 17).

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. I graded each finding against the key's known true facts and possible false alarms, and checked claims inline on the package data. The checks: on the 12 non-marker genes the agreement holds (circ_corr 0.992, median 17.9 deg; 0.994 without AURKAIP1). AURKAIP1 has resultant length 0.073 in K562 and 0.065 in RPE1. PCA on random genes gives phase R of 0.017-0.075. The signed offsets are systematic: all 20 S genes peak later in RPE1 (median +20 deg) and 19 of 22 G2M genes peak earlier. Kendall tau on peak order is 0.835. The exact mean |diff| is 16.54 deg.

findings.reason: The key names this as a false alarm: saying circ_corr is unreliable because the per-gene peaks split into S and G2/M groups (peak R 0.57-0.77; agrees with R_diff/R_sum). It also says a missing permutation null is at most a presentation weakness. The categorical-label baseline is a fair point about how sensitive the test is, but it shows no disagreement between the lines. My checks support agreement: within-group correlations stay high (about 0.87 for S genes, about 0.83-0.89 for G2M genes), and the 12 held-out non-marker genes give 0.992. Conclusions 1-3 still stand.

The data confirm the pattern. All 20 S/G1-S genes peak later in RPE1 (median +20 deg). 19 of 22 G2M genes peak earlier (median about -9 to -10 deg). Kendall tau is 0.835 (CDC45 crosses DHFR, TYMS and MCM7). So the SUMMARY sentence that the gene order is 'the same' is literally overstated. The key does not cover this. Still, the key treats the 15-deg median difference as agreement. Part of the offset may come from differences in cell density between the lines, which affect the peak estimator, rather than from the label itself. Whether this invalidates 'same ruler' and RPE1 as a transfer target needs deeper analysis than I can do here, so I mark it disputed rather than confirmed.

The narrow points are correct. Direction and the 45-deg S anchor are set by construction, and 31 of 43 compared genes are Tirosh markers. The key itself says the positive sign is a convention. But the implied problem, that agreement is forced or circular, is the key's listed false alarm. circ_corr magnitude is the same with or without orientation, and on the held-out non-marker genes I get circ_corr 0.992 (median 17.9 deg). So this is only a presentation issue in the summary wording.

This contradicts a known true fact in the key: RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform (Replogle Perturb-seq), so the comparison is across cell lines, not batch or platform. The key also lists the differences in normalisation, panel and marker count as non-errors that do not drive the result. The finding targets the scope of next-step conclusion 4, not the headline.

Confirmed: PCA on random genes also gives R near 0 (0.017-0.075), so R is weak evidence of a cycle, and cell density around the circle is uneven (468/729 cells in the 270-300 deg bin). The summary only says cells spread 'all around', not evenly. The key says the ring is confirmed by the S/G2M separation (108.8/97.1 deg), so the conclusion that each line gives a usable circle stands. The finding does not claim there is no cycle.

Correct but minor. The Whitfield degrees are used only as a gene list, which the key confirms. Correlations with the reference (0.88/0.84) match the key. AURKAIP1 is flat (R 0.073/0.065, detected in 97% of cells). Including it only adds the largest discrepancy, so it cannot inflate the agreement.

The key treats the expression-above-mean weighting as a design choice applied the same way to both lines, and missing bootstrap CIs as at most a presentation weakness. The point about cell density is plausible but does not overturn the result.

True that score_genes does not keep markers out of the control pool, but the key shows excluding them changes nothing material: peaks move under 0.5 deg, orientation is the same, circ_corr 0.9832, median 15.4 deg. The finding itself says it is minor and only describes the README inaccurately.
Confirmed: the exact mean |diff| is 16.54 deg. It is stored as 16.5, and Python's f'{16.5:.0f}' prints '16' (rounds half to even). A trivial rounding issue in the reported value.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key marks B6874 as clean ("error": null), so there is no documented error to detect. Under the key's rule, any load-bearing error claim counts as a false alarm unless code run on the package confirms a real error. I re-ran the package functions inline. F1's figures reproduce: the categorical-label baseline gives circ_corr 0.982 with a median of 8.3 deg, and the within-group correlations are 0.874 and 0.888. Still, F1 is the anticipated "bimodal peaks make circ_corr unreliable" false alarm, and the reviewer's own within-group numbers back up agreement. F3's systematic offsets also reproduce: 20 of 20 S genes shift positive (p=1.9e-6), 19 of 22 G2M genes shift negative, Kendall tau is 0.836 and 70 of 861 pairs are discordant. Whether this offset is a real calibration mismatch or an effect of cell density in the peak estimator is not settled, so I marked F3 disputed rather than a confirmed error. No finding shows a confirmed load-bearing error.

findings.reason: This is the key's anticipated false alarm that circ_corr is unreliable because the per-gene peaks are bimodal (S vs G2M), combined with the missing-null false alarm. Its numbers do reproduce: the categorical baseline gives 0.982 with a median of 8.3 deg, and the within-group correlations are 0.874 (S) and 0.888 (G2M). But the reviewer's own within-group permutation null (95th percentile 0.85) is well below the observed 0.983, and the within-group correlations are high. So the evidence supports continuous agreement, and 'conclusions 1-3 cannot stand' overreaches. The key's facts (peak R 0.57/0.77; agreement with the resultant statistic, 0.947) say the statistic is well-behaved here.

The specific facts are correct. Each line gets a reflection and a rotation, so S peak = 45.0 in both and the shared direction is a convention (the key admits the positive sign is a convention), and 31 of 43 compared genes are Tirosh markers (I confirmed the 12 non-markers). Calling the direction in conclusion 2 a 'finding' is a fair presentation point. But the orientation cannot create gene-by-gene agreement: the circ_corr magnitude is the same without it, which the key flags as the expected false alarm. 'Separation below 180 guaranteed' is trivial, since the metric is min(d, 360-d), and it does not force the ~100 deg observed. The headline is not affected.

The data claims reproduce. S genes: 20/20 have a positive RPE1-K562 shift (sign test p=1.9e-6), median +20.1 deg. G2M genes: 19/22 negative, median -9.2 deg. Kendall tau is 0.836 with 70/861 pairs discordant, so 'the gene order is the same' is literally an overstatement. One example is a little off: CDC45 at 91.0 deg is not past TYMS at 95.2 deg. The key does not cover systematic offsets. Some of the pattern may come from the expression-weighted peak estimator and the different cell densities (RPE1 has many cells at 120-150 deg) rather than from a different ruler. Without further checks I cannot tell whether this invalidates 'same ruler' and the transfer-target conclusion.

Confirmed: PCA on random genes gives R of 0.017-0.075, the same range as 0.079/0.043, so R near 0 says little. The theta histogram is uneven, with 468/729 cells in the 270-300 bin and 297/217 in 180-270. The finding does not claim there is no cycle; the S/G2M separation still confirms the ring. It is a valid point about weak supporting evidence, but not load-bearing.

This contradicts the key's known true fact that RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform (Replogle Perturb-seq). The key lists treating the same-lab/same-platform design, panel differences or K562 normalisation as errors among its false alarms. The processing differences it cites (normalisation, 87 vs 93 markers) are documented, and the key says they do not drive the comparison. Conclusion 4 is a scope note about next steps, not the headline result.

True, but minor. The Whitfield degrees are used only as a gene list, which the key says is fine and lists as a false alarm if called misuse. The per-line correlations with the reference (0.88/0.84) match the key. AURKAIP1 is indeed non-cycling: its weighted resultant is 0.073/0.065, it is detected in 97% of cells, and it has the largest discrepancy at 52.5 deg. That is worth noting, but one gene does not change the result.
