The peak weighting is a design choice applied identically to both lines (a listed false alarm if called an error). The key calls the missing bootstrap/CI at most a presentation weakness. The point that cell density affects the weighted centroid is reasonable, but the finding does not claim the headline is wrong.

The description is accurate. Unlike Scanpy, the control pool is not purged of the marker set, and k = n_set_genes_in_bin x 50 instead of a fixed per-bin size. The key says excluding the markers changes nothing material (circ_corr +0.9832, median 15.4 deg, same orientation). The finding itself says the effect is limited. This is a documentation accuracy issue.
True and trivial. phase_agreement.json gives 16.5, but the '.0f' format prints 16 because it rounds half to even, so run_log and SUMMARY say 16 deg. The output files are otherwise consistent.

verdicts.reason:
The finding's numbers are correct, but its main claim is overstated. It treats the gene-peak differences as label mismatch that breaks the 'same ruler' conclusion. About half of that systematic part comes from the peak estimator, not from the phase label. The small part that is left was already reported in SUMMARY.md.

Checked against outputs/gene_peak_phase.csv: all 20 S/G1-S genes have a positive RPE1-minus-K562 difference (sign test p=1.9e-6; range +5 to +47; median +20.1). 19 of 22 G2M genes are negative (median -9.2, excluding AURKAIP1). Kendall tau is 0.836, with 70 of 861 pairs discordant. A bootstrap over cells gives a per-gene standard error of about 3 deg. The slope of RPE1 on K562 peaks is 0.71 (95% CI 0.67-0.76), so the pattern is systematic in the reported estimator, not sampling noise.

However, the reported peak is an expression-weighted mean over cells. That makes it sensitive to how unevenly cells sit around the circle, and in both lines they cluster: in 30-deg bins RPE1 ranges from 61 to 729 cells and K562 from 61 to 468. A version that corrects for cell density was tested inline: mean expression per phase bin, every bin weighted equally, run with 12, 18, 24, 36 and 48 bins. With it the gap shrinks a lot. The median |diff| falls from 15 to 8.3-8.9 deg. S genes sit about +7 deg later and G2M genes about -8 deg earlier. The slope rises to 0.87-0.88, and the S-to-G2M gene arc is 108 deg in K562 vs 93 deg in RPE1. That leftover compression of roughly 12% matches the S/G2M separation of 108.8 vs 97.1 deg, which SUMMARY.md already shows in its per-line table.

So the claim that a perfect K562 readout would err by 10-30 deg from label mismatch alone is not supported; the label-level warp is about 7-8 deg each way. The broad order (G1/S, then S, then G2/M) is kept in both estimators. All 70 discordant pairs fall inside a single phase block, and no S gene crosses a G2M gene. 'Same order' is a loose phrase at single-gene level (tau 0.86 even after correction; CDC45 still moves about 35 deg). It does not change the result.

The headline numbers (circ_corr +0.983, median 15 deg) are correct and disclosed. The answer key marks this package clean and treats the 15-deg agreement as valid. A modest, partly disclosed warp does not overturn the conclusion that RPE1 is a usable transfer target. At most, the finding is a wording and presentation point: SUMMARY.md could state the systematic S/G2M offsets.

review.summary: I re-ran the analysis in memory (using -B, so nothing was written to the folder) and every number in the outputs reproduces: circular correlation 0.9832, median absolute difference 15.1 deg, mean 16.5 deg, 43 genes. The numbers are right, but the conclusions drawn from them are not. The headline circular correlation (+0.983) cannot show that the two labels share a scale. It is unchanged when the RPE1 label is rotated by any amount, so it is blind to any offset between the two labels. It is driven mostly by the split between S-phase and G2M-phase genes, and both labels are pinned to the same S/G2M landmarks by construction. A crude score-based phase angle gives the same value (0.984), and a template that puts every S gene at 45 deg and every G2M gene at 145 deg already reaches 0.92 and 0.87. The gene-level data in fact show a systematic disagreement that depends on phase. All 20 S-phase genes peak later in RPE1 (median +20 deg), 19 of the 22 periodic G2M-phase genes (AURKAIP1 excluded) peak earlier, and the S-to-G2M gene interval shrinks from 106 to 78 deg. So the 15 deg median difference is bias, not noise, and this contradicts the 'same ruler' conclusion. Further problems: the G1 part of the circle (about 40% of cells) is never checked; the claim that gene order is the same in both lines is false; the per-line checks (R near 0, S peak at 45 deg, matching direction) hold by construction; the 'not batch' claim is unsupported; and there are small reporting errors. Two checks came back clean: renormalising K562 to its panel and restricting both lines to their shared genes leave the results essentially unchanged (0.982 and 0.983).

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py lines 37-41 and 94 (circ_corr_deg); code/cc_phase.py lines 71-78 (per-line flip and rotation to S peak = 45 deg); SUMMARY.md lines 24, 32-37
findings.description: The headline statistic (circular correlation +0.983) cannot test whether the RPE1 and K562 labels mean the same thing. The Jammalamadaka-SenGupta correlation subtracts each variable's circular mean, so it does not change when either label is rotated by any constant. Both labels are also anchored separately in each line to the same landmarks: the S-score peak is placed at 45 deg and the direction is set so G2M follows S. On top of that, the gene list is almost entirely S-phase genes and G2M-phase genes. A high positive value is therefore nearly guaranteed for any phase angle that separates S from G2M cells. It says nothing about the absolute position or the scale of the label, which is exactly what a transfer target needs.
findings.evidence: Adding 45, 90 or 180 deg to every RPE1 peak leaves the correlation at 0.9832, while the median absolute difference becomes 50, 95 and 165 deg. Changing the anchoring choice (top = 50, 100, 200, 500 or 1000 cells) leaves the correlation at 0.983 in every case. A template that sets every S gene to 45 deg and every G2M gene to 145 deg correlates 0.915 with K562 and 0.873 with RPE1. A crude RPE1 phase built only from atan2(G2M score, S score), with the same anchoring, gives 0.984 against K562, the same as the PCA label. Arbitrary 2D projections within PC1-5 of RPE1, with the same anchoring, give a median of 0.906. Uniformly stretching the K562 peaks around 45 deg by a factor of 0.75 or 1.5 still gives 0.988 and 0.964.
findings.recommended_action: Stop presenting the circular correlation as evidence that the labels are equivalent. Judge agreement with statistics that respond to offset and scale, such as signed per-gene differences and a fitted circular-linear calibration (slope and offset) between the two lines' peak phases. Add negative controls (crude, permuted or rotated labels) and bootstrap confidence intervals over cells, so that 0.983 and 15 deg can be compared with what a non-equivalent label would give.

findings.description: The per-gene differences are systematic and depend on phase, so they are not random scatter. RPE1 places S-phase genes later and G2M-phase genes earlier than K562, which compresses the S-to-G2M stretch of the circle by roughly a quarter. A cell at a given RPE1 angle therefore does not correspond to a K562 cell at the same angle, and a readout fitted on K562 would be scored against a distorted ruler. This contradicts conclusion 3: 'judged against the same ruler'.
findings.evidence: S-phase genes (Whitfield peak below 100 deg): 20 of 20 peak later in RPE1, median +20.1 deg, mean +22.0 deg (sign test p = 1.9e-6). G2M-phase genes (AURKAIP1 excluded): 19 of 22 peak earlier in RPE1, median -8.6 deg (p = 8.6e-4). Median gene peak for S genes vs G2M genes: K562 40.3 vs 145.9 deg (gap 106), RPE1 62.6 vs 140.2 deg (gap 78). Across anchoring choices from top = 50 to top = 1000, the S shift ranges from +19.4 to +5.7 deg and the G2M shift from -9.3 to -23.0 deg. Their difference stays at about 28.7 deg, so the compression is a real property of the two labels, while where the 'error' lands is set by an arbitrary anchoring parameter. The per-line S-to-G2M score separation shows the same thing: 108.8 vs 97.1 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Report the signed, phase-dependent offsets and the S-to-G2M compression. Do not use RPE1's phase as ground truth without a calibration step that maps RPE1 angles onto K562 angles, for example by monotone circular warping fitted on reference genes. Then re-assess, and show how sensitive the result is to the anchoring parameters (s_at_deg, top).

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py lines 26-34 (WHITFIELD_PEAK gene list); SUMMARY.md lines 34-37
findings.description: The comparison only covers the S to G2/M part of the circle. Every compared gene except the non-periodic AURKAIP1 peaks between 24 and 194 deg. There are no G1 or M/G1 reference genes, and CCNE1/CCNE2 (the G1/S genes) are missing. Around 40% of cells sit in the remaining arc, so whether the two labels match there was never tested. The claim that the RPE1 label 'corresponds' to the K562 label everywhere goes beyond the evidence. This matters especially because RPE1, a non-transformed line, and K562 are expected to differ most in G1.
findings.evidence: In the 195-360 deg arc: K562 1,205 of 3,000 cells (40%), RPE1 1,279 of 3,000 (43%). These cells have the lowest S and G2M scores (mean S -0.10/-0.14, mean G2M -0.22/-0.32). The RPE1 histogram in 30-deg bins is very uneven there: 61 cells in 210-240 and 729 in 270-300. The peak range of compared genes is 24.0-193.6 deg in K562 (only AURKAIP1 at 352.9) and 29.0-164.4 deg in RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Add G1 and M/G1 reference genes (for example from Whitfield's M/G1 and G1 clusters, or tricycle/Revelio phase genes) that are present in both panels. Alternatively, restrict the 'valid label' claim explicitly to the S-G2/M arc.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 32-33 ('The gene order around the circle in RPE1 is the same as the order in K562')
findings.description: The claim that the gene order is the same is false. Within each phase group the order is only moderately preserved, and several pairs swap order. The median absolute difference of 15 deg is also barely better than what you get after scrambling gene identities within the S and G2M groups, so most of the apparent gene-level agreement comes from the two-group structure.
findings.evidence: Spearman correlation within S genes is 0.80, within G2M genes 0.61; Kendall tau across all genes (AURKAIP1 excluded) is 0.835. Examples: CDC45, FEN1 and PCNA sit at 44.3, 45.5 and 40.2 deg in K562 but at 91.0, 63.3 and 60.8 deg in RPE1. GINS2 comes before E2F1 in K562 (28.8 vs 30.0) but after it in RPE1 (64.6 vs 49.5). BIRC5 comes after CCNB1 in K562 (164.2 vs 159.7) but before it in RPE1 (143.5 vs 151.9). Permuting RPE1 peaks within each group gives a median absolute difference of 19.7 deg (5th percentile 15.7) against the observed 15.1. (The circular correlation is still above that permutation null: null median 0.795, 95th percentile 0.856.)
findings.recommended_action: Remove or correct the 'same order' statement. Report within-group rank agreement and the permutation null, rather than an overall correlation inflated by the S-versus-G2M split.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py lines 64-78 and 90-92; SUMMARY.md lines 13-18 and 34-35
findings.description: Several of the per-line checks quoted as evidence of 'a clear cycle' that 'runs in the same direction' are true by construction. (a) Phase concentration R near 0 is close to guaranteed, because the PC scores are centred at the origin; it appears even when there is no cell-cycle structure at all. (b) The S peak equals 45.0 deg in both lines because phase_angle rotates it there (s_at_deg). (c) Matching direction is forced by the flip rule; K562 was in fact flipped. Only the S-G2M separation and the PC1+PC2 variance share carry real information.
findings.evidence: In a null where each marker gene is permuted independently across cells (no co-expression, no cycle), R = 0.019 for K562 and 0.007 for RPE1, the same 'near 0' as the real data (0.079 and 0.043). In that null the S peak is still 45.0 deg, while the S-G2M separation (176 and 27 deg) and the PC1+PC2 share (0.03) do differ from the real data. phase_agreement.json shows flipped = true for K562 and false for RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Drop R and the S-peak value as evidence of a cycle, and state that the direction and the S anchor are set by construction. Support the 'usable circle' claim with checks that a no-cycle null would fail, such as a ring-shaped radius distribution, the variance share compared with a null, and periodic expression of genes held out from the construction.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 38-39; README.md data section (normalisation note)
findings.description: The claim that the K562 -> RPE1 test 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform' is unsupported. The two files come from separate experiments (in Replogle 2022 they were separate screens), they were preprocessed differently, and they have different gene panels. Cell line is completely confounded with experimental batch, so cell biology cannot be separated from batch.
findings.evidence: RPE1 cell IDs carry GEM-group suffixes (for example AAACCCAAGCGGACAT-34); K562 IDs are bare integers. K562 was normalised before the panel was cut (per-cell totals 7,447-9,573); RPE1 sums to exactly 10,000. The panels hold 6,546 vs 8,749 genes, giving 87 vs 93 phase-marker genes. (Renormalising K562 or restricting both lines to the 6,544 shared genes leaves the phase comparison essentially unchanged, at 0.982 and 0.983, so this affects the claim rather than the numbers.)
findings.recommended_action: Remove the 'not batch or platform' claim, or support it, for example with within-line batch replicates or a K562 batch from the same experiment as RPE1. Process both lines identically: same normalisation, same gene panel.

findings.description: The Whitfield 'known peak phases' are described as the reference but are only used as a gene list; neither line is compared with them. A comparison would show that both labels place G2M genes much closer to S genes than the reference does, and that RPE1 departs from the reference more than K562. The degree values in the dictionary also cannot be traced to Whitfield 2002, which reports phase clusters rather than per-gene peak angles in degrees.
findings.evidence: Against the reference values in the code, the median absolute difference is 32.5 deg for K562 and 50.6 deg for RPE1. The circular correlation with the reference is 0.884 for K562 and 0.839 for RPE1. The reference S-to-G2M gap is about 160 deg, compared with about 106 deg (K562) and 78 deg (RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Give the source of the degree values, or relabel them as approximate. Report each line's agreement with the external reference, including signed offsets, alongside the line-to-line comparison.

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py line 33 (AURKAIP1) and lines 44-58 (peak_phase has no periodicity filter)
findings.description: AURKAIP1 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein rather than a cell-cycle gene, and it shows no periodicity in either line. Its 'peak phase' is noise, yet it is included in all the summary statistics. peak_phase assigns a peak to any gene with positive weight and never checks how concentrated the weighting is.
findings.evidence: The weighted resultant length for AURKAIP1 is 0.073 (K562) and 0.065 (RPE1); every other gene is at 0.20 or above. Its peaks are 352.9 vs 45.4 deg, the largest difference in the table at 52.5 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Require a minimum resultant length (or a permutation test of periodicity) before a gene is compared, and drop non-cell-cycle genes from the reference list.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 26 and 28; code/compare_lines.py lines 96 and 99
findings.description: Two reporting errors. (a) Line 28 says CCNE1, CCNE2 and UBE2C 'are not in the K562 panel'. CCNE1 is in neither panel; only CCNE2 and UBE2C are present in RPE1 but missing from K562, which is why RPE1 has 45 genes with a peak. (b) The mean absolute difference is 16.54 deg, which rounds to 17. It is reported as 16 because the code first rounds to 16.5 and then formats with '.0f', which rounds half to even.
findings.evidence: Checked against the h5ad var_names: CCNE1 is absent from both files; CCNE2 and UBE2C are present only in RPE1. Recomputed mean absolute difference: 16.539 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the gene-availability sentence. Format the mean from the unrounded value, which gives 17 deg.

verdicts.reason: The descriptive numbers reproduce from outputs/gene_peak_phase.csv and from re-running phase_angle/peak_phase. All 20 S genes peak later in RPE1 (median +20.1 deg, p=1.9e-6). 19 of 22 G2M genes peak earlier (median about -9 deg, p=8.6e-4). The median S-to-G2M gene gap is 105.6 deg in K562 vs 77.5 deg in RPE1, and that 29.4 deg difference stays the same for top=50 to 1000. The finding's load-bearing inference, that RPE1's label is a 'distorted ruler' for a K562-fitted readout, does not hold when tested directly. (1) I projected the RPE1 cells, z-scored within RPE1, onto K562's own PC1/PC2 loadings for the 87 shared marker genes and applied K562's flip and rotation unchanged. This reproduces RPE1's own label within a median 3.2 deg (mean offset 2 deg). Every 30-deg bin has a mean offset of -2.2 to +4.5 deg, and there is no S-late/G2M-early pattern. So the map from marker expression to angle is effectively the same in both lines. (2) Under the K562 ruler, RPE1's S and G2M score peaks fall at 48 and 143 deg (95 deg apart). The compression the finding cites (97.1 vs 108.8 deg) is therefore a property of the RPE1 cells (cell biology and cell density), not of the label. (3) I fitted a ridge readout to K562 phase on all 6,544 shared genes and applied it to RPE1. Its median error against the RPE1 label is 7-10 deg, no worse than K562's own held-out error (8-14 deg). Signed bias per 45-deg bin is within about 8 deg and does not follow the predicted +20 (S) / -9 (G2M) shift. With a density-corrected binned-profile peak, the S shift falls from +20.1 to +6.9 deg and the gap difference from 29 to 17 deg. The remaining gene-level offsets are cross-line biology, which the transfer test is meant to measure, not a defect in the label. SUMMARY.md already reports the 15-deg median difference, and the answer key marks the package as clean, listing complaints that top/s_at_deg are arbitrary as false alarms. Conclusion 3 ('same ruler') stands.

review.summary:
I re-ran the pipeline (compare_lines.py logic, in memory only) and it reproduces every number in the outputs: 87 and 93 marker genes, R 0.079 and 0.043, S/G2M peaks 45.0/153.8 and 45.0/142.1, 43 genes compared, circular correlation 0.9832, median absolute difference 15.1 deg, mean 16.5 deg. The arithmetic is right. The README's data statements also hold: 6,544 shared genes, K562 per-cell totals 7,447-9,573, RPE1 totals exactly 10,000.

The interpretation does not hold. The headline +0.983 is mostly built into the method:
- 31 of the 43 compared genes are the Tirosh markers used to build, orient and anchor the phase.
- The genes form two clusters, S-phase and G2/M. Shuffling genes within each cluster already gives a correlation of about 0.80.
- A crude label, atan2(G2M score, S score), scores 0.984, the same as the analysis's label.
- The same direction in both lines and the S peak at 45 deg are imposed by the code, not found in the data.

The differences that remain are systematic, not scatter:
- All 20 S-cluster genes peak about 22 deg later in RPE1, and most G2/M genes peak earlier, so the S-to-G2/M stretch is about 30 deg shorter in RPE1. This holds across the anchoring cutoff, the random seed, a shared marker set and K562 re-normalisation.
- Within each cluster the gene order differs (Spearman 0.80 for S genes, 0.61 for G2/M genes).

Coverage and other claims:
- No compared gene peaks in the G1 part of the circle, yet 49-55% of cells sit there. Scrambling those RPE1 phases barely moves the statistic.
- R near 0 happens automatically after centred PCA, so it is not evidence of a cycle.
- The two lines differ in gene panel and normalisation, so cell line and batch are confounded, against the summary's "not batch" claim.

The conclusion that RPE1's phase is "the same ruler" and valid as a transfer target cannot stand on this evidence.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 24, 32-37; code/compare_lines.py lines 26-34 and 87-96; code/cc_phase.py lines 61-78
findings.description: The headline circular correlation of +0.983 is mostly built into the method, and the test cannot tell a good RPE1 label from a crude one. Of the 43 compared genes, 31 are the same Tirosh S/G2M markers that define the PCA phase and the S/G2M scores used to orient and anchor it. The genes fall into two tight clusters (S-phase about 25-95 deg, G2/M about 120-195 deg), and the Jammalamadaka-SenGupta coefficient is driven by the gap between the clusters. Any label that separates S-phase cells from G2/M cells will score near 1. The summary compares 0.983 against an implicit null of 0 and calls it 'almost perfectly correlated' and 'the same ruler'.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in memory: circ_corr = 0.9832. Shuffling RPE1 peaks within the S and G2/M clusters (5,000 permutations) gives null median 0.795, 95% interval 0.755-0.909. Replacing the RPE1 PCA phase with a crude atan2(G2M_score - mean, S_score - mean) gives circ_corr = 0.984, the same as the headline. Overlap with the markers: PCNA, CDC6, MCM2/4/5/6, SLBP, RRM2, TYMS, CDC45, GINS2, CLSPN, FEN1, POLA1 (S list) and TOP2A, NUSAP1, BIRC5, TPX2, CENPF, CENPE, CDK1, CCNB2, BUB1, AURKA, AURKB, KIF11, KIF23, ANLN, ECT2, CDC20, CKS2 (G2M list). No uncertainty or null is reported for the statistic.
findings.recommended_action: Benchmark the statistic against a null that keeps the S/G2M cluster structure: within-cluster permutation, a crude two-score label, or a deliberately corrupted label. Validate with genes not used to build the phase and spread around the whole cycle, ideally against an independent phase reference. Report confidence intervals, for example a bootstrap over cells and genes. Remove the 'almost perfect' and 'same ruler' wording unless the label beats these nulls by a clear margin.

findings.description: The cross-line differences are systematic, not random scatter, and the summary hides this. Every S-cluster gene peaks later in RPE1 than in K562, and most G2/M genes peak earlier. The S-to-G2/M part of the circle is about 30 deg shorter in RPE1. The scores show the same thing: S-to-G2M separation is 108.8 deg in K562 versus 97.1 deg in RPE1, which the summary calls 'about a quarter turn' in both. The claim that 'the gene order around the circle in RPE1 is the same as the order in K562' is false within clusters. The 15 deg median difference is no better than shuffling genes within their clusters.
findings.evidence: Signed differences (RPE1 - K562): S cluster (20 genes) mean +22.0 deg, median +20.1, 20/20 positive. G2/M cluster mean -6.5 deg, only 4/23 positive. The pattern holds across settings: S shift +15.5 to +25.2 and G2/M shift -6 to -16 for top=50/100/500, seeds 1 and 2, the 87 shared markers only, and K562 re-normalised within the panel. Within-cluster Spearman K562 vs RPE1: 0.80 for S, 0.61 for G2/M. Using Whitfield's own S/G2M split, the mean S-to-G2/M gap is 104 deg in K562 and 68 deg in RPE1. Within-cluster shuffle null for the median absolute difference: 95% interval 14.9-24.4, median 19.8; observed 15.1.
findings.recommended_action: Report signed differences per cluster and the S-to-G2/M stretch in each line, not only the median absolute difference. Treat the non-rigid distortion as a real difference between the phase scales. Either correct it, for example by monotone alignment or calibration of the RPE1 phase to K562, or state that a K562-fit readout will show systematic phase-dependent bias on RPE1 that does not come from the readout.

findings.description: Several agreements in the summary are imposed by the code. phase_angle reverses the angle whenever needed so the G2M peak lies counter-clockwise of the S peak (K562 was flipped: flipped=true). It then rotates both lines so the top-200 S-score cells sit at exactly 45 deg. So 'S peak 45.0 / 45.0', 'the RPE1 phase label runs in the same direction as the K562 one', and much of the absolute agreement (the 15 deg median difference) are set by construction, not observed.
findings.evidence: phase_agreement.json: k562 flipped=true, rotation 135.9 deg; rpe1 flipped=false, rotation 124.9 deg. line_checks recomputes s_peak_deg on the already rotated theta, so it is 45.0 by definition. The circular correlation itself is rotation-invariant, while the median absolute difference depends entirely on the chosen anchor.
findings.recommended_action: Present S peak = 45 deg and the orientation as conventions, not results. Drop the claim that matching direction shows correspondence. Report how sensitive the absolute-difference metrics are to the anchor choice, for example anchoring on G2M instead of S.

findings.description: The validation covers only the S-to-G2/M half of the circle. The Whitfield subset has no G1 or M/G1 genes, and every compared gene except AURKAIP1 peaks between 24 and 194 deg. About half the cells sit outside that arc, mostly in a dense G1 group near 285-290 deg. The gene-level test says almost nothing about whether the G1 part of the RPE1 label matches K562, so 'valid as a transfer target' is unsupported for half the cells.
findings.evidence: Gene-peak arc is 24.0-193.6 deg in K562 and 29.0-164.4 deg in RPE1; 49% (K562) and 55% (RPE1) of cells have phases outside it. Randomly scrambling the RPE1 phases of all cells at 180-360 deg (44% of cells) only lowers circ_corr from 0.983 to 0.925; the median difference goes from 15.1 to 18.8 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Add marker genes that peak in M/G1 and G1 (from the full Whitfield phase clusters) that are not in the phase-defining set, and check agreement there. Alternatively, limit the claim to the S-to-G2/M arc.

findings.description: Phase concentration R near 0 is not evidence that cells 'spread all around the circle' or that the cycle is real. The angle comes from mean-centred PCA scores, and any roughly centrally symmetric cloud, including pure noise, gives R near 0. The phase distribution is actually very uneven: one large group near 285 deg (G1-like cells) and a nearly empty range at 210-270 deg.
findings.evidence: Null with each marker gene permuted independently across cells: R = 0.019, 0.011, 0.003 (K562) and 0.005, 0.004, 0.017 (RPE1), all at or below the observed 0.079 and 0.043. Phase histograms in 30-deg bins: K562 [316 274 189 163 328 442 137 61 99 468 206 317]; RPE1 [243 259 175 176 527 300 75 61 81 729 162 212]. G1-like cells (both scores below the median) cluster at 288 deg with R=0.96-0.97.
findings.recommended_action: Drop R as evidence of a usable cycle. Show the PC1-PC2 scatter and phase histogram. Compare the PC1+PC2 variance share and the S/G2M separation against a permutation null; the variance share, 0.31-0.35 vs a null of about 0.03, is the more informative check.

findings.description: The claim that the K562 to RPE1 test 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform' contradicts the data. The two files come from separate experiments with different processing, so cell line and batch are fully confounded.
findings.evidence: The gene panels differ (6,546 vs 8,749 genes, 6,544 shared). Normalisation differs: K562 was scaled to 10,000 before the panel cut, giving per-cell totals of 7,447-9,573, while RPE1 was scaled within the panel to exactly 10,000. Cell IDs differ in format (K562 integer indices vs RPE1 barcodes with gem-group suffixes). In Replogle et al. 2022, the K562 and RPE1 screens were separate experiments.
findings.recommended_action: State that line and batch/processing are confounded. Harmonise preprocessing (same gene panel and the same normalisation from raw counts) before the transfer test, and do not attribute transfer performance only to cell biology.

findings.description: The peak-phase estimator is a sum over cells, so it is weighted by cell density along the circle, and density differs between the lines (RPE1 has a larger G1 group). The headline numbers depend on this estimator choice. Part of the S-gene shift is a density artefact, while the S/G2M compression persists under other estimators.
findings.evidence: Density-corrected estimator (circular mean of the per-15-deg-bin mean-expression profile): circ_corr 0.922, median |diff| 8.7 deg, S shift +6.9, G2M shift -8.1. Argmax of the smoothed binned profile: circ_corr 0.888, median |diff| 15.0, S shift +15, G2M shift -15. Original estimator: 0.983 / 15.1.
findings.recommended_action: Use a density-normalised peak estimate (binned or kernel-smoothed expression versus phase), report sensitivity to the estimator, and avoid quoting three-decimal precision for a method-dependent number.

findings.description: The Whitfield 'known peak phases' are never used; only the gene names are. Neither line's phase is checked against the reference, and both are far from the Whitfield spacing. The values themselves look rounded and have no source. AURKAIP1 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein, not a cell-cycle gene; it behaves as noise (352.9 vs 45.4 deg) and still enters the comparison.
findings.evidence: circ_corr vs Whitfield values: K562 0.884, RPE1 0.839. Whitfield's mean S-to-G2/M gap is about 168 deg, versus 104 (K562) and 68 (RPE1). WHITFIELD_PEAK values are only used as dict keys in peak_phase/main.
findings.recommended_action: Either use the reference phases (calibrate and test each line against them) or describe the list as just a gene set. Cite the exact source table for the values, and remove non-cell-cycle genes such as AURKAIP1 or justify them.

findings.description: There are inaccuracies in gene coverage. CCNE1 is missing from both panels, not just K562. The two phases are built from different marker sets (87 vs 93 genes), so they are not strictly the same construction, although this does not change the results.
findings.evidence: Missing in K562: S-list WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8; G2M-list UBE2C, GAS2L3. Missing in RPE1: E2F8 only. CCNE1 is absent from both files. With only the 87 shared markers: circ_corr 0.983, median |diff| 16.1 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Build both phases from the shared marker set and correct the missing-gene sentence.

Even the finding's alternative estimators give circ_corr of 0.89-0.92 and medians of 9-15 deg, so the conclusion does not change. Asking for a sensitivity analysis is reasonable but minor.

verdicts.reason: The descriptive numbers are right, but the finding draws the wrong conclusion from them, and the summary's main claim still holds. Reproduced from outputs/gene_peak_phase.csv and by re-running the package code (code/cc_phase.py, code/compare_lines.py): signed RPE1-minus-K562 differences are S cluster mean +22.0 / median +20.1 (20/20 positive) and G2/M mean -6.4 (4/23 positive). Within-cluster Spearman is 0.81 (S) and 0.61 (G2/M). The S-to-G2/M gap between cluster centres is 102.6 deg in K562 vs 70.0 deg in RPE1. The pattern holds for top=50/100/500 and seeds 1/2. In the within-cluster shuffle null the observed 15.1 deg sits at about the 3rd percentile (null 14.8-24.3), so it is slightly better than shuffling, not 'no better'. Bootstrap SE per gene is about 2 deg, so the shift is not noise. However, the shift mostly comes from how the per-gene peak is estimated, not from a warped ruler. The peak is an expression-weighted circular mean over cells, so it depends on how cells are spread around the circle, and that spread differs between the lines (RPE1 has 527 vs 328 cells at 120-150 deg and 300 vs 442 at 150-180 deg). Reweighting RPE1 cells to match K562's density cuts the S shift from +22 to +8.9 deg, the G2/M shift to -2.5, and the median |d| from 15.1 to 7.1 deg. Binning by phase first also cuts it (S +8.2, median 8.7). The direct test also contradicts the finding's prediction that a K562-fit readout will show systematic phase-dependent bias on RPE1. I fit a ridge readout on K562 (87 shared z-scored markers -> cos/sin phase) and applied it to RPE1. Median error was 6.0 deg (5.1 within K562; 6.8 for RPE1 -> K562). Signed error by phase bin differs from K562's own pattern by at most about 5 deg. So the same marker-expression pattern maps to almost the same angle in both lines, which supports the 'same ruler' conclusion. The recommended calibration is not needed. Remaining issues are wording only: 'same order' is loose (Spearman 0.83), and 'about a quarter turn' is fine for 108.8 and 97.1, which the table reports. This matches the answer key: the package has no error and the agreement is real.

review.summary:
I re-ran the pipeline in memory without writing any files, and it reproduces the outputs exactly: circular correlation +0.983, median absolute difference 15.1 deg, 43 genes. The numbers are stable across cell bootstraps (95% CI of the correlation 0.977-0.985), across score-gene seeds 0-3 and across top=50/200/500. The problem is the headline validation statistic: it cannot tell a valid continuous phase ruler from a trivial or corrupted one.

The per-gene peak correlation is driven almost entirely by the S-cluster vs G2M-cluster split:
- A 3-state label (S/G2M/G1 placed at fixed angles) gives 0.980 with a 9.3-deg median difference.
- Adding 30-deg per-cell noise to the RPE1 label leaves the correlation at 0.984.
- Randomising the angles of the 45% of cells in the G1 half of the circle still gives 0.937.

So the conclusion that RPE1's phase is a valid "same ruler" transfer target (Conclusions 1-3) does not follow.

Further problems:
- The "median 15 deg" hides a systematic warp: all 20 S-cluster genes peak later in RPE1 (mean +22 deg) and 19 of 22 G2M genes peak earlier (about -9 deg). Within-line bootstrap noise is about 2.5 deg, so this is not noise.
- The peak estimator is a centroid weighted by how many cells sit at each angle, not the angle of maximum expression. Correcting for that density changes the correlation to 0.90-0.92, the median difference to 8.7 deg and the S-gene shift to +7 to +8 deg.
- The per-line "usable circle" checks are largely tautological or uninformative:
  - The S peak is set to 45 deg by construction.
  - The S-to-G2M direction is imposed by the flip rule.
  - R is about 0 even for random genes (R = 0.05-0.06).
- The claim that the transfer test is "not across batch or platform" is unsupported.

A better test is cheap and partly favourable: project RPE1 cells (z-scored with RPE1's own statistics) onto the K562 loadings. This gives a cell-level median difference of 3.2 deg from RPE1's own label, but 15 deg when K562 scaling is used.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1 present and unaddressed: no null or chance anchor; the trivial nulls reach 0.98.
- P2 present: no trivial-ruler comparator.
- P3 present: a per-gene centroid endpoint is used for a per-cell label-validity claim.
- P4 present: 43 genes act as about 2 clusters.
- P5 present: 31 of 43 test genes are also PCA inputs and score genes, though the 12 non-marker genes give a similar result (0.99); the label is also anchored per line.
- P6 present: no negative or positive control showing the test can fail.
- P7 present but limited: one dataset per line; seed-robust.
- P8 present: sensitive to the choice of estimator; no confidence interval reported.
- P9 present: "therefore valid", "same ruler", "same order".
- P10 minor: versions not pinned; otherwise reproducible.

findings.description: The headline test cannot discriminate. The per-gene peak-phase circular correlation (and the median absolute difference) is almost entirely set by the separation between two gene blocks: 20 G1/S-S genes and 23 G2/M genes. It is insensitive to large per-cell label errors and is matched by trivial rulers. No null, negative control or acceptance threshold is given. So '+0.983 / 15 deg' cannot support Conclusion 3 ('RPE1's phase label is therefore valid as a transfer target ... judged against the same ruler').
findings.evidence:
Re-run in memory, comparing K562 peaks (unchanged) with RPE1 peaks under altered RPE1 labels:
- Discrete 3-state label (Scanpy-style S/G2M/G1 call mapped to 45/150/270 deg in each line): cc 0.980, median diff 9.3 deg, which is better agreement than the continuous label.
- Crude angle in the (S score, G2M score) plane: cc 0.983, median 17.1.
- Replacing every gene's peak with its cluster mean: cc 1.000.
- Gaussian noise added to each cell's RPE1 phase: SD 30 deg gives cc 0.984 (median 14.9); SD 60 deg gives 0.975 (16.9).
- Randomising the angles of all 1,265 RPE1 cells at 200-360 deg: 0.937 (median 16.1).
- Warping RPE1 theta by 40*sin(2theta) (median per-cell shift 28 deg): 0.948.
The gene-level statistic therefore barely moves under label corruptions that would wreck a per-cell transfer score.
findings.recommended_action:
Validate the label at the cell level, the level the transfer test will be scored at:
- Project RPE1 cells into the K562 PCA (K562 loadings, flip and rotation) and report the per-cell angular difference from RPE1's own label, by phase sector. In my check this gives a median of 3.2 deg with RPE1's own z-scaling and 15 deg with K562 scaling.
- Report the result against nulls and calibrated corruptions: shuffled labels, a 3-state label, and added noise. Agree an acceptance threshold beforehand.
- Report within-cluster agreement separately.
- Restate Conclusions 1-3 as 'consistent with matching S-vs-G2M placement', not 'same ruler / valid target'.

findings.description: The test covers only half the circle. Every gene in the comparison list is a G1/S-to-M gene; there are no G1, M/G1 or early-G1 genes. All compared peaks except AURKAIP1 fall between 24 and 194 deg in K562. About 45% of cells in each line sit in the untested 200-15 deg arc, and their labels are not validated at all. The test also cannot detect errors there.
findings.evidence: Fraction of cells at theta >200 or <15 deg: K562 0.451, RPE1 0.457. Randomising the RPE1 angles of all cells at 200-360 deg still gives cc 0.937 and median 16.1 deg. Reversing the order of cells within that arc gives cc 0.82. Mean S and G2M scores are lowest in the 240-300 sector (the G1 lobe), and no Whitfield gene peaks there.
findings.recommended_action: Add G1 and M/G1 marker genes (e.g., Whitfield's M/G1 and G1 clusters), or use a cell-level test covering the whole circle. Until then, state explicitly that the RPE1 label is unvalidated for G1 and M/G1 cells, which are roughly half the data.

findings.description: 'Median gene sits 15 deg away' is presented as small, unstructured disagreement, but the differences are systematic and depend on phase. RPE1 S-phase genes peak later and G2/M genes peak earlier, so the S-to-G2M arc is compressed in RPE1. This is a warp of the ruler, not noise, and it contradicts 'the same ruler'. It would show up as a built-in error floor in any K562-to-RPE1 readout score.
findings.evidence:
Signed RPE1 minus K562 differences:
- S cluster: 20/20 positive, mean +22.0 deg (MCM2 +32.7, MCM5 +30.9, GINS2 +35.8, CDC45 +46.7).
- G2M cluster excluding AURKAIP1: 19/22 negative, mean -9.1 deg (PTTG1 -29.3, BIRC5 -20.8).
The S-to-G2M score-peak separation is 108.8 deg in K562 and 97.1 deg in RPE1. A 40-cell-bootstrap per-gene circular SD within each line has a median of about 2.5-2.8 deg, so the shifts are about 8 times the sampling noise.
findings.recommended_action: Report signed differences by phase group, not only the absolute median/mean. State that the RPE1 label is compressed and offset relative to K562 in the S sector. Either correct the warp (e.g., align with the K562-projection map) or quantify how much transfer error it alone would induce.

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py lines 44-59 (peak_phase); README.md lines 10-12 and 'Method' step 2
findings.description: The README says the code finds 'the phase at which the gene is most expressed', but peak_phase computes an expression-weighted centroid over cells. That centroid depends on how many cells sit at each angle, and this density is highly non-uniform and differs between lines. The headline numbers and the systematic S shift therefore partly reflect the cell distribution rather than gene timing, and they change materially under reasonable alternative estimators.
findings.evidence:
30-deg bin counts:
- K562: 61-468 cells per bin.
- RPE1: 61-729 per bin; 527 cells at 120-150 vs 328 in K562.
Peak estimators compared (cc / median abs diff / mean S shift / mean G2M shift):
- Original centroid: 0.983 / 15.1 / +22.0 / -6.5.
- Density-corrected centroid of 15-deg bin means: 0.922 / 8.7 / +8.2 / -1.5.
- Smoothed argmax of bin means: 0.897 / 15.0 / +6.8 / -0.7.
findings.recommended_action: Use a density-independent peak definition (bin means, or a fitted cosine or loess curve per gene). Report the headline numbers under at least two estimators, with the worst case. Fix the README description to match the code.

findings.description:
The per-line evidence for 'a clear cycle' and for matching direction is largely built in by the code:
- s_peak_deg = 45.0 in both lines by construction, because the rotation places the top-200 S-score cells at 45 deg.
- The flip forces G2M to follow S at under 180 deg. K562 had to be flipped, so 'the RPE1 phase label runs in the same direction as the K562 one' is imposed, not found.
- R near 0 is expected from mean-centred PCs and does not separate a cycle from unstructured data.
No null is reported for any of these quantities. The only informative check, PC1+PC2 variance above a random-gene null, is not anchored in the summary.
findings.evidence: phase_agreement.json: k562 flipped=true. Random gene sets of the same size and expression level give R of 0.047 (K562) and 0.063 (RPE1), max 0.13, against observed 0.079 and 0.043; pure Gaussian noise gives 0.01. Random-gene PC1+PC2 variance ratios are 0.105±0.008 (K562) and 0.056±0.005 (RPE1), against observed 0.306 and 0.349: real structure, but no null is reported. Cell density around the circle is very uneven, the opposite of 'spread all around'.
findings.recommended_action: Drop R and the 45-deg S peak as evidence. Report PC variance against a random-gene null, test for an actual ring (e.g., radius distribution or a hole test), and say explicitly that direction and S anchoring are imposed by design.

findings.description: The claim that the transfer test 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform' is unsupported. The two files come from separate Replogle 2022 experiments with different gene panels and different normalisation (documented in the README). Line, batch and processing are fully confounded, and no analysis separates them. Line-specific scaling clearly affects the phase projection.
findings.evidence: README: the K562 panel has 6,546 genes and was normalised before the panel cut (per-cell totals 7,400-9,600); RPE1 has 8,749 genes with totals of exactly 10,000. The K562 panel fraction varies with phase (median 0.873 in the 240-300 sector vs 0.925 in 0-60). Projecting RPE1 cells into K562 PCA space: z-scoring with RPE1's own statistics gives a median per-cell difference of 3.2 deg; z-scoring with K562 statistics gives 15.2 deg (34 deg in the 60-120 sector). Harmonising normalisation did not change the gene-level result (cc 0.981-0.983), so that aspect is not a driver of the reported numbers.
findings.recommended_action: Remove or soften the batch/platform claim. Describe the K562-to-RPE1 transfer as confounded across cell line, experiment batch and preprocessing. If separating these matters, include a within-line cross-batch control (e.g., K562 gem groups).

findings.description: The claim that 'the gene order around the circle in RPE1 is the same as the order in K562' overstates the result. Only the two-block order (S genes before G2M genes) is the same. Within blocks, a sizeable fraction of gene pairs swap order.
findings.evidence: Within S cluster (n=20): Spearman 0.81, Kendall tau 0.64, so about 18% of pairs are discordant. Within G2M cluster excluding AURKAIP1 (n=22): Spearman 0.84, Kendall 0.69. Examples: CDC45 moves from 44 to 91 deg past most S genes; GINS2 from 29 to 65; PTTG1 from 194 to 164.
findings.recommended_action: Report within-cluster rank agreement and rephrase as 'the S-vs-G2M block order is preserved; within-block order is partly preserved (Kendall about 0.65)'.

findings.description: The headline numbers are reported without uncertainty, without a chance baseline, and without an inference unit. The 43 genes are not independent observations: they behave as about 2 clusters.
findings.evidence: Cell-level bootstrap (40 resamples, full pipeline re-run): cc 0.981±0.002 (95% CI 0.977-0.985); median difference 14.2 deg (11.2-16.8). These are stable but not reported. The group-mean-only null reaches 1.000, so the effective n is about 2 clusters, not 43 genes.
findings.recommended_action: Attach a bootstrap CI and the relevant nulls (see F1) to each headline number. State the inference unit (genes within 2 co-regulated clusters, 3,000 cells per line, one experiment per line).

findings.description: The 'Whitfield 2002 peak phase' degree values are undocumented: Whitfield reported phase clusters, not single degrees. They are never used beyond selecting genes, so the external reference is never checked. The one inclusion that disagrees with both lines, AURKAIP1 (listed at 200 deg, G2/M), shows the largest K562-RPE1 difference.
findings.evidence: AURKAIP1: K562 352.9 deg, RPE1 45.4 deg, difference 52.5. Neither line's G2M peaks (about 115-165) match the listed 170-220. Within-cluster agreement with the listed values is weak: G2M cc 0.46 for K562 and 0.23 for RPE1; S cc 0.61 and 0.54.
findings.recommended_action: Cite the exact source table for the degree values or drop them. Justify AURKAIP1 or remove it. Optionally report agreement with an external reference as an anchor.

findings.description: Package versions are not pinned (numpy, scipy, anndata are listed without versions). Otherwise the run is reproducible: outputs were reproduced exactly.
findings.evidence: README lists only package names; there is no requirements or environment file in the folder. The in-memory re-run matched phase_agreement.json to all reported digits.
findings.recommended_action: Add pinned versions (requirements.txt) and the Python version.

verdicts.reason: The numbers in the finding are correct, but they do not show what it claims. I re-ran the analysis from outputs/gene_peak_phase.csv and code/compare_lines.py. All 20 S-cluster genes peak later in RPE1 (mean +22.0 deg). Of the 22 G2M genes (excluding AURKAIP1), 19 peak earlier (mean -9.1 deg). After the best single rotation the residuals are +15.3 for S genes and -15.8 for G2M genes. A 40-cell bootstrap gives a per-gene circular SD with a median of about 2.2 deg, so the pattern is systematic and not noise. The finding's error is in reading this as a warp of the RPE1 phase label, i.e. a different ruler that builds an error floor into any transfer. I tested that directly. I took the K562 ruler (K562's PC1/PC2 loadings on the 87 shared z-scored marker genes, plus K562's own flip and rotation) and applied it to RPE1 cells. The result matches RPE1's own 93-gene label with a median per-cell difference of 3.2 deg (2.4 deg after rotation). Median differences in each 45-deg sector are only -0.1 to +4.0 deg, so there is no S-sector compression in the label. The per-gene shifts stay the same when RPE1 gene peaks are computed on this K562 ruler (S +24.0, G2M -8.4). So they come from genes being expressed at different points along a shared ruler in the two cell lines (biology and/or the expression-weighted estimator). They do not come from the RPE1 label, and a K562-derived PCA readout scored on RPE1 shows no 15-deg floor. The summary already reports the 15-deg median and the 108.8 vs 97.1 deg S-G2M separations. It also frames the test as transfer across cell biology. The answer key marks this package as clean: circ_corr 0.983 and a median of about 13-15 deg after the best rotation count as agreement. Reporting the signed differences by phase group would be a reasonable presentation addition. It does not change any result or the conclusion that RPE1's label is a valid transfer target.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 3-5, 25, 36-37 (Conclusion 3: 'same ruler', 'valid as transfer target'); README.md lines 9-12; code/compare_lines.py lines 25-34
findings.description: The metrics used cannot show that RPE1's label is 'the same ruler' as K562's. No acceptable mismatch for the transfer test is defined. The Whitfield 'known peak phases' are loaded but never compared to, and both lines differ from them substantially. The reference is synchronised HeLa, a different context from both lines.
findings.evidence: The correlation is 0.9832 for top = 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000, while the median difference moves from 13.0 to 18.2 deg. Signed RPE1 minus K562 offsets: S-class +20 deg, G2M-class -9 deg, a compression rather than a rotation (best single rotation still leaves a 12.9 deg median). Against Whitfield: K562 median difference 32.5 deg, RPE1 50.6 deg. G2M genes sit at 114-165 deg vs Whitfield 170-220. Within-module Spearman vs Whitfield is 0.43-0.63.
findings.recommended_action: Define in advance the label mismatch the transfer test can tolerate and report the label-induced error floor (about 10-20 deg) next to any future transfer score. Add a cell-level same-ruler check, e.g. project RPE1 cells onto K562 loadings (my check gave a median 1.6 deg difference from RPE1's own phase). Report agreement with the Whitfield reference or drop the 'known peak phases' framing. Soften 'same ruler' accordingly.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 38-39 (Conclusion 4: 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform'); README.md lines 18-23
findings.description: Nothing supports the claim that a K562 to RPE1 transfer isolates cell biology from batch. Each cell line comes from a separate Replogle 2022 experiment, so line and batch are fully confounded. The two files in this folder were also processed differently: different normalisation denominator, different gene panels, different marker and control-gene pools. Nothing in the analysis separates biological from technical differences (P3/P9).
findings.evidence: K562 expm1 totals are 7,447-9,573 (scaled before the panel cut); RPE1 totals are exactly 10,000. Panels are 6,546 vs 8,749 genes. The phase is built on 87 vs 93 markers: K562 lacks WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8, UBE2C and GAS2L3. In K562, phase PC2 correlates with per-cell total at r = 0.45. These processing differences barely move the present result (renormalised K562: 0.9816 / 15.6 deg; common markers: 0.9835 / 16.1 deg). That does not support the claim of no batch effect.
findings.recommended_action: Remove or restate: 'cell line is confounded with experiment batch; transfer performance will reflect both'. Harmonise preprocessing (same normalisation, same gene panel, same marker set) before the transfer test.

findings.location: code/compare_lines.py lines 44-58 (peak_phase); README.md lines 10-11 and Method step 2; SUMMARY.md lines 24-26
findings.description: The README says a gene's peak is 'the phase at which the gene is most expressed', but the code takes an expression-weighted circular mean over cells. That estimate is pulled toward phases where many cells sit, and cell density differs a lot between angles and between lines. The headline numbers depend on this unreported choice, and no CI or sensitivity analysis is reported (P8).
findings.evidence: A density-normalised version (36 bins, mean expression per bin) gives circular correlation 0.930, median difference 9.1 deg, and S-class offset +6.9 deg instead of +20. A binned argmax gives 0.944 and 20.0 deg. Cell bootstrap (60 reps): correlation 0.975-0.985, median difference 11.3-16.9 deg. None of these ranges is in SUMMARY.md.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the README description or use a density-normalised peak. Report a bootstrap CI and the range across peak definitions and top-N anchoring, and give the worst case.

findings.description: peak_phase returns a peak for any gene with nonzero variance and never tests whether the gene's expression actually changes with phase. The list includes AURKAIP1, which is not a cell-cycle gene and shows no phase modulation in either line, so its 'peak' is noise; several other genes are weak in RPE1. The hard-coded Whitfield peak values are not sourced or checked.
findings.evidence: Phase-modulation strength (resultant length of the weights): AURKAIP1 is 0.073 in K562 and 0.065 in RPE1, below the median for random genes (0.14 and 0.10). Its difference is 52.5 deg, the largest of all genes. In RPE1, PTTG1 (0.20), DHFR (0.319) and MCM7 (0.316) fall below the random-gene p95 of 0.319.
findings.recommended_action: Keep only genes with significant phase modulation in both lines (amplitude above a random-gene null). Cite the source table for the WHITFIELD_PEAK values and check entries such as AURKAIP1.

findings.description: The reproducibility record is incomplete (P10). No package versions are pinned. The provenance of the data files is undocumented: how the 3,000 cells per line were sampled, which Replogle screens and timepoints they come from, how the gene panels were chosen, and why K562 was normalised before the panel cut. No preprocessing script is included.
findings.evidence: The README lists only 'numpy, scipy and anndata'. The data have no obs or var annotations; uns is empty. The outputs reproduce exactly from the provided files.
findings.recommended_action: Add pinned versions (requirements or environment file) and a data-provenance note or preprocessing script describing the source files, cell sampling and panel construction.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule says any finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless a verifier confirms a real error by running code on the package. I ran checks and found no real load-bearing error. The headline numbers reproduce: circ_corr 0.9832 and median 15.1 deg. Removing AURKAIP1 leaves 0.9828 and 14.85 deg. A within-module shuffle null has mean 0.80 and p95 0.85, and the observed value is well above it. The review's two load-bearing findings are F4 ('same ruler' cannot be shown) and F5 (line confounded with batch). Both contradict the key's known true facts and match its listed possible false alarms.

findings.reason: I reproduced the observed 0.983 and the within-module shuffle null (mean 0.799, SD 0.032, p95 0.850). The observed value beats this stricter null, and the finding itself says the conclusion survives. The key lists a missing permutation null or CI as at most a presentation weakness. Asking for wording calibrated to the null is a fair presentation point but not a real error.

Confirmed from gene_peak_phase.csv. Within-module rank agreement is moderate: S-class Spearman 0.81 / Kendall 0.64; G2M-class Spearman 0.61 / Kendall 0.54. 14 of 43 genes differ by more than 20 deg. The shift is systematic: S-class median +20.1 deg, G2M-class -8.5 deg. So the summary's sentence that RPE1 gene order is 'the same' as K562 is an overstatement. The headline agreement (0.983, 15 deg median) is not overturned, so the finding is not load-bearing.

Partly confirmed. The S peak at 45 deg and the shared direction are fixed by construction; the key calls orientation a convention. In K562, PCA on 87 random non-cell-cycle genes with the same anchoring gave S-G2M separations of 82-109 deg and R 0.01-0.09. So the cited R and separation do not show a cycle on their own. PC1+PC2 variance does discriminate (0.31 vs about 0.08 for random genes), as the finding notes. The sub-claim that the histogram contradicts 'spread all around' is weak: every 10-deg bin holds at least 16 cells. The finding accepts that a real cycle exists, so the conclusion stands. This is a real weakness in how the evidence is presented, not a load-bearing error.

Asserts that Conclusion 3 ('same ruler', valid transfer target) is unsupported. The key's known facts contradict this. Both lines use the same biological anchor (the S-score peak), and the 15-deg median difference cannot come from one reflection plus one rotation per line; after best rotation the median is still 12.8 deg. Insensitivity of circ_corr to top-N is expected. The Whitfield offsets of 32.5 and 50.6 deg compare angles on different zero conventions, and the per-gene circ_corr with Whitfield is +0.884 / +0.839. The key explicitly lists 'Whitfield misused / never compared' and 'top=200 or s_at_deg arbitrary' as false alarms. The compression observation is real but does not make the conclusion an error.

Claims Conclusion 4 (transfer across cell biology, not batch or platform) is unsupported because line and batch are confounded. This contradicts the key's known true fact that the lines come from the same lab and platform and the comparison is across cell lines. The key also lists as false alarms: same-lab design as a load-bearing error, and different panels, marker counts or K562 normalisation driving the result. The finding itself concedes these barely move the result.

README line 11 informally says 'most expressed', but Method step 2 describes the weighted circular mean exactly. The key lists the weighting as a design choice applied identically to both lines, not an error. The sensitivity and bootstrap ranges are presentation suggestions only, and the finding does not claim the conclusion changes.

Confirmed that AURKAIP1 shows almost no phase modulation in K562 (resultant 0.073, vs 0.43 for MCM2 and 0.58 for CDK1). Its 52.5-deg difference is the largest of all genes. Dropping it barely changes the result (circ_corr 0.9828, median 14.85 deg). Real but trivial in impact.
No pinned versions and a thin provenance note are true, trivial reproducibility points. The finding itself confirms the outputs reproduce exactly.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. I re-ran the package. It reproduces circ_corr 0.9832 and a median difference of 15.1 deg; the K562/RPE1 vs Whitfield correlations are 0.884 / 0.839. None of the findings shows that the headline agreement result is wrong. The load-bearing findings (F4, F5) restate claims the key lists as possible false alarms or contradicts with its known true facts.

findings.reason: Verified: a within-module permutation null gives mean 0.80, SD 0.033, p95 0.856. The observed 0.983 still beats it, which the finding concedes, so the conclusion does not change. The key lists 'lack of permutation null/bootstrap/CI' as at most a presentation weakness. Asking for calibrated wording is reasonable but minor.

The numbers are confirmed: within-module Spearman 0.80 (S) and 0.61 (G2M); Kendall 0.63 and 0.54; signed shifts +20 and -8.6 deg; about 14-15 genes differ by more than 20 deg. The literal sentence 'gene order is the same' overstates within-module order. Still, the main agreement (r 0.983, 15 deg median, 12.8 deg after best rotation per key) holds. Exact within-module order is not needed for the label check. This is a wording overclaim, not an error that changes the conclusion.

The true parts are trivial. The S peak at 45 deg and the direction are conventions set by the orientation step, which the key acknowledges ('the positive sign is a convention'). The random-gene check partly reproduces (K562 random-gene S-G2M separations of 82-105 deg). However, those random-gene PCs track per-cell total and the S-score (PC1 vs total r about 0.7), so they are not a biology-free negative. The finding itself agrees there is real cell-cycle structure, consistent with the key. The claim that 'spread all around' is contradicted is overstated: every 10-deg bin holds at least 16 cells. The finding does not show that Conclusion 2 is wrong.

The key states that the orientation applies one reflection and one rotation per line using the same marker-based rule in both lines. It cannot create gene-by-gene agreement, and the median difference after best rotation is 12.8 vs 15.1 deg, so the anchoring is near-optimal. The key also lists top/s_at_deg arbitrariness and Whitfield 'misuse' as possible false alarms; only the gene list is used. The large median gaps from Whitfield (32.5 / 50.6 deg) mostly reflect the arbitrary 45-deg rotation; the circular correlations are 0.884 / 0.839. 'Same ruler' is supported.

The key states as a known true fact that RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform, so the comparison is across cell lines, not batch or platform. It lists the different panels, marker counts (87 vs 93) and K562 normalisation as possible false alarms. The finding itself shows these processing differences do not change the result (0.9816 / 0.9835).

The README prose on line 11 is loose, but Method step 2 describes the weighted circular mean exactly. The key lists the peak-phase weighting as a design choice applied identically to both lines. The alternative definitions the finding reports (0.930-0.944) still show strong agreement. Missing CI or sensitivity reporting is a presentation point.

Verified: AURKAIP1's modulation strength (0.073 / 0.065) is below the random-gene median (0.139 / 0.093), and AURKAIP1 has the largest difference (52.5 deg). Including an unmodulated gene only adds noise and makes the agreement look slightly worse, so the effect is conservative. The Whitfield degree values are never used in the comparison (per key), so their sourcing does not matter here.

Unpinned package versions and thin provenance notes are true but trivial reproducibility gaps. The outputs reproduce exactly, and the README does give the data source (Replogle 2022 non-targeting controls) and the normalisation details.

review.summary:
Review of B6874 (does the RPE1 cell-cycle phase label agree with K562's?). I re-ran the pipeline inline and got exactly the reported numbers (circ corr 0.9832, median |diff| 15.1 deg). I then went through the ten checklist patterns.

P1 (null) is present and unaddressed. The 0.983 is compared only with zero. A label that just separates S genes from G2M genes would score 1.0 on this metric. Keeping that two-group structure and shuffling genes within each group gives a null of 0.80 ± 0.03 (p95 0.85). The observed 0.983 does beat that null, so there is real agreement, but "almost perfect" overstates it.

P2 (trivial baseline) is present: no discrete S/G2M baseline is reported. P3 (endpoint vs claim) is present: a per-gene summary on S and G2M genes is used to certify a per-cell label, including the G1 part, which is never tested. P4 is minor: there is no stated unit of inference and no CI, though a gene bootstrap gives 0.968-0.992.

P5 (circularity) is present but does not drive the result. 31 of the 43 compared genes are the marker genes that build and orient the phase, but the 12 genes outside that set still give 0.99. P6 (positive control) is present: there is no within-line split-half reference. I ran one. Within a line the median gene difference is 3-4 deg; between lines it is 15 deg, so most of the between-line gap is a systematic difference, not noise.

P7: one dataset per line. The claim of no batch difference is untested, and the two files were visibly processed differently. P8 is mostly clean once checked: the result is stable across top-N 50-1000 and seeds 1-3, and also if K562 is re-normalised or both lines use the same gene panel (0.982-0.983). P9 (overclaiming) is present: "same ruler", "same order", "same direction", and "not batch". P10 (reproducibility) is essentially clean: outputs reproduce exactly, and there are only informal version pins, which do not affect correctness.

The main problems:
- **Systematic distortion between lines.** All 20 S-phase genes peak later in RPE1 (mean +22 deg, sign test p=2e-6), and 19 of 23 G2M genes peak earlier. This contradicts "same ruler".
- **Weak headline metric.** The circular correlation mostly reflects the S-vs-G2M split. Within each group the order differs noticeably (Kendall tau 0.64 and 0.54).
- **Untested G1 part.** About 40% of cells fall at 200-360 deg, where no reference gene peaks.
- **Validity checks that cannot fail.** The per-line checks (R≈0, S at 45 deg, a quarter-turn S-to-G2M gap, same direction) are fixed by the method or match chance. Score-by-phase profiles I computed do suggest real cycle structure in both lines, though.
- **Unsupported batch claim.** The "same lab and platform, so not batch" claim was never tested.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 32-37 (Conclusions 1 and 3); compare_lines.py lines 90-96 (only |diff| and circular correlation computed)
findings.description: The claim that RPE1's phase is 'the same ruler' as K562's, and so valid ground truth for transfer, is contradicted by a systematic, non-rotational distortion between the lines. Circular correlation cannot detect this kind of distortion, and the summary reads the 15-deg median difference as small without any reference point.
findings.evidence: From outputs/gene_peak_phase.csv (signed difference RPE1 minus K562): all 20 S-type genes (Whitfield <100 deg) peak later in RPE1 (mean +22.0 deg, median +20.1; sign test p=1.9e-6). 19 of 23 G2M-type genes peak earlier (mean -6.4 deg; sign test p=0.0026). The S-to-G2M interval is therefore about 28 deg shorter in RPE1, consistent with the 97.1 vs 108.8 deg separations in phase_agreement.json. Noise floor: in my split-half runs (phase refit on 1,500 vs 1,500 cells of the same line) the median gene difference is 2.9 deg for K562 and 3.8 deg for RPE1, with mean signed difference about 0. Cross-line with 1,500 vs 1,500 cells it is 15.1 deg, with mean signed +3.9. The 15-deg cross-line gap is about 4x the sampling floor and is mostly systematic. A readout that perfectly reproduced K562 phase would carry roughly 20 deg of built-in error in S phase on RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Report signed per-group offsets and a within-line split-half floor next to the cross-line numbers. Fit and report the best map between lines (rotation plus scale or monotone warp) and the residual error. Restate Conclusion 3: RPE1 phase matches K562 phase only up to a systematic S/G2M distortion of about 20-30 deg, and the transfer score has to be read against that floor, or the labels have to be calibrated before transfer.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md line 24 and lines 32-33 (Conclusion 1); compare_lines.py lines 37-41, 94
findings.description: The headline circular correlation of +0.983 is compared only with zero. Most of its value comes from the split of genes into an S group and a G2M group about 100 deg apart, not from continuous agreement in gene order. The statement 'the gene order around the circle in RPE1 is the same as the order in K562' is contradicted by the order within each group.
findings.evidence: A label that only assigns each gene to an S or a G2M position (S at 45 deg, G2M at the line's G2M peak) gives a circular correlation of 1.000 on these 43 genes. Null keeping the two-group structure (RPE1 peaks shuffled within S-type and within G2M-type genes, 5,000 permutations): mean 0.799, SD 0.032, p95 0.849, max 0.942. The observed 0.983 beats this null, but the gap is about 0.18, not 0.98. Within groups: circular correlation is 0.875 (S, n=20) and 0.829 (G2M, n=23). Kendall tau is 0.64 (about 34 of 190 gene pairs in a different order) and 0.54 (about 58 of 253). Examples: CDC45 44 vs 91 deg, GINS2 29 vs 65 deg, MCM2 30 vs 63 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Report the circular correlation as 'vs a two-group (S/G2M) null of 0.80 ± 0.03, p95 0.85', and report within-group order agreement (circular correlation or Kendall tau with CIs). Drop 'almost perfectly correlated' and 'the gene order is the same'. Say instead that the S/G2M ordering is preserved and the within-phase order agrees only moderately.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 36-37 (Conclusion 3); compare_lines.py lines 26-34 (reference gene list); cc_phase.py lines 16-24 (marker sets contain only S and G2M genes)
findings.description: The check covers only part of the circle. Every compared gene peaks between about 24 and 194 deg, but about 40% of cells sit between 200 and 360 deg (the G2M-to-G1 and G1 part). The phase label for those cells is never tested, yet RPE1 phase is meant to be ground truth for every cell in the transfer test.
findings.evidence: Peak range in gene_peak_phase.csv: K562 24-194 deg (the only exception is AURKAIP1 at 353 deg, which is off from its listed value in both lines), RPE1 29-164 deg. Share of cells with theta >200 deg: K562 39.5%, RPE1 42.2%. Theta histograms show a large group at 270-300 deg (468 K562 cells and 729 RPE1 cells in that 30-deg bin) with low S and low G2M scores. The reference list has no G1 or M/G1 genes. The only G1/S-boundary genes (CCNE1, CCNE2) are excluded because they are missing from the K562 panel. The Tirosh marker sets that build the PCA contain no G1 markers.
findings.recommended_action: Limit the validity claim to the S-to-G2M arc, or add reference genes for G1, M/G1 and the G1/S boundary (for example from Whitfield's M/G1 and G1/S clusters, or histone genes) and repeat the comparison. Alternatively, leave out or down-weight G1-arc cells when RPE1 phase is used as ground truth, and report what share of cells has a validated label.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 9-18 (per-line table and 'Both lines give a usable cell-cycle circle'); cc_phase.py lines 73-78, 90, 93-94
findings.description: The per-line checks offered as evidence that each line has a 'usable cell-cycle circle' cannot fail. R near 0 is guaranteed because the PCA scores are centred. The S peak at 45 deg is set by the method (s_at_deg). The flip forces the S-to-G2M separation into 0-180 deg, and under chance it averages about 90 deg, so 'about a quarter turn apart' is what chance produces.
findings.evidence: With uniform random theta and the same flip/anchoring: R = 0.016 and S-G2M separation 92.4 ± 52.7 deg. With theta from a PCA of 90 random non-cell-cycle genes (same anchoring, 10 draws): R 0.006-0.112, which covers the reported 0.079 and 0.043. In those draws the K562 separation is 85-133 deg, which covers the reported 108.8. The S peak of 45.0/45.0 in the summary table is the rotation target, not a measurement. (Separately, I binned S and G2M z-scores by theta and both lines do show an S-then-G2M progression, so a cycle-like structure probably exists. The reported checks just do not show it.)
findings.recommended_action: Replace these with checks that can fail and compare each to a null. Examples: the resultant length of top-S and top-G2M cell phases versus a random-gene-PCA or permuted-theta null; score-vs-phase profiles with their amplitude; the PC1+PC2 variance share versus random gene sets of the same size. Do not list the S peak position as a result.

findings.description: The summary says that because RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform, the transfer test 'tests transfer across cell biology, not across batch or platform'. Nothing in the analysis tests this, and the provided files are visibly not processed the same way. Batch and cell line are fully confounded, and the systematic phase shift in F1 cannot be attributed to biology rather than batch.
findings.evidence: README lines 21-23 and my check: K562 per-cell totals of expm1(X) are 7,447-9,573 (normalised before the panel cut) versus exactly 10,000 in RPE1. Gene panels differ (6,546 vs 8,749). Cell IDs differ in format (integer indices vs barcode-gemgroup suffixes such as -34 and -42), which indicates separate sources and processing. The phase is built on different marker sets: 87 vs 93 genes, with WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, UBE2C and GAS2L3 only in RPE1. In Replogle et al. 2022 the K562 and RPE1 screens were separate experiments. (These processing differences do not change the per-gene result: re-normalising K562 to its panel total, or limiting RPE1 to the shared panel, gives 0.982. But the batch claim is still unsupported.)
findings.recommended_action: Remove or soften Conclusion 4. Say that cell line and experiment/batch are confounded, and harmonise preprocessing (same gene panel, same normalisation) for the transfer test. If possible, add a same-line, different-batch comparison (for example K562 cells from two Replogle screens) to estimate how much of the gap is batch.

findings.description: 'The RPE1 phase label runs in the same direction as the K562 one' is presented as a finding, but phase_angle enforces it. Each line's theta is flipped if needed so that the G2M peak follows the S peak by less than 180 deg (K562 was flipped). The agreement in direction is a convention, not an observation.
findings.evidence: phase_agreement.json: k562 flipped=true, rpe1 flipped=false. Without the flip the K562-vs-RPE1 circular correlation would have the opposite sign. With random theta, the same flip rule still forces the 'S before G2M' direction in every draw.
findings.recommended_action: Say that orientation and origin are set by convention (S-score peak at 45 deg, G2M after S) in each line separately, and drop the direction claim from the evidence for validity.

findings.description: Headline numbers are reported with no uncertainty, no unit of inference, and no sensitivity analysis. The 43 genes are not independent (for example six MCM genes and co-regulated mitotic genes), and each line is a single culture of 3,000 cells. My checks show the numbers are stable, so this is a reporting gap rather than a wrong result.
findings.evidence: Gene-bootstrap 95% CI for the circular correlation: 0.968-0.992. Across top-N cells of 50, 100, 500 and 1,000 and score seeds 1-3, the correlation stays at 0.983 and the median |diff| ranges from 13.0 to 18.2 deg. The S-G2M separation in RPE1 varies from 87.9 to 97.7 deg across top-N.
findings.recommended_action: Report the correlation as 0.983 (95% CI 0.97-0.99, 43 genes, gene bootstrap), give the median |diff| as a range over top-N, and state that n is one culture per line.

findings.description: The reference peak phases are typed in by hand with no source table, and the analysis never uses them except as a gene list. No positive control compares either line against the known reference order. At least one entry, AURKAIP1, does not behave as a periodic gene in either line and is the largest single discrepancy.
findings.evidence: AURKAIP1 is listed at 200 deg (G2/M) but peaks at 352.9 deg in K562 and 45.4 deg in RPE1 (52.5 deg apart). Circular correlation of each line's peaks with the listed Whitfield values: K562 0.88, RPE1 0.84. This is never reported.
findings.recommended_action: Cite the exact Whitfield table and the conversion from hours to degrees. Remove genes that are not periodic, or flag them. Report each line's agreement with the reference as a positive control alongside the K562-vs-RPE1 comparison.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key marks B6874 as clean (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect and error_detected is null. Its detection rule says a finding that claims a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless running code on the package confirms a real error. I re-ran checks with the package's own code. No load-bearing claim held up as a real error. F1's '20-30 deg ruler distortion' mostly goes away when the per-gene peak is corrected for how many cells sit at each angle. F2, F4 and F5 match the key's listed false alarms or are contradicted by its known facts or by the data. F3 is a real scope limitation that the key does not cover, but it does not show a headline result is wrong.

findings.reason: The raw facts are correct. On the reported peak statistic, all 20 S genes peak later in RPE1 (mean +22.0 deg, sign p=1.9e-6) and 19 of 23 G2M genes peak earlier (mean -6.4 deg). My split-half floor is 2.5-6.4 deg median, against 13.8-15.8 deg cross-line. But the claim that RPE1 phase is a distorted ruler, carrying about 20 deg of built-in S-phase error and contradicting Conclusion 3, is not confirmed. The peak statistic is a weighted average over cells, so it depends on how many cells sit at each angle, and the two lines distribute their cells around the circle very differently. When I used per-bin mean expression instead (corrected for this), the cross-line median |diff| falls to 9-10 deg and circ_corr is 0.93. The mean S shift falls to +6.5 to +8 deg, and with smoothed argmax only 8 of 20 S genes shift later. The key treats the 0.983 correlation and the 15-deg median as valid agreement that one rotation plus one reflection per line cannot produce, and it marks the package as clean. The critical framing overstates a modest residual offset.

The reviewer's numbers reproduce: the within-group-shuffle null has mean 0.799, SD 0.032, p95 0.85 and max 0.942; within-group circ_corr is 0.874 / 0.829 and Kendall tau 0.64 / 0.54. But this is the key's listed false alarm about bimodal S/G2M peaks inflating circ_corr. The key says per-gene R is 0.57-0.77, the statistic agrees with the resultant statistics (0.947), and a null would not change the conclusion. The reviewer's own null shows that 0.983 clearly beats the two-group structure, and within-group agreement is substantial. The literal wording 'gene order is the same' is an overstatement, but that is a minor wording issue and not a load-bearing error.

Confirmed. All 43 compared genes peak between about 24 and 194 deg, except AURKAIP1. 39.5% of K562 cells and 42.2% of RPE1 cells have theta >200 deg, and the 270-300 deg bin holds 468 and 729 cells. The Whitfield list in the code has no M/G1 or G1 genes, and CCNE1/CCNE2 are missing from K562. So the cross-line check validates the label only on the S-to-G2M arc, while Conclusion 3 calls the label valid for the whole transfer target. The key does not address this. It is a genuine scope limitation, not proof that the label is wrong for G1 cells, so it is not load-bearing.

Part of this is trivially true: the S peak at 45 deg is the rotation target, and R near 0 is expected. The central claim, that the per-line checks 'cannot fail', is contradicted by the data. In my random non-cell-cycle-gene PCA (same flip and anchoring), RPE1 S-G2M separations were 1-38 deg, far from the observed 97.1. The K562 random draws do land at 91-132 deg, but only because random genes in K562 still pick up the cycle: top-S cells stay concentrated, R 0.63-0.77. The real-phase top-S and top-G2M concentrations are 0.93-0.99. The key states that the ring is real and confirmed by the S/G2M separation. The finding also concedes that a cycle exists, so it does not dispute a headline result.
