findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha per arm by cross-validation on K562 only (nested inside the source), or report a sweep of at least 3 points and give the worst case for the headline contrast. Update the results table, since every R_diff changes by about 0.03 at the CV-chosen alpha.

findings.description: The 95% CI resamples only RPE1 test cells, with the K562-fitted readout and the phase labels held fixed. It leaves out variability from the training cells, from the label construction, and from having a single source-to-target pair. The claim is about cell-line transfer, yet only one pair in one direction was tested. Conclusion 3 then generalises to SCFM evaluation and to 'C2S comes out ahead'.
findings.evidence: Reversing the direction (RPE1 to K562, alpha=1000) changes the picture a lot. Model 0.758 vs expr_512_rank 0.632 (+0.126) and vs sentence-matched rank 0.570. Model vs presence is +0.036 in reverse but -0.031 forward. Between-direction differences are roughly 5-10 times the forward CI width (about 0.026), so the reported CI does not capture the variability that matters for the claim.
findings.recommended_action: Refit the readout inside the bootstrap by resampling K562 training cells as well, report both transfer directions, and add more layers and cell lines if available. State the inference unit (one cell-line pair; 3,000 cells is not the replication unit). Limit Conclusion 3 to this pair, layer and readout.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py:53-64 (theta from PCA of marker-gene log-expression); code/transfer.py:99-101; SUMMARY.md:20-22, 30-32
findings.description: The target angle is computed from the log-expression magnitudes of 87 (K562) or 93 (RPE1) Tirosh marker genes, and those genes are inputs to the expression arms. The expr_full ceiling and the decomposition of the 'tokenisation loss' (0.068 from keeping 512 genes plus 0.036 from dropping values) therefore largely measure how close each encoding stays to the label's own construction, which mostly lies outside a 512-gene sentence. They are not an intrinsic cost of the tokenizer for cell-cycle information. Conclusion 2 also says the loss happens 'before the first layer', but no layer-0 representation was ever measured.
findings.evidence: A ridge on the 87 marker genes alone reaches R_diff 0.918 with 12.7 deg median error, better than expr_full (0.878). All genes except the markers give 0.839. Only 8.5 of the 93 RPE1 marker genes appear in an average RPE1 cell sentence.
findings.recommended_action: Use a phase label that does not come from the evaluated features: for example a held-out marker set excluded from all arms, an external reference such as tricycle/Revelio projection fitted on other data, or FUCCI-like ground truth. Alternatively, drop the marker genes from every expression arm. Rephrase Conclusion 2 as a comparison of linear readouts against a marker-derived label, and drop 'before the first layer' unless an embedding or layer-0 arm is added.

findings.description: The wording goes beyond what the evidence supports. Layer-21 activations are a deterministic function of the cell sentence, so they cannot contain information the input lacks. The analysis can only show that a linear ridge readout transfers better or worse. The model's input also carries more than the baseline arm: the RPE1-only genes, gene-name identity, and the tie order. So 'adds information beyond its input', 'its processing adds a small amount of cell-cycle information' and 'C2S comes out ahead' are not supported, especially given F1 to F3.
findings.evidence: The verdict string 'MODEL ADDS information beyond its input encoding' is hard-coded for a lower CI bound > 0 (transfer.py:136). Summary Conclusion 1 states it as fact.
findings.recommended_action: Restate as 'a frozen linear (ridge, alpha=...) readout of layer-21 activations transfers K562 to RPE1 phase about as well as / slightly better or worse than a linear readout of the same top-512 gene list', with the encoding-dependence and the metric disagreement stated up front. Name the negative and parity results as findings.

findings.description: The 'true' RPE1 phase is a noisy, line-specific proxy. It comes from a separate PCA in each line on different marker sets (87 vs 93 genes), and PC1-2 explain only about a third of the marker variance. Label quality and cross-line agreement are never reported, so it is unclear how much of every arm's error is label noise.
findings.evidence: phase_angle_oriented info: K562 pc12_var_ratio 0.306, S-to-G2M separation 108.8 deg (flipped=True). RPE1 pc12_var_ratio 0.349, separation 97.1 deg. Marker genes used: 87 in K562 vs 93 in RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Compute theta on the shared marker set in both lines and report label diagnostics (variance ratio, S/G2M peak separation, agreement with discrete phase calls). Treat the phase angle as a marker-derived proxy in the write-up.

findings.description: The provenance and reproducibility scaffolding is thin. The .h5ad files used for extraction are not included. The manifests record no model revision or commit and no input-file hash. There is no requirements or environment file with versions. So it cannot be confirmed that the activations came from exactly the matrices in data/ with the same gene order, which matters for F1.
findings.evidence: The manifests contain only model name, unit, layers, max_genes, prompt, dtype and counts. README says the matrices were 'stored as .h5ad at the time'. No requirements.txt or environment.yml exists in the folder. (The activations do align with the cells well enough to give R_diff 0.79.)
findings.recommended_action: Add pinned package versions, the HF model revision hash, and checksums of the extraction inputs to the manifests. Save the actual per-cell gene lists (cell sentences) next to the activations, so a baseline matching the model's input exactly can be built and checked.

grade_a.detection_reason: F1 meets the key's detection rule. It says the cell sentences take the top 512 nonzero genes from each line's full panel (K562 6,546, RPE1 8,749), while top_k_encode (code/transfer.py:45-58) takes the top 512 from the 6,544 shared genes only. So the baseline's genes and ranks differ from what the model saw. F1 prescribes the fix: build the baseline from the same full-panel top 512 as the sentence. It also shows the verdict flips to parity. I re-ran this inline: the exact-sentence (full-panel, stable sort) rank baseline gives R 0.7905, and model minus baseline is -0.0012 [-0.0128, +0.0115]. That matches F1's numbers and the key's -0.0011/-0.0022 PARITY result. F1 also mentions tie-breaking, which the key lists as a minor false alarm. But the full-panel versus shared-gene selection is the central point of the finding, not a tie-only claim.

findings.reason: F1 names the shared-gene versus full-panel top-512 selection in top_k_encode (lines 45-58) and prescribes building the baseline from the full-panel top 512. I confirmed by re-running that the exact-sentence baseline gives model - baseline -0.0012 [-0.0128, +0.0115] (PARITY), which overturns the 'MODEL ADDS' verdict. The extra claims about tie-breaking and the presence-only arm are secondary.

Confirmed by an inline paired bootstrap (2,000 draws). On median angular error the model is significantly worse than expr_512_rank: +2.42 deg [+1.50, +3.40]. Against the full-panel rank baseline it is +3.09 [+2.15, +4.03]. SUMMARY mentions the disagreement only as a caveat but still concludes the model 'transfers phase better', and only R_diff was bootstrapped. This is a genuine problem with the headline wording that the key does not list.

The key's other_real_issues says the fixed, untuned alpha=1000 is a valid concern and the verdict depends on it: it is neither a detection nor a false alarm. The reviewer's sweep matches the key: about -0.006 at alpha 100 and +0.024 at 1e4 against the exact-sentence baseline. 5-fold CV on K562 picks 1e4, as in the key.

The key lists this under other_real_issues: the bootstrap covers only target-cell sampling and does not refit the ridge, so training variation is left out. It calls this valid but minor. The finding's extra points about scope (one cell-line pair, one direction) overlap a scope limitation the key treats as a stated caveat. The reverse-direction numbers were not checked. The finding does not overturn the headline on its own.

This is mainly the key's listed false alarm that a marker-derived phase label is circular with the expression features. The label is the target for every arm and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. Losing marker magnitudes by truncating to 512 genes is a real cost of the input format for this label, so the claim that the 'tokenisation loss' is an artifact is not established. The 'before the first layer' wording point is minor.

The overclaiming point is valid. Layer-21 activations are a deterministic function of the cell sentence, so the analysis can only show that a linear readout transfers better, not that the model 'adds information beyond its input'. The verdict string is hard-coded. The key does not list this issue. Part of the finding (RPE1-only genes in the input) restates facts the key says hold in both versions, and part of it relies on F1-F3.

This overlaps the key's possible false alarm that phase labels computed separately in each line may not match. They are oriented by marker biology, and R_diff ignores a fixed rotation. The diagnostics the reviewer reports (separations 108.8 and 97.1 deg) agree with the key. The finding only asks for label diagnostics to be reported and does not show that any result is wrong.

True that there is no requirements file with versions and that the manifests lack a model revision and input hashes. These are reproducibility hygiene gaps. The key confirms that data/ matches the source h5ad files exactly and that the outputs reproduce byte for byte.

grade_b.detection_reason: F1 meets the detection rule. It says the cell sentences take the top 512 nonzero genes from each line's full panel (K562 6,546, RPE1 8,749). It also says top_k_encode (code/transfer.py:45-58) takes the top 512 from the 6,544 shared genes only, so the baseline gets different genes and ranks than the model saw (overlap 436.8/512 in RPE1). It prescribes building the baseline from the full-panel top 512. It also brings in tie-breaking, but the shared-gene vs full-panel selection is stated explicitly. I re-ran its sentence-matched baseline at alpha 1000: model minus baseline = -0.0012 [-0.0129, +0.0106], which is parity. The key's exact-sentence value is -0.0011 and its full-panel value is -0.0022, so the headline 'MODEL ADDS' verdict flips. No other finding names the selection mismatch. F6 mentions only RPE1-only genes in the input, which the rule says is not enough.

findings.reason: It names the shared-gene restriction in top_k_encode vs the full-panel top 512 in cell_sentences, points at transfer.py:45-58, and prescribes the full-panel selection. My re-run reproduces its numbers: sentence-matched baseline 0.7905, delta -0.0012 [-0.013, +0.011], parity. Presence-only arm 0.8202, delta -0.031. These agree with the key's corrected result. The tie-breaking part is a possible false alarm in the key, but here it is secondary to the correct selection-mismatch claim.

I confirmed it with my own paired bootstrap (1,000 draws). Model minus expr_512_rank median error is +2.41 deg [1.57, 3.34], vs the sentence-matched baseline +3.09 [2.16, 4.01], and vs presence +5.39 [4.47, 6.26]. The SUMMARY does mention the metric disagreement as a caveat, but it never shows the gap is significant and still concludes the model 'transfers phase better'. This is a genuine issue that the key does not list.

The key's other_real_issues lists the untuned fixed alpha=1000 with a verdict that depends on it as a valid concern: neither a detection nor a false alarm. F3's numbers are consistent with the key: at alpha 1e4, model minus sentence-matched rank is +0.024, and CV picks 1e4.

The key lists target-only bootstrap variance (no refit on resampled K562) as a minor, valid issue. I confirmed the reverse-direction numbers: model 0.758, rank 0.632, sentence-matched 0.570, presence 0.7225. It is a fair point about scope and uncertainty. It does not show the forward headline is wrong.

This is essentially the key's listed possible false alarm about circularity: the label is built from marker genes that are also features. I confirmed the numbers: the marker-only ridge scores 0.918, and about 8.3 markers per RPE1 sentence. But the label is the same target for every arm and is not a leak. The tokenizer really does drop most marker genes, which is a genuine cost for cell-cycle information, so the claim that the decomposition is not a tokenizer cost does not hold. The 'before the first layer' wording point is trivial.

The overclaim is genuine. Layer-21 activations are a deterministic function of the sentence, so at most the analysis shows better linear accessibility, not 'information beyond its input'. Its note that the model's input has RPE1-only genes does not name the shared vs full-panel selection, so under the rule it is not a detection of the documented error.

The label diagnostics are accurate and match the key (S/G2M separation 108.8 and 97.1 deg). Asking for label-quality reporting is reasonable but minor. The key notes that labels are oriented by marker biology and that R_diff ignores a fixed rotation, so line-specific labels are not an error.

The provenance gaps are real: no model revision, no input hashes, no environment file. They are reproducibility hygiene only. The key confirms data/ matches the source h5ad files exactly and the activations are byte-identical to the original.

review.summary:
I reran the pipeline inline without writing any files, and it reproduces the reported numbers exactly: model 0.789, expr_512_rank 0.792, expr_full 0.878, expr_512_mag 0.820, model minus rank -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105]. I also checked that activation rows line up with the expression rows: within-line cross-validated phase prediction gives R about 0.89–0.91 when rows are aligned and about 0.01–0.03 when they are shuffled. The headline claim of parity does not hold up.
(1) The ridge penalty was fixed at alpha=1e3 and never tuned. Choosing it by 5-fold cross-validation on K562 picks 1e4 for both arms. At that setting the model beats the rank encoding by +0.018 [+0.008, +0.027], so the analysis's own rule says "MODEL ADDS".
(2) Encoding rank linearly is an arbitrary choice. Two other encodings carry the same or less information and do better than both the model and the linear-rank arm: log-rank, and plain presence in the top 512 with order discarded. Against them the model is -0.018 [-0.029, -0.007] and -0.020 [-0.030, -0.009], so the same rule says "MODEL LOSES".
(3) On median angular error, the model is significantly worse than the rank arm: +3.5 deg [2.7, 4.4].
(4) The bootstrap resamples only RPE1 cells. Refitting the readout on resampled K562 cells gives an SD of 0.027 for the model-minus-rank difference, about 4x the spread the reported CI implies.
(5) The phase label is built from the expression of the same marker genes that the expression arms use as features. This inflates the "tokenisation loss". The decomposition behind "almost the whole gap" also depends on alpha and on the encoding.
Smaller issues: the code's tie-breaking does not match how cell sentences are built; the two cell lines use different gene panels; and their normalisation differs, although the README says it is the same.

findings.description: The parity verdict only holds at the single untuned ridge penalty alpha=1000. The same alpha is applied to a 2,304-dim activation space and a 6,544-dim rank space without being selected for either arm. When alpha is chosen by cross-validation on the source data alone (K562), the verdict flips to 'MODEL ADDS information'.
findings.evidence: Sweeping alpha gives model vs rank R_diff of: 1e2 0.708 vs 0.716; 1e3 0.789 vs 0.792; 1e4 0.821 vs 0.803; 1e5 0.795 vs 0.597. 5-fold CV on K562 picks alpha=1e4 for both arms (model CV R 0.893, rank CV R 0.852). At alpha=1e4 the paired bootstrap of model - expr_512_rank is +0.0175, 95% CI [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0)=1.0, which the script's own rule (lines 136-139) calls 'MODEL ADDS'.
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha for each arm by nested CV on K562 only (never on RPE1), then report the verdict at those values together with the full alpha sweep. Do not claim parity unless it holds across reasonable hyperparameters.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:45-60 (line 57 rank values np.arange(k,0,-1)); README.md:40-41; SUMMARY.md:12, 26-27, 33-34
findings.description: The baseline 'expr_512_rank' is presented as 'the information a cell sentence carries'. In fact it is one particular linear numeric encoding of rank (512..1), read out linearly. Other encodings carry the same information (log-rank) or strictly less (binary top-512 membership, no order), and both do clearly better than the model at the same alpha. So 'model vs its input' depends on an arbitrary encoding choice, and under these alternatives the model is significantly worse.
findings.evidence: At alpha=1e3 R_diff is: rank(orig) 0.792, log1p(rank) 0.807, presence-only 0.809, model 0.789. Paired bootstrap (2,000 draws): model - log_rank = -0.0181 [-0.0290, -0.0072]; model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091]. Both mean 'MODEL LOSES' under the verdict rule. At alpha=1e4: presence 0.820, log_rank 0.820, model 0.821, rank 0.803.
findings.recommended_action: Treat the input-information baseline as the best linear readout over several encodings of the same top-512 list (presence, rank, log-rank, etc.), or define a principled upper bound. Report the model against that best baseline, and remove 'the model's input' as a label for the linear-rank arm.

findings.description: The second pre-declared metric contradicts parity. The bootstrap only tests R_diff. On median angular error the model is significantly worse than its input encoding, yet the summary calls it 'slightly worse' and says the metrics 'lean the same way'. The claim that the model 'neither adds nor loses' is therefore not supported.
findings.evidence: Point estimates: model 23.3 deg vs expr_512_rank 19.8 deg. Paired bootstrap (same seed/scheme, 2,000 draws): delta median error = +3.53 deg, 95% CI [+2.71, +4.41], P(model worse)=1.0. At the CV-selected alpha=1e4 the metrics also disagree: the model is better on R_diff (0.821 vs 0.803) but worse on median error (20.8 vs 18.7 deg).
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap and report CIs for the median-error contrasts too. State that the model loses information on that metric. Do not draw a parity conclusion when the two metrics disagree.

findings.description: The paired bootstrap resamples only the RPE1 test cells. It ignores how much the K562-fitted scaler and ridge vary with the training sample, and the uncertainty in the PCA-derived phase labels. The reported CI on model - expr_512_rank (half-width about 0.012) therefore greatly understates the uncertainty. So does the caveat 'the CI allows a gain of up to 0.0105 or a loss of up to 0.0144'.
findings.evidence: I refit both arms on 25 bootstrap resamples of the K562 cells (alpha=1e3) and scored them on the full RPE1 set. The model - rank difference had mean +0.008, SD 0.027, range -0.047 to +0.071. The target-only bootstrap implies an SD of about 0.0063 (CI width 0.0249/3.92), roughly 4x smaller.
findings.recommended_action: Use a two-level bootstrap: resample K562 cells and refit, and resample RPE1 cells and score. Ideally also re-derive the phase labels inside each draw. Report the wider intervals and revise the equivalence statement.

findings.description: The verdict rule treats 'CI contains 0' as evidence of parity (absence of evidence taken as evidence of absence). No equivalence margin is set in advance. The conclusions also go beyond the design. Only layer 21 was measured, so 'carries what it is given through 21 layers' is untested. 'Neither adds nor loses' and 'C2S comes out even' are stated as established facts.
findings.evidence: Verdict code: lo <= 0 <= hi -> 'PARITY'. No equivalence bound or TOST appears anywhere. Only layer_21 activations exist (manifest layers [21]). SUMMARY line 28 says 'neither adds nor loses'.
findings.recommended_action: Set an equivalence margin in advance and test it formally (TOST or CI inside the margin), using the corrected uncertainty from F4. Drop the claims about information flow through layers unless several layers are analysed. Soften conclusion 3.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py:53-68 (label from standardized expression of marker genes); code/transfer.py:91, 101-103; SUMMARY.md:30-34
findings.description: The target is circular with respect to the expression arms. The phase label is the angle in the PC1-PC2 plane of the standardized log-expression of the 87-93 Tirosh marker genes. The same genes, with their magnitudes, are features in expr_full and expr_512_mag, which can approximately reconstruct the label's defining linear projection. The 'tokenisation loss' and the model's 0.089 gap to expr_full are therefore partly measured against a target defined in the very magnitude space the cell sentence discards. This undermines 'the loss to raw expression is the tokenizer' and the claim that expression in the model's own input encoding is the fair baseline.
findings.evidence: Removing the 87 shared marker genes from the features: expr_full falls 0.878 -> 0.839 and expr_512_rank falls 0.792 -> 0.663. Most of the rank arm's signal comes from the label-defining genes, and the expression arms have direct access to the magnitudes that define the label.
findings.recommended_action: Define the phase target independently of the evaluated features. For example, hold the marker genes out of all feature sets, or use an orthogonal phase reference such as FUCCI or an external tricycle projection. Otherwise state clearly that the expression arms have privileged access to how the label is defined.

findings.description: The decomposition in conclusion 2 ('0.058 from keeping 512 genes, 0.029 from dropping values ... almost the whole gap') is an artefact of alpha=1e3 and of the linear-rank encoding. It does not hold under CV-selected alpha or other encodings of the same information.
findings.evidence: At the CV-selected alpha=1e4: expr_full 0.897, expr_512_rank 0.803, model 0.821. The tokenisation gap is 0.094 and the model sits 0.076 below expr_full, closing about 19% of the gap rather than 'none'. At alpha=1e3, presence-only (no values, no order) scores 0.809, so 'dropping values' costs 0.011 (0.820-0.809), not 0.029.
findings.recommended_action: Recompute the decomposition with tuned alpha and the best encoding of each information level, and report its sensitivity. Remove 'almost the whole gap' unless it holds robustly.

findings.description: top_k_encode does not reproduce the actual cell sentence. It picks the top 512 with argpartition/argsort, which breaks ties arbitrarily. The cell sentences use a stable descending sort over nonzero genes, so ties go to the lower column index. log1p expression has many exact ties, so the selected gene set and ranks differ from what the model saw.
findings.evidence: In RPE1 the median cell has 164 genes tied at the 512th value. On average 29.2 (K562) and 24.0 (RPE1) of the 512 selected genes per cell differ from the stable-sort cell sentence, and 7.3% / 6.3% of rank-matrix entries differ. The effect on the headline is small: an exact cell-sentence rank encoding gives R_diff 0.7905 vs 0.7916.
findings.recommended_action: Build the rank baseline with the same function (anndata_to_ranked_genes: nonzero only, stable sort) that produced the model input.

findings.description: The baseline and the model do not see the same genes. K562 cell sentences come from a 6,546-gene panel and RPE1 sentences from an 8,749-gene panel, so RPE1 sentences contain many genes that never occur in K562 sentences. The rank arm silently drops these, while the model receives them as an extra source of domain shift. So expr_512_rank is not 'the same information as the model's 512-gene cell sentence' in the target line.
findings.evidence: On average only 444.8 of the 512 top genes in an RPE1 cell are in the shared panel (511.997 in K562). About 67 genes per RPE1 sentence are absent from the K562 vocabulary.
findings.recommended_action: Rebuild the cell sentences (and activations) on the shared gene panel in both lines, or report this asymmetry and its effect on the model-vs-input comparison.

findings.description: The two cell lines are not normalised the same way, despite the README's claim. RPE1 rows sum to exactly 10,000 (after expm1) over the stored genes. K562 rows sum to 7,447-9,573, so K562 was apparently normalised before subsetting to its gene panel. Because the scaler is frozen on K562, this per-cell scale shift affects only the magnitude arms (expr_full, expr_512_mag), not the rank arm or the model, which biases the 'tokenisation loss' contrasts.
findings.recommended_action: Re-normalise both lines the same way over the shared genes before building the magnitude features. Correct the README.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. The key's detection rule only warns that a claim that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only would be false here. No finding makes that claim: F9 correctly says the selection is made on the full panel and the non-shared genes are dropped afterwards. I re-ran checks with the package code. All of the review's numbers reproduce: F1/F7 alpha sweep, F2 encodings, F3 median-error bootstrap, F4 training bootstrap, F6 marker-gene removal, F9 shared-gene count, F10 row sums.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue: the ridge alpha is fixed and untuned, and the verdict depends on it. I reproduced it. At alpha 1e4, which 5-fold CV on K562 selects, model - expr_512_rank = +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], so the verdict becomes MODEL ADDS. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm.

Verified at alpha 1e3 with 2,000 paired draws. R_diff is rank 0.7916, log_rank 0.8074, presence 0.8091, model 0.7894. model - log_rank = -0.0181 [-0.029, -0.0072] and model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], so both give MODEL LOSES. At alpha 1e4 all three are at parity with the model. The key lists 'linear rank values are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm, but only as a design-choice concern. This finding shows with data that the parity verdict at the declared alpha flips under equally valid encodings of the same top-512 information. That is a real robustness problem, similar to the alpha sensitivity.

Verified: median error 23.28 vs 19.78 deg; paired bootstrap delta +3.53 [+2.71, +4.41], P = 1.0. At alpha 1e4 it is still +2.0 [+1.1, +2.9] while R_diff favours the model. SUMMARY calls this 'slightly worse' and says the metrics 'lean the same way' to support 'neither adds nor loses'. A significant loss on the second metric goes against that wording. The headline verdict rule uses R_diff only, so this is a challenge to how the summary words its conclusion.

The key lists this as valid but minor: the bootstrap covers only target-cell sampling, and the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells. I checked with 15 K562 resample refits. model - rank had SD about 0.031 (range -0.064 to +0.058), versus about 0.0063 implied by the target-only CI. So the finding is right that the CI understates the uncertainty. Wider intervals would still contain 0, so the verdict does not change.

In principle the point is fair: no equivalence margin is set, and phrases like 'through 21 layers' are rhetorical. But the CI is reported and narrow, and the SUMMARY caveat already says 'Parity is not proof of zero effect' and gives the bounds. The key treats 'only one layer' as scope, not an error. So this is wording and overstatement, not a wrong result.

The key names this exact concern as a possible false alarm: the label is built from marker genes that are also features. The label is the target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. The marker-removal numbers reproduce (expr_full 0.839, rank 0.663). But removing the markers from the expression arms while the model still sees them is not a fair test. The magnitude advantage the finding describes is exactly the tokenisation loss the analysis means to measure.

The numbers are correct. At alpha 1e4: full 0.8968, rank 0.8035, model 0.8209. Presence-only scores 0.809 at alpha 1e3. So the exact 0.058/0.029 split depends on alpha and on the encoding, which follows from F1 and F2. The qualitative Conclusion 2 still holds, though: at alpha 1e4 the tokenizer loss (0.093) is larger than the model's whole gap to expr_full (0.076). The claim that the decomposition 'does not hold' overstates the problem.

The key lists tie-breaking between argpartition and the stable sort as true but not load-bearing. An exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 vs -0.0022, the same verdict. The finding itself says the effect is small (0.7905 vs 0.7916) and marks it minor, which is consistent with the key.

The facts are accurate. I count 444.8 of 512 RPE1 top genes in the shared panel, and the key reports a mean of 67.8 non-shared genes per RPE1 sentence. The finding correctly says selection uses the full panel, so it does not trigger the key's false-detection rule. The key lists dropping non-shared genes from the baseline as a possible false alarm because it is unavoidable for a frozen cross-line readout. This is a minor asymmetry, not a flaw.

Row sums verified: expm1 of K562 rows sums to 7447 / 9137 / 9573 (min / median / max), while RPE1 rows sum to 10000. So 'same normalisation' is loosely worded. But the finding's own fix, re-normalising both lines over the shared genes, leaves expr_full almost unchanged (0.8778 vs 0.8784 at alpha 1e3; 0.8972 vs 0.8968 at alpha 1e4). The claimed bias in the tokenisation-loss contrasts is negligible.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect and error_detected is null. No finding makes the claim the detection rule marks as false, which is that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only. F9 notes that the non-shared genes are dropped, but it does not claim the selection is made from the shared set.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue: alpha is fixed at 1000 and untuned, and the verdict depends on it. I reproduced the numbers. At alpha 1e4, model - expr_512_rank = +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0)=1.0, which the script's rule calls MODEL ADDS. The key also reports that CV on K562 picks alpha 1e4. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm. It targets the headline parity verdict.

I reproduced the numbers at alpha 1e3. R_diff is rank 0.7916, log-rank 0.8074, presence 0.8091 and model 0.7894. Model - log_rank = -0.0181 [-0.0290, -0.0072] and model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], both 'MODEL LOSES' under the script's rule. At alpha 1e4 all of these are at parity with the model. The key lists the generic objection ('linear rank values are arbitrary') as a possible false alarm, on the grounds that the rank arm carries the sentence's information. That reasoning does not rebut this evidence: the presence encoding carries strictly less information than the sentence and still significantly beats the model. So the parity verdict depends on an arbitrary encoding choice as well as on alpha, a robustness problem like the key's alpha issue.

Verified. On median error the model is 23.28 deg vs 19.78 deg for expr_512_rank. A paired bootstrap (2,000 draws, seed 0) gives a difference of +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41] with P(worse)=1.0. At alpha 1e4 the model is still worse on median error, +2.0 deg [1.1, 2.9], even though it is better on R_diff. SUMMARY reports 23 vs 20 deg but calls it 'slightly worse' and never tests it. 'Neither adds nor loses' is therefore not supported on the second pre-declared metric. Not in the key.

The key lists this as valid but minor: the bootstrap covers only target cells, and the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells. My own check (25 K562 resamples, seed 1) gave an SD of about 0.031 for model - rank, against about 0.006 implied by the target-only CI. That supports the finding's claim of roughly 4x understatement. It widens the uncertainty and weakens the equivalence caveat, but it does not by itself overturn the parity verdict.

Treating 'CI contains 0' as parity with no equivalence margin is a fair methodological point. However, SUMMARY's caveats already say parity is not proof of zero effect and give the CI bounds. The key treats the single-layer limitation as scope stated in the caveats, not an error. 'Through 21 layers' just means the information is present at layer 21, which was measured. This finding is about wording and framing.

The key explicitly lists this as a possible false alarm: the label is built from marker genes that are also features. The label is the same target for every arm, the model's sentences contain the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into fitting. The ablation numbers reproduce (expr_full 0.839 and rank 0.663 without the 87 markers). They only show that marker genes carry phase information, as expected, not a privileged leak.

The numbers check out. At alpha 1e4, expr_full is 0.897, mag 0.828, rank 0.803 and model 0.821. At alpha 1e3, presence scores 0.809. So the exact 0.058/0.029 split does move with alpha and encoding. But the qualitative conclusion 2 still holds: at the CV-chosen alpha the tokenisation loss (0.094) is larger than the model's whole gap to expr_full (0.076), so the loss is still the tokenizer and not the model. The claim that the decomposition 'does not hold' is overstated, and the remaining point is the alpha-sensitivity already covered by F1 and F2.

The key lists tie-breaking by argpartition vs the stable sort as true but not load-bearing: the exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], the same verdict as -0.0022. The finding itself marks this minor and reports a negligible effect (0.7905 vs 0.7916).

The facts are correct: about 67 non-shared genes per RPE1 sentence (key: mean 67.8). But the key lists 'restricting the rank baseline to shared columns throws away the non-shared genes the model saw' as a possible false alarm. Dropping them is unavoidable for a frozen cross-line readout, and the selection and ranks of the kept genes match the sentence. Treating these genes as the model's extra domain shift is part of the design being tested, not a flaw.

Confirmed. expm1 row sums in K562 are 7447 / 9137 / 9573 (min / median / max), while RPE1 is exactly 10000, so README's 'same normalisation' is inaccurate. When I renormalised both lines over the shared genes, expr_full stayed at 0.878 and expr_512_mag moved only from 0.820 to 0.818. The model and rank arms are unaffected, so the effect is negligible.

review.summary: The code runs and reproduces every reported number: model 0.7894, expr_512_rank 0.7916, and the same contrasts. The headline claim does not hold up under checks. "Parity" between layer 21 and its input encoding depends on one ridge penalty (alpha = 1000) that was never tuned, and 5-fold CV on K562 rejects it for every arm. At the alpha CV picks for the model and for three of the four arms (1e4), model - expr_512_rank = +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0) = 1.0. By the analysis's own rule that verdict is "model adds information". On the second metric the model is clearly worse: median error is +3.5 deg [2.7, 4.4] versus expr_512_rank, which the summary reports as only "slightly worse". Conclusions 2 and 3 have three problems. They call a chosen setting (--max-genes 512) "the tokenizer". They leave out that the phase label is built from the same expression values the magnitude arms use (dropping the 87 label genes lowers expr_full from 0.878 to 0.839). And they frame the result as "adds/loses information", which a single linear readout cannot measure. Smaller problems: the rank encoding does not reproduce the cell sentence's tie handling (little effect on the numbers), the bootstrap only resamples RPE1 cells, and the README's statement that both lines share the same normalisation is wrong.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:97 (Ridge(alpha=1e3), same for every arm); SUMMARY.md:26-29, 18, 43; README.md step 6 (line 49)
findings.description: The headline 'parity' verdict (model - expr_512_rank CI spans 0) depends on one fixed, untuned ridge penalty that is applied to every arm, even though the arms differ in dimension (2,304 activations vs 6,544 genes) and in feature distribution. Choosing alpha by cross-validation on K562, the source line (no target data used), rejects alpha = 1000 for every arm. At the alpha CV picks, the contrast becomes positive, and with a common alpha of 1e4 its CI excludes 0. The verdict rule then returns 'MODEL ADDS information'.
findings.evidence: Rerun with 5-fold CV on K562 (transfer R_diff on RPE1, K562-CV R_diff in brackets): model alpha 1e3 gives 0.789 (cv 0.890); alpha 1e4 gives 0.821 (cv 0.895, best). expr_512_rank alpha 1e3 gives 0.792 (cv 0.854); 3e3 gives 0.812 (cv 0.876, best); 1e4 gives 0.803 (cv 0.872). CV also picks 1e4 for expr_full (0.897) and expr_512_mag (0.828). Paired bootstrap of model - expr_512_rank (2,000 draws): at alpha 1e3, -0.0022 [-0.0142, +0.0109] (reproduces the report). At 1e4 for both, +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0) = 1.000. At CV-chosen alphas (1e4 vs 3e3), +0.0093 [-0.0008, +0.0206], P(>0) = 0.963. At 1e5 the gap widens to 0.795 vs 0.597. The summary only mentions the single alpha as a caveat (line 43).
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha separately for each arm by cross-validation inside K562 (nested, with the scaler refit per fold). Report the contrast at the selected alphas and show a sensitivity curve over alpha. Withdraw the claim that the model 'neither adds nor loses' unless it holds under tuned readouts. Under source-CV tuning the evidence leans toward the model doing slightly better than its rank encoding.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:26-29 and 39-40; code/transfer.py:115-121 (bootstrap covers R_diff only)
findings.description: The second pre-specified metric contradicts 'transfers phase equally well'. The median angular error of the model is clearly and significantly worse than that of expr_512_rank. Because no bootstrap is run for median error, the summary can describe it only as 'slightly worse' and 'leaning the same way'.
findings.evidence: Point estimates: model 23.3 deg vs expr_512_rank 19.8 deg (outputs/transfer_results.json). Paired bootstrap of the median-error difference at alpha 1e3 (2,000 draws, same cells): +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41], P(>0) = 1.000. So on this metric the model loses accuracy relative to its input encoding.
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap both metrics and report both contrasts. Either state that the model is worse on median error, or explain why R_diff alone should decide. Remove 'equally well' and 'neither adds nor loses'.

findings.description: The verdict reads 'CI contains 0' as 'parity', which treats absence of evidence as evidence of equivalence. No equivalence margin is set in advance and no equivalence test (e.g. TOST) is run. The 'adds/loses information' framing is also ill-posed. The activations are a deterministic function of the cell sentence, so they cannot hold more information than it does. What is measured is how well one ridge readout at one alpha decodes phase linearly and transfers. The statement 'carries what it is given through 21 layers' is not supported because only layer 21 was tested.
findings.evidence: Verdict code: 'PARITY' if lo <= 0 <= hi. Conclusion 1: 'So the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information. It carries what it is given through 21 layers'. Only --layers 21 was extracted (manifest.json).
findings.recommended_action: Set an equivalence margin before looking at results and test it. Rephrase the result as 'linear transferable decodability under ridge readout'. Drop the claims about information content and about all 21 layers, or support them with other layers and nonlinear or tuned readouts.

findings.description: Calling the 0.087 'tokenisation loss' a property of the tokenizer or model is wrong. Most of it (0.058) comes from keeping only 512 genes, which the analyst chose for extraction (--max-genes 512). It is not built into the C2S tokenizer or model: C2S cell sentences can be longer within the 8,192-token context. In addition, the two parts of the 'decomposition' add up to the total by construction (they telescope), and 'almost the whole gap' just restates that model ≈ expr_512_rank at alpha = 1000, which F1 shows is not robust.
findings.evidence: extract_activations.py has --max-genes default 512 as a free parameter, and max_len is 8,192 tokens. Contrasts: 0.0582 + 0.0285 = 0.0867 = expr_full - expr_512_rank (arithmetic identity). At alpha 1e4: expr_full 0.897, expr_512_rank 0.803, model 0.821. The model's gap to full expression (0.076) is then clearly smaller than the 'tokenisation loss' (0.094).
findings.recommended_action: Label the 512-gene truncation as an analysis/extraction setting, not 'the tokenizer'. If the attribution matters, extract with more genes. Present the gap decomposition under tuned alphas with uncertainty, and soften Conclusion 3.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py:53-64 together with code/transfer.py:101-102 (expr_full / expr_512_mag arms); SUMMARY.md:30-34
findings.description: The target label is circular for the magnitude arms. Phase theta is the PC1-PC2 angle of standardised log-expression of the Tirosh marker genes, and expr_full and expr_512_mag receive exactly those values as features. Part of their advantage over the rank and model arms therefore comes from recovering the label's own definition, not from better access to cell-cycle biology. This inflates the 'tokenisation loss' that Conclusions 2-3 attribute to the input format.
findings.evidence: Dropping the 87 Tirosh marker genes from expr_full lowers its transfer R_diff from 0.878 to 0.839 at alpha 1e3, about 45% of the 0.087 'tokenisation loss'.
findings.recommended_action: Define phase from a held-out gene set, or exclude the label-defining genes from every expression arm, or use an independent phase reference. Report how the gap decomposition changes.

findings.description: expr_512_rank does not reproduce the actual cell sentence. Cell sentences (cell_sentences.py:131-133) keep only nonzero genes, sorted with a stable sort, so ties are broken by column (genomic) order. top_k_encode uses argpartition and an unstable argsort, so tie-breaking is arbitrary. Values are heavily tied in these data, so the gene set and the order differ from the sentence the model actually saw. The claim that it is 'the model's input' is therefore only approximate. The effect on results is small.
findings.evidence: A median of 169 genes share the 512th-ranked value, and only ~441 genes per cell are strictly above it. About 488 of the top 512 genes share a tied value. The top-512 gene set matches the cell sentence's set in only 0.6% of K562 cells (mean overlap 483 of 512). A faithful encoding gives R_diff 0.7905 vs 0.7916 at alpha 1e3.
findings.recommended_action: Build the rank arm with the same function used for the cell sentences (anndata_to_ranked_genes), so the comparison uses exactly the model's input.

findings.description: The paired bootstrap resamples only RPE1 test cells. It treats the K562-trained readout, the K562 and RPE1 phase PCAs, and the orientation step as fixed. The reported 95% CIs, including the bound in SUMMARY.md:38 ('gain up to 0.0105 or loss up to 0.0144'), therefore understate the uncertainty of a transfer result and of the parity bound.
findings.evidence: Inside the loop, only i = rng.integers(0, n, n) indexes the fixed predictions preds[nm][i]. There is no refitting on resampled K562 cells and no recomputation of theta.
findings.recommended_action: Use a two-level bootstrap: resample K562 cells, refit the scaler and ridge (and ideally recompute phase), then resample RPE1 cells. Report the wider intervals.

findings.description: The README says RPE1 has the 'Same format and normalisation' as K562, but the two matrices are normalised differently. RPE1 rows sum exactly to 1e4 after expm1. K562 rows do not, which suggests K562 was normalised before its genes were subset. This difference shifts magnitude features between source and target. It does not change the reported numbers: renormalising both lines on the shared genes gives expr_full 0.878 again. Renormalising K562 alone gives 0.846.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the README, or renormalise both lines the same way (e.g. on the shared genes) before the magnitude arms.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key marks B7392 as clean ("error": null), so there is no documented error to detect. None of the findings makes the claim the key calls false, namely that the 512-gene baselines select genes from the shared set only. F6 is about tie-breaking, which the key treats as a minor, non-load-bearing point. I re-ran the checks with the package python: point estimates match outputs/transfer_results.json. At alpha 1e4, expr_full / model / expr_512_rank give 0.897 / 0.821 / 0.803. Bootstrapping the median-error difference (model - expr_512_rank) gives +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41]. Dropping the 87 markers gives expr_full 0.839. K562 expm1 row sums are 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 (min / median / max); RPE1 rows all sum to 10,000.

findings.reason: This matches the key's other_real_issues item that alpha is fixed at 1000 and untuned, and that the verdict depends on it. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm. The reported numbers match the key: at alpha 1e4, +0.0175 [+0.0074/5, +0.0274]; K562 CV picks 1e4 for the model; at alpha 1e3 the result is -0.0022. The finding challenges the headline PARITY verdict.

I confirmed this by re-running it. A paired bootstrap of the median-error difference (model - expr_512_rank, 2,000 draws, seed 0) gives +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41], with P(>0) = 1.0. So on the second reported metric the model is clearly worse, while SUMMARY says it 'transfers phase equally well' and that the gap is 'slightly worse'. The key does not mention this. The verdict metric is R_diff, but this undercuts the 'equally well / neither adds nor loses' wording.

This is about interpretation. Reading a CI that contains 0 as 'parity' without an equivalence margin is a fair statistical point, but SUMMARY's caveat already says parity is not proof of zero effect and gives the CI bounds. The information-content framing and the '21 layers' wording are loose, not wrong results. The verdict rule itself is pre-specified and applied correctly.

The alpha-1e4 numbers check out (0.897 / 0.803 / 0.821), and the decomposition does telescope by construction. However, decompositions are expected to telescope, and in this analysis the 512-gene sentence is defined as the model's input (manifest max_genes 512). So calling the cost 'tokenizer' rather than 'extraction setting' is a labelling issue, and the alpha-dependence part repeats F1. The key does not list it as an error.

The key lists this explicitly as a possible false alarm: the label is the target for every arm, and the model's sentence contains the same marker genes. The label is computed from marker biology separately in each line and does not leak from RPE1 into training. The number (0.878 to 0.839 without markers) is reproducible, but it shows that markers are informative. It does not show circular inflation of the comparison.

The key treats argpartition versus stable-sort tie-breaking as true in a small way but not load-bearing. With the exact-sentence baseline the contrast is -0.0011 versus -0.0022, and the verdict is the same. The finding itself rates this as minor with a small effect (0.7905 vs 0.7916), consistent with the key.

This matches the key's other_real_issues item that the bootstrap covers only target-cell sampling and the ridge is not refit, which the key calls minor and valid. The finding says the CIs understate uncertainty, not that the headline is wrong.

I confirmed it: K562 expm1 row sums are 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 (min / median / max) and RPE1 rows are exactly 10,000, so the README's 'same normalisation' line is inaccurate. The finding itself says the reported numbers do not change, so this is a documentation inaccuracy with no effect on the results.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key marks B7392 as clean, with no documented error, so error_detected is null. No finding makes the false claim named in the detection rule, that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only. F6 does question top_k_encode, but only on tie-breaking, which the key lists as true but not load-bearing.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue: the parity verdict depends on the untuned alpha of 1000. The numbers match the key: at alpha 1e4 the contrast is +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], and I reproduced +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274]. At alpha 1e3 it is -0.0022. CV on K562 favours alpha 1e4 for the model. One small mismatch: the finding says CV picks 3e3 for expr_512_rank, while the key says 1e4 with fold seed 0 (3e3 and 1e4 score almost the same). The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm.

Confirmed by rerunning. At alpha 1e3 the model's median error is 23.3 deg vs 19.8 deg for expr_512_rank. A paired bootstrap of the difference (2,000 draws) gives +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41], P(>0) = 1.0. The model is still worse at alpha 1e4: +2.0 deg [1.10, 2.88]. The summary calls this 'slightly worse' and says the model 'transfers phase equally well', but the README makes median error the second metric and it shows a significant loss. The key does not list this issue.

The points are partly true but mostly about framing. 'CI contains 0' is not an equivalence test, and 'information' is loose wording for linear decodability. However, the verdict rule was set in advance and SUMMARY line 38 already says parity is not proof of zero effect, with explicit bounds. Reading 'through 21 layers' as a claim about every layer is a stretch. The finding does attack the headline wording, so it is load-bearing in what it claims.

Calling the loss 'the tokenizer' is loose. The 512-gene cap is an extraction setting: --max-genes 512, while cell_sentences defaults to 1024 within an 8,192-token context. The decomposition adds up by construction, which is how a decomposition should work, not a defect. Under alpha 1e4 the model's gap to expr_full shrinks (0.076 against a 0.094 encoding loss), which supports Conclusion 2 more than it undermines it. The measured numbers stand, so this is mainly a labelling issue.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm. Every arm predicts the same label, and the model's sentence contains the same marker genes, so this is not a leak. Removing the 87 most cell-cycle-informative genes would lower any arm's score whether or not the label were circular. The 0.878 to 0.839 drop therefore does not show circularity or an inflated tokenisation loss.

The key lists this as true in a small way and not load-bearing. Using the exact sentence genes gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111] vs -0.0022, the same verdict. The finding itself calls the effect small (0.7905 vs 0.7916) and does not claim the verdict changes.

This matches the key's second other_real_issue. The bootstrap resamples RPE1 test cells only, and the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells. The key calls it valid but minor. It does not overturn any headline claim.

Confirmed. expm1 row sums are 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 (min / median / max) for K562 and exactly 10,000 for RPE1, so the README's 'Same format and normalisation' is inaccurate. The finding itself says the reported results do not change. This is a documentation inaccuracy.

review.summary: The code runs as described. Inline re-runs (no files written) reproduce every number in outputs/ and SUMMARY.md: the row ids are the identity mapping, there are no NaN/inf values, every cell has at least 512 nonzero genes, and there are 6,544 shared genes. The headline "parity" verdict does not survive scrutiny. (1) It depends on the untuned ridge alpha = 1000. Five-fold CV on K562 picks alpha = 1e4 for the model, expr_512_rank and expr_full alike, and at that alpha model minus expr_512_rank = +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], P(>0) = 0.9998, so the script's own rule returns "MODEL ADDS information". (2) The second metric was never bootstrapped. Done paired, it shows the model significantly worse than its input encoding: +3.5 deg median error [+2.7, +4.4] at alpha = 1000 and +2.0 deg [+1.1, +2.9] at alpha = 1e4. The two metrics therefore disagree in direction at the CV-chosen alpha, and the summary's "lean the same way" hides a significant result. (3) "Parity" is read from a CI that spans 0, with no equivalence margin. That CI comes from target-only resampling with the readout held fixed; refitting on resampled K562 cells gives an SD of 0.028 for the contrast, against a reported half-width of about 0.012. (4) "Neither adds nor loses information" is contradicted by within-line decoding. The model beats the rank encoding in K562 (CV 0.886 vs 0.819) and in RPE1 (0.909 vs 0.848). (5) The phase label is computed from the same marker genes the expression arms receive as features, which inflates those arms and the "tokenisation loss" decomposition: removing the 87 markers drops expr_512_rank from 0.792 to 0.663. Smaller issues: claims about "through 21 layers" and "before the first layer" are untested; the rank encoding breaks ties differently from the cell sentence (negligible effect on results); and the phase label itself is noisy and defined differently in each cell line.

findings.description: The parity verdict depends on one fixed, untuned ridge penalty (alpha = 1000) shared by all arms. Choosing alpha the standard way (CV on the source cell line, per arm) gives alpha = 1e4 for the model, expr_512_rank and expr_full, and at that alpha the headline verdict flips from PARITY to MODEL ADDS information. So Conclusions 1 and 3 ('at parity', 'C2S comes out even') and the gap decomposition in Conclusion 2 are artefacts of the hyperparameter.
findings.evidence: Inline sweep, 5-fold CV R_diff on K562, then RPE1 transfer R_diff. Model: alpha 1e3 gives CV 0.886, transfer 0.789; alpha 1e4 gives CV 0.893, transfer 0.821. expr_512_rank: alpha 1e3 gives CV 0.819, transfer 0.792; alpha 1e4 gives CV 0.853, transfer 0.804. expr_full: alpha 1e3 gives CV 0.913, transfer 0.878; alpha 1e4 gives CV 0.936, transfer 0.897. Paired bootstrap (5,000 draws, seed 0) at alpha = 1e4: model - expr_512_rank = +0.0175, 95% CI [+0.0074, +0.0274], P(>0) = 0.9998, which is 'MODEL ADDS' under the rule in transfer.py:134-139. At alpha = 1e4 the gaps also change: expr_full - rank = 0.093 and model - full = -0.076, so the model recovers part of the tokenisation loss.
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha per arm by cross-validation within K562 only (nested, so no target information is used), report results across a range of alpha, and re-derive the verdict. Do not claim parity unless it holds at CV-chosen penalties.

findings.description: The second pre-specified metric (median angular error) shows the model significantly worse than expr_512_rank, but it was never tested. The summary describes it as the metrics 'leaning the same way' and still concludes the model 'transfers phase equally well'. At the CV-chosen alpha the two metrics point in opposite directions, so neither metric supports 'parity'.
findings.evidence: Paired bootstrap of the median error difference (model - expr_512_rank) on the same RPE1 resamples. At alpha = 1000: +3.53 deg, 95% CI [+2.71, +4.41], P(>0) = 1.0. At alpha = 1e4: +2.0 deg [+1.10, +2.88], while R_diff favours the model (+0.0175). Mean absolute error after rotation (alpha = 1000): model 31.0 deg vs rank 29.2 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap every reported metric for each contrast. Report that the model is significantly worse on angular error at alpha = 1000, and that the metrics disagree. Remove 'transfers phase equally well' and 'C2S comes out even'.

findings.description: The bootstrap resamples only the RPE1 evaluation cells and keeps the K562-fitted scaler and ridge fixed. It therefore ignores training-set variability, which is the main source of uncertainty when comparing two readouts. The reported CI, and the caveat that the effect lies between -0.0144 and +0.0105, understate the uncertainty by more than a factor of 2.
findings.evidence: Twenty refits on bootstrap-resampled K562 cells (alpha = 1000), each scored on all 3,000 RPE1 cells: model - expr_512_rank transfer R_diff has mean +0.0088, SD 0.028, range [-0.064, +0.058]. The reported 95% CI half-width is about 0.012.
findings.recommended_action: Use a two-level bootstrap that resamples source cells and refits, plus resamples target cells, or repeat the analysis on independent source/target splits. Update the CI and the caveat bounds.

findings.description: The analysis concludes 'parity' and 'the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information' because a 95% CI contains 0. That is absence of evidence, not evidence of equivalence. No equivalence margin was set in advance, so the verdict rule cannot establish parity.
findings.evidence: verdict = 'PARITY' if lo <= 0 <= hi. No margin or TOST is used anywhere. SUMMARY line 28 states 'So the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information', which goes beyond what a non-significant difference shows. Given F3, the properly estimated CI is far wider still.
findings.recommended_action: Pre-specify an equivalence margin (e.g. relative to the 0.029 'dropping values' effect) and use a TOST or a CI-within-margin test. Otherwise call the result inconclusive, not parity.

findings.description: The claim that layer 21 'neither adds nor loses' information relative to its input encoding is contradicted by within-cell-line decoding. In both lines, layer-21 activations carry substantially more linearly decodable phase information than the rank encoding. The transfer metric mixes information content with robustness to the K562-to-RPE1 shift, so the frozen-transfer result cannot support a statement about information content.
findings.evidence: 5-fold CV R_diff, alpha = 1000. K562: model 0.886 vs expr_512_rank 0.819 (0.893 vs 0.853 at alpha = 1e4). RPE1: model 0.909 vs expr_512_rank 0.848.
findings.recommended_action: Report within-line decodability next to transfer, and restrict any claim to transfer performance under this protocol. Drop 'neither adds nor loses' and 'carries what it is given'.

findings.description: The target label is circular for the expression arms. theta is computed by PCA on z-scored expression of the Tirosh marker genes, and the expression arms get those same genes, with magnitudes, as ridge features. The ladder full > mag > rank > model therefore partly measures how closely each encoding matches the formula that defines the label, not how much cell-cycle information it holds. The 'tokenisation loss' decomposition (0.058 + 0.029) and 'the fair baseline' argument rest on this circular construction. The label is also defined differently in each line (87 markers in K562, 93 in RPE1, with separate PCA loadings).
findings.evidence: In-sample K562 R_diff (alpha = 1000): expr_full 0.9986, expr_512_rank 0.993, model 0.939. Removing the 87 marker genes from the features: expr_full falls from 0.878 to 0.839, and expr_512_rank falls from 0.792 to 0.663 (-0.13), even though only about 7-8 markers per cell sit in the top 512. phase_angle_oriented info: K562 n_cc_genes = 87, RPE1 n_cc_genes = 93.
findings.recommended_action: Use a phase label that does not come from the feature genes: hold out the marker genes from all expression arms, or define phase on held-out markers or an external reference (e.g. a tricycle projection with fixed loadings applied to both lines). Then repeat the decomposition and qualify Conclusions 2-3.

findings.description: Several statements are not tested by the analysis. 'It carries what it is given through 21 layers' and 'costs 0.087 before the first layer' imply a layer trajectory, but only layer 21 was extracted. expr_512_rank is a hand-built bag-of-ranks over shared genes, not the tokenizer output or the embedding layer, so calling its gap 'the tokenizer' is an interpretation. The arithmetic decomposition also changes with alpha (see F1).
findings.evidence: manifest.json: layers = [21]. No embedding-layer or early-layer arm exists. At alpha = 1e4, full - rank = 0.093 vs model - full = -0.076, so 'almost the whole gap' becomes about 80%, with the model recovering 0.0175.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the layer-trajectory wording, or extract layer 0 / embedding and intermediate layers and include them as arms. Describe expr_512_rank as a proxy for the input encoding.

findings.description: expr_512_rank does not reproduce the cell-sentence ordering exactly. The cell sentence (cell_sentences.py:131-133) uses a stable descending sort over nonzero genes. top_k_encode uses argpartition plus a non-stable argsort, so ties (common in log1p normalised counts) are broken differently, both at the 512 cutoff and within the list. The README claim that it 'carries the same information' is therefore only approximately true. The impact on the results is negligible.
findings.evidence: Every 10th cell: on average about 31 (K562) and 27 (RPE1) of the 512 genes differ between the two selections (max 90). About 86% of shared genes sit at different rank positions. A median of about 165 genes tie with the 512th value. Rebuilding the arm with the exact cell-sentence ordering gives R_diff 0.7905 vs 0.7916 (median error 20.3 vs 19.8 deg).
findings.recommended_action: Build the rank arm with the same function as the model input (anndata_to_ranked_genes with stable ties), or document the approximation.

findings.description: The ground-truth phase angle is noisy, yet the analysis treats it as exact. PC1-PC2 explain only about 31% (K562) and 35% (RPE1) of marker-gene variance. Neither label noise nor label-estimation uncertainty in RPE1 (its PCA is fitted on the evaluation cells) is mentioned or propagated.
findings.evidence: phase_angle_oriented info: pc12_var_ratio 0.306 (K562), 0.349 (RPE1). S-G2M peak separation is 108.8 deg in K562 and 97.1 deg in RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Add a caveat on label quality. Ideally, check robustness to the label definition (e.g. a fixed-loading projection, or recomputing theta within bootstrap draws).

grade_a.detection_reason: The key for B7392 is marked 'clean' (error: null), so it has no documented error to detect. Its detection rule only warns against one false claim: that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only. No finding makes that claim. F8 talks about top_k_encode, but only about how ties are broken. It does not say the selection is restricted to shared genes.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue: alpha is fixed at 1000, never tuned, and the verdict depends on it. The key says to grade it as neither a detection nor a false alarm. I reproduced the numbers. At alpha 1e4, model R_diff is 0.821 and expr_512_rank is 0.803. The difference is +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], P(>0) = 0.9998, so the verdict becomes MODEL ADDS. The key also says 5-fold CV on K562 picks 1e4 for the model and for the rank baselines. The PARITY headline is therefore not robust.

Not in the key, and I confirmed it. With the same 5,000 paired RPE1 resamples (seed 0), median error for model minus expr_512_rank is +3.54 deg [+2.71, +4.42], P(>0) = 1.0, at alpha 1000. At alpha 1e4 it is +2.00 deg [+1.09, +2.91], while R_diff favours the model. SUMMARY only calls the model 'slightly worse (23 vs 20 deg)' and never tests it. So the claim that it 'transfers phase equally well' is undercut on the second pre-specified metric. The verdict rule itself was pre-specified on R_diff only, which limits the impact somewhat.

The key lists this as a valid but minor issue: the bootstrap covers only target-cell sampling, and the ridge is never refit on resampled K562 cells. I checked the size. Twelve refits on bootstrap-resampled K562 cells, each scored on all RPE1 cells, gave model minus rank a mean of +0.006 and SD of 0.033 (range -0.064 to +0.058). That is consistent with F3's SD of 0.028 and much wider than the reported CI half-width of about 0.012. It weakens how precise the parity claim looks, but it does not show the headline is wrong.

The point is formally correct: the rule calls parity whenever the CI contains 0, with no equivalence margin or TOST. But SUMMARY already says 'Parity is not proof of zero effect' and gives the CI bounds (-0.0144 / +0.0105), which are narrow next to the 0.029 to 0.087 effects it discusses. The only real overreach is the wording 'neither adds nor loses'. The key does not list this. The finding claims the parity verdict is unsupported, so it is load-bearing in what it asserts, but the substance is largely already caveated.

Not in the key, and the numbers are confirmed. 5-fold within-line CV R_diff at alpha 1000: K562 model 0.886 vs expr_512_rank 0.819, RPE1 0.909 vs 0.848. At alpha 1e4: K562 0.893 vs 0.852. Layer 21 holds more linearly decodable phase than the rank encoding, so the general claim that 'the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information / carries what it is given' overreaches what a frozen-transfer result can show. The K562 comparison is fair because K562 sentences contain almost no non-shared genes. The RPE1 comparison is slightly unfair to the rank arm, which is restricted to shared genes.

The key lists 'the phase label is built from marker genes that are also expression features, which is circular' as a possible false alarm. The label is the target for every arm, the model's sentences contain the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. Labels being computed separately per line (87 vs 93 markers) is also listed as a false alarm: orientation comes from marker biology, and R_diff ignores rotation. F6 uses this to argue that Conclusions 2-3 are artefacts, which the key rejects.

A wording point. 'Through 21 layers' and 'before the first layer' are rhetorical, since only layer 21 was extracted (manifest: layers [21]). The README already presents expr_512_rank as 'meant to carry the same information' as the sentence, not as the tokenizer output. True but trivial. The alpha-dependence part overlaps with F1.

The key lists tie-breaking (argpartition vs stable sort) as 'true in a small way, but not load-bearing': the exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 vs -0.0022, the same verdict. F8 itself calls the impact negligible (0.7905 vs 0.7916), which matches the key.

The numbers are correct: pc12_var_ratio is 0.306 for K562 and 0.349 for RPE1, and S-G2/M separation is 108.8 and 97.1 deg. But this is a general caveat about label quality that applies equally to every arm. It does not show any conclusion is wrong, and fitting the RPE1 label's PCA on the RPE1 cells is the stated design.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key (<EVAL_ROOT>/studyB/keys/B7392.json) marks B7392 as clean, with error: null, so there is no documented error to detect. None of the findings makes the false claim the detection rule warns about, that the 512-gene baselines choose genes from the shared set only. F1 (the verdict depends on the untuned alpha) matches the key's first 'other_real_issues' entry. The key says to grade that kind of finding as neither a detection nor a false alarm. F3 (the bootstrap leaves out training-set variation) matches the key's second 'other_real_issues' entry. I re-ran the checks inline with the package's own functions. They reproduced the numbers behind F1, F2, F3, F5 and F9 exactly.

findings.reason: The key's other_real_issues names this concern directly: alpha is fixed at 1000 and never tuned, 5-fold CV on K562 picks 10000, and at 10000 the contrast is +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274] (MODEL ADDS). My re-run gave model 0.821 vs rank 0.803 at alpha 1e4, and a bootstrap delta of +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274]. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, not a detection and not a false alarm. It claims the headline PARITY verdict flips.

Confirmed. A paired bootstrap of median angular error (model minus expr_512_rank) at alpha 1000 gave +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41], P(>0) = 1.0. At alpha 1e4 it gave +2.0 deg [1.10, 2.88], while the R_diff difference was +0.0175. SUMMARY reports the 23 vs 20 deg gap as 'slightly worse', never tests it, and still says layer 21 'transfers phase equally well'. On the second reported metric the model is significantly worse, so the claim is overstated. This problem is not in the key.

The key's other_real_issues lists this as valid ('ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells... Minor; valid'). Twenty K562-resample refits (rng seed 1) reproduced the finding's numbers exactly: mean +0.0088, SD 0.0278, range [-0.064, +0.058]. The intervals are wider than reported, but the finding does not show that the headline direction is wrong.

It is true that no equivalence margin or TOST was set, and that 'neither adds nor loses' overstates what a non-significant result shows. But the SUMMARY caveat already says 'Parity is not proof of zero effect' and gives the CI bounds (+0.0105 / -0.0144). Those bounds are tight compared with the ladder's other effects (0.029, 0.058). This is mainly a wording and framing point, although it targets the headline verdict.

Numbers confirmed: 5-fold within-line CV R_diff at alpha 1000 is K562 model 0.886 vs rank 0.819, and RPE1 model 0.909 vs rank 0.848. Conclusion 1 goes beyond the frozen-transfer result when it says the model 'neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information'. Within each line, phase is clearly more linearly decodable from layer 21 than from the rank encoding. This is an interpretive overreach not listed in the key.

The key lists this exact concern under possible_false_alarms: the label is built from marker genes that are also features, but it is the target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. The point that labels are computed separately per line (87 vs 93 genes) is also a listed false alarm: the labels are oriented by marker biology, the S and G2/M peaks agree within 12 deg, and R_diff ignores a fixed rotation. Removing the marker genes removes real cell-cycle signal, which does not show circularity.

The manifest confirms that only layer 21 was extracted, so 'through 21 layers' is loose wording. The README itself presents expr_512_rank as a stand-in for the input encoding. These are wording points, and the part about alpha repeats F1.

The key lists tie-breaking under possible_false_alarms as 'true in a small way, but not load-bearing'. With the exact sentence genes and order, the contrast is -0.0011 vs -0.0022 and the verdict is the same. The finding itself says the impact is negligible (0.7905 vs 0.7916), which matches the key.

The numbers check out: pc12_var_ratio is 0.306 (K562) and 0.349 (RPE1), and the S-G2/M separations are 108.8 and 97.1 deg. Label noise affects every arm the same way, so asking for a caveat on label quality is reasonable but minor.

review.summary: The headline result is that C2S-Scale layer 21 is "at parity with its input": model minus expr_512_rank = -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105]. It does not hold up. Re-running the pipeline inline reproduces the reported point estimates exactly. But the parity verdict changes with every analysis choice I tested. (1) Ridge alpha: cross-validation within K562 picks alpha = 1e4 for both the model and rank arms, not the fixed 1e3. At 1e4 the verdict becomes "MODEL ADDS" (+0.0175 [0.0076, 0.0275]). Across alpha = 1 to 1e6 the contrast runs from -0.081 to +0.198, so all three verdicts occur. (2) Rank encoding: a presence-only or log-rank encoding of the same top-512 gene set gives "MODEL LOSES" (-0.020 and -0.018, both CIs below 0). (3) Transfer direction: RPE1 to K562 gives model 0.758 vs rank 0.547 (+0.211 [0.189, 0.233]). Within K562 the model also decodes phase much better than the rank encoding (CV 0.894 vs 0.816). (4) The second reported metric, median angular error, is significantly worse for the model: +3.5 deg [2.7, 4.4]. The summary calls this a "lean" and does not test it. Conclusion 2 (the gap to raw expression is "the tokenizer") also depends on two things. First, a normalisation mismatch the README does not disclose: K562 rows sum to 7.4k–9.6k after expm1, RPE1 rows to exactly 10k. Renormalising K562 moves expr_full from 0.878 to 0.846. Second, a phase label built from marker-gene expression: expr_full sees all of these genes, while a cell sentence contains a median of only 7–9 of them. Verdicts on the ten checklist patterns: P1 clean (constant and random floors are reported). P2 clean (expression baselines are present). P3 present and unaddressed (the label is derived from the expression features; linear decodability is described as "information"). P4 present, partly acknowledged (the bootstrap resamples target cells only; one source and one target line). P5 present (marker genes used for the label are also features; normalisation confound). P6 mostly clean (the ladder of arms detects contrasts of about 0.03). P7 present, partly acknowledged (one model, layer, direction and readout; the reverse direction changes the verdict). P8 present and unaddressed (alpha and encoding change the verdict). P9 present ("neither adds nor loses", "carries what it is given through 21 layers", "the tokenizer, not the model"). P10 present (no pinned environment or model revision; the extraction inputs are not provided). Only checks run inside B7392 back these findings. A monitor I set up by mistake also streamed lines from unrelated task-output files; none of that was used.

findings.description: The parity verdict depends on one untuned ridge penalty. The analysis fixes alpha = 1000 for every arm. Selecting alpha by cross-validation on the source cell line only (no target leakage) picks alpha = 1e4 for both the model and expr_512_rank. At that alpha the pre-specified rule returns 'MODEL ADDS information', not parity. Across the alpha grid all three verdicts occur.
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha per arm by nested CV on the source line, or report a sweep. Restate the verdict at the CV-selected alpha (that gives 'model adds' at +0.018). Limit any parity claim to the alpha range where it holds, and say that it does not hold at the source-optimal alpha.

findings.description: expr_512_rank is presented as 'the same information a cell sentence carries', but it is one arbitrary linear encoding (linear ranks 512..1) of that information. Other equally faithful encodings of the same top-512 sentence transfer better than the model. With those encodings the verdict rule says the model LOSES information. Parity is therefore a property of the chosen encoding, not of the model versus its input. Ridge decodability is also not information content.
findings.evidence: Same pipeline, alpha = 1000, K562->RPE1: rank 0.7916; binary presence of top-512 genes 0.8091; log-rank 0.8074; model 0.7894. Paired bootstrap (1000 draws): model - binary = -0.0198 [-0.0298, -0.0091]; model - logrank = -0.0181 [-0.0293, -0.0071]. Both CIs lie entirely below 0.
findings.recommended_action: Report several input encodings (presence, linear rank, log rank, and the model's own embedding layer / layer 0 if obtainable). Define the comparator as the best of them, or report the range. Reword 'adds/loses information' as 'more/less linearly decodable by a ridge readout under frozen transfer'.

findings.description: Only one transfer direction (K562->RPE1) is tested. Running the identical frozen protocol in reverse (RPE1->K562) gives a large model advantage over its rank-encoded input. Within K562 the model also decodes phase much better than the rank encoding. 'The model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information. It carries what it is given through 21 layers' cannot stand. At most, parity is specific to this one direction under these settings.
findings.evidence: RPE1->K562 with the same scaler/ridge (alpha 1e3): model 0.758 (25 deg), expr_full 0.770, expr_512_mag 0.699, expr_512_rank 0.547 (31 deg), binary presence 0.706. Model - rank = +0.211 [0.189, 0.233] (1000 paired draws). Within-K562 5-fold CV at alpha 1e3: model 0.894 vs rank 0.816 vs full 0.916.
findings.recommended_action: Report both transfer directions and the within-line CV. Restate Conclusion 1 as direction- and setting-specific, or drop it. Add at least one more held-out cell line before claiming parity in general.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md:39-40; code/transfer.py:134-139 (verdict based on R_diff only)
findings.description: The summary's second metric, median angular error, shows the model significantly worse than its input encoding. The summary calls this a 'lean' and leaves it untested. On that metric the verdict rule would be 'loses', which contradicts 'equally well' and 'neither adds nor loses'.
findings.evidence: Paired bootstrap (2000 draws, same cells per draw): median error model - expr_512_rank = +3.53 deg [2.71, 4.41], P(>0) = 1.00. Against an exact cell-sentence replica of the rank arm: +3.09 deg [2.15, 4.03].
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap every reported metric's contrast and report it. State that parity holds on R_diff only and that the model is worse on median error. Pre-specify which metric decides the verdict.

findings.location: README.md:18 ('Same format and normalisation'); data/k562_expression.npz; SUMMARY.md:30-32 (Conclusion 2)
findings.description: The two expression matrices are not normalised the same way, although the README says they are. K562 per-cell totals after expm1 vary (probably normalised over a larger gene set, then subset). RPE1 totals are exactly 10,000. Frozen transfer of the magnitude-based arms (StandardScaler and ridge fit on K562, applied to RPE1) is sensitive to this. So the decomposition in Conclusion 2 (0.058 'from keeping only 512 genes', model 0.089 below expr_full) rests on a preprocessing inconsistency.
findings.evidence: expm1 row sums: K562 min/median/max 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573; RPE1 9,999.998 / 10,000 / 10,000.002. Renormalising K562 to 10,000 per cell before log1p changes expr_full transfer R_diff from 0.878 to 0.846. expr_512_mag is unchanged (0.821). expr_full - expr_512_mag therefore drops from about 0.058 to about 0.026, and model - expr_full from -0.089 to about -0.057.
findings.recommended_action: Harmonise normalisation, for example by renormalising both lines over the shared genes from raw counts. Rerun all arms, correct the README claim, and restate the Conclusion 2 decomposition with the harmonised numbers.

findings.location: code/cc_phase.py:56-64 (label = PCA angle of marker-gene expression); code/transfer.py:101-103; SUMMARY.md:30-34
findings.description: The endpoint is circular for the expression arms. The 'cell-cycle phase' label is atan2(PC2, PC1) of the standardised expression of 87–93 S/G2M marker genes in the same cells. expr_full receives exactly those genes' values, but each cell's 512-gene sentence contains only a handful of them. Part of the 'tokenisation loss' therefore measures how closely each encoding matches the recipe that defines the label, not cell-cycle information in general.
