The label is also a noisy proxy: PC1-PC2 explain only 31–35% of marker variance.
findings.evidence: Marker genes present in each cell's top-512: K562 median 9 (5–95%: 1–20); RPE1 median 7 (0–22). Label PCA: 87 markers in K562 and 93 in RPE1; pc12_var_ratio 0.306 (K562) and 0.349 (RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Define phase from features that are kept out of all predictor sets (for example, remove the marker genes from every arm's features, or use an independent label such as a held-out marker split). Rerun the ladder. Describe the endpoint as 'transfer of a marker-PCA phase angle' before drawing information conclusions.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:115-121 (bootstrap over target cells only), 134-139; README.md:46-50; SUMMARY.md:26-28, 38
findings.description: Parity is inferred from a non-significant difference with no pre-specified equivalence margin. The bootstrap also understates uncertainty: it resamples only RPE1 cells and holds fixed the K562-fitted scaler and ridge and both PCA-derived labels. Source-side and label-estimation variability are therefore left out. The caveat at line 38 notes that parity is not zero effect, but Conclusion 1 still says 'neither adds nor loses'.
findings.evidence: The verdict rule is 'CI contains 0 => parity' (transfer.py:136-137) with no equivalence bounds. Only target indices are resampled (transfer.py:119-121), and the readout is fit once (transfer.py:94-98).
findings.recommended_action: Use a two-level bootstrap (resample K562 cells and refit; resample RPE1 cells and recompute the label PCA). Pre-specify an equivalence margin and run a TOST-style test. Word the result as 'no detectable difference at alpha=1e3 on R_diff', not as 'neither adds nor loses'.

findings.description: The conclusions overreach the evidence. The evidence is one model, one layer (21), one readout position (the last token, which is the last subword of the 512th-ranked gene), one direction, one cell-line pair, one readout and one alpha. Yet the summary claims a mechanism ('carries what it is given through 21 layers'), an attribution ('the loss ... is the tokenizer, not the model'), and a general methodological rule for SCFMs. The 512-gene cap is an extraction setting (--max-genes 512), not a property of the C2S tokenizer, so 0.058 is not a 'tokenizer' cost.
findings.evidence: Intermediate layers are not analysed, so 'through 21 layers' is untested. The manifests show max_genes 512 chosen at extraction. Conclusion 3 generalises to 'an SCFM' from a single model. F1–F3 show the verdict changes with alpha, encoding and direction.
findings.recommended_action: Restate at the evidence level ('under this protocol, layer-21 last-token ridge decodability of a marker-PCA phase angle transfers K562->RPE1 about as well as a linear rank encoding at alpha=1e3'). Remove the mechanistic and general claims, or add layers, directions, cell lines and models to support them.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:55-56 (argpartition / unstable argsort); code/cell_sentences.py:131-133 (stable, gene-order tie-break)
findings.description: expr_512_rank does not reproduce the actual cell-sentence gene set. About 73 of the 512 slots per cell are filled from about 165 genes tied at the cutoff value. argpartition breaks these ties differently from the stable genomic-order sort used to build the sentences. The model's input also includes RPE1-only genes (about 66 per cell) that the rank arm drops. The effect on R_diff is small.
findings.evidence: Overlap between argpartition and cell-sentence gene sets: K562 median 486/512; RPE1 422/446 shared genes. An exact cell-sentence replica gives 0.7905 vs 0.7916; model - exact = -0.0012 [-0.013, +0.012].
findings.recommended_action: Build the rank arm with the same stable ranking used by cell_sentences.anndata_to_ranked_genes, and document the RPE1-only genes.

findings.description: The phase label is built from different marker sets in the two lines: 87 in K562 and 93 in RPE1 (UBE2C, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, WDR76 and GAS2L3 are missing from K562). The source and target labels are therefore defined differently. The effect is negligible here.
findings.evidence: An RPE1 label recomputed on the 87 shared markers agrees with the original at R_diff 0.995 (median 1.7 deg). Arm R_diff values change by at most 0.002.
findings.recommended_action: Use the intersection of marker genes across both lines for the label, and state this in the README.

findings.description: Reproducibility gaps. There are no pinned package versions or requirements file. The HF model revision is not recorded in the manifests. The .h5ad inputs used for activation extraction are not provided, so the activations cannot be regenerated or checked against data/. transfer.py was modified (12:32) after the outputs were written (log 07:53, json 10:56). Rerunning the current code does reproduce the point estimates exactly.
findings.evidence: The manifests list only 'vandijklab/C2S-Scale-Gemma-2-2B' with no revision. No environment file exists in the folder. File mtimes: transfer.py 12:32; run_log.txt 07:53; transfer_results.json 10:56.
findings.recommended_action: Add a requirements/lock file and the model commit hash. Include the extraction inputs or a checksum that links them to data/. Regenerate the outputs with the final code and record the runtime and hardware.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule only warns against one specific false claim: that the 512-gene baselines select genes from the shared set only. No finding makes that claim. F9 correctly says selection is from the full panel, with only tie-breaking differences. I checked the main numerical claims inline with the package's own functions and they reproduce: binary/log-rank encodings 0.8091/0.8074 vs model 0.7894, with model - binary = -0.0198 [-0.0298, -0.0091]. The reverse direction gives model 0.758 vs rank 0.547 (+0.211 [0.189, 0.233]). Median-error contrast is +3.53 deg [2.69, 4.38]. K562 expm1 row sums are 7,447/9,137/9,573 vs RPE1 at exactly 10,000. Renormalising K562 moves expr_full from 0.878 to 0.846, while expr_512_mag stays at 0.821.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue. Alpha is fixed at 1000 and never tuned. 5-fold CV on K562 picks 1e4, and at that alpha model - expr_512_rank = +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], so the verdict becomes 'model adds'. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither the documented error nor a false alarm. The reported numbers match the key.

Verified inline at alpha 1000. Binary presence of the top-512 genes scores 0.8091 and log1p-rank scores 0.8074, against model 0.7894. Model - binary = -0.0198 [-0.0298, -0.0091] and model - logrank = -0.0181 [-0.0293, -0.0071], both entirely below 0. The key lists 'linear ranks are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm ('a design choice'), but its rebuttal covers only the generic point. Here the data show the verdict flips to 'loses' even with a presence-only encoding, which carries less information than the sentence. Like alpha, this is a real robustness problem for the parity claim.

Verified inline. RPE1->K562 with the same protocol gives model 0.758, rank 0.547, binary 0.706 and full 0.770; model - rank = +0.211 [0.189, 0.233]. Part of this asymmetry probably comes from RPE1 sentences having ~68 non-shared genes, so the reverse direction is not a clean mirror. Even so, the general claim 'neither adds nor loses ... carries what it is given' does not survive outside the one tested direction. The within-K562 CV gap at alpha 1000 (0.894 vs 0.816) points the same way. The key's scope caveats cover layer, cell count and platform, not direction.

Verified inline. The paired bootstrap of median angular error gives model - expr_512_rank = +3.53 deg [2.69, 4.38], P(>0) = 1.0. SUMMARY calls this a 'lean' without testing it, yet still says 'equally well'. R_diff was the pre-specified verdict metric, so this qualifies the headline rather than overturning it. It is still a genuine, confirmed inconsistency.

Verified. K562 expm1 row sums run 7,447 / 9,137 / 9,573 while RPE1 is exactly 10,000, so README's 'Same format and normalisation' is inaccurate. Renormalising K562 changes expr_full from 0.878 to 0.846 and leaves expr_512_mag at 0.821. That alters the Conclusion 2 decomposition. It does not affect the rank or model arms, so the parity verdict is unchanged. The reviewer's renormalisation is one alternative, not a definitive harmonisation, and Conclusion 2's qualitative point (input format accounts for most of the gap) roughly survives.

The key explicitly lists this as a possible false alarm. The label is the common target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same marker genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. The low PC1-PC2 variance ratio is a description, not a defect.

The key lists target-only bootstrap uncertainty (no refit on resampled K562 cells) as a minor, valid other_real_issue. The point about no equivalence margin is a fair statistical-practice criticism. SUMMARY's caveat (line 38) already partly concedes that parity is not proof of zero effect. Neither point overturns the point estimate.

Mostly a scope and wording critique. The key says single layer, single model and cell-line limits are scope already stated in the caveats, not errors. Two sub-points are true but are wording issues: the 512 cap is an extraction setting (max_genes 512) rather than an inherent tokenizer property, and 'through 21 layers' is untested. The substantive robustness concerns it mentions are covered separately by F1-F3.

The key lists tie-breaking as true in a small way but not load-bearing. The exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], the same verdict. The finding itself rates this minor and its numbers are consistent with the key: exact replica -0.0012, and the RPE1-only genes match the key's mean of 67.8 per cell.

True (87 vs 93 markers, per the key's known facts), but the finding itself reports negligible impact: label agreement 0.995 and arm changes of at most 0.002. The key's possible false alarms note that labels are oriented by marker biology and R_diff ignores rotation.

These reproducibility gaps are real but trivial: no lock file, no model revision, no h5ad inputs. The mtime observation does not matter, because the key states that rerunning transfer.py reproduces the outputs byte for byte, and the finding itself concedes the point estimates reproduce.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean', so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule says only that the false claim to watch for is 'the 512-gene baselines choose genes from the shared set only'. No finding makes that claim. F9 correctly says the selection is made from the full panel; its only point is about how ties are broken.

findings.reason: The key's other_real_issues names exactly this as valid: alpha is fixed at 1000 and the verdict depends on it. 5-fold CV on K562 picks 1e4, and at 1e4 the full-panel selection gives model - rank = +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], so the model comes out ahead. F1's numbers match the key (+0.0175 [0.0076, 0.0275]). The key says to grade this as neither a detection nor a false alarm.

I verified this by rerunning at alpha 1e3, K562->RPE1. Binary top-512 presence gives 0.8091 and log-rank 0.8063, against model 0.7894. Paired bootstrap: model - binary = -0.0198 [-0.0298, -0.0091] and model - logrank = -0.0171 [-0.0280, -0.0059]; both CIs lie entirely below 0. The key does list 'linear rank values are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm. But its reason (same membership/order information) does not answer F2's point, which the data confirm: other encodings of the same, or even less, sentence information flip the pre-specified verdict to 'loses'. That makes the parity verdict encoding-specific.

I verified the reverse frozen transfer (RPE1->K562, same scaler/ridge, alpha 1e3): model 0.758 (25 deg), rank 0.547 (31 deg), expr_full 0.770, binary 0.706. That is a large model advantage, and within K562 the model also beats the rank encoding (consistent with the CV numbers in F1). The key does not mention this. It shows the general claim 'neither adds nor loses ... carries what it is given' does not hold beyond this one direction and setting. Some of the reverse-direction gap may come from the RPE1-side shared-column truncation (about 444 kept genes), but the binary arm and the within-line CV point the same way.

I verified it: paired bootstrap of median-error model - expr_512_rank = +3.53 deg [2.69, 4.38], P(>0) = 1.0. The SUMMARY gives the 23 vs 20 deg figure but calls it a 'lean' and does not test it, while still claiming 'equally well'. Applying the same rule to the second reported metric would give 'loses'. The key does not mention this. The median error uses the best rotation for each arm, which the key says is applied equally, so the comparison is fair.

I verified it. K562 expm1 row sums run from 7,447 to 9,573 (median 9,137), while RPE1 sums are exactly 10,000, so README line 18 ('Same format and normalisation') is inaccurate. Renormalising K562 to 10k drops expr_full transfer from 0.878 to 0.846; expr_512_mag is unchanged (0.821). The key does not cover this. It changes the Conclusion 2 decomposition (0.058 becomes about 0.026). It does not change the headline model-vs-rank verdict, because both of those arms are scale-invariant. The qualitative claim 'almost the whole gap' also survives (model - full about -0.057; tokenisation loss about 0.055). So it is a real problem, but not load-bearing.

The key lists label circularity (the phase label is built from marker genes that are also features) as a possible false alarm. The label is the target for every arm, there is no leak from RPE1 into training, and the model's sentence contains the same genes. The supporting facts are true (median 9/7 markers in the top-512; PC1-2 variance 0.306/0.349). But that the full-expression arm carries more marker information is exactly the tokenisation loss being measured, not an artifact.

The key's other_real_issues confirms that the bootstrap covers target-cell sampling only, with no refit on resampled K562 cells, and calls it 'Minor; valid'. The missing pre-specified equivalence margin is also a valid statistical point, though SUMMARY line 38 partly acknowledges it. It argues that uncertainty is understated, not that the estimate is wrong.

Mostly scope and wording. The key lists 'only one layer ... scope, not an error' as a possible false alarm, and the SUMMARY caveats state 'One model, one layer, one readout'. Its sharper points are true but semantic: max_genes 512 is an extraction setting rather than the tokenizer itself, 'through 21 layers' is untested, and the generalisation to SCFMs is too broad. The parts that bear on the verdict are taken from F1-F3.

The key lists tie-breaking (argpartition vs stable sort) as 'true in a small way, but not load-bearing'. With the exact cell-sentence baseline, model - baseline = -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], which matches F9's -0.0012. F9 itself says the effect is small. The roughly 66 RPE1-only genes per cell match the key (mean 67.8), and the key says dropping them is unavoidable.

I verified 87 vs 93 markers. WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, UBE2C and GAS2L3 are absent from K562; E2F8 is absent from both lines. The key states that labels are computed separately in each line, with S/G2M peaks agreeing and R_diff invariant to rotation. The finding itself reports a negligible effect (at most 0.002).

The reproducibility and documentation gaps are true: there is no requirements file and no model revision, and transfer.py has mtime 12:32, after the outputs. They are minor. The key confirms that rerunning reproduces the outputs byte for byte and that data/ matches the source h5ad files exactly, and the finding itself admits the point estimates reproduce.

review.summary:
I reran the pipeline inline without writing any files, and the reported numbers reproduce exactly: R_diff is model 0.7894, expr_512_rank 0.7916 and expr_full 0.8784. The headline verdict ("the model is at parity with its input", model − expr_512_rank = −0.0022, CI [−0.0144, +0.0105]) does not survive basic checks, because it depends on three arbitrary choices.

(1) Ridge alpha is fixed at 1000. This is not the K562-cross-validated optimum for any arm; 5-fold CV on K562 picks 1e4 for all of them. At 1e4 the model beats the rank arm (0.821 vs 0.803, +0.0175, CI [+0.0075, +0.0274]), which the analysis's own rule would call "MODEL ADDS". At alpha ≤ 100 the model is below the rank arm.

(2) The linear rank encoding (512…1) is a weak stand-in for what a cell sentence carries. At the reported alpha, a plain top-512 presence encoding beats the model (0.809–0.820; model − presence −0.020, CI [−0.030, −0.009]), and so does log-rank (−0.017, CI [−0.028, −0.006]). Both are functions of the cell sentence, so on these the verdict becomes "MODEL LOSES". The claimed "0.029 cost of dropping expression values" disappears: presence with cell-sentence tie-breaking gives 0.820, the same as magnitudes. The rank arm also does not reproduce the cell sentence. About 99% of cells have a tie at the 512 cutoff, with about 169 genes tied there. As a result the top-512 sets differ by about 29 genes per cell, and about 477 of the 512 rank values per cell differ.

(3) On the second metric, median angular error, the model is clearly worse (+3.5°, CI [2.7, 4.4], P = 1.0). The summary calls this "slightly worse".

The bootstrap only resamples RPE1 cells. Also resampling the K562 training cells and refitting gives an SD of 0.027 for the key contrast, about four times the reported CI half-width. The conclusions also overreach: they speak of information carried "through 21 layers" when only layer 21 was measured; they say "the loss is the tokenizer, not the model"; and they draw a general SCFM conclusion from one model, one layer, one readout and one pair of cell lines. The phase label is a PCA angle of the marker genes' expression levels, computed separately in each cell line. That favours the expression arms that carry those levels, and it limits what "cell-cycle information" can mean here.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1 clean (constant and random floors are given).
- P2 present and unaddressed (the baseline chosen is weak, while equivalent encodings beat the model).
- P3 present and unaddressed (the label is derived from expression; the "cell-summary" readout is the last gene's token).
- P4 present and unaddressed (fixed-source bootstrap; only one pair of cell lines).
- P5 present (the rank arm does not reproduce the cell sentence).
- P6 present and unaddressed (no positive control for the parity result).
- P7 present and only partly acknowledged.
- P8 present and unaddressed (no sweep of alpha or of the encoding; median error not bootstrapped).
- P9 present.
- P10 minor gaps.

findings.description: The PARITY verdict depends on the single, untuned ridge penalty alpha=1000, which is not the cross-validated optimum for any arm. Under in-domain (K562) cross-validation the verdict flips to MODEL ADDS. At smaller alpha the model is below the rank arm. The headline 'model is at parity with its input' is one point on an alpha curve along which the sign of the contrast changes.
findings.evidence:
I swept alpha on the same frozen K562->RPE1 protocol (RPE1 R_diff, model / expr_512_rank):
- alpha 1: 0.591 / 0.672
- alpha 10: 0.661 / 0.678
- alpha 100: 0.708 / 0.716
- alpha 1e3: 0.789 / 0.792 (reported)
- alpha 1e4: 0.821 / 0.803
- alpha 1e5: 0.795 / 0.597
5-fold CV on K562 picks alpha=1e4 for model, expr_full, expr_512_rank and presence alike. CV R_diff for model is 0.896 at 1e4 vs 0.894 at 1e3; for rank 0.849 vs 0.816; for expr_full 0.940 vs 0.916. At alpha=1e4 the paired bootstrap of model − expr_512_rank gives +0.0175, 95% CI [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0)=1.0. That is 'MODEL ADDS information' under the README's own verdict rule. At alpha=1e4 expr_full is 0.897, so the 'tokenisation loss' becomes 0.094, larger than the whole model gap of 0.076.
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha per arm by cross-validation inside K562 only, never on RPE1, or report the full alpha sweep. State the verdict for each alpha and restrict any claim to the range where it is stable. Under CV-selected alpha the summary must report that the model exceeds the linear rank encoding, not parity.

findings.description: expr_512_rank (linear ranks 512..1) is treated as 'the information a cell sentence carries'. It is in fact one arbitrary and weak linear encoding of that information. Other encodings that use the same or less information beat the model, so the 'parity' and 'tokenizer explains the gap' conclusions come from the choice of baseline encoding. The binary top-512 presence encoding is a strict function of the cell sentence. The decomposition 'dropping expression values costs 0.029' is also an artifact of the linear-rank coding.
findings.evidence:
All results at the reported alpha=1000, same frozen protocol:
- Presence of top-512 genes, same argpartition set as the analysis: R_diff 0.809. Model − presence = −0.0198, 95% CI [−0.0301, −0.0091], P(>0)=0.000.
- Log-rank encoding: R_diff 0.806. Model − log-rank = −0.0170, CI [−0.0280, −0.0061].
- Presence built with the cell sentence's own stable tie-breaking: R_diff 0.820, identical to expr_512_mag (0.820). Dropping values therefore costs about 0, not 0.029.
Under the README's verdict rule all of these comparisons say 'MODEL LOSES information', not parity.
findings.recommended_action: Report the model contrast against several information-equivalent encodings of the cell sentence: presence, linear rank, log-rank and rank bins. Treat the best of them as the information ceiling of the input. Restate conclusion 1, and conclusion 2's split into 0.058 and 0.029, so they reflect that the result depends on the encoding.

findings.description: The second metric, median angular error, shows a clear deficit for the model, but it is never bootstrapped. The summary dismisses it as 'slightly worse' and says the two metrics 'lean the same way'. Applying the same paired bootstrap and verdict rule to median error gives 'MODEL LOSES', which contradicts the parity headline.
findings.evidence: Paired bootstrap over RPE1 cells (2,000 draws, seed 0) of median error, model minus expr_512_rank: +3.53 deg, 95% CI [+2.71, +4.41], P(>0)=1.00. Mean absolute error after the best rotation is also worse: model 31.0 deg vs rank 29.2 deg.
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap every reported metric and apply the verdict rule to each. State plainly that the model is significantly worse on median and mean angular error. The verdict should be called metric-dependent rather than parity.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:116-121 (bootstrap resamples RPE1 cells only); SUMMARY.md:4, 27, 38
findings.description: The CI treats the K562-fitted scaler and ridge as fixed. Only the 3,000 RPE1 evaluation cells are resampled. Variability from the 3,000 K562 training cells is ignored, and so is variability in the phase labels, which come from PCA on the same cells. The claim is about transfer between cell lines, yet there is only one source/target pair, so the bootstrap over cells does not address the unit of inference. The CI quoted in the summary, and the caveat that 'the CI allows a gain of up to 0.0105 or a loss of up to 0.0144', understate the uncertainty severalfold.
findings.evidence: I resampled K562 training cells with replacement, refit the scaler and ridge (alpha=1000), and scored model − expr_512_rank on RPE1 (60 draws). SD = 0.027, range [−0.045, +0.063]. With RPE1 cells resampled as well, the 2.5–97.5 percentiles are [−0.038, +0.063], against the reported [−0.0144, +0.0105].
findings.recommended_action: Use a two-level bootstrap that refits on resampled K562 cells and scores on resampled RPE1 cells, or repeated source subsampling, and report that interval. Also name the unit of inference: one cell-line pair from one screen. Pre-specify an equivalence margin before any parity claim.

findings.location: code/transfer.py:55-56 (argpartition + non-stable argsort) vs code/cell_sentences.py:131-133 (stable sort, ties by column order); README.md:41; SUMMARY.md:12
findings.description: The rank arm does not reproduce the model's input. Expression values are log1p of normalised counts and have heavy ties. Cell sentences break ties stably by column order, which is genomic order, while top_k_encode breaks them arbitrarily via argpartition. The genes chosen at the 512 cutoff and almost all rank positions therefore differ from the actual cell sentence. In RPE1, about 67 of each cell's top-512 slots are genes outside the shared set: the model sees them, but the rank arm drops them. Labelling the arm 'the model's input' is inaccurate.
findings.evidence:
- K562: 99.4% of cells have a tie spanning ranks 512/513. A median of 169 genes share the cutoff value and only 441 are strictly above it. The top-512 values contain a median of only 64 distinct values.
- The argpartition set and the stable (cell-sentence) set differ by about 29 genes per cell, and about 477 of the 512 rank values per cell differ.
- The stable-tie rank arm gives R_diff 0.7905, against 0.7916 for the analysis's arm. Presence gives 0.820 with stable ties against 0.809 with argpartition.
- The RPE1 rank arm holds on average 444.8 shared genes out of 512.
findings.recommended_action: Build the baseline encodings from the exact ranked gene lists used to make the cell sentences: same tie-breaking, same nonzero filter. Document that most of the cell sentence's tail and within-tie order reflects genomic column order, not expression. Rerun the contrasts.

findings.description: The endpoint is not cell-cycle phase as such. It is atan2 of the first two PCs of z-scored marker-gene expression, computed separately in each line on different marker sets. Those same marker magnitudes are features in the expression arms. The label is therefore partly a function of the expression features, which favours arms that carry magnitudes (expr_full, expr_512_mag). This inflates the 'tokenisation loss' and 'dropping values' components that the summary attributes to the tokenizer. It also means any cell-cycle information the model has beyond this PCA proxy cannot be credited, so 'neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information' cannot be tested with this endpoint.
findings.evidence:
- K562 phase uses 87 markers (WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8, UBE2C and GAS2L3 are missing); RPE1 uses 93.
- PC1–PC2 explain only 30.6% (K562) and 34.9% (RPE1) of marker variance.
- The orientation is flipped in K562 and not in RPE1.
- The expr_full features include every marker gene whose standardised magnitudes define theta.
findings.recommended_action: Restate the endpoint literally, as 'recovery of a marker-PCA phase proxy'. Add a label that does not come from the evaluated features, for example markers held out from the features, or an orthogonal phase annotation. Alternatively, remove the marker genes from all feature arms and check whether the ladder and the parity verdict hold.

findings.description:
The conclusions overreach the evidence in three ways.
1. 'Neither adds nor loses' and 'carries what it is given through 21 layers' infer equivalence from a CI that spans 0, with no pre-specified margin. Only layer 21 was read out, with no embedding/layer-0 or intermediate-layer readout, so nothing was shown about information flow through the layers.
2. 'The loss to raw expression is the tokenizer, not the model' is a decomposition of linear-readout losses on hand-built encodings. It is not a measurement of the model's tokenizer or of any model layer.
3. Conclusion 3 generalises to SCFM evaluation in general from one model, one layer (21 of Gemma-2-2B's 26), one ridge readout, one label definition and one cell-line pair from one screen.
findings.evidence:
- The manifest lists layers [21] only; there is no layer-0 or static input-embedding arm.
- transfer.py contains no equivalence test.
- Caveat line 43 admits 'One model, one layer, one readout', yet conclusion 3 states a general rule ('Comparing an SCFM with raw expression charges it for its tokenizer').
- F1–F4 show that the verdict changes with alpha, encoding and metric.
findings.recommended_action: Replace 'neither adds nor loses' and 'through 21 layers' with a statement limited to layer 21, this readout and this alpha. Add an embedding-layer and multi-layer readout if information flow is to be claimed. Present conclusion 3 as a hypothesis, and test it on at least one further model, a second cell-line pair and several readouts.

findings.description: The headline is a null finding (no difference), but there is no positive control showing that the protocol can detect a model gain or loss of plausible size. Examples would be noise-injected activations, a randomly initialised model or an earlier layer. Given the source-side variance in F4, the power to detect differences of about 0.02–0.03 is unclear.
findings.evidence: No arm in transfer.py has a known, planted difference relative to expr_512_rank. The only reference arms are the constant and random floors (0.043 / 0.017).
findings.recommended_action: Add a calibration arm with a known degradation, for example the activations with added Gaussian noise or a random projection of the rank encoding. Show that the paired contrast and the verdict rule detect it at the stated CI width.

findings.description: The 'cell-summary' activation is the residual stream at the last token, which is the final subword of the 512th (lowest-ranked) gene. Because of ties, that gene is effectively picked by genomic column order. No summary or query token follows the gene list in the prompt template, and no other pooling (mean over gene tokens) was tested. The model arm may therefore understate what the model represents, which matters for any 'model loses or adds' interpretation.
findings.evidence: DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE in cell_sentences.py:25-28 puts the instruction before the genes. The cell-summary unit stores hidden[li][-1]. A median of 169 genes is tied at the cutoff value (see F5).
findings.recommended_action: Report a mean-pooled or prompt-suffix readout as a sensitivity arm, and describe the 'cell-summary' activation accurately as the last gene token's residual stream.

findings.description:
There is no reproducibility scaffolding:
- No requirements or environment file, and no package versions.
- The model is referenced as 'vandijklab/C2S-Scale-Gemma-2-2B' with no pinned revision.
- The compute dtype (bfloat16 by default; --dtype was not passed) is not recorded in the manifest.
- The .h5ad inputs used for extraction are not included, so the correspondence between activations and cells cannot be checked independently.
- transfer.py was modified (12:32) after the outputs were written (07:53 and 10:56). The outputs do reproduce on rerun.
findings.evidence: The manifest has no revision hash and no dtype field. There is no environment file in the folder. The file timestamps show code newer than outputs.
findings.recommended_action: Add a pinned environment, the model revision hash and the compute dtype to the manifest. Record a hash of the extraction inputs, and regenerate the outputs from the final code.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' (error: null), so there is no documented error to detect. None of the findings makes the claim the key names as false, which is that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only. F5 says the RPE1 rank arm holds about 445 shared genes out of 512. That fits the package's full-panel selection, and the key confirms it.

findings.reason: This is the key's first listed other_real_issue: alpha is fixed at 1000 and never tuned, and the verdict depends on it. 5-fold CV on K562 picks alpha 1e4, and at that alpha model - rank is +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], so the verdict becomes MODEL ADDS. The reviewer's numbers match the key. The key says to grade this as neither a detection nor a false alarm.

I re-ran these checks. Binary top-512 presence (same argpartition set, alpha 1000) scores R_diff 0.809, and model - presence is -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091]. Log-rank scores 0.806, with model - logrank -0.0165 [-0.0277, -0.0054]. Presence with stable tie-breaking scores 0.820, the same as expr_512_mag. Presence is a strict function of the cell sentence, yet under the README's own rule it gives 'MODEL LOSES'. So the parity verdict and the 0.029 'dropping values' cost depend on choosing linear ranks. The key lists 'linear ranks are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm. Its rebuttal ('same membership and order information') does not answer the confirmed result that the verdict flips.

Confirmed. A paired bootstrap of median angular error (model - expr_512_rank, 2,000 draws, seed 0) gives +3.53 deg [+2.71, +4.41], P(>0) = 1.0. The SUMMARY calls this 'slightly worse' and says both metrics 'lean the same way'. It still concludes the model 'neither adds nor loses' information, but the second metric shows a significant deficit. Not in the key. The verdict rule is defined on R_diff only, which softens the issue somewhat.

This is the key's second other_real_issue (minor): the CIs ignore training-side sampling because the ridge is never refit on resampled K562 cells. I checked the size with 15 K562 resample-and-refit draws. The SD of model - rank was 0.031, with a range of -0.064 to +0.058, consistent with the reviewer's 0.027. The reported CI is far too narrow, but a wider interval still spans 0, so the parity verdict itself does not change.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm: argpartition and stable-sort tie-breaking differ, which is true but small. The reviewer's own evidence shows the effect is small: the stable-tie rank arm scores 0.7905 vs 0.7916 (I got model - stable_rank -0.0012 [-0.0128, +0.0115], same verdict). Dropping the roughly 67 non-shared RPE1 genes is unavoidable in a frozen cross-line readout, and the key also lists that as a false alarm. The finding does not claim shared-only selection.

This matches two possible false alarms in the key. One is label circularity: marker genes are both label inputs and expression features. The other is per-line phase computation. The key says the label is the same target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1. Orientation comes from marker biology, with S/G2M peaks agreeing within 12 deg, and R_diff ignores rotation. The descriptive facts (87/93 markers) are correct, but the claimed bias that would invalidate the conclusions is the listed non-issue.

Mostly a scope and wording complaint. The key says one layer, one readout and one cell-line pair are stated in the caveats, so this is scope rather than an error. SUMMARY line 38 already says parity is not proof of zero effect and gives the CI bounds. Phrases like 'through 21 layers' and the general conclusion 3 do overreach, but this is presentation and does not show a result is wrong on its own. The parts that do carry weight are covered by F1-F4.
True: there is no positive-control or calibration arm. This is a reasonable suggestion for a null result, but it is a design nicety, not an error.

Accurate. DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE puts the instruction before the genes, and the cell-summary unit stores hidden[-1], which is the last gene's final subword. This is a design limitation and a reasonable sensitivity suggestion. It does not show the stated results are wrong.

True as stated: there is no environment file, the manifest has no model revision or dtype, and transfer.py's timestamp is newer than the outputs. The reviewer admits the outputs reproduce, and the key confirms a byte-for-byte reproduction. This is reproducibility housekeeping only.

grade_b.detection_reason: Key B7392 has status 'clean' and error null, so there is no documented error to detect. The key's detection rule only warns that a claim that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set alone would be FALSE here. No finding makes that claim: F5 correctly says the selection runs over the full panel and that the shared columns are kept afterwards.

findings.reason: This matches the key's first other_real_issue. Alpha is fixed at 1000 without tuning, and the verdict depends on it. The key reports that 5-fold CV on K562 picks alpha=1e4, where model - full-panel rank = +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274] ('MODEL ADDS'). The reviewer's figure, +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], agrees. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm.

I reran this at alpha 1000. A top-512 presence encoding (argpartition set) gives R_diff 0.809. Model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], P(>0)=0. With stable tie-breaking, presence gives 0.820, the same as expr_512_mag. Presence carries less information than the cell sentence, yet it significantly beats the model. So 'parity with its input / neither adds nor loses' and the 0.029 'dropping values' figure depend on choosing the linear rank coding. The key does list 'linear ranks are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm, calling it a design choice. But its rationale (the rank arm carries the same information) does not address the confirmed result that an encoding with less information beats the model under the same readout. I treat this as a genuine robustness problem, similar to the alpha dependence.

Confirmed. A paired bootstrap of median error (model - expr_512_rank, 2,000 draws, seed 0) gives +3.53 deg [+2.71, +4.41], P(>0)=1.0. The summary reports 23 vs 20 deg but calls it 'slightly worse' and never tests it. On the second metric the model is significantly worse, which weakens 'neither adds nor loses'. The summary partly discloses the direction, which lowers the severity, but the problem is real and not in the key.

The key lists this explicitly: 'The bootstrap CIs cover only target-cell sampling; the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells... Minor; valid but not the documented error.' It widens the uncertainty around parity but does not by itself overturn the headline.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm: argpartition vs stable-sort tie-breaking is 'true in a small way, but not load-bearing'. The exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], the same verdict. The reviewer's own figures show the rank arm barely moves (0.7905 vs 0.7916). Dropping non-shared RPE1 genes is also listed as a false alarm, since it is unavoidable for a frozen cross-line readout. The facts are correct, but the 'major' severity is overstated.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm: the label is built from marker genes that are also features, but that label is the target for every arm and is not a leak. The descriptive facts are correct: 87/93 markers, PC1-2 variance 30.6%/34.9%, K562 flipped and RPE1 not. The flip is just the biology-based orientation step, though, not a defect. The claim that this inflates the tokenisation loss and makes the claim untestable is never demonstrated.

Partly fair on wording: 'neither adds nor loses' from a CI that spans 0, and 'through 21 layers' when only layer 21 was read out. But SUMMARY's caveats already state 'Parity is not proof of zero effect' with the CI bounds, and 'One model, one layer, one readout'. The key treats one layer and one cell-line pair as scope, not an error. This is mainly overreach in wording and scope.
No positive or calibration control exists. True, but it is a suggestion for a stronger design, not an error in the reported results.

Accurate: DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE puts the instruction before the genes, and the cell-summary vector is hidden[li][-1], the last gene's final subword. No other pooling is tested. This is a design limitation and sensitivity suggestion, not shown to change results.

True: the manifest has no model revision or dtype, there is no environment file, the h5ad inputs are absent, and transfer.py (12:32) is newer than the outputs. The key confirms the outputs reproduce byte for byte, and the reviewer concedes this. This is reproducibility housekeeping only.

review.summary: Review of <CODE_ROOT>/analysis-tasks/B7392 against the ten-pattern checklist. Running the arms inline (nothing written) gives back every reported number exactly: model 0.7894, expr_full 0.8784, expr_512_mag 0.8201, expr_512_rank 0.7916, contrast -0.0022 [-0.0144, +0.0105]. The headline "parity" verdict does not hold up. It depends on two choices made once and never tested: ridge alpha = 1000, and a linear rank encoding as the "fair" input baseline. (1) Alpha: K562-only 5-fold CV picks alpha = 1e4 for every arm. At that alpha, model - rank = +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], which is "MODEL ADDS" by the script's own rule. Across alphas from 1e2 to 1e6 the contrast swings from -0.09 to +0.20. (2) Encoding: a binary presence encoding of the same top-512 genes carries strictly less information than the rank list, yet it transfers better (0.809 for the coded gene set, 0.820 for the exact sentence set). Against it, model - presence = -0.020 [-0.030, -0.009], which is "MODEL LOSES". Further problems: the transfer in the opposite direction (RPE1 -> K562) is far from parity (model 0.758 vs rank 0.547); the bootstrap ignores refit variance, and a two-level bootstrap gives roughly ±0.07 rather than ±0.012; "CI spans 0" is read as equivalence without a margin; the phase label is built from the magnitudes of the same marker genes the expression arms use (marker genes alone give 0.918); and the summary words its conclusions too strongly. Checklist verdicts: P1 clean (constant/random floors present; a depth-only baseline gives 0.127). P2 present and unaddressed (the trivial baseline chosen is a weak encoding of the input). P3 present and unaddressed (label circularity; "information" means linear decodability at one alpha). P4 present and unaddressed (target-only bootstrap; a single source/target pair). P5 present and unaddressed (hyperparameter and encoding picked without a sweep; label confound). P6 present and unaddressed (no power check or positive control for the null "parity" finding). P7 present, partly acknowledged (one direction, layer, model, seed; reverse direction contradicts). P8 present and unaddressed (no alpha sweep; CI too narrow). P9 present and unaddressed ("neither adds nor loses", "carries ... through 21 layers", "is the tokenizer, not the model"). P10 minor gaps (no pinned versions or model revision; .h5ad inputs to extraction not provided).

findings.description: The parity verdict holds only at the one ridge penalty used (alpha = 1000). That value was neither tuned nor swept. Across reasonable alphas the model - expr_512_rank contrast changes sign and size. The alpha chosen by cross-validation on the source cell line alone makes the script's own rule return 'MODEL ADDS information', not parity.
findings.evidence: Rerun with the same frozen K562 -> RPE1 protocol, R_diff on RPE1 as model / expr_full / expr_512_rank. alpha 1e2: 0.708 / 0.854 / 0.716. alpha 1e3: 0.789 / 0.878 / 0.792 (reported). alpha 3e3: 0.813 / 0.892 / 0.812. alpha 1e4: 0.821 / 0.897 / 0.804. alpha 3e4: 0.820 / 0.884 / 0.742. alpha 1e5: 0.795 / 0.818 / 0.597. alpha 1e6: 0.683 / 0.623 / 0.774. Paired bootstrap (2,000 draws) for model - rank: at 1e4, +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], P(>0) = 1.0; at 1e5, +0.198 [+0.181, +0.213]. K562 5-fold CV picks alpha = 1e4 for model (CV R 0.893), expr_full (0.936), rank (0.853) and presence (0.880); alpha = 1e3 is below the best for every arm. At the CV-chosen alpha the summary's decomposition numbers also change (model - full = -0.076, full - rank = +0.093).
findings.recommended_action: Choose alpha per arm by CV on K562 only (nested, with no target information), or report the full sweep. Restate the verdict at the CV-chosen alpha (it becomes 'model adds ~0.017'), or limit the claim to the alpha range where it holds. Remove 'parity' from the headline unless it survives the sweep.

findings.description: Linear rank values (512..1) fed to a ridge are treated as 'the same information a cell sentence carries' and used as the fair input baseline. They understate that information. A binary encoding of which genes are in the top 512 is a strict function of the rank list, so it holds less information, yet it transfers better than the rank encoding and significantly better than the model. Against this equally 'input-only' baseline the model loses information. The claim 'dropping expression values costs 0.029' is therefore an artefact of the encoding, not a loss of information.
findings.evidence: R_diff RPE1 at alpha 1e3: presence of the top-512 set as coded = 0.809; presence of the exact stable-sorted sentence set = 0.8202; log-rank = 0.807; rank as coded = 0.792; expr_512_mag = 0.8201; model = 0.789. Paired bootstrap: model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], P(>0) = 0.0; model - log-rank = -0.0181 [-0.0290, -0.0072], P(>0) = 0.0; presence - rank = +0.0176 [+0.0073, +0.0279]. Under the README verdict rule (step 6) these give 'MODEL LOSES information'. Exact presence (0.8202) equals magnitude (0.8201), so 'dropping values' costs about 0, not 0.029 (SUMMARY.md:22, 31-32).
findings.recommended_action: Report several encodings of the model's input (presence, rank, log-rank, rank plus presence). Use the best of them, or one picked by source-only CV, as the input baseline. Drop or rewrite Conclusion 2's split into 0.058 + 0.029 and Conclusion 3's 'C2S comes out even', which depend on the weakest encoding.

findings.description: The general conclusions ('the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information', 'C2S comes out even', advice for SCFMs in general) rest on one transfer direction, one layer, one model and one seed. In the reverse direction, with the same protocol and alpha, there is no parity: the model beats the rank-encoded input by about 0.21.
findings.evidence: RPE1 -> K562, alpha = 1000, same scaler/ridge/R_diff: model 0.758, expr_full 0.770, expr_512_rank 0.547 (model - rank about +0.21). K562 -> RPE1 (reported): 0.789 / 0.878 / 0.792. The Caveats mention 'one model, one layer, one readout' but not the direction, and Conclusion 3 generalises to SCFMs anyway.
findings.recommended_action: Report both transfer directions and, if possible, more layers (including an embedding-layer or layer-0 floor) and a second model. Limit the conclusions to the conditions where they hold, and delete the general SCFM 'practical reading' unless it is supported across conditions.

findings.description: The paired bootstrap resamples only the RPE1 test cells, with the K562-fitted scaler and ridge held fixed and the per-line phase labels fixed. It leaves out variance from the training sample and from estimating the readout, so the reported CI on model - rank is far too narrow. The caveat 'the CI allows a gain of up to 0.0105 or a loss of up to 0.0144' misstates the uncertainty. There is also only one source/target pair, so the unit of inference is a single cell-line transfer, not 3,000 cells.
findings.evidence: Two-level bootstrap (resample K562 cells and refit both arms, then resample RPE1 cells), 40 reps, alpha 1e3: model - rank mean +0.0075, SD 0.037, 2.5-97.5% [-0.077, +0.064]. That is about 3 times wider on each side than the reported [-0.0144, +0.0105].
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap the whole pipeline (resample source cells and refit, resample target cells, and ideally recompute the phase labels), or use repeated source subsampling. Report the wider interval, state that the inference unit is one cell-line pair, and correct the caveat.

findings.description: The verdict rule reads 'CI contains 0' as 'parity'. There is no equivalence margin and no power analysis or positive control showing the pipeline would detect a meaningful gain or loss. Conclusion 1 then turns this non-rejection into 'the model neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information'. The model is also worse on the second metric (median error 23 vs 20 deg), and that difference is not tested.
findings.evidence: transfer.py:136-137: verdict = 'PARITY' if lo <= 0 <= hi. No equivalence bound (TOST) is defined. With the proper two-level uncertainty (F4: about ±0.07) the procedure would call any difference below about 0.07 'parity'. Median error is reported for points only (SUMMARY.md:12-13, 39-40), with no bootstrap.
findings.recommended_action: Set an equivalence margin in advance and run TOST. Add a positive control, e.g. degrade or augment the input-encoding arm by a known amount and show the pipeline detects it. Bootstrap the median-error difference too. Reword Conclusion 1 to 'no detectable difference at alpha = 1000'.

findings.description: The target label theta is the atan2 of the first two PCs of z-scored log expression of the 87-93 Tirosh marker genes. It is computed separately in each line with different marker sets and loadings. The expression arms see exactly those marker magnitudes, so their advantage partly reflects closeness to how the label was built, not biological phase information the tokenizer throws away. 'The loss to raw expression is the tokenizer' mixes up encoding loss with label circularity.
findings.evidence: Ridge on expression of the 87 shared marker genes alone: R_diff 0.918, which beats all-gene expr_full (0.878). Non-marker genes only: expr 0.839, rank 0.663. The phase PCs explain only 31% (K562) and 35% (RPE1) of marker variance, and the marker sets differ between lines (87 vs 93 genes).
findings.recommended_action: Restate what the endpoint measures (recovery of a marker-PCA angle derived from expression). Also report results with the marker genes held out of all feature sets, or with a label that does not come from the same expression values (e.g. a rank-based or external phase label such as a tricycle reference projection). Soften Conclusion 2.

findings.description: The summary words its conclusions beyond the evidence. 'It carries what it is given through 21 layers' and 'costs 0.087 before the first layer' are untested: only layer 21 was read, and there is no embedding-layer, layer-0 or random-weight comparison. 'Neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information' treats linear ridge decodability at one alpha as information content. 'The loss ... is the tokenizer, not the model' is a causal attribution drawn from a subtraction of arm scores.
findings.evidence: The manifests (data/act_*/manifest.json) list layers [21] only. No arm uses token embeddings or earlier layers. F1 and F2 show the sign of model - input changes with alpha and with how the input is encoded, so information statements are not supported.
findings.recommended_action: Replace with evidence-grade wording, e.g. 'at layer 21 with ridge alpha = 1000, a linear readout of the model co-varies with phase about as well as a linear readout of rank-encoded top-512 expression'. Remove the claims about 'through 21 layers' and 'before the first layer' unless an embedding or early-layer arm is added.

findings.description: expr_512_rank is not the model's actual input. top_k_encode breaks ties with argpartition and an unstable argsort. The cell sentences use a stable sort over nonzero genes, so ties follow column (genomic) order. Ties are common at the 512 cutoff. In RPE1, the 2,205 genes outside the shared set appear in the model's sentence and affect its activations, but they are dropped from the rank arm.
findings.evidence: Over 300 sampled cells per line, the overlap between the rank arm's gene set and the true sentence set averages 94-95% (minimum 82%). The same gene sits at the same position only about 12% of the time. A median of ~75 of the 512 kept genes are tied at the cutoff value. An exact stable-sort rank arm gives R_diff 0.7905 vs 0.7916, so the effect on the point estimate is small, but README.md:41 overstates how closely the arm matches.
findings.recommended_action: Build the input-encoding arms from the exact gene lists produced by anndata_to_ranked_genes (stable sort, nonzero genes only). State that non-shared genes are seen by the model but not by the expression arms.

findings.description: Reproducibility gaps. The activations were extracted from .h5ad files that are not in the folder, so nothing can check that their cell and gene order matches data/*.npz (row_cell_ids assumes it does). The manifests do not record the model revision or commit, the tokenizer version, or the compute dtype (the --dtype default is bfloat16). No package versions are pinned. outputs/transfer_results.json is timestamped later than run_log.txt, although its contents match the reproduction.
findings.evidence: The manifest fields are only model, unit, layers, max_genes, prompt, store_dtype, n_cells, n_rows, d_model. The README lists 'numpy, scipy and scikit-learn' with no versions. File times: run_log.txt 07:53, transfer_results.json 10:56.
findings.recommended_action: Ship or checksum the .h5ad inputs, or a cell and gene order map. Record the model revision hash, tokenizer version and compute dtype in the manifest. Add requirements with pinned versions, and regenerate outputs in a single run.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key's status is 'clean' with error = null, so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule only warns that a finding saying the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only would be false. No finding makes that claim: F8 is about ties and dropped non-shared columns, not shared-set selection. The issues the review raises are graded against the key's other_real_issues (alpha sensitivity, bootstrap scope) and its possible_false_alarms.

findings.reason: This matches the key's other_real_issues entry that the parity verdict depends on the untuned alpha = 1000. The key's numbers agree with the finding: model - rank at alpha 1e4 is +0.0175 [+0.0074, +0.0274], and K562 5-fold CV picks alpha = 1e4. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm. It challenges the headline parity verdict.

I reran it. At alpha 1e3, presence-of-top-512 scores R_diff 0.809 against rank 0.792 and model 0.789. Paired bootstrap for model - presence: -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], P(>0) = 0. So an input-only encoding that carries strictly less information flips the verdict to 'loses', and the 0.029 'dropping values' cost depends on the encoding. The key lists the generic objection that linear ranks are arbitrary as a possible false alarm ('design choice'). This finding goes further and shows with data that the verdict and decomposition change, which is a real robustness problem. It is alpha-specific: at alpha 1e4, presence is 0.820 against model 0.821.

Verified. In the reverse direction (RPE1 -> K562, alpha 1e3): model 0.758, expr_full 0.770, rank 0.547. Presence (0.706) is also well below the model, and at alpha 1e4 the model is still ahead (0.812 vs rank 0.642 / presence 0.735). Parity holds in only one direction, yet the summary generalises in Conclusions 1 and 3. The caveats name one model/layer/readout but not the direction. This is partly a scope issue, but it is confirmed and undercuts the general claims.

This is in the key's other_real_issues (the bootstrap covers only target-cell sampling, and the ridge is not refit; the key calls it valid but minor). My quick two-level check (resample K562 cells, refit, resample RPE1; 8 reps) gave SD of about 0.035 for model - rank, consistent with the finding's 0.037. So the reported CI and the caveat's bounds are clearly too narrow. It widens the uncertainty but does not overturn the parity verdict itself.

The point that 'CI contains 0' with no equivalence margin is not a proof of equivalence is fair. But the SUMMARY caveat already says 'Parity is not proof of zero effect' and gives the CI bounds. The untested median-error difference is a small gap. Its force mostly comes from F4. This is wording and inference framing, not an error in the results.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm: the phase label comes from marker genes that are also expression features. The label is the same target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same genes, and nothing leaks from RPE1 into training. Recasting Conclusion 2's tokenizer loss as label circularity is not supported as an error.

Wording about 'through 21 layers', 'before the first layer' and 'information' versus linear decodability is somewhat loose. These are interpretive phrasing issues, and the substantive sensitivity points are already covered by F1, F2 and F3.

The key confirms that argpartition and the stable sort break ties differently, and that non-shared genes are dropped, but calls this not load-bearing. The exact-sentence baseline gives -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], the same verdict. The finding itself rates it minor and reports a negligible point-estimate effect (0.7905 vs 0.7916). The README wording is slightly overstated.

These are reproducibility hygiene points: no h5ad files, no model revision or dtype in the manifest, no pinned versions, and the output timestamp. The key states that data/ matches the source h5ad exactly, row_cell_ids is 0..2999, and the script reproduces the outputs byte for byte. Nothing here affects the results.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key marks B7392 as clean (status 'clean', error null), so there is no documented error to detect. None of the findings makes the key's false claim that the 512-gene baselines pick genes from the shared set only. F8 correctly says the non-shared genes are dropped after the full-panel selection. The findings that hold up are the key's listed other_real_issues: F1 (verdict depends on alpha) and F4 (bootstrap covers target cells only). F2 is an additional robustness problem that the data confirm.

findings.reason: This is the key's first other_real_issue: alpha is fixed at 1000 and not tuned, and the PARITY verdict depends on it. The finding's numbers match the key: at alpha 1e2, model - rank is about -0.008. At alpha 1e4 it is +0.0175 [+0.0075, +0.0274], against the key's [+0.0074, +0.0274]. K562-only 5-fold CV picks 1e4, where the model comes out ahead. The key says to grade this as a valid concern, neither a detection nor a false alarm. It challenges the headline verdict.

I reproduced it with the package protocol at alpha 1000. Binary top-512 presence scores R_diff 0.8091 and log-rank 0.8063, against rank 0.7916 and model 0.7894. Paired bootstrap (2,000 draws): model - presence = -0.0198 [-0.0301, -0.0091], P(>0) = 0. Model - log-rank = -0.017 [-0.028, -0.006]. Presence - rank = +0.0176 [+0.0073, +0.0279]. So an encoding with less information than the sentence gives 'MODEL LOSES' under the package's own rule. The 0.029 'dropping values' cost also depends on the encoding. The key lists 'linear rank values are arbitrary' as a possible false alarm and calls it a design choice. That rebuttal is about information content, and this finding concedes it. The finding instead shows that the headline verdict and Conclusion 2's split depend on the encoding. That is a genuine robustness problem, like the alpha issue the key accepts. A grader who reads the key's rebuttal strictly could call it disputed.

The numbers reproduce. Reverse RPE1 -> K562 at alpha 1000 gives model 0.7583, expr_full 0.7696, rank 0.5469, so there is no parity in that direction. But the reverse run is confounded by the panel asymmetry. RPE1 sentences contain about 68 non-shared genes per cell (key). Those genes are dropped from the rank features, so the rank ridge is trained on about 444 shared nonzero genes per cell and then applied to K562 cells that have 512. The rank arm's collapse may be a baseline artefact rather than evidence that the model adds information. The key treats one layer, one setup and so on as scope, not an error. The direction is not in the caveats, so the generalisation point has some merit, but I cannot settle what the reverse result means without deeper checks.

The key lists this as a valid (minor) other issue: the bootstrap resamples only RPE1 cells and the ridge is not refit on resampled K562 cells. I checked the size with 12 two-level reps: model - rank SD is about 0.036, close to the finding's 0.037. So the reported plus or minus 0.012 interval does understate uncertainty by about 3 times. A wider interval does not overturn the PARITY call. It only weakens it and corrects the caveat, so it is not load-bearing.

The verdict rule (CI contains 0 means parity) is stated plainly in the README. SUMMARY caveat 1 already says parity is not proof of zero effect and gives the gain and loss bounds. Caveat 2 already reports the median-error direction (23 vs 20 deg). The wording 'neither adds nor loses' in Conclusion 1 is somewhat overstated, and an equivalence margin would be nicer, but this is mainly a wording and rigor nicety, not a demonstrated error.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm. The phase label is built from marker genes that are also expression features, but it is the same target for every arm, the model's sentence contains the same genes, and there is no leak from RPE1 into training. The key also covers the separate per-line labels: they are oriented by marker biology, the S and G2/M peaks agree within 12 deg, and R_diff ignores rotation. Showing that marker-only expression predicts a marker-derived angle well is expected and does not invalidate the comparison. The finding uses this to attack Conclusion 2.

This is a wording critique. 'Through 21 layers' and 'before the first layer' are rhetorical descriptions of an input-encoding versus layer-21 comparison, and the SUMMARY caveats state the one-layer scope. The substantive parts (alpha and encoding dependence, non-rejection read as equality) are already covered by F1, F2 and F5. True, but it does not add a separate error.

The key lists this as a possible false alarm that is 'true in a small way, but not load-bearing'. argpartition breaks ties differently from the stable sort. The exact-sentence baseline gives model - baseline -0.0011 [-0.0132, +0.0111], against -0.0022, so the verdict is the same. The finding itself rates it minor and reports 0.7905 vs 0.7916, which is consistent with the key. Dropping the non-shared genes is unavoidable in a frozen cross-line readout. The finding correctly says selection is done on the full panel, so this is not the key's 'shared-set only' false claim.

The reproducibility gaps are real but trivial: no .h5ad files, no model revision or dtype in the manifests, no pinned versions, and a later timestamp on the JSON. The key confirms data/ matches the source h5ad exactly, row_cell_ids is 0..2999 in order, and the run reproduces the outputs byte for byte. Housekeeping only.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced the finding's numbers by running code inline. I imported transfer.py's own R_diff, med_err and top_k_encode, used the same StandardScaler, Ridge(alpha=1000), full-panel top-512 selection and seed-0 paired bootstrap, and wrote no files. The forward direction matches the package: model 0.789, expr_full 0.878, expr_512_rank 0.792, model minus rank -0.0022 [-0.0142, +0.0109]. Reversing it (fit on RPE1, apply to K562) gives model 0.758 (25 deg), expr_full 0.770 (23.8 deg), expr_512_mag 0.699 and expr_512_rank 0.547 (31.3 deg). Model minus rank is +0.211, 95% CI [+0.189, +0.234], so by the package's own rule the model adds information and there is no parity. Tuning does not explain this. Across alpha 100, 1000, 3000 and 10000 the reverse gap stays between +0.17 and +0.29: model 0.712/0.758/0.785/0.812 vs rank 0.423/0.547/0.602/0.642. Choosing the top 512 from shared genes only still leaves gaps of +0.13 to +0.20. With 5-fold CV inside one cell line at alpha 1000, the model also beats the rank encoding: RPE1 0.909 vs 0.848, K562 0.886 vs 0.819. The K562 -> RPE1 numbers themselves are correct. The problem is that SUMMARY.md states general conclusions that this evidence contradicts: Conclusion 1 says the model 'neither adds nor loses cell-cycle information', Conclusion 2 blames the loss on the tokenizer, and Conclusion 3 says that against the fair baseline 'C2S comes out even' and gives advice for SCFMs in general. In the reverse direction the input encoding loses 0.22 and the model gets most of it back. The caveat 'one model, one layer, one readout' does not mention transfer direction. The answer key's 'scope only' false alarm covers a bare 'only one layer' remark, not concrete evidence that reverses the verdict. The issue is similar to the key's valid concern that parity breaks under other alpha values: the parity claim holds only under these exact conditions, so it affects the stated conclusions.

review.summary: I re-ran the pipeline and it reproduces the reported numbers exactly: linear circ-R2 0.929 for expression and 0.894 for STATE, kNN 0.858 and 0.819. Cell alignment checks out. expression_controls.cell_idx equals select_controls(), the marker columns match markers.npz to 0.0, and the STATE cell_idx is 0..2999. The results are stable across 10 CV seeds (within about 0.002) and across probe sizes from 10 to 100 PCs. Fitting PCA inside each fold changes nothing (0.893). Shuffling phi gives -0.007. So the arithmetic and the headline value hold. The problems are in what the numbers are said to mean, and one structural confound. (1) The expression comparator contains the 87 marker genes that define phi. With those genes removed, expression scores 0.895, the same as STATE's 0.894 at every probe size. The "96% of expression" gap and "expression does at least as well" therefore come entirely from target leakage. (2) The claim that STATE "adds nothing beyond" expression was never tested. (3) phi is built on z-scores pooled across four cell lines. Line identity alone gives circ-R2 0.26, STATE separates the lines with 100% accuracy, and the within-line circ-R2 is lower: STATE 0.857, expression 0.903, K562 STATE 0.834. (4) STATE received log1p input, off its training distribution, from a pipeline that cannot be verified here. That limits the general claim and the practical recommendation. There are also smaller issues: the kNN comparison is weakened by whitening, the discrete phase calls are artifacts of centring, and two markers are lost to outdated gene symbols.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 23-25 (What it means #3); also line 5
findings.description: The summary says STATE's layer-11 vector 'keeps cell-cycle state, but adds nothing beyond it' and that 'STATE is like the expression it reads'. The analysis cannot support either statement. It only measures how well one target defined from expression (phi, built from marker genes) can be decoded. That tells us nothing about information STATE carries beyond expression, or how STATE organises it. There is also no null representation, such as a randomly initialised STATE or a random projection of the same input. Without one, 'STATE keeps it' cannot be told apart from what any function that preserves its input would show. The mechanistic sentence about protein-embedding tokens and mean pooling 'not washing out' the program was not tested either.
findings.evidence: decode_phase.py computes only circ_r2 of phi (cos/sin) from 20 PCs of each representation. No analysis compares information beyond phi, and no null or random-model baseline is run. SUMMARY line 23-24: 'adds nothing beyond it'.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the 'adds nothing beyond it' and 'STATE is like the expression' claims, or test them directly. For example, decode targets that are not defined from expression, or measure the variance in STATE left after regressing on expression. Add null baselines: a random-weight STATE model, or a random linear projection of the same log1p input.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 18-22 and 27 (claims #1, #2, #4); code/decode_phase.py lines 33-36, 101-103 (expression representation includes the marker genes)
findings.description: phi is a linear function of z-scored expression of 87 marker genes, and all 87 are columns of the expression representation. The expression 'reference' therefore partly decodes its own inputs. That makes claim #1 ('the loop is clearly in the input… almost perfectly') close to tautological. It also means the reported gap (0.929 vs 0.894, '96% of the expression value', 'expression does at least as well') comes from target leakage, not from STATE losing information. Once the marker genes are removed, expression and STATE are indistinguishable. A caveat says the probe 'favours expression', but the quantitative interpretation in the results is still built on the leaked comparator.
findings.evidence: I re-ran the same probe with the 87 marker columns dropped from expression. Linear circ-R2 for expression-minus-markers vs STATE: 0.278 vs 0.273 at DIM=2, 0.532 vs 0.506 at DIM=5, 0.885 vs 0.884 at DIM=10, 0.895 vs 0.894 at DIM=20, 0.892 vs 0.892 at DIM=50, 0.895 vs 0.892 at DIM=100. With markers included, expression gives 0.929 at DIM=20.
findings.recommended_action: Use expression without the phi-defining marker genes as the fair comparator, or define phi from markers held out of every representation. Report STATE as roughly equal to marker-free expression (about 0.89), and drop the '96%' ratio and the 'expression does at least as well' wording.

findings.location: code/cc_common.py lines 51-56 (select_controls pools all lines) and 70-110 (z-scoring and PCA of markers across pooled cells); SUMMARY.md lines 5-6 and 35
findings.description: phi is defined on marker z-scores pooled across four cell lines. Those lines differ systematically in baseline marker expression and in phase composition. Part of the 'phase' variance is therefore between-line variance. STATE (like expression) identifies the line perfectly, so the probe can earn credit just by recognising the line. The headline 0.894 and 0.929 are inflated relative to within-line phase decoding. The caveat only says the cells are pooled; it does not quantify or correct for this.
findings.evidence: Per-line circular mean of phi: HepG2 -18°, Jurkat +143°, K562 +87°, RPE1 -62°. Discrete phase mix differs by line, e.g. HepG2 50% G1 vs Jurkat 11% G1. A one-hot cell-line covariate alone predicts phi with circ-R2 0.260. A logistic regression on STATE's 20 PCs classifies line with 5-fold accuracy 1.000. If the pooled CV predictions are scored against a within-line baseline (each line's own circular mean), STATE drops to 0.857 and expression to 0.903. Scoring each line separately with the pooled phi: STATE 0.863, 0.849, 0.834, 0.883 and expression 0.929, 0.899, 0.875, 0.924 (HepG2, Jurkat, K562, RPE1).
findings.recommended_action: Define phi within each cell line (or regress line out of the markers first), evaluate decodability within line or with line-stratified folds, and report per-line results. Alternatively, restrict to a single line. State the headline as a within-line number.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 5, 26-27, 31-32; README.md lines 47-50; code/extraction/build_inputs.py lines 24-35
findings.description: STATE-SE was run on log1p(CP10k) values instead of the raw counts it expects. That puts it off its training distribution, which the authors acknowledge. Even so, the headline is stated as a property of 'STATE-SE layer 11' in general, and #4 recommends it for practical phase decoding and phase-aware comparisons. The caveat assumes the shift can only 'weaken the signal', but its effect could go in either direction, for example through how the model samples and weights genes. The extraction cannot be checked from this package: state_loader.py, the weights and the source data are all missing.
findings.evidence: build_inputs.py writes X = stored log1p(CP10k) floats into the h5ad given to extract_state.py. expm1 row sums of the stored values are 7,447-9,573, so these are not counts. extract_state.py imports state_loader, which is not included.
findings.recommended_action: Limit the claims to 'STATE-SE run on log1p(CP10k) input'. Remove or qualify the practical recommendation in #4. If possible, repeat the extraction on a dataset with raw counts, or check whether the inference pipeline applies its own log transform (double-logging).

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 21-22; code/cc_common.py lines 114-120 (prep whitens before kNN); code/decode_phase.py line 51
findings.description: The inference 'the kNN probe does no better than the linear one, so a linear read-out already captures it' rests on a handicapped kNN. kNN runs on whitened PCs, which give low-variance noise components the same weight as signal components. kNN also scores below linear for expression, where phi is by construction close to a linear function of the input. So the comparison says little about whether the phase is stored nonlinearly.
findings.evidence: STATE kNN (k=15) on the same 20 PCs without whitening: 0.869, vs 0.819 with whitening. The linear probe gives 0.894.
findings.recommended_action: Use a tuned nonlinear probe (unwhitened kNN with k chosen in an inner CV, a kernel ridge or a small MLP) before drawing conclusions about linearity, or drop the sentence.

findings.location: code/decode_phase.py lines 33-36, 101-103 vs README.md line 25 (G1 rule); outputs/decodability.json phase_counts; code/cc_common.py lines 107-108
findings.description: G1 is called when both mean z-scores are below 0, and the z-scores are centred on this pooled sample. The G1 fraction is therefore set by the centring, not by biology. Only 25% of cells are called G1, with 40% in S and 35% in G2M. For these proliferating lines that split is implausible. The calls are reported as 'phase counts' and are used to orient and rotate phi.
findings.evidence: Phase counts: G1 747, S 1208, G2M 1045. The scores are means of z-scores that are zero-centred by construction (cc_common.py lines 70-76).
findings.recommended_action: Score against background gene sets (Seurat-style control genes) or a calibrated threshold. Report the discrete counts only as orientation aids, not as phase proportions.

findings.description: The Tirosh marker lists use outdated gene symbols. Two markers whose current names are in the gene list are therefore dropped: MLF1IP (now CENPU) and HN1 (now JPT1). The README's '37 and 50 of them are in the gene list' undercounts what is available, and phi is built from fewer markers than possible.
findings.evidence: Missing from expression genes: S = MLF1IP, WDR76, CCNE2, MSH2, EXO1, E2F8; G2M = UBE2C, FAM64A, HN1, GAS2L3. CENPU and JPT1 are present in expression_controls.npz genes.
findings.recommended_action: Map the marker symbols to current HGNC names (e.g. use Seurat's cc.genes.updated.2019) before matching.

findings.description: The README says the cell vector is the mean over non-CLS positions of expressed genes. In the code, the expressed-gene mask is applied only when batch[7] is not None; otherwise every non-CLS position is averaged. The hook is on transformer_encoder.layers[11], which is the 12th of 16 layers in 0-based indexing, so 'layer 11 of 16' is ambiguous. Neither point can be checked from the package.
findings.evidence: extract_state.py lines 59 and 65-66: 'counts = batch[7] ... if batch[7] is not None else None'; 'if counts is not None: valid &= (counts[i, :T] > 0)'.
findings.recommended_action: Log whether the expression mask was applied and how many positions were pooled per cell. State the layer as 0-based (12th of 16) or rename it.

grade_a.detection_reason: The key marks B8045 as clean ("error": null), so there is no documented error to detect. Rerunning the package confirmed its numbers: expression 0.929 / kNN 0.858, STATE 0.894 / kNN 0.819, and the STATE cell_idx is correctly mapped through select_controls() (the rows match). Several findings repeat the key's listed false alarms: marker leakage into the expression comparator (F2), pooling of cell lines (F3) and log1p input (F4). The rest are wording overreach or minor details.

findings.reason: F1 says claim #3 ('adds nothing beyond it', 'STATE is like the expression it reads') is unsupported. In context the claim is a conservative one about cell-cycle readout, and it fits the data: STATE 0.894 is below expression 0.929. The key lists 'SUMMARY says STATE adds nothing beyond expression' as an appropriate, non-overstating statement. The sentence about mean pooling not washing out the program is directly supported, because the pooled embedding does decode phase at 0.894. A random-weight baseline would not make the literal claim that STATE keeps the phase false. At most this is wording overreach, not a load-bearing error.

The reviewer's numbers reproduce exactly: with the 87 markers dropped, expression scores 0.895 vs STATE 0.894 at DIM=20, and the other dims match too. But the key lists this exact claim as a false alarm: it is a stated caveat and design choice, and SUMMARY calls expression an upper reference that the probe favours. The marker-free rerun actually supports the summary. 'Expression does at least as well' still holds (0.895 >= 0.894), and the loop is still clearly in the input without the markers. The recommendation to drop that wording is therefore wrong.

The reviewer's numbers reproduce: per-line circular means of -18/143/87/-62 deg, and pooled-phi per-line STATE 0.863/0.849/0.834/0.883. But the key lists 'pooling makes phase a cell-line label' as a false alarm. When phase is re-scored within each line (the reviewer's own proposed fix), STATE gets 0.938/0.906/0.859/0.930 and expression 0.943/0.934/0.914/0.950, so the headline is not inflated by between-line variance. Pooling is a stated caveat in the SUMMARY.

The key explicitly says the log1p (non-count) input is a stated caveat, not a load-bearing error. SUMMARY lines 31-32 and README lines 49-50 disclose it. The reviewer's description of the caveat as assuming the shift can 'only' weaken the signal misreads the text, which says 'could weaken'. The extraction scripts being non-runnable is by design, per the key.

Verified: unwhitened kNN on STATE gives 0.869, vs 0.819 whitened. So whitening does handicap kNN, and the reported kNN numbers understate it. But 0.869 is still below the linear 0.894, so the summary's statement that kNN does no better than linear still holds. True but trivial.

It is true by construction that the G1 call depends on the pooled zero-centring. However, the key says the phase recipe is the intended design, implemented correctly, and the discrete calls are used only to orient and rotate phi. The claim that a 25% G1 share is 'implausible' is speculative. This does not affect the circ-R2 results.

Verified: CENPU and JPT1 are in the gene list, while MLF1IP and HN1 are not, so updated symbols would add 2 markers. FAM64A/PIMREG is absent either way. This is a genuine but trivial point: 2 of about 89 markers would not materially change phi or the results. The key treats 37/43 and 50/54 as the intended design.

The conditional expressed-gene mask and the 0-based layers[11] indexing are reference-only extraction details. The key lists mean pooling and layer choice as design choices, and the extraction scripts are not runnable by design. A documentation-clarity nit only.

grade_b.detection_reason: The key marks B8045 as clean ("error": null), so there is no documented error to detect. Its detection rule says any finding that claims a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless running code on the package confirms it. I ran inline checks and confirmed the reviewer's numbers: marker-free expression gives 0.895 vs STATE 0.894 at 20 PCs; unwhitened kNN gives STATE 0.869 and expression 0.912; the per-line circular means are -18, +143, +87 and -62 degrees; CENPU and JPT1 are in the gene list. None of these shows that a headline result is wrong.
