review.summary: I reviewed the analysis at <CODE_ROOT>/analysis-tasks/B8833. geometry.py is computed correctly: rerunning shape_stats on the three .npz files gives exactly the values in outputs/. The cell rows line up across models (cell_idx, pseudotime and labels match, and the state cluster codes map alphabetically). The order scGPT > Geneformer > STATE also holds in all 10 halves, including norm CV. The problems are with what the numbers mean and with how the embeddings were made. (1) In every model PC1 is a sequencing-depth axis. On the 200 cells with counts, PC1 correlates with log total UMI at r = 0.95 (scGPT), 0.91 (Geneformer) and 0.98 (STATE). Depth plus gene count explains 70% of scGPT's embedding variance and 58% of Geneformer's. PC1 carries no cell-type information (kNN accuracy 0.17 and 0.09, against a chance level of 0.19). So "cells lie close to one axis" describes library size, not the cell manifold. (2) scGPT was given raw UMI counts instead of the 51-bin values its checkpoint was trained on. This puts depth directly into the input and makes the scGPT embeddings non-standard. (3) Geneformer was tokenized non-canonically: log1p is applied before dividing by the gene medians, and the context is cut to 2048. (4) STATE's d90 of 775 depends on sample size: it is 289 at 500 cells, 645 at 2,134 and 775 at 4,269. It also falls outside the halves range (644-650), which the summary leaves out when it says the halves "agree closely". (5) More than half of STATE's variance lies in PCs beyond 100, which carry no cell-type signal. This fits stochastic, unseeded noise from cell-sentence sampling, not a diffuse manifold. (6) Norm CV is computed on uncentred embeddings, although the README says all measures are mean-centred. It mostly reflects how large the shared mean offset is. A centred version reverses the order, so "compact on all four measures" partly rests on an offset artefact. Smaller issues: claim 4 overstates what the halves test, and norm CV halves are not computed. The layer, token-count and pooling choices differ between models. Weights are loaded with strict=False and nothing checks for missing keys. The extraction scripts silently reuse old outputs when resuming. The width caveat holds for PR: projecting STATE to 512 dimensions still gives PR 51.7.

findings.description: The dominant axis that makes scGPT and Geneformer look 'compact' is sequencing depth (library size and number of detected genes), not cell biology. PR, PC1 share and d90 therefore mostly measure how strongly each model encodes depth. They do not measure how compact the cell manifold is. 'Its gut cells lie close to one axis' and 'one dominant direction' describe a technical axis.
findings.evidence: Using the 200 cells in data/raw/gut_epithelium_first200.h5ad (rows 0-199 of each .npz, alignment confirmed), PC1 scores correlate with log total UMI at r = 0.951 (scGPT), 0.914 (Geneformer) and 0.977 (STATE), and with the number of detected genes at r = 0.87, 0.88 and 0.97. Linear regression on log depth and log n_genes explains 70.2% of scGPT's embedding variance and 58.4% of Geneformer's (STATE: 12.4%). After regressing depth out, PR rises from 1.69 to 2.72 (scGPT), 2.71 to 6.73 (Geneformer) and 47.5 to 84.5 (STATE), and scGPT's PC1 share falls from 0.76 to 0.57. In the full 4,269 cells, PC1 carries no cell-type information. Cell-type eta^2 on PC1 is 0.089, 0.056 and 0.058. 10-NN cell-type accuracy on PC1 alone is 0.165 for scGPT and 0.085 for Geneformer, against a majority-class rate of 0.187. scGPT's cell-type structure sits in PCs 3-512, which hold only 7% of the variance (kNN 0.56-0.67). Between-cell-type variance is only 4-7% of the total in every model.
findings.recommended_action: Do not describe the dominant PC as the cell manifold. Report how much of each model's variance is explained by depth and n_genes. Recompute the measures after regressing out log total counts and log n_genes, or on depth-matched or downsampled cells. Add a biology-anchored measure, such as between-type variance fraction or kNN label agreement. Reword Conclusions 1-3 accordingly.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py lines 54-70 (tokenize: raw counts used as values), line 77-80 (no <cls>), models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json (input_style: binned, n_bins: 51)
findings.description: scGPT whole-human was pretrained on per-cell quantile-binned expression (input_style 'binned', n_bins 51, values 1-50). The extraction feeds raw UMI counts as the continuous values. These are out of distribution and are clipped at 512 by scGPT's ContinuousValueEncoder. Raw counts scale directly with sequencing depth, which plausibly produces scGPT's extreme depth-driven PC1 (see F1) and its 'most compact' result. Genes are also ordered by raw count and cut to the top 1,200, and no <cls> token is prepended, unlike scGPT's standard tokenization. The scGPT embeddings therefore do not represent the frozen model under its intended input, and the headline claim about scGPT cannot stand as stated.
findings.evidence: args.json: "input_style": "binned", "n_bins": 51, "max_seq_len": 1200. extract_scgpt.py line 60 appends expr[idx] (raw counts from sparse_row) as the value, with no normalisation or binning anywhere. On the 200 example cells, the maximum raw input value has a median of 418 and reaches 4,874. A median of 5.9% of the kept values per cell exceed the maximum bin of 50. 197/200 cells are truncated to exactly 1,200 tokens. scGPT PC1 correlates with log depth at r = 0.95, and depth explains 70% of its variance.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract scGPT embeddings with the documented preprocessing: normalise total counts, log1p, bin each cell into 51 bins, prepend <cls> with pad value, and use scGPT's own tokenize_and_pad_batch or embed_data. Then recompute all geometry statistics and check whether the scGPT ranking survives.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_geneformer.py line 129 (np.log1p(expr / rs * 1e4)), lines 54-58 (divide by median, rank), line 27 (MAX_SEQ_LEN = 2048)
findings.description: Geneformer's rank-value encoding is computed on counts/total*1e4 divided by the gene's corpus median, with no log. Here log1p is applied first and the log value is then divided by the median, which is on the non-log scale. log1p is monotonic per gene, but dividing log values by medians from a different scale changes the order across genes. The token sequences therefore differ from Geneformer's canonical input. The context is also cut to 2,048 tokens, although Geneformer V2-316M has max_position_embeddings 4,096. The Geneformer embeddings are non-canonical and their geometry, including the 'second place' result, is not that of the model under its intended input.
findings.evidence: Line 129 calls tokenize(np.log1p(expr / rs * 1e4), ...), and line 56 computes norm = e_nz / m_nz. Example: a gene with normalised value 100 and median 10 scores 10 canonically but log1p(100)/10 = 0.46 here, while a gene with value 5 and median 1 scores 5 versus 1.79. The order flips. models/geneformer_v2_316m/config.json gives max_position_embeddings 4096, and cells have up to 8,557 detected genes.
findings.recommended_action: Tokenize with Geneformer's TranscriptomeTokenizer, or replicate it exactly: normalise to 1e4, divide by the median, no log, and use a 4,096-token context for V2. Then re-extract and recompute.

It also keeps growing with the number of cells. The summary quotes d90 = 775 as a fact ('775 PCs for 90% of the variance'). Its statement that 'the random halves agree closely' lists PR and PC1 share but leaves out the d90 halves, which contradict it. d90 also depends on width: projecting STATE to 512 dimensions drops it to 328.

Rerunning shape_stats on random subsets of STATE gives d90 = 289 (n=500), 457 (n=1,000), 645 (n=2,134), 716 (n=3,000) and 775 (n=4,269). PR and PC1 share are stable over the same subsets. A random orthogonal projection of STATE to 512 dimensions gives d90 = 328 and PR = 51.7.

Note that d90 does not converge with sample size, or replace it with a size-stable measure such as PR, or d90 after denoising or a Marchenko-Pastur noise cut. Compare d90 only at matched width and sample size.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 30-31 (Conclusion 3); code/extraction/extract_state.py lines 72-74 and 103-122 (stochastic STATE cell-sentence dataloader, no seed)
findings.description: Most of STATE's 'diffuseness' sits in directions that carry no cell-type information. This fits noise, plausibly from STATE's random sampling of genes when it builds cell sentences: no seed is set, so embeddings are not reproducible and each cell gets one random draw. Such noise would raise PR and d90 without the cell manifold being more diffuse. 'STATE is by far the most diffuse' therefore cannot be read as a property of its cell geometry until the noise is measured.
findings.evidence: STATE's PCs beyond 100 hold 52% of the variance, and PCs beyond 200 hold 41%. 10-NN cell-type accuracy is 0.834 on PCs 1-20 but 0.204 on PCs 100-300, 0.181 on PCs 300-800 and 0.170 on PCs 800-2048, at or below the chance rate of 0.187. extract_state.py sets no torch or numpy seed before create_dataloader or inference. d90 grows with n (F4), which is typical of a heavy noise-like tail.
findings.recommended_action: Extract STATE twice, or with several seeds, and measure test-retest variance per cell. Average embeddings over repeated sentence draws, or use deterministic sentence construction. Report PR and d90 after removing the noise floor. Set and record seeds.

findings.location: code/geometry.py line 43 (norms of uncentred X); README.md line 15; SUMMARY.md lines 25-27
findings.description: README says all four measures use the mean-centred covariance spectrum, but norm CV is computed on uncentred embeddings. It is therefore set mostly by the size of the shared mean vector relative to the spread between cells. That offset differs by architecture and LayerNorm placement and has nothing to do with manifold compactness. 'Per-cell norms are almost constant, so cells differ by direction, not by size' reflects the large common offset. 'Most compact on all four measures' relies partly on this offset-driven measure. A centred analogue gives the opposite order.
findings.evidence: The ratio of the mean vector's norm to the mean per-cell norm is 0.977 (scGPT), 0.966 (Geneformer) and 0.748 (STATE). RMS distance to the centroid divided by the mean-vector norm is 0.22, 0.27 and 0.89. The CV of each cell's distance to the centroid is 0.51 (scGPT), 0.36 (Geneformer) and 0.13 (STATE), the reverse of the norm-CV order (0.0031 < 0.0186 < 0.0284).
findings.recommended_action: Correct the README description. Either drop norm CV as a compactness measure or compute a centred version, and explain that the uncentred CV mainly reflects the mean offset. Remove 'on all four measures' and the 'direction, not size' interpretation unless they are supported by a centred analysis.

findings.description: The code computes half-sample stability only for PR, PC1 share and d90, not for norm CV, so the outputs do not support 'same on every measure and in every random half'. verdicts.reason:
The finding's numbers check out, and they bear on how Conclusion 3 is worded. The mechanism it proposes is plausible but could not be tested inside the package. The STATE-last ranking survives.

Checks run on data/embeddings/*.npz with inline numpy:

1. **Variance in STATE's tail.** PCs beyond 100 hold 52.0% of STATE's variance, and PCs beyond 200 hold 40.9%. For Geneformer the figure beyond PC100 is 4.4%; for scGPT it is 0.1%.

2. **Cell-type information by PC band.** 10-NN cell-type accuracy (leave-one-out) is:
   - PCs 1-20: 0.833
   - PCs 20-100: 0.319
   - PCs 100-300: 0.189
   - PCs 300-800: 0.180
   - PCs 800-2048: 0.185
   The majority-class rate is 0.187.

3. **The tail is specific to each cell.** I predicted each cell's tail coordinates from the mean of its 10 nearest neighbours. Neighbours were taken from STATE PCs 1-20 or from Geneformer PCs 1-50. For STATE PCs 100-2048, R2 is -0.08 to -0.10, which is the same as using random neighbours (-0.10). For comparison, Geneformer PCs 20-100 reach R2 0.41.

4. **The tail looks like noise.** In the 200 shipped raw cells, the size of a cell's STATE tail (norm on PCs beyond 100) tracks inverse depth: Spearman rho -0.94 with total counts and -0.90 with detected genes. The size of the head (PCs 1-20) does not (rho about 0).

5. **No seed is set.** extract_state.py sets no seed anywhere; grep finds no seed call. As far as I know, arc-state's sentence collator breaks expression ties at random with torch.randperm, but I could not confirm this here: arc-state and the STATE weights are not installed. In the 200 cells, the slot-2047 cutoff falls at count 1-5, and median about 35% of the 2,047 slots are filled from a pool of about 1,771 tied genes. So run-to-run differences are plausible. Their size cannot be measured without the weights. The answer key reports re-extraction checks for scGPT and Geneformer but none for STATE.

6. **Effect on the claims.** If the cell-specific tail is removed, STATE's numbers change a lot. Geneformer's barely move.
   - STATE as reported: PR 56.5, PC1 0.113, d90 775.
   - STATE, top 20 PCs only: PR 6.78, PC1 0.332, d90 14.
   - STATE, each cell averaged with its 15 nearest neighbours: PR 6.86, PC1 0.339, d90 50.
   - Geneformer, same two treatments: PR 2.21 / 2.10, PC1 0.64 / 0.66.
   - scGPT: about 1.8 under every version.

   So STATE is still the least compact, and Conclusions 3 and 4 keep their ranking. But the headline figures (PR 56, d90 775, 'no direction holds more than about 11%') and the caveat's '30-fold PR gap' come mostly from cell-specific variance that holds no cell-type information, possibly sampling noise. Read as the geometry of the cell manifold, the gap is roughly 3-fold, not 30-fold.

**Severity.** The issue affects the magnitude and interpretation claims, not the model order. It is not the key's documented error, which is scGPT being fed unbinned raw counts. The key treats the STATE numbers as computed correctly, and that is true: the problem is what they are taken to mean.

review.summary:
I re-ran geometry.py's statistics, and they reproduce the reported table exactly: PR 1.82/2.73/56.48, PC1 share 0.724/0.576/0.113, d90 3/20/775, norm CV 0.0031/0.0186/0.0284. Cell order, labels and pseudotime match across the three files. The arithmetic is right, but the summary's interpretation does not hold up.

(1) scGPT was given raw UMI counts as input values. Its checkpoint (args.json) was trained on values binned into 51 levels within each cell, so the scGPT embeddings are out of distribution.

(2) In every model the dominant PC is a sequencing-depth axis, not a biological one. In the 200 cells that have counts in the package, log library size and gene count explain 70% (scGPT) and 58% (Geneformer) of embedding variance, against 1-3% for cell type. PC1 alone predicts cell type no better than chance. So "cells lie close to one axis" describes depth.

(3) Norm CV is computed on uncentred vectors, so it mostly measures the mean offset. A centred version reverses the model order, which undercuts "on all four measures".

(4) STATE's d90 of 775 grows steadily with the number of cells and lies outside its own random-half range (644-650). The summary leaves that range out while saying the halves "agree closely".

(5) Geneformer's tokenization differs from the model's standard: it log-transforms before dividing by gene medians and caps input at 2,046 genes (the model takes 4,096).

The model order may survive a depth correction (it does on the 200 cells), but the size of each gap and what "compact cell manifold" means both need to be redone.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py lines 54-70 (tokenize: val = expr[idx]; no <cls>); models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json (input_style 'binned', n_bins 51)
findings.description: scGPT receives raw UMI counts as expression values. The whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on values binned within each cell (51 bins, 0-50), which by design do not depend on depth. scGPT's standard embedding pipeline also adds a <cls> token, which is missing here. The scGPT embeddings are therefore out of distribution and carry library size directly. scGPT's 'most compact' numbers (PR 1.82, PC1 72%, d90 3) rest on these embeddings.
findings.evidence: In the 200-cell h5ad, raw counts go up to 4,874; the median per-cell maximum is 417.5, compared with bin indices of 0-50. 197 of 200 cells have the full 1,200 tokens, so sequence length is constant. Among those 197 cells, scGPT PC1 still correlates r=0.947 with log library size and r=0.905 with the mean log raw value of the input tokens. Depth therefore enters through the raw values. On those cells, depth (log library size, log gene count) explains 70% of scGPT embedding variance.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract scGPT with its standard preprocessing: per-cell binning into n_bins=51, <cls> prepended, pad_value -2, as in scgpt.tasks.embed_data / DataCollator(do_binning=True). Then rerun geometry.py and revise every scGPT claim.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 25-31 (conclusions 1-3); code/geometry.py lines 40-50 (no technical-covariate control)
findings.description: The dominant direction in all three embeddings is sequencing depth (library size / genes detected), not cell identity. 'Compactness' here mostly measures how strongly each model encodes depth. The claims that 'its gut cells lie close to one axis', 'one dominant direction' and 'cell manifold' compactness cannot be read as biological geometry. Depth is unrelated to cell type in these cells (R² = 0.004), so it is technical variation.
findings.evidence: First 200 cells (the only ones with counts): PC1 correlates with log library size at r = 0.951 (scGPT), 0.914 (Geneformer) and 0.977 (STATE). Depth explains this share of embedding variance: 70.2%, 58.4% and 12.4%; cell type explains 1.1%, 2.9% and 6.8%. On all 4,269 cells, 10-NN cell-type accuracy from PC1 alone is 0.165 / 0.085 / 0.160. That is at or below the majority-class rate (0.187); PCs 2-50 give 0.57 / 0.56 / 0.86. After regressing out depth on the 200 cells, scGPT PC1 falls from 0.757 to 0.574, PR rises from 1.69 to 2.72 and d90 from 3 to 7. Geneformer PR rises from 2.71 to 6.73 and d90 from 16 to 53. STATE PR rises from 47.5 to 84.5.
findings.recommended_action: Compute library size and gene count for all 4,269 cells from the full matrix. Report their correlation with each PC, and recompute the four measures after regressing them out (or on depth-matched cells). Rewrite conclusions 1-2 so that PC1 is identified as a depth axis, not a cell-manifold axis.

findings.location: code/geometry.py lines 43 and 49 (norms of uncentred X); README.md line 15; SUMMARY.md lines 25-27 and 32
findings.description: Norm CV is computed on uncentred embeddings, so it mostly reflects the large constant offset of each model's residual stream (post-LayerNorm bias and mean), not the spread of the cloud. This contradicts the README's statement that all four measures use the mean-centred covariance spectrum. A centred version of the same idea reverses the model order, so 'most compact on all four measures' and 'cells differ by direction, not by size' depend on this offset artifact.
findings.evidence: scGPT: the mean vector's norm is 21.15 against a mean per-cell norm of 21.65. The offset dominates, and two dimensions have means of -12.9 and -12.5. The CV of distance to the centroid is 0.510 (scGPT), 0.356 (Geneformer) and 0.132 (STATE), the reverse of the uncentred norm CV (0.0031 / 0.0186 / 0.0284). The RMS spread relative to the offset is 0.22 / 0.27 / 0.89.
findings.recommended_action: Drop uncentred norm CV as a compactness measure, or replace it with a centred radial-spread statistic and report that. Fix the README description, and remove 'on all four measures' unless it still holds.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 18, 20-21, 30; outputs/run_log.txt (d90 halves 644-650); code/geometry.py line 47

The summary reports half ranges only for PR and PC1, omits the d90 ranges that run_log.txt contains, and says the halves 'agree closely'. Conclusion 3 then cites 775 PCs as an intrinsic property. The long tail looks noise-like, possibly from extraction noise such as STATE's stochastic gene-sentence sampling.

findings.description: Geneformer's input differs from the model's documented tokenization. Expression is log1p-transformed before dividing by gene medians; Geneformer ranks normalized counts divided by the median, with no log, and the medians were computed on non-log values. Since log1p is nonlinear and medians vary by gene, this changes the gene ranking. Input is also capped at 2,048 tokens, although V2-316M accepts 4,096. Both changes alter the gene set and order for most cells.
findings.evidence: tokenize() is called on np.log1p(expr/rs*1e4) and then divides by the medians. MAX_SEQ_LEN is 2048, while the config gives max_position_embeddings 4096. In the 200 available cells, 92.5% have more than 2,046 expressed genes, so they are truncated, while only 36.5% would exceed the native 4,094.
findings.recommended_action: Tokenize with Geneformer's own TranscriptomeTokenizer settings for V2 (no log, median scaling of normalized counts, model_input_size 4096). Re-extract and rerun.

Depth explains 70% (scGPT), 58% (Geneformer) and 12% (STATE) of the embedding variance. Cell type explains only 4–7% of the variance. So "scGPT has the most compact cell manifold" mostly measures how strongly each model encodes library size. (2) scGPT was given raw UMI counts as input values. Its checkpoint was trained on binned values (args.json: input_style "binned", n_bins 51), so the headline model's embeddings come from input it never saw in training. Model weights are loaded with strict=False and missing keys are never checked. STATE extraction sets no random seed. The conclusions are worded as general model properties even though the layer-11 comparison is not like-for-like across models.

Log depth plus log gene count explain 70% (scGPT), 58% (Geneformer) and 12% (STATE) of embedding variance, while cell type explains only 4-7%. So "cells lie close to one axis" describes a technical axis. Regressing out depth makes scGPT's PR 1.69->2.72 and PC1 share 0.76->0.57, and Geneformer's PR 2.71->6.73 and d90 16->53. The ranking survives this 200-cell check, but the magnitudes and the "cell manifold" reading do not.

(3) STATE's d90 = 775 depends on sample size and width:
- it is 289, 457, 645, 716 and 775 at n = 500, 1000, 2134, 3000 and 4269;
- it is about 290 after random projection to 512 dimensions;
- the d90 range across the halves (644-650), which the summary leaves out, does not include 775.

Also, only 55 STATE eigenvalues exceed a column-permutation null.

(4) Norm CV is computed on uncentred vectors, which contradicts the README. It is dominated by the shared mean offset (and probably by the post-LayerNorm outputs of scGPT and Geneformer). Measured relative to the centred spread, its order changes. So "same order on every measure" and "cells differ by direction, not by size" are not supported.

(5) Geneformer's tokenisation departs from the standard pipeline: it applies log1p before median scaling and truncates to 2046 tokens, though the model accepts 4096 and 185/200 cells exceed that.

(6) Other problems: a single layer is compared at different relative depths (acknowledged, but the conclusions are not limited accordingly); there is no chance or simple baseline; "not a sampling effect" is overstated, since only cell-level halves of the same dataset were tested; the norm-CV half-sample claim is not in the outputs; and there are several minor reproducibility gaps.

Checklist verdicts:
- P1 present, unaddressed
- P2 present, unaddressed
- P3 present, partly acknowledged (layer / mean-pool vs CLS)
- P4 present (cell-level halves only)
- P5 present (depth confound not residualised; different truncation per model; 800-per-type cap)
- P6 not applicable (no null finding)
- P7 present, acknowledged (one tissue, one layer)
- P8 present for d90 and norm CV, fine for PR and PC1
- P9 present ("cell manifold", "not a sampling effect", "differ by direction, not by size")
- P10 minor (extraction not runnable, resume logic without provenance, no pinned environment)

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py lines 54-70 (tokenize: val = raw counts, line 60) and 113-117 (values fed to model._encode); models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json lines 10-12; SUMMARY.md lines 16, 25-27
findings.description: scGPT receives raw UMI counts as the continuous 'values' input, but the whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on per-cell binned values (input_style 'binned', n_bins 51, i.e. values 0-50). The value channel therefore runs out of its training distribution and scales directly with sequencing depth. The scGPT row of the results (PR 1.82, PC1 72.4%, d90 3, norm CV 0.003) and the headline 'scGPT has the most compact cell manifold' describe the model on malformed input, not scGPT as used in practice.
findings.evidence: args.json: "input_style": "binned", "input_emb_style": "continuous", "n_bins": 51. No normalisation or binning appears anywhere in extract_scgpt.py. In the 200-cell raw file, the values actually fed in (top 1200 in-vocabulary genes per cell) have median 3, but 5.5% exceed 50 (the largest trained bin), the per-cell maximum has median 417.5, and 0.24% exceed 512 (scGPT's encoder clamp). scGPT PC1 has Spearman rho 0.97 with total UMI counts over those 200 cells, and log depth plus log gene count explain 70% of scGPT embedding variance.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract scGPT using its own preprocessing: normalize_total + log1p, then per-cell binning into 51 bins, as in pretraining. Recompute all four measures and the ranking. Until then, drop or explicitly qualify the scGPT row and conclusion 1.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 25-31 (conclusions 1-3) and lines 16-18; code/geometry.py lines 40-50 (no covariate adjustment)
findings.description: In all three models the dominant direction is a library-size / gene-count axis, not cell biology. 'Compactness' (high PC1 share, low PR and d90) mostly measures how strongly each embedding encodes sequencing depth. The conclusions read PC1 as the shape of the gut-cell manifold ('gut cells lie close to one axis', 'one dominant direction'). That reading cannot stand. The reported magnitudes are driven by a technical confound that was never controlled.
findings.evidence: First 200 cells, which have raw counts: Spearman rho between PC1 and total counts is 0.97 for scGPT, Geneformer and STATE alike. Rho between PC1 and number of genes detected is 0.89, 0.99 and 0.97. Log depth plus log number of genes explain 70% (scGPT), 58% (Geneformer) and 12% (STATE) of embedding variance. After regressing these out (200 cells), PR goes 1.69->2.72 for scGPT, 2.71->6.73 for Geneformer and 47.5->84.5 for STATE. PC1 share goes 0.757->0.574 (scGPT) and 0.578->0.340 (Geneformer). d90 goes 3->7 (scGPT) and 16->53 (Geneformer). On all 4269 cells, cell type explains only 7.1% / 4.4% / 6.6% of total variance and 8.9% / 5.6% / 5.8% of PC1. The model order survives residualisation in this 200-cell check.
findings.recommended_action: Regress out log total counts and log number of genes (and any batch or donor covariates) on all 4269 cells using the full count matrix, then recompute PR, PC1 share, d90 and norm CV. Report raw and residualised values side by side. State in the summary what PC1 is (a depth axis), and describe compactness as a mix of technical and biological variance unless the residualised analysis shows otherwise.

findings.description: d90 is not a stable property of the STATE embedding. It grows steadily with the number of cells and depends heavily on width. The headline '775 PCs for 90% of the variance' is therefore a sample-size artefact. The summary's stability paragraph reports the half-sample ranges for PR and PC1 only. It omits the d90 halves (644-650), which do not include the full-sample 775, while still claiming 'the random halves agree closely'. Most of the variance behind STATE's large d90 sits at noise level.
findings.evidence: STATE d90 by subsample size: 289 (n=500), 457 (1000), 645 (2134), 716 (3000), 775 (4269). PR is stable by comparison (52.4-56.5). The halves in geometry.json/run_log show d90 644-650 against 775 for the full set. A bootstrap 95% interval for d90 (30 resamples) is 660-667, which also excludes 775. A random Gaussian projection of STATE to 512 dimensions gives d90 of about 290 (3 seeds), against 775 at the native 2048 dimensions. Only 55 STATE eigenvalues exceed the top eigenvalue of a column-permutation null, and they carry 42% of variance; the other 58% lies in a noise-level bulk. For scGPT and Geneformer, d90 is stable (3-3 and 18-20).
findings.recommended_action: Report the d90 half-sample range alongside PR and PC1 in the summary. Show d90 as a function of n, or replace it with a sample-size-robust statistic (e.g. PR, or the number of eigenvalues above a matched null). Drop the '775 PCs' number from the conclusions, or restate it as 'not converged; increases with n'. Evaluate width effects with width-matched projections for d90 as well as PR.

findings.location: code/geometry.py lines 43 and 49; README.md line 15; SUMMARY.md lines 25-27 and 32-33
findings.description: Norm CV is computed on uncentred embeddings, contradicting README line 15 ('All four use the full covariance spectrum of the mean-centred embeddings'). It does not measure how compact the cloud's shape is. It mostly reflects the size of the shared mean offset relative to the spread, plus the LayerNorm at the output of post-LN layers (scGPT nn.TransformerEncoderLayer, Geneformer BERT). Adding a constant vector to every cell would lower it without changing the cloud at all. The claims 'on all four measures' and 'same order on every measure', and the interpretation 'cells differ by direction, not by size', rest on this statistic. In addition, the other three measures are all functions of one eigenvalue spectrum, so the 'four measures agree' framing overstates independent support.
findings.evidence: scGPT: norm of the mean vector = 21.1 against an RMS centred spread of 4.6. Two coordinates carry 72% of the squared mean norm (mean values 12.9 and 12.5). Mean pairwise cosine similarity is 0.952 (scGPT), 0.935 (Geneformer) and 0.561 (STATE), so scGPT cells all point in almost the same direction. sd(norm) divided by RMS centred spread is 0.014 (scGPT), 0.072 (Geneformer) and 0.043 (STATE), which orders the models scGPT > STATE > Geneformer, not scGPT > Geneformer > STATE. The CV of centred norms fully reverses the order (0.51 / 0.36 / 0.13). Dropping the 5 highest-variance coordinates raises scGPT's norm CV from 0.003 to 0.026.
findings.recommended_action: Either remove norm CV from the compactness ranking or replace it with an offset-invariant statistic (e.g. sd of centred norms divided by RMS spread), and state which architecture applies LayerNorm at the hooked output. Correct README line 15. Rephrase conclusion 4 as 'three spectrum-based measures computed from one covariance', not four independent measures.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_geneformer.py lines 48-59 and 129 (log1p before median scaling), line 27 (MAX_SEQ_LEN = 2048); models/geneformer_v2_316m/config.json (max_position_embeddings 4096)

The Geneformer row (PR 2.73, PC1 57.6%, d90 20) therefore comes from a gene order and gene set that differ from what the model was trained on.

review.summary:
I reviewed B8833 against all ten checklist patterns: three-model cell-embedding "compactness" (participation ratio, PC1 share, d90, norm CV) on 4,269 fetal gut cells. geometry.py reproduces every number in outputs/ and SUMMARY.md: an in-memory rerun matches geometry.json exactly. Cell order and labels match across the three files, and STATE's codes map to names correctly. The arithmetic is sound, but the interpretation does not hold up.

(1) The scGPT extraction feeds raw UMI counts as gene values. The checkpoint was trained on per-cell 51-bin values (args.json: input_style "binned", n_bins 51). So the scGPT numbers come from an off-distribution input. scGPT's geometry (on the first 200 cells: PR 1.69, PC1 75.7%) closely mirrors the raw-count matrix itself (PR 1.45, PC1 82.5%), not the log-normalised matrix (PR 111). The headline "scGPT has the most compact manifold" therefore cannot be credited to the model.

(2) In all three models PC1 is a sequencing-depth axis. On the 200 cells with raw data, PC1 correlates with log total counts at |r| = 0.95 / 0.91 / 0.98. The models' PC1s correlate 0.90-0.92 with each other, and cell type explains only 6-9% of PC1. Depth explains 70% of scGPT's variance on those 200 cells. Removing it changes the magnitudes a lot (PR: scGPT 1.69 to 2.72, Geneformer 2.71 to 6.73, STATE 47.5 to 84.5), though the order survives.

(3) The Geneformer tokenisation departs from the official one: it applies log1p before dividing by gene medians and truncates at 2,048 tokens. The model has 4,096 positions and the median cell has about 3,500 genes.

(4) d90 is not stable. For STATE it depends on sample size (458 / 645 / 717 / 775 at n = 1000 / 2134 / 3000 / 4269) and on width (about 328 after a random projection to 512 dimensions). The full-sample 775 falls outside the halves range (644-650), and the summary leaves out the d90 halves range.

Further gaps: there is no baseline (input expression or random-weight models). The layer depth differs between models (this is acknowledged, but the conclusions are not limited to it). The norm CV is dominated by each model's mean offset. The halves were not computed for norm CV, and "not a sampling effect" claims more than resampling the same cells can show. The extraction cannot be rerun here, and weights load with strict=False.

Pattern verdicts:
- P1, no chance anchor: present, unaddressed.
- P2, no trivial or input baseline: present, unaddressed.
- P3, the measured object is mean-pooled gene tokens at one layer, not "the cell manifold": partly acknowledged.
- P4, cell-level resampling only, no donor count: present.
- P5, depth confound not residualised, and the inputs were preprocessed differently per model: present, unaddressed.
- P6, no null claims: not applicable.
- P7, one tissue, one layer, one pooling: acknowledged.
- P8, d90 unstable in n and width, and the summary reports halves selectively: present.
- P9, "cell manifold", "not a sampling effect", "differ by direction, not by size": present.
- P10, extraction not reproducible, silent strict=False loads: present.

Checks that came out clean: the order also holds within each of the seven cell types, so cell-type composition does not drive it. STATE's PR (about 48-55) survives width matching, so the width caveat holds for PR, though not for d90.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py lines 54-70 (tokenize) and 113-118; models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json; claim in SUMMARY.md lines 16, 25-27
findings.description: scGPT is given raw UMI counts as its continuous value input, with no normalisation, no log1p and no 51-bin per-cell binning. Its genes are cut to the top 1,200 by raw count, and ties among count-1 genes are broken by gene-index order. The checkpoint was pretrained on binned values with random gene sampling. The scGPT embeddings, and so the headline 'scGPT has the most compact cell manifold of the three', describe a misconfigured, off-distribution input pipeline, not scGPT's representation.
findings.evidence:
args.json: "input_style": "binned", "n_bins": 51, "trunc_by_sample": true. In tokenize(), val = expr[idx] (raw counts) is passed straight to model._encode(values=...).

In the 200-cell raw file:
- 39.5% of cells have a maximum count above 512 (the training values are at most 50).
- 98.5% of cells have more than 1,200 in-vocabulary expressed genes, so nearly every cell is truncated by raw-count rank.

scGPT's geometry tracks the raw-count matrix: on those 200 cells, the raw-count input has PR 1.45 and PC1 82.5%, scGPT has PR 1.69 and PC1 75.7%, and log1p-CP10k input has PR 110.6. scGPT's PC1 correlates |r| = 0.80 with the raw-count PC1 but only 0.31 with the log-normalised PC1, and r = 0.95 with log total counts.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract with scGPT's own preprocessing: normalize_total + log1p, per-cell binning into 51 bins, the pretraining pad/cls conventions, and sampled (not top-count) truncation to 1,200 genes. review.summary:
I reviewed the analysis against all ten checklist patterns. I reproduced every number in outputs/ and SUMMARY.md exactly by running shape_stats inline, with no files written. The model ranking scGPT > Geneformer > STATE holds across the 10 random halves and still holds after linearly removing sequencing depth, but the claims built on it do not stand as written. Depth (log library size plus log genes detected, measurable only in the 200 shipped cells) explains 70% of scGPT's embedding variance, 58% of Geneformer's and 12% of STATE's. PC1 correlates with library size at rho 0.97-0.99 in all three models, and PC1 alone gives chance-level cell-type kNN accuracy. So "cells lie close to one axis" describes a sequencing-depth axis, not a biological manifold. For scGPT this follows from feeding raw UMI counts into a value encoder that was pretrained on per-cell binned values: with sequence length fixed at 1,200 tokens, PC1 follows the mean raw input value at rho 0.98. Geneformer's tokenization also departs from the model's own scheme (log1p before median scaling, and a 2,048-token cap where V2 accepts 4,096). STATE's "775 PCs" is not a stable property: it is 288/456/645/775 at n=500/1000/2134/4269 and 329 after a random projection to 512 dimensions. The full-data value lies outside the half-sample range, and SUMMARY leaves that range out. PCs 101-775 carry chance-level cell-type information. Norm CV is computed on uncentred vectors and is close to fixed by the post-LayerNorm output: scGPT per-cell SD over dims is 0.957±0.003, so norm ≈ sqrt(512)×0.957. "Cells differ by direction, not by size" therefore holds by construction, and the README is wrong that all four measures are spectrum-based. The pattern verdicts:
- P1 (no chance-baseline anchor), P2 (no trivial or random-weights baseline), P4 (resampling at cell rather than donor level), P5 (depth confound) and P9 ("manifold" wording) are present and unaddressed.
- P7 (single layer and tissue): the layer mismatch is acknowledged but the conclusions are not limited to it.
- P8 (stability): partly addressed by the random halves, but d90 is unstable and norm CV was never computed on the halves.
- P10 (reproducibility): versions and commits are not pinned, weights load with strict=False, and STATE has no seed.
- P3 (endpoint–object mismatch): this is the "manifold" wording point.
- P6 (positive control): clean, because the analysis reports no null finding.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 25-31 (Conclusions 1-3); code/geometry.py lines 40-50 (no covariate adjustment)
findings.description: Sequencing depth drives most of the variance in the two models called 'compact'. The headline numbers (PC1 72%/58%, PR 1.82/2.73) and the phrase 'cells lie close to one axis' therefore describe how strongly each model's mean-pooled embedding tracks library size or gene count, not the shape of a biological cell manifold. Neither the analysis nor the caveats mention this confound.
findings.evidence: Raw counts exist only for the 200 shipped cells (data/raw/gut_epithelium_first200.h5ad); embedding rows 0-199 match them by cluster code and pseudotime. In those cells, Spearman rho of PC1 with library size is 0.97 for scGPT, 0.97 for Geneformer and 0.97 for STATE; with genes detected it is 0.89, 0.99 and 0.97. A linear regression on log(n_genes) and log(library size) explains R2 = 0.70 (scGPT), 0.58 (Geneformer) and 0.12 (STATE) of total embedding variance. The figures are similar within progenitor cells only (n=120): R2 0.71, 0.60 and 0.14, so cell-type mix does not explain it. After depth residualization on the 200 cells, scGPT PC1 share falls from 0.757 to 0.574 and PR rises from 1.69 to 2.72; Geneformer PC1 falls from 0.578 to 0.340 and PR rises from 2.71 to 6.73. Using all 4,269 cells, kNN (k=10) cell-type accuracy from PC1 alone is 0.15 for both scGPT and Geneformer, against a majority-class rate of 0.187. Between-type variance is only 4-7% of the total in every model.
findings.recommended_action: Report and remove the depth axis before calling anything a 'manifold'. Residualize the embeddings on log library size and log genes detected (or compare depth-matched cells) using the full count matrix, and report PR, PC1 and d90 before and after. Add a measure that links geometry to biology, such as how much variance cell type or pseudotime explains. Rewrite Conclusions 1-3 to say the dominant direction in scGPT and Geneformer is a depth axis.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py lines 54-70 (tokenize) and 77-80 (build_model); models/scgpt_whole_human/args.json (input_style binned, n_bins 51)
findings.description: The scGPT embeddings come from out-of-distribution input. Raw UMI counts go straight into the continuous value encoder, but the whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on per-cell binned values (input_style 'binned', 51 bins), which remove depth. The input is also cut to the top 1,200 genes by raw count with arbitrary tie-breaking. The headline scGPT result therefore reflects this preprocessing rather than scGPT's representation of the cells. The README and SUMMARY (line 6-7) also say pooling is over 'the cell's expressed genes', but scGPT pools only the 1,200 retained tokens.
findings.evidence: args.json lists "input_style": "binned", "n_bins": 51 and "max_seq_len": 1200. tokenize() passes raw counts with no normalization, log1p or binning. In the 200 available cells, maximum counts per cell reach 4,874 (median 417), far above the 0-50 bin range. 197 of 200 cells have more than 1,200 in-vocab expressed genes. At the cutoff, a median of 827 genes share the cutoff count, and about 301 are kept purely by np.argsort tie order. With length fixed at 1,200 tokens (197 cells), scGPT PC1 tracks the mean clamped raw input value at rho 0.983 and library size at rho 0.967. Depth enters through the raw values that binning would have removed.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract the scGPT embeddings with the checkpoint's own preprocessing: normalize_total, log1p and per-cell binning into 51 bins, with <cls>/pad handling as in scGPT's tokenize_and_pad_batch. Choose the truncated genes the way scGPT does (random sampling, or a stable documented rule). Recompute the geometry and restate Conclusion 1 only if it survives.

findings.description: STATE's d90 = 775 depends on sample size and width and does not describe the model's cell cloud. The summary's stability statement leaves out the d90 halves, which do not contain the full-data value. The STATE spectrum has a long tail that looks like noise, and that tail sets d90.
findings.evidence: run_log.txt reports STATE d90 = 775 on all cells but 644-650 on every half, so the full value lies outside the half range. SUMMARY line 20-21 quotes only the PR and PC1 halves. Inline subsampling gives d90 = 288, 456, 645, 718 and 775 at n = 500, 1000, 2134, 3000 and 4269, still rising. A random orthonormal projection of STATE to 512 or 1,152 dimensions gives d90 = 329 or 579, while PR stays at 54-57. Half of STATE's variance (52%) sits beyond PC100. kNN cell-type accuracy from PCs 101-775 is 0.202, against a majority-class rate of 0.187, compared with 0.81 from PCs 1-10. Only 56 eigenvalues exceed the largest eigenvalue of a column-permuted null. The STATE extraction (extract_state.py) uses STATE's sampled cell-sentence dataloader with no seed set. Token-sampling noise is a plausible source of this tail but was not tested.
findings.recommended_action: Do not report d90 as a model property without showing it at matched n and matched width. Report d90 halves next to the PR and PC1 halves, and drop or qualify '775 PCs'. Estimate the noise floor, for example by re-extracting STATE twice with different seeds and measuring within-cell variance, or by comparing with a Marchenko-Pastur or column-permuted spectrum. findings.description: Geneformer's tokenization does not match the model's own scheme. The script applies log1p to depth-normalized counts and then divides by the gene medians; Geneformer ranks normalized counts divided by medians with no log. Since log1p(x)/m does not preserve the ranking of x/m, the gene order fed to the model is changed. The input is also capped at 2,048 tokens although V2-316M takes 4,096 (config max_position_embeddings 4096), so most cells are truncated. The Geneformer numbers are therefore not those of the model under its intended input.
findings.evidence: Line 129 computes tokenize(np.log1p(expr / rs * 1e4), ...), and line 56 computes e_nz / m_nz. Line 27 sets MAX_SEQ_LEN = 2048. In the 200 shipped cells the median is about 3,476 expressed genes (range 788-8,557), so most cells exceed 2,046 gene tokens. Geneformer PC1 tracks genes detected at rho 0.99 (see F1).
findings.recommended_action: Re-tokenize with Geneformer's TranscriptomeTokenizer settings for V2 (no log, rank by normalized count divided by median, input size 4096) and recompute. At minimum, report how sensitive the Geneformer geometry is to these two choices.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 25 and 37-38 (Conclusion 1 vs caveat); code/extraction/* LAYER = 11
findings.description: Each model-level ranking ('scGPT has the most compact cell manifold') rests on one fixed layer index. That index is at a different relative depth in each model: the last layer of scGPT, but 12/18 of Geneformer and 12/16 of STATE. The caveat acknowledges this, but Conclusions 1-4 are still stated without qualification. Pooling also differs across models: top 1,200 tokens for scGPT, top 2,046 for Geneformer, and a sampled 2,048-token sentence for STATE. The comparison is therefore not like-for-like.
findings.evidence: In SUMMARY, line 37-38 is the caveat, while line 25 claims 'most compact ... on all four measures' without naming the layer. Only layer 11, one tissue and one pooling scheme were run (README; geometry.py line 82).
findings.recommended_action: Either compute the measures at matched relative depth (for example the final layer and the middle layer of each model, or a depth sweep) or limit every conclusion to 'layer index 11, gene mean-pool'. Add a CLS or cell-embedding comparison.

findings.description: 'Same on every measure and in every random half... It is not a sampling effect' goes beyond what the code shows. norm_cv is never computed on the halves. The halves overlap and are drawn from the same cells, donors and dataset, so the min-max range is not a confidence interval. Donor or batch variation, extraction randomness and other tissues are untested.
findings.evidence: The halves loop at line 71 covers only participation_ratio, pc1_share and d90. An inline check of norm_cv on the halves does preserve the order (0.0029-0.0032 / 0.0179-0.0190 / 0.0276-0.0288), but the analysis never ran it. The cells come from multiple donors, and no donor field is used or resampled.

findings.description: There is no null or chance anchor and no trivial baseline (P1/P2). PR, PC1 share and d90 are given without reference values. That leaves open how much of the compactness is learned and how much comes from mean-pooling LayerNorm-ed tokens; a random-weights model, a static-input-embedding mean-pool or a PCA of log-normalized expression would settle it.
findings.evidence: Inline column-permuted nulls give PR of about 201 (scGPT), 160 (Geneformer) and 1,350 (STATE), against observed 1.82, 2.73 and 56.5. Only 3, 2 and 56 observed eigenvalues exceed the null maximum. None of this, nor any baseline model, appears in the analysis.
findings.recommended_action: Give each statistic a null value (for example 'PR 1.82 vs column-permuted null 201'). Add a randomly initialized model of the same architecture and the input-embedding-only mean-pool as floors, plus PCA of the log-normalized expression on the same cells.

findings.location: SUMMARY.md lines 1, 25-27 ('cell manifold', 'cells lie close to one axis', 'cells differ by direction, not by size')
findings.description: The wording claims more than the measures support. PR, PC1 share and d90 come from a linear covariance spectrum, not from manifold geometry. Given F1 and F4, the 'one axis' and 'direction, not size' statements describe technical and architectural features, not cell biology.
findings.evidence: All measures in geometry.py lines 32-50 are linear eigen-spectrum statistics or norm statistics. The dominant axis is depth (F1), and the norm constancy comes from LayerNorm (F4).
findings.recommended_action: Replace 'manifold' with 'linear variance spectrum of mean-pooled activations'. Describe PC1 as a depth-correlated axis unless it survives depth correction.

findings.location: code/extraction/extract_scgpt.py line 84; state_loader.py line 62; extract_state.py lines 72-74, 107-121; README.md 'Extraction step'
findings.description: Reproducibility and integrity gaps (P10). Both scGPT and STATE load their weights with strict=False and never check or report missing keys, so a silently partly random model would go unnoticed. STATE's cell-sentence sampling has no seed. No versions are pinned for the scGPT source commit, transformers or torch. The full count matrix is not included. The STATE pooling falls back to every non-CLS position, including sampled unexpressed genes, whenever batch[7] is None.
findings.evidence: Line 84 of extract_scgpt.py is m.load_state_dict(sd, strict=False), and the return value is discarded. No seed is set in extract_state.py. The README names only 'arc-state 0.11.1'. No environment file exists.
findings.recommended_action: Assert that no transformer-layer keys are missing, set and record seeds, pin package versions and repository commits, record the run log of each extraction (missing keys, number of genes mapped, cells kept), and archive the full input matrix or give its CELLxGENE accession and filter.

grade_a.detection_reason: F2 meets every part of the key's detection rule. (1) It points at extract_scgpt.py tokenize, lines 54-70, and build_model. (2) It says raw UMI counts go straight into scGPT's continuous value encoder with no normalisation, log1p or binning. (3) It cites args.json input_style 'binned' and n_bins 51, so the checkpoint expects binned input. (4) It concludes that the scGPT embeddings are out of distribution, so the headline scGPT result reflects preprocessing rather than the model. It recommends re-extracting with 51-bin values and restating Conclusion 1 only if it survives. I checked its supporting numbers on the 200 shipped cells and they match: maximum count per cell up to 4,874 (median 417), 197 of 200 cells over 1,200 in-vocab genes, a median of 827 genes tied at the cutoff and 301 kept by tie order. No other finding names the binned-input mismatch. F1 only says PC1 tracks depth, which the key says is not enough on its own.

findings.reason: The numbers are accurate; I reproduced them on the 200 cells. PC1 Spearman with library size is 0.97, 0.97 and 0.97, with genes detected 0.90, 0.99 and 0.97, and between-type variance is 4-7%. But the key's known true facts say PC1 tracks depth in every model and in both versions, as expected when mean-pooling over a variable number of expressed genes. Its possible false alarms list 'PC1 being a depth axis is the load-bearing error'. F1 presents the depth confound as the critical flaw behind the headline and never names the raw-versus-binned scGPT input, which is the actual cause of the scGPT collapse.

F2 finds the key's documented error: raw UMI counts reach scGPT's continuous value encoder while the checkpoint was pretrained on per-cell 51-bin values (args.json). It ties this to the scGPT headline and Conclusion 1. The extra details on tie-breaking in the top-1,200 truncation and the 'expressed genes' wording are accurate but secondary.

It is true that STATE d90 depends on sample size: 775 on all cells against 644-650 on the halves. It is also true that SUMMARY omits the d90 halves. The key calls this a sample-size effect on a long-tailed 2,048-wide spectrum that changes no ranking, and F3 broadly agrees on the cause. STATE stays last on every measure, so qualifying '775 PCs' is a reporting improvement, not a substantive error.

README line 15 does say that all four measures use the mean-centred covariance spectrum, but norm CV uses uncentred per-cell norms (geometry.py line 43). I confirmed that centred norm CV is 0.51, 0.36 and 0.13, the reverse of the reported order. scGPT's near-constant pooled norm is consistent with post-LayerNorm outputs, and the key agrees that norm CV does not reveal the input problem. So the 'direction, not size' remark adds little. The formula itself is correctly coded per the key, and the finding does not affect the main ranking or the documented error.

This is exactly the key's 'other_real_issues' entry: the extractor ranks log1p(CP10k)/median instead of CP10k/median and caps input at 2,048 tokens instead of 4,096. The key says it is correct but not load-bearing; with Geneformer's own convention no conclusion changes. I confirmed the median of 3,476 expressed genes, range 788-8,557.

The layer-11 relative-depth mismatch is already a caveat in SUMMARY lines 37-38. The key lists 'different relative depth of layer 11' as a possible false alarm if treated as load-bearing. Asking for qualified conclusions is fair scoping but does not identify a wrong result.

This is true. The halves loop at geometry.py line 71 covers only PR, PC1 and d90, so 'same on every measure and in every random half' is not backed for norm CV. Overlapping halves are not a CI. The ordering on halves does hold as reported, so this is a minor overstatement.
The lack of null or baseline references (permuted spectrum, random-weights model, expression PCA) is a reasonable methodological suggestion. It does not show any reported result is wrong.
This is a terminology point. 'Manifold' overstates linear covariance-spectrum statistics. It is a wording issue only.

The code claims are accurate: strict=False with the return value unchecked in scGPT, no seed in the STATE dataloader, unpinned versions, and the pooling fallback when batch[7] is None. The key says re-running extract_scgpt.py reproduces the stored rows, so no silent weight-loading failure occurred. These are reproducibility-hygiene points only.

grade_b.detection_reason: F2 meets the key's detection rule. It says raw UMI counts go straight into scGPT's continuous value encoder with no normalization, log1p or binning. It says the whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on per-cell 51-bin values (args.json input_style 'binned', n_bins 51). It places the problem in extract_scgpt.py tokenize, lines 54-70, which matches the key's location. It also ties the problem to the result: the scGPT embeddings are out of distribution, so the headline scGPT result reflects preprocessing, and Conclusion 1 holds only if it survives re-extraction with binning. The key names exactly this defect. F1 also notes the depth axis, but the key says depth tracking alone does not count.

findings.reason: The numbers check out. For PC1 against library size I get Spearman rho 0.968, 0.968 and 0.971 across the three models, and 0.895 and 0.993 against genes detected. But the key lists 'Claiming PC1 being a depth axis is the load-bearing error' as a possible false alarm. Its known true facts say PC1 tracks depth in every model and in both versions, including binned scGPT (0.69), which is expected when mean-pooling over a variable number of genes. F1 presents depth as the critical reason the compactness headline is invalid. It never names the real cause, the unbinned scGPT input.

This is the key's documented error. Raw counts go into the continuous value encoder although the checkpoint was pretrained on 51-bin values (args.json), located at extract_scgpt.py tokenize, lines 54-70. F2 links this to the scGPT embeddings being out of distribution and to the headline ranking in Conclusion 1. Its extra points about truncation tie-breaking and pooling wording are side details.

True as stated. STATE's d90 depends on the number of cells (775 on the full data against 644-650 on the halves), and the summary leaves out the d90 halves. The key agrees this is a sample-size effect on a long-tailed spectrum that changes no ranking. F3 does not claim a bug, so it is not the listed false alarm, but the problem is only about how d90 is reported.

Confirmed. Norm CV is computed on uncentred X, and scGPT's pooled vectors show the LayerNorm signature: per-cell mean 0.017 and SD 0.957 across dimensions, almost the same in every cell. The mean vector's norm is 21.15 against an RMS spread of 4.64. Centred norm CV is 0.51, 0.36 and 0.13, the reverse of the reported order. This matches the key's other_real_issues. The extractor ranks log1p(CP10k)/median instead of CP10k/median, and it caps input at 2,048 tokens instead of 4,096. Both deviations are real. Adding null or baseline anchors is a reasonable methodological suggestion. Its absence does not make any reported result wrong.
A wording complaint: 'manifold' is used for linear spectrum statistics, and the finding leans on F1 and F4. Not a substantive error.
